Amenities in the room do meet Paradisus standards from Punta Cana. This will never be a true Circle experience. If you are looking for that Circle hotel ask questions before you go.

reviews.author: Kati B
reviews.title: Upgrade your room
reviews.text:
Once we paid to upgrade our room, our stay was wonderful. The first room given to us was in the basement and looked up at the delivery drivers coming in each day. The room smelled like mold and the huge air conditioning vent was moldy and needed to be cleaned. It was extremely dated.

Our new room was lovely and beautiful.

reviews.author: Shannon H
reviews.title: Ian 5 star recommended at the pool bar!!
reviews.text: Rating was 3 stars because of their air conditioning issues and no bathrooms close to the pools. BUT Ian at the pool bar was absolutely amazing ! The best service by far! Ian is a 5 star recommendation!!!

reviews.author: kathia2605
reviews.title: Good food, bad service and lack of maintenance
reviews.text:
The good: the food is delicious in all the restaurants, the beach is very beautiful and the service from Carlos and Alejandro is excellent at the Nespresso bar.

The bad: the hotel is already old and lacks maintenance. In the room the coffee maker did not work well, the capsules got stuck. The air made a very strange noise so it had to be at maximum power. The girl at the reception at The Reserve very apathetic. Upon check out they told us that we could leave our bags at the desk at The Reserve and they would deliver them to the main lobby. When requesting my car, I had to wait more than 30 minutes because they didn't know where the suitcases were, they never sent them. The service in all restaurants leaves a lot to be desired.

What saves the stay is the food.

reviews.author: uma K
reviews.title: This place is not for vegetarians.
reviews.text:
This resort was spectacular. Pool and beaches were clean. Our room was ocean view suite and very nice and clean. The staff were super friendly. But the food was terrible. As it is we have limitations being vegetarians. For breakfast, we thought of having some omelet, bread/bakery items, fruits etc. Bread, bakery items and even Pizza was like biting into cardboard. omelet was okay. Survived on fruits for breakfast. For lunch and dinner, we thought we could have authentic Mexican beans, rice, burritos or enchiladas which we normally eat in US but to our surprise none of those vegetarian options were available including beans!  Every dessert looked nice but tasted of nothing. After first day, every day I had to call the manager at the Buffett to make some beans and stir fry vegetables for us during lunch which he did manage to provide and we are grateful for that, but I shouldn’t be requesting and waiting to find the manager to get my meal every day. The same we had to do during dinner, request for vegetarian meal. It is all inclusive resort and we pay as much as anyone else so why not provide some decent veggie options. We shouldn’t be begging and requesting the staff for food. We survived only because of some wonderful staff. 
I wouldn’t recommend wasting your money on the spa. It is very filthy especially the steam rooms, pools. Only thing positive about the spa is again friendly staff.

reviews.author: Abraham
reviews.title: Nikte is not what we expected.
reviews.text:
The restaurants are always full and without a reservation option, very high waiting time up to 2 hours.
The benefit of booking as Nikte vs a lower rate was not seen.
Very few beds for the number of guests, we could not find a place on any day when we arrived, our things in the sun and on the floor where a bed was unoccupied.
There was the option of Balinese beds with extra crust (high for my taste).
A lot of pressure to get into their business talks (timeshare).

On the contrary, the KidsDom team was very friendly and kept the children very interested in each activity (except vacations).

reviews.author: Laura R
reviews.title: 3 star resort fun with kids not for foodies
reviews.text:
This is a large sprawling resort that has lots of potential with some money put into it from corporate. You can tell it was once luxurious and well maintained. I’m not sure what happened but it seems they stopped maintenance and have left it to deteriorate (but may be remodeling from one end to the other) There was a strike earlier this year by staff and you can tell it’s 50/50 with them. They seem overworked. The rooms seem like they are robbing Peter to pay Paul with items breaking, non functioning and missing. I would hate to stay here during full capacity. 

The gym and spa were quite nice and staff at the spa was wonderful. My facial was great and my friends massage was as well. Spa is a bit small for such a large resort. 

Our first room was missing outside chairs, fridge was not filled. At 11 pm first night it filled with sewer gas that was so toxic I walked down to the lobby in my robe because front desk didn’t answer my calls. IMO they are too shortstaffed at night. About 2 hours later and a few trips to the desk we were moved to an ADA room same floor ocean view which was beautiful! There were issues there as well but I was thankful we got moved. This was all in pyramid 1 which I highly recommend for kids. It’s quiet. Right in front of the kids area of the pool and rooms have full kitchens. 

Kids club was great! My child wasn’t into it but most kids will be. Great free childcare all day with breaks so you can feed your kids. Tip them well! Get a schedule so you don’t miss anything. 

Drinks and food are the downfall here and it’s really bad. The options are minimal liquor wise unless you visit specific bars and they run out of certain things. The juices are super tart or sugary but I expect that at an all inclusive at this price. The food is so monotonous and flavorless and from what I can tell all comes from the buffet one way or the other. By the 3rd day I didn’t even want to eat because it all tasted the same. They really need to figure out this food situation as lines are crazy at night but they do have buzzers now so you can get a drink or wander around. We ate everywhere but the Italian restaurant and I expect it comes from the pasta bar during lunch service. 

The ice cream parlor outside was my kids favorite she loved it! Beach is beautiful and close. The you have to pay for beds (250) but can negotiate if it’s slow.

reviews.author: giselnataliaerazo
reviews.title: I give it 3.5 out of 5.
reviews.text: In general very good, the pool, the restaurants, the beach and the employees are excellent. The room and cleaning if a regular. But you can have a good experience depending on what your character is like.

reviews.author: stevenga0
reviews.title: Okay
reviews.text: Was fun, but room is outdated and lacking a lot of activities. Some restaurants had great food and others had long wait times for food that was mediocre. Staff is friendly and great location for resort

reviews.author: erassocs
reviews.title: Wedding Trip
reviews.text: While the staff was friendly and the rooms were clean, the hotel shows it age. There is also no air conditioner in the atrium or public restrooms.  Its hard to relax and enjoy the gardens when you are constantly sweating.  The public restrooms have no air flow, so they are hot and smell like urine if you lucky if not straight open sewer smells.

reviews.author: R S
reviews.title: Not My Cup of Tea
reviews.text:
The staff were generally good. Several bartenders were exceptionally kind and friendly. Pascual was a waiter that went out of his way to make us feel welcome. The majority of the other waiters were nice enough, but less than attentive after food was delivered. 

Facility wise, there were some problems.  I noticed a roach in the buffet room early in our stay. I recognize this is an ongoing fight they have to content with, but it is what it is. Also, noticed there were government stickers on the front of the Hotel stating some type of health or safety issue. I am not fluent in Spanish and didn't take the time to translate. We stayed in the southern-most building on the property and felt pretty isolated and alone most of the time.  I wonder if it might have something to do with using credit card points to book through a 3rd party agency. 

I got sick one day, not sure why, and there was a maintenance crew that was hammering. This was very annoying while trying to rest from sickness. I had to call the front desk 3 times to get it to stop.

My wife, 2 small children, and I were stopped by the military on the beach and questioned as to where we were going and where we were staying. This was mid day and a little disconcerting. 

The restaurant group across the street Rosa Negra group, which contains several restaurants in an over-water setup was amazing. We toured all the restaurants, but  ate at Chambeau. It was outstanding. After being sick, and not really trusting the food at the resort, it was a welcome experience. 

The pools were very very warm, way too warm for my liking.

My kids loved experiencing the turtles hatching on the beach. 

I love Mexico and I hate to complain but I don't think I will be going back to Paradisus or Cancun. Though the beach is much better in Cancun, I generally prefer Cabo San Lucas, based on my experience.

reviews.author: Lenabean25
reviews.title: Meh
reviews.text: I would not come here again. We came with a chartered group so we didn’t choose this location. It was okay but nothing special. We had a leak in our room and they said “yeah, just put towel down” and didn’t seem to care. Staff was inattentive and not terribly friendly.  Staff seemed clueless whenever we asked for anything as if it was everyone’s first day working there. Food was very good. Bar was great. Pool was very nice and well maintained. It certainly was not horrible. But I’ve stayed at much better places

reviews.author: pcosta68
reviews.title: NIKTÉ Disappointment
reviews.text: Hotel rooms need updating +++ (especially Nikté), the beach area needs to be better organized, there is lack of food variety in buffet, concierge service not satisfactory, disappointing NIKTÉ experience…not sure if I would go back.

reviews.author: Alanna T
reviews.title: Not if you have kids
reviews.text:
If you’re good with a family hotel that doesn’t allow kids anywhere post 9pm this is the one (currently sat in bed in my room writing this)!

Food is good for an all inclusive, the hotel is spotless, and the views are great. However…

I’ve NEVER been to a resort that’s happy to give 14 year olds alcohol in a bar, and then tell you that your impeccably behaved children that they are banned from the one place there is entertainment in the evening. Literally ridiculous!!

Depends what you’re after, but I would strongly recommending not coming here with children

reviews.author: lzelaya88
reviews.title: Just ok
reviews.text: Service is spotty with the exception of the two bartenders Salvador and Levy at the Asian fusion bar/restaurant in the middle of the mall looking resort.  They were gracious, funny and helpful.  At aqua marina we experienced sad, bored & unmotivated waiters.

reviews.author: Humberto354
reviews.title: They do not comply with what they offer at the time of booking (nikte)
reviews.text:
We booked in the nikte package but they did not respect some services offered on the page at the time of booking such as butler services, premium drinks were charged separately and in the room they were not provided even when it says they are included, no restaurant reservations or lounge chairs.

The treatment of some waiters was not very attentive and cordial, they forgot what we ordered.

reviews.author: Veronica P
reviews.title: Paradisus Cancun August/September
reviews.text:
In general, my stay at the hotel was very good. What I didn't like was that when I arrived they didn't have the room I had paid for and they offered me a lower one than the one I had. I had to pay for an upgrade so they would give me the same room I had but with a sea view since I had it with a view of the lagoon.

The coffee bar they have is spectacular, especially Alejandro's service is excellent, always with a smile and he offers you absolutely everything, he even improves your original order.
In general the service is good

reviews.author: Ana G
reviews.title: I would take away a star
reviews.text:
They made me wait a long time before giving me my PREMIUM SUITE with a view of the Lagoon. The photo I attached corresponds to the view I had… view of the Lagoon? Only it was one floor below the reception… my eyes then went to the parking lot. I ask for a room change and they give me an ocean view room (not a premium suite) that was under maintenance (they said it was the only one available). They charged me almost 5,000 pesos more for three days. In total 26,000 pesos for three days. The sea view room should have continued maintenance and attached photos to support my words.
A hotel of that category and that price cannot afford to accommodate its clients in rooms like that. Not to mention the treatment of the receptionists who treat you as if they were doing you a favor. They lack a customer service course.
The rest of the staff excellent. Especially the waiters from all areas. I congratulate them for their always kind treatment.

reviews.author: Ravi26v
reviews.title: Wonderful ambience with great pools and beach access, major disappointment was food
reviews.text:
Hotel looks extraordinary, feels like a Paradise, beach access is great, pools are awesome, kids rooms is great, spa is good. 

Drawbacks: 
1. Restaurants are not great expect for Malva 
2. Rooms doesn’t feel like 5 starts 
3. Being in tropical climate Air conditioning needs to be powerful 
4. All the included entertainment options are not disclosed ahead (kayaking, photography, etc) 
5. Coupons are useless

reviews.author: Alex Fabricio Jaramillo
reviews.title: Blue agave restaurant
reviews.text:
Separate note, the hotel… is good, beautiful but at times its staff is careless. If you don't have the "all-inclusive" bracelet, they don't pay attention to you or make problems with each order. I found an empty water bottle on the 0th floor on Monday, by Thursday, it was still in the same place.

Its restaurants are very good but those that take the medal are Cielito Lindo and Blue Agave, in the latter, Very good tacos. Especially the chistorra one. The gringa de pastor and the cochinita are recommended.

Normal portions for a hotel and reasonable price

Exceptional attention from Daniel and his manager Barbara.

reviews.author: shoney
reviews.title: So conflicted…
reviews.text:
My husband I were vacationing at majestic elegance costa mujeres and decided to extend the trip 2 nights.  Back in 1997 we stayed here so we decided to go back to where our first trip occurred… enjoy some nostalgia 

Check in:  awful.  Long line. Slow.  

Lobby: stunning.  Incredibly hot.  This is a theme throughout.  

Service: impeccable. We sat in the upper tier beach section after check in.  I thought it might be so when the server approached I asked. He said since no one was here could he please get us lunch and drinks.  Why not?? He brought us out more than we ordered and it was lovely. 

The service everywhere was great. I don’t have names but everyone was wonderful. 

The room:  it was ok. Bed and linens were fine. No snacks or mini bar stocked on check in but replenished the next day    The tub was cracked the drain was scary. Not the nice walk in shower we have been accustomed to in the years since our visit 

The food:  this is where they shine. Fantastic meals.  Food quality and presentation on point.  The whole fried fish and coconut shrimp at the restaurant by the pool was absolutely fantastic.   The lack of a/c is an issue.  The first night we went tot the outside Mexican buffet. It was fine but the homemade to order marquesita was unforgettable.  Perfect.  Entertainment was great.  
Italian;  my husband didn’t wan to go because of the lack of a/c but we went early and got a table next to fountain.  Food and service fantastic. So glad went 

Bathrooms: the bathroom by the pool downstairs from the lunch restitution was gross. Like really gross. Lobby bathroom
 Was a little better but not much 

Pools.   Way too deep.  Too hot in august to enjoy. Didn’t feel clean. Left quickly

Beach: perfect. Had a ball in the water and drink service was great 

Overall: beautiful property.  Older facilities. Fantastic food    Way too hot !!!  Lack of air conditioning during. A Mexican heat wave was unbearable!!!

reviews.author: victorbotello01
reviews.title: Fumigate
reviews.text: The trip made them lose the cockroaches in the room, they have to take great care of that aspect, not suggesting a room change was also very discouraging, it costs nothing to the hotel, they were not full anyway.

reviews.author: joannicprat
reviews.title: Family vacation
reviews.text:
We stayed 7 days. We paid for the nikte room. We traveled with a girl and a baby.
I do not recommend nor would I choose the nikte option again, it feels like a scam.
The truth is that the hotel is very good but it seems that it is going downhill....you can see it in the details, in the old facilities, in the food, in the drinks, in the pools and in the restaurants.
I don't think I will return to this hotel again.

reviews.author: Raul Mota
reviews.title: Bad restaurants, only Malva is an option
reviews.text: Restaurants in general need to improve service, Malva is the only one to recommend as they offer buffet with variety, Cielito Lindo and rest long waiting time, hotel service if you are US citizen it is guarantee you will be well served, rest or mexican will not be good served

reviews.author: Imaphleb
reviews.title: Mixed review
reviews.text: Property is beautiful but lacking A/C in areas that should have it. Pool is beautiful but needed more cleaning (maintenance was being done on it). Food was ok, not wonderful. Restaurants were mostly good. Staff were very nice/helpful. “Circle” staff too pushy.

reviews.author: Richard M
reviews.title: Hotel needs to spend money on renovating bedding and A/C’s. And expand front desk staff so you not stuck in lines twice.
reviews.text: Food always good at Paradisus. Checkin always slow and this is third time needed to wait until 4pm for room. Mattresses here need to be replaced feel old and way to soft. A/C units extremely noisy. Pool and beach fine actually better beach than playa Carmen Paradisus but food choices there much broader. I came back again because manager In playa Carmen gave us 2 nights free for the long wait for our room last trip but even though there is no expiration date on it when I tied to use it was told policy is it’s only for 60/90 days after issue. Manage told me next trip didn’t say in 90 days or less and I got delayed as I developed cancer and landed in hospital for almost 2 years in and out. Anyway I think next trip will be Hyatt, crown plaza or Westin.

reviews.author: lead372023
reviews.title: Not as good as it used to be last year
reviews.text: A few of the restaurants near the pool were not open anymore maybe due to staff shortage. Watch out for your stuff at the pool. Staff threw my towel and shirt in the bin because they “didn’t see anyone there”. Unprofessional. At least hold my shirt at the towel desk. Hotel room was set at 65 degrees but probably never went below 75. AC could have been better. Probably gonna try a different hotel next year.

reviews.author: Paola V
reviews.title: Great service not so great accommodations
reviews.text: Service was excellent and the food was great but the hotel is old and needs an update specially in the rooms and pool area. The lobby and restaurants look good but the rooms need to be remodeled. They are old and the shower was not in the best condition either. The pool wasn’t great needs to be clean better. But the service was great

reviews.author: Marlenne R
reviews.title: Wish it was cooler
reviews.text: The pool and beach area were great. Food was okay, but I liked that there was a good variety . Overall a good resort for family. I loved that they had tons of activities every night. However, I did not like that the room was never cool enough. Every single restaurant that we went to was HOT . Everywhere that we walked inside the resort was very hot. I love the beach but when it’s time for dinner , I like to feel refreshed after a nice shower but that was never the case. I stayed there 6 nights. People were very nice.

reviews.author: 260kathyf
reviews.title: Beautiful Property -- Rooms need some TLC
reviews.text:
Though we completed the pre-check process, it still took almost an hour to check in.  Many more clerks are needed at the check-in desk.  Some signage would be most helpful, after standing around for quite some time, we found out that the Reserve check in is in  Building 5.

The lack of air conditioning in the common area of the main lobby building (Building 3) made it very uncomfortable.  Some of the entertainment is in the Ginger Bar, I felt bad for the performers and everyone watching, sweat was dripping from everyone.  

The room needs some updating, though the bed was very comfortable.  The tile in the bathroom, though pretty, looks as though the construction crew forgot to clean up after the job, splats of grout here there and everywhere, plus they left construction writing on tiles.  The lighting in the bathroom is very dim, the makeup mirror light would not turn on.  Our sliding glass door would not slide open to the balcony, we finally called maintenance to have them fix it, after 3 days someone came to look at it and had to adjust the wheels.  It was a temporary fix as it happened again.  New patio doors would be a huge plus.  

The grounds are beautiful, the staff is very friendly and very hard working.  I don't know how they all work in high humidity heat like that year around, very impressive.  I give the bar tenders and food staff A+++.  The entertainment was enjoyable and the food was VERY good, there was nothing that I didn't like.

Overall, not a bad place to stay, but it would be oooooh so much better with a few updates.  

The pools were very nice, we spent a lot of time swimming.  A few more chairs/loungers is much required if you don't want to spend money on a cabana every day.  The loungers, few that there are, were all claimed by 7am each morning.

reviews.author: Vanessa C
reviews.title: Not gluten free friendly
reviews.text:
I’m going to write this review in full disclosure because I wish someone would’ve fully informed me about this place before I went as I am going to inform you now. Please keep in mind we paid extra for VIP service or what they call “The Reserve” guests. 

First and foremost, the staff gets 5 stars. They were absolutely amazing. I will provide you with names with places below. 

Checking in: Upon your arrival, you walk into Tower three. I read that you are to be served a drink from when you walk in however, that was not provided. As noted, we paid extra for the reserved package. I was surprised that while regular guest were provided an air-conditioned lounge to check in, we were told to walk pass two towers to find the reserve check in area in the heat. Our room wasn’t ready, we had to wait an hour, so we sat with the concierge Abel. He told us that the reservations for the restaurants were no longer applicable and that they got rid of that three weeks ago. This is something I wish we would have known prior to us leaving to our vacation because nowhere on the website does it say this information. Throughout our stay, Abel did acknowledge my birthday by sending a treat to our room, and helped us with a reservation to their steakhouse. However, when it came to verify whether or not the Italian restaurant on site had any gluten-free options, it was like pulling teeth.  It took him a long time to respond to me to see whether or not I am able to eat at that restaurant, which by the time he had confirmed that they had a gluten-free options, it was too late to eat there.  

Restaurants: If you have a gluten allergy, do not come here. The options for food are extremely low. I also am allergic to corn therefore, I hardly was able to eat much.

Lemon fish: This place is Japanese infused and mainly serve sushi. The manager Daniel gave the absolute best service ever. Since this restaurant was in tower three, reserved area is in tower five, I was not able to consume the alcohol that they had there due to my allergies. Daniel was nice enough to have someone go to the reserved area and get the type of liquor that I could drink. Miguel was our server and he was the only server out of the whole weekend that started with a question “Do you have any food allergies?” I was very thankful that he cared to ask and was able to make my own sushi roll that did not contain gluten or corn. It was my birthday, so they brought me some fruit and sang happy birthday to me. Daniel and Miguel went above and beyond for my birthday and I really appreciate them for that.  

Sal (steakhouse)- Not a lot of gluten-free options since a couple of their meats are marinated. While the restaurant was great, and the service was good, our server was Ignacio, I would not recommend their version of a top sirloin. I asked for medium, however it came out medium rare, and I was not able to cut into it. Our server did ask if I wanted another steak however, at that point I was over it.  

Sante- We ate breakfast here every morning, this is strictly only for reserve guests. The views are beautiful and the food was decent.  Servers like Moises and Luis made our trip. I was having a tough time not being able to eat much and Moises was so funny and full of life that he made my day just with his laugh. 

The Spa/Salon: The morning of my birthday my hair was tangled and I was not able to brush it. Lol. It had been knotted from the braids I had from the day before. I called the salon to see if they would be able to give me at least a blowout and if possible, curl my hair. I spoke to Alfredo, who informed me that the salon was going under renovations. However, he was going to call me back and see what he could do. Within minutes he called back and gave me the good news that they could take me in. When I got there, Christina and Isabell took care of me.  Isabell did such a great job on my hair and I am so grateful that they were able to take me in on my birthday.  

Overall, would I ever come back? Absolutely not. While the staff was incredible, the food was mediocre. I appreciate that they acknowledged my birthday, and everyone would greet you every single morning, noon, and or night. The views and beach were beautiful. Did I feel like VIP? Not really. While having better liquor was great, I’m not much of a drinker, I expected better from the restaurants.

reviews.author: veronica i
reviews.title: Very disappointed
reviews.text:
We have a bad experience with people in the lobby at the check in . They made us to wait until 11 pm to decide to switch our room. Ee had no AC in the old room, we reprted several times  but they ignored us. 
But at the breakfast and lunch the Pascual team made our stay very pleasnt. Pascual is a very kund  and he pay attention to the customers. Also    Manuel Ledesma, Antonio and Reynaldo. Thank to them our stay was a success. We have been very disappointed with the customer service the hotel has,
We will not come back and we will not recommend this until
Something change.
Thank you Pascual team.

reviews.author: Miamiagent123
reviews.title: Beautiful hotel, but slacking on service.
reviews.text:
To start off, this resort is beautiful. The view of the beautiful torques water is breath taking. That’s the good. Now for the bad. For a 5 star hotel I felt they missed the mark. Our room’s A/C was not working properly. While they did offer us to change rooms- we felt it was an inconvenience- they brought us a floor fan, which it helped. This was a major issue because the entire resort is a solarium with natural plants hanging from the different floors- your room and other closed spaces were the only area air conditioned. In the Mexico heat this was not the greatest thing to feel hot all day no matter the time. 

The food in all the restaurants were subpar - serving sizes, quality of the food and the 1 hour and 30 minutes wait. You can’t reserve a time and we’re forced to either wait and wonder around the resort or eat at the buffet which had minimal options. I would say though the breakfast was pretty good- possibly the best meals available. The pool was nice, deeper than usual and not tailored for kids unless they know how to swim well. There were about 50 chairs tops, very little for how large the pools stretched. The majority of the lounging chairs were beds that were for daily rent of 250/day. If you weren’t up by 7am good luck finding a chair post 9am. 

What made this experience pretty good despite all of this was our concierge Sheratory Elias  who consistently made sure we were being attended to and went above and beyond to make our stay as comfortable she could. one bartender Salvador who worked on the 1st floor by the beds and Yesenia who was one of our pool servers who made our experience better!

reviews.author: Alfredo S
reviews.title: It was a great hotel in the past. It’s nice but not an impressive stay.
reviews.text: For a week vacation the hotel covered our needs with a clean room, good food and great spa. The kids care was great, we got lots of help from the concierge on tips using the hotels events. Would I stay again, probably not, would I recommend? Maybe if the stay is less than $250 per night.

reviews.author: UncleFro
reviews.title: Great location a bit to high of a price for the value
reviews.text: When booking in this hotel, be aware of the transportation to the hotel. The Uber app works but apparently local taxi hate Uber drivers. This hotel does not have specific transportation transportation costs in our case two adults two kids $71. The beds by the pool are extra. Only a few bars have premium drinks.

reviews.author: Big B
reviews.title: Vacation with the boys
reviews.text: The sports bar is very fun to be at with the waiters and bar tenders named Karwa, gaby, valentin, and gingerz. They did a very good job, there may not be too many places but the sports bar is the place to be here.

reviews.author: CastG
reviews.title: Family trip with kids- must read
reviews.text:
Just returned from a 6 night trip from Paradisus Cancun. I traveled with family & young children (19 in our group) a few things you should be aware of.

First the negatives:
-No AC in 90% of the hotel :( I wish we knew that before booking because I would have thought twice before going. Our room had AC & maybe 2 restaurants I remember. My brother's room was hot, the AC was terrible. The buffet had AC only in the first few tables (which were never available) if you ever been to Cancun you know the heat + humidity is very uncomfortable. 
-Restaurants were long waits so that was frustrating with young children. They do have outdoor pool service for food & room service so that was a great alternative.
-The Reserve/Nikte upgrade was a total waste of money. Our Concierge didn't do much for us & I didn't even meet him in person the entire time I was there. :( Don't waste your $$ it is not worth it, we had zero perks. 
-Check in took 1 hour min, even though we were Reserve/Nikte it still took way too long. Luckily I was prepared with snacks for my kids since they were hungry.
-The food is ok, nothing memorable or incredible. 

The Positives:
-The hotel itself is gorgeous with beautiful scenery to take pictures. The lobby is very jungle like with lots of greenery (which explains the no AC).
-Everything was very clean & well maintained.
-The Staff is very friendly & helpful, they were always willing to assist with whatever we needed. The staff is what makes the experience worth it minus the concierge lol. 
-Our house keeping lady kept checking in with us everyday & was on top of it.
-The beach & pools are amazing but the pool water did feel too warm at times.  

All in all we had a great time & made the most of our trip. We are not super picky travelers but we spent a lot of $$ on this trip so we expected 4 star quality.  We will pick another place next time :(

reviews.author: Sarat V
reviews.title: Summer Family vacation
reviews.text: It was a much-anticipated family vacation. This isn't our first tripto Paradisus. We have a lot of good memories from a trip 9 years ago. The reason we booked again is because of that. Not one, not two, but five rooms. Despite everything else being top notch, I'm really disappointed that none of the rooms have air conditioning. Despite repeated calls and complaints, they just gave me a fan. That's it? We paid thousands per room, and we get a fan?

reviews.author: Curlies
reviews.title: Not as good as it used to be
reviews.text:
We have been to Paradisus multiple times over the years - adults only section, reserve (previously royal service). 

We used to love our meals at LaPalapa (now Sante) but menu changed for worse and a number of items are no longer available - e.g. eggs benedict (now extra charge via room service only). Lunch options no longer include spring rolls and the snack/food options available in the Reserve Lounge (Piramide 5) are also limited - used to be hot options like eggs benedict, spring rolls, macaroons etc. Other restaurant menus changed for worse too - we used to like Mole, Fuego, Vento, Market Grill etc, had plenty choices - now a number of dishes are "extra charged" and also the selection of food is not as good as it used to be (mainly focused on seafood).

The reserve pool and beach are very relaxing - beautiful setting, great drinks service, pool concierage are fantastic too! Royal Service Butler has been replaced with Concierage, its not as good, less personalised. 

Staff works hard (overall the service is excellent!) but seem to be less happy - there was a strike during our stay (limited services were available during the strike/services commenced later). The above combined with cost cutting reflected in quality of stay (and increasing cost of stay) does not encourage to return to Paradisus - other 5 star resorts in Cancun offer better value for money.

It's supposed to be 5 star hotel and at the check in we have not been even offered a cold towel or a drink. 

Overall its disappoing to see the hotel heading in a bad strategic direction, cost cutting is likely to discourage loyal clients and returning visitors who are aware of disappointing changes implemented over the last couple of years.

reviews.author: Karen R
reviews.title: Not as good as it used to be
reviews.text:
This was my 4th time in paradisus cancun and probably my last one .
I used to love coming here because of the great stuff and good food, this time i can’t say the same.
Food isn’t as good as it used to be, staff are not very friendly anymore and it was hard to get a reservation for dinner to the restaurants we wanted to try. and at dinner time It took us more than 20 min to finally be greater. We even convinced some friends to come with us and i know their experience wasn’t what they were expecting.
I’m glad we upgraded to reserve because the only good part about this trip is that we got to see Rene from Kanna area and always makes sure we are having a good time and always so happy to see us. We got to meet Moises and Miguel that took such a good care of us at the reserve area. 
I hope this place goes back to what it used to be because I would love  to come back to see Moises Miguel and Rene.
Thank you guys for been the past part of our trip

reviews.author: Evandro L
reviews.title: A great resort, but could be better if they stop focusing on business meetings.
reviews.text:
First of all, I would like to say I had a great time and I do recommend the hotel.
However, there are some things they definitely need to re-visit.

The good points: 
Drinks were great
Staff was great
Sea is amazing
Hotel is gorgeous
Ice cream 

The points to improve:
Restaurants: some of them were good, some not quite good. But none of them were excellent. I've been to 4 and 3 star hotels which the food was better.

Kids areas: I booked this hotel because of some pictures I've seen of the indoor soft play areas for my kids. They took that out to make a escape room, which is just nonsense for a resort (but probably is a thing for business meetings, that seems to be their focus now). They have now a small area, where you can only leave your kids with the staff (you can not play with them yourself), which is not what we were looking for.

Concierge: It's very cool to have a concierge service. But my concierge was not very good. She did not sort anything I asked and could not get the reservations I wanted for the restaurants. She just wanted me to waste 2h on a Melia Circle meeting that I did not want to attend. To book restaurants, the hotel could create an app that would be easier for us than having to rely on the concierge.

Swimming Pool area: Probably my biggest disappointment. They are putting the Balinese beds all around the pool and charging $250 usd per day to use it. If you do not want to pay this, there are some very limited chairs, that usually gets taken very early.  I got down to breakfast at 8.30AM and all the chairs were taken, which was annoying as I have 2 babies with me.

It feels that the hotel started to focus only on making money and forgot about the comfort and quality for the clients.
That lead to a focus on Business meetings and the stupid Bali beds all around.
It's still a good resort, but management should revisit their focus/strategy.

reviews.author: erwinespi1026
reviews.title: Needs maintenance
reviews.text: Rooms needed an update. Staff are nice except the people at front desk. I booked 2 nikte rooms but they treat it as a standard room. They were even going to put us on separate floors even though I requested 4 months ago at the time of booking to put us close together since we have kids and elderly. Complete disregard for our safety as a family! I got so upset and eventually they put us on the same floor. Concierge is non existent as they don’t reply to you. Will definitely NOT book here again.

reviews.author: jamesV8732NO
reviews.title: 3-star, not a 5 star property
reviews.text: Needs a renovation. Property calls itself a 5-star; it is three star at best. All areas including guestrooms need a renovation. Very worn looking. AC was LOUD in the guestrooms. Some of my associates had rooms that would not cool down. No AC in open lobby areas - very hot and humid. And this is not open air - these areas are separated by doors to the exterior. Staff was very friendly and food was ok. Lemon Fish (Paid restaurant) the food was great.

reviews.author: RonH80
reviews.title: What changed?
reviews.text:
In 2020 we stayed here and had an excellent experience.  Services, food, and amenities were great! This resort was actually recommended by our friends, So we had to try it. After our visit, COVID hit and the world shut down. 3 years later, this was the first choice to come back because we had such a good experience. However this time the experience was far from what we originally enjoyed. I can only describe this experience with a single term: "Inconsistent".

I read some of the recent reviews and compared the experience people had. The commonality I have found is that if you didn't have a more "enhanced" reservation, your quality and consistency of experience would differ (Yes, you do get what you pay for).  As an non "enhanced" example, no one wished us farewell on our last day, no one wished us a happy anniversary when every day that we went to a restaurant (even on the day of the anniversary) they would ask "Are you celebrating anything special this evening", we would tell them. Not a word. So I am not entirely sure what the point of asking if you really have no intentions of making a special day more special.

** The positives **: These member's/restaurants is what gave us the positive experiences

Baggage to the room - Sorry forgot his name. But he was very friendly and helpful

Carlo's @ Malva on May 6 evening. He was very nice, friendly, and attentive

Rogelio - Not sure of his position, but he showed genuine interest in our concerns at the front of house. He actually remembered us two days after and asked if we resolved everything.

Antonio @ Agua Marina on May 7. Very good service and friendly.

Miguel @ Lemon Fish on May 9. Very friendly, no questions asked. great service.

Raphael @ Lemon Fish on May 10.  Very friendly, Good service

Ivon, Rubi, Tessa, Itzel, Brenda @ Kidsdom for all the days we had our kids there. They by far get our biggest praise. Our kids couldn't get enough of them. We had to drag our kids out of the kids club because they enjoyed it so much. Thank you!!!  This service and team have always been consistent in quality and care! 

Agua Marina - Great food if you like seafood. The taste, consistency, and quality of food were great here. Hit and miss on service when it gets busy. 

Lemon Fish - If you like Japanese sushi, this is not bad. We ate here twice. Both food quality and service were consistent. I am always hesitant to have raw fish in a foreign country. But the quality was good.

Blue Agave - tacos were good. 

Malva (Buffet) - I am mixed about this place. Inconsistent on quality and variety.  My kids loved coming to the buffet due to the wide range of foods they can select from.  

Overall, no one got sick from the food. That's always a positive. Other than the buffet, all the restaurants we went to were good.

The facility grounds appeared to have been well-kept in terms of the greenery and plants. The hotel tried to clear some of those seaweeds, but honestly. Having 5 people with satchels going back and forth hand-picking them is not productive and not doing any damage to the never-ending seaweed. You need some sort of industrial vacuum to siphon the seaweed out.

Live Music - The live music was good. When they did have them, they were great. The trio at Augua Marina, the Mariachi band one night, and the stage music with singer by the lunch box pool one night. They were good. The music selection and energy were good.

**The Negatives **

As much as I would like to name every person who didn't provide us with a positive experience, I do recognize that most of these staff don't get paid much and rely on this job to support their families. So I would provide this portion of our review as feedback and the reason why we would not be coming back to Paradisus Cancun on next trip to Mexico.

Guest services -  On the first day we were there. we had requested "new" soaps, lotions, body washes, etc. For anything that required a pump and refillable, we requested brand new ones. Our kids had skin sensitivities and would cause serious reactions if the contents of the pumps were in any way contaminated.  We requested this the evening we arrived. We didn't get what we needed till the next day after lunch. But what made the wait for a relatively simple request was not so simple. In between this time, we had called guest services multiple times requesting "new" items, no one showed. Then we went to the front desk and made the same request multiple times. At one point we got ready for the beach before lunch, walked to the front counter and requested again. At that time, the front desk tells me they have already placed it in our room. I said, "its not possible, we just walked down from our room from". So the staff turns his screen to face me to show me it has been done as if I am accusing him of making it up.  I told the staff that we never left the room until now. How could they have replaced all the handpumps when we are in the room? So I caved, and I walked back to my room took a look at the same room we left a few minutes before, and walked back to the front counter to tell him. No, it has not been replaced. This time I had physically removed all the pump soaps and lotions and placed them in the closet so that they understand we need "new" products.  When I told the person at the front desk I had done this, he did not seem pleased. I even called him out saying "Look, I not wanting to take these products home, I just want new ones".  Not sure what clicked in this person's head to understand what I needed. But finally, the person understood I didn't want to re-fill my pumps and I wanted "new" unused ones.  To add insult to injury, he then demanded that I take him to our room and collect the pumps I had removed.  So I walked him to our room, grabbed all of them, and placed it in his hands. Not impressed. We walked back down and I then asked if they can deliver the pumps to the front desk so I can grab it from them. The staff said ok and I went off for the day.  When the day was coming to an end and our family was ready to come back, I went to the front desk to collect the items.  They didn't have it there. They told me a supervisor had sent up the new products. I went up and checked and they appeared to be new.  This process started at around 8 pm May 6 till around May 7, 3 pm.  Wow! That was the first 24 hours

In addition, we had been requesting basic amenities in our room for the first 5 days. each time guest services would either bring partial items requested or not show up at all. This trip really tested our patience to the point I had an argument with my spouse. My spouse is very humble and understanding. But the breaking point for us both is when we showed up in the afternoon around 3 pm, our room was not even made. Then when we came back again just before getting ready for dinner, we realized we were missing towels. Not enough for our family. They just didn't replenish it.  So my spouse called and complained not only about the lack of attention, but one of the towels had a stain on it, as if someone wiped their butt with it. My spouse was very upset and when we tried to convey our displeasure with the guest services, they said "You had a fight because of towels?". There were no apologies for the deficiencies and when we said we threatened to write a review, this person tells us to "Go write a review". As if he didn't care. So here it is.  Customer service was one of the highlights we looked forward to coming back to. But this time, it was below the standard of care and attention by the guest services.  They were insulting, condescending, and not helpful.

Oh, but there is more.  two days before we were about to leave, we get a call from guest services telling us how they valued our business and return to Paradisus, So they'd like to offer us some specials for spas or services.  So you insult us, anger us, discard our requests for 5 days during our stay, then come back and tell us how you value our business.  Really?!?!?!

strangely two days before we leave they also started to deliver full sets of towels in addition to what was provided. Trying to make up for the poor customer service? Nice try but the damage was done. If I operated a luxury resort, regardless of staffing shortages, renovations, or customer requests...Customer Service should NEVER be sacrificed. People can get over delays and shortfalls.... but never customer service.

Cleanliness:
The rooms were ok. There are some obvious TCL needed for the rooms but were in satisfactory condition. We had the lagoon view room with two twin beds.

Pool side was ok. In the morning, if you didn't notice, many of the chairs had some sort of poop on the chairs and towels. That was gross. Probably from the birds or rodents? I dunno.  Watch for it. Looked like little drops of green Hershey kisses. Yuck

Beach side. Service was inconsistent. You have one day where the person was on the ball and tended to all your needs, and check on you.  The other times, you had to go get your own drinks or had to approach them standing in the back.

Food and Hygiene:
The one thing that really grossed us out was the buffet. It wasn't that long ago that the world shut down because of COVID and the spread of this virus.  I guess we haven't learned about sanitation and food handling.  PLEASE have enough tongs or serving utensils!!!!!!! and a place to put them back. We saw serving utensils and tongs handled by people and then place the tongs right into the food.  Staff needs to monitor this. During the 7 nights we were here, every day I have seen guests go to the bathroom and walk straight out without washing their hands. Can you imagine those people handling the tongs and then placing the tongs right on top of the food? OMG.

Pest control.  Need to do something about the fruit flies at the buffet. People don't realize how many of those fruit flies have landed on literally every piece of fruit. Once I saw this, I stopped my kids from eating pre-cut fruits.

Amenities:
One noticeable difference was the lack of amenities for guests.   We sense a significant budget restraint on some things that we thought would have been available. My spouse liked the spin classes, variety of poolside food, and certain giveaways. Non-existent this time. 

Reservations:
We had booked directly through Melia this time versus a third-party travel provider. Although it appears there were more perks and attention being a rewards member, most of the "perks" were not really a perk other than to tempt you to upgrade. One thing I had an issue with was that we were offered an ocean-view room upgrade for a certain rate prior to checking in/confirming our booking.  But once we checked in, they stopped communicating with us. We attempted to get the rate that was offered to us when we got there, but they said this was through reservations and not them.  It made no sense, so we didn't upgrade for that reason. Pretty cut and dry when it comes to cents and dollars.

Exchanging to Pesos:
You can do it at the front desk. But be careful.  We approached the check-in staff about exchange rates from USD to Pesos. The staff made up a rate that was not the hotel's rate.  We checked online and the rate is not even close. Then I approached the supervisor what the hotel rate was. This was not the same rate as what the staff member quoted us.  So we went back to the check-in counter a few hours later and asked again. "How much is the exchange from USD to Pesos". He gave us a rate that was not what the supervisor quoted from the hotel computer. I then asked him directly. "What is your hotel rate?". Then he punches the numbers in the computer and gives us the appropriate value. That is very dishonest, and unprofessional. All I could say was WOW. I didn't expect that.

So how does this all sum up for us?  We won't return.  We are truly disappointed that we feel this way. There were some positives out of this trip. But the negatives have really left us with a bad taste. Some of the staff you have on hand right now need to bring their level of customer service back up to the quality and care of what your resort is claiming to have and what we experienced a few years back.  There was more staff on hand to draw in income services than there are for those who would provide the proper customer service and attention for EVERY guest regardless of how much you pay, what room you stay at, or how much you tip. A few years ago your staff set the bar for service and quality very high. This past week, it has shown that this bar has diminished. If you are short-staffed, say you are short-staffed and will be slower. Honesty comes a long way. I am optimistic that we would return and give it another try. But based on how things went this time around, I don't believe our review would be taken seriously just like how the staff didn't care that we would write a review or consider how the impact of our experience would cause me to write such a detailed and lengthy review.  These reviews seem to be the driving force for a lot of employees at the hotel more than tips. It's a thing now I guess.  I gave credit to those who earned it. Good Luck Paradisus Cancun!

reviews.author: Kayleigh D
reviews.title: Food was not great and drinks were very watered down
reviews.text: The food left a lot to be desired and the drinks were just sugar. We drank consistently all weekend and never felt drunk. The staff was great. Upbeat, hardworking and friendly. The rooms weren't bad but they were really hard to find and there should have been way more signage/maps posted. Restaurants had small menus. Beds were very uncomfortable and the pillows almost made us MORE uncomfortable than not. They did keep the place very clean throughout the weekend. Worth noting we went for the Paradise Blue Music Festival, although the food/drinks and level of service should be the same.

reviews.author: Debbie J
reviews.title: Not for Large groups
reviews.text:
We did a destination wedding, we had 32 in our group, unfortunately, the new setup is NOT Accommodating for large groups, on 2 different nights they canceled our reservations (we had 2 separate reservations for 15) one of the reservations were canceled. they told us it was fair to the rest of the guests...

That being said.. individually I think you will be wonderful.

I did not give them 5 stars based on actions of the resort.

reviews.author: 0504Traveller
reviews.title: Average Stay with Poor Service
reviews.text:
I was traveling to Cancun to celebrate a friend’s birthday so we were looking for an all-inclusive hotel that would have good service, good access to the beach and the pool, and overall provide a nice time during our short stay.  I have stayed at Melia properties both in New York (review here) as well as an all-inclusive in Punta Cana and both properties were decent – the all-inclusive was a large property with average food, decent rooms and sub-par service.  This was the expectation I had going into Paradisus, and because of both this expectation as well as we were going for a celebration, I decided to try out the Reserve by Paradisus which is supposed to provide an upgraded service. 

I booked the room through the Melia app as through the app there was a discount in addition to the discounted rates given to MeliaRewards members.  Booking the hotel and selecting the room type was very easy to do through the app so that was very convenient.  Once I booked the room, I contacted the hotel regarding accommodations for the celebrations as well as for transportation.  In other all-inclusive which I have stayed out, transportation has been included but in both Cancun and Punta Cana it was not included.   The hotel recommended a service to use, and I generally go through those recommendations as if there is a delay or something happens, I can contact the hotel with any issue.  During the communication with the hotel, I was also asked to fill out pre-arrival information including special requests.  I filled out the form, connected to the transportation and booked that, and was all set to enjoy my experience in Cancun.

The lack of service continued during the check-in process.  The Paradisus is a large property comprised of many pyramids across a wide land size.  You enter the property through the main pyramid which has a small check-in and check-out section to the left-hand side.  We went in there to check-in and were instructed that because we were reserve, we would check-in at a different pyramid and thus were walked to the Reserve pyramid.  The attendant who walked us through was nice but could not answer any questions and kept repeating “your Reserve agent will answer all the questions”.  The pyramids are designed in a similar fashion with an open layout in the middle, stores, restaurants, or hotel facilities on the ground floor in the middle and guest rooms on the top floors surrounding the open atrium.  The Reserve pyramid is also designed this way with the check-in desks as well as a lounge on the ground floor and guest rooms on the top floor.  The check-in attendant was busy helping someone else when we arrived so they asked us to wait in lounge.  On the ground floor in the open atrium, the Reserve has a lounge which serves complimentary drinks, coffee, tea, as well as heavy snacks.  The lounge was open in morning until mid-evening so you could stop here for breakfast, a late snack, a lite lunch, drinks and snacks or a lite dinner.  There were many tables surrounding the lounge and sitting in the open atrium was very nice and peaceful.  After a little while, the hotel attendant came in and said they were ready to check us in.  
The check-in attendant had zero customer service, was quite rude towards the end, and only wanted to go through their speech and not answer any questions or provide any additional information.  It was not a welcoming nor pleasant process and at the end, we were told that in fact our rooms were not ready and that we would have to wait in the lounge until our concierge came to get us.  I was not aware of this prior but booking with the Reserve comes with a Concierge who is supposed to help and provide tailored assistance through your stay – to this day I am still not sure what their purpose is besides making reservations as many of the questions or requests we made were responded with “you need to contact this person”. 

The Concierge led us to our room which was a standard room with 2 beds – we had originally booked a ‘lagoon view’ but the definition of this was a room facing the busy street with a lagoon way behind it – it was not calming nor soothing so we requested to upgrade to an ocean view.  This upgrade came at a costs, even though the booking had included discounted upgrades and spa credits.  The upgraded room had a large balcony facing the resort and ocean view and it was much better in terms of noise and view.  Both rooms were laid out in the similar fashion and, ironically, both had issues with the room.   As you entered the room, on the left were the closets which contained a safe, places to hang your clothes, slippers, robe, as well as other items.  On the right was the bathroom which contained a sink in the middle and a separate toilet area to the right and a shower to the left – there is supposed to be a sliding door on the bathroom to ensure privacy.  

The bathroom contained refillable bottles with toiletries including hand wash and lotion near the sink and shampoo, body wash, and conditioner in the shower – the shower contained both a handheld and rain shower and while the water pressure was good, the water went everywhere.  The oddest thing about the bathroom was that the shower faced the room and instead of a wall it was a glass partition with a thin sheet covering it – this meant that the person inside the room could see directly into the shower.  I have seen this design in other properties and I am not sure whether this was a design aspect to let light it, but it provides no privacy and is very uncomfortable – we asked that the curtain be doubled to ensure some privacy between the room and the bathroom.  Despite this design flaw, the bathroom was a decent size and had enough amenities and toiletries.

The room itself was also a decent size and contained the following – along the left side was a bench to either site or to store luggage and next to this was a long desk on top and below were drawers as well as a cabinet which contained water, soft drinks, water, and some food items.  Since this is an all-inclusive, most of the contents in the mini-bar were complimentary and should be refilled each day and refilled based on the preference of the client – ours were refilled only upon request and even though it took a couple of calls.  Above the desk was a TV mounted on the wall and finally along the left side was a table with two chairs.  On the right side of the room were the two double beds with a nightstand in the middle – the beds were comfortable and provided a decent night sleep.  There were outlets on the desk and on the nightstand but not next to the beds.  The room size was comfortable for 2 people plus their stuff to comfortable walk around and not be crowded.  The best part about the room was the balcony, which was very large in size, contained two lounge chairs plus a table, and looked out onto both the resort as well as the ocean.  My friend who wanted to layout and hear the ocean got up early and spent the rest of their mornings on the balcony since it was large, peaceful and convenient.

The Paradisus is an all-inclusive which means everything is included and no additional payments or fees are needed – expect for add-ons.  Add-ons included spa services, certain restaurants had additional items which were not included in the all-inclusive, as well as tours and activities needed to be paid for.  There were plenty of restaurants that were included in the all-inclusive including Italian, Latin, Mediterranean, buffets, as well as fast food.   In addition to food, beverages including alcoholic beverages were included in the all-inclusive.  Both my friend and I have dietary restrictions and neither of us had an issue finding something to eat – in fact, this was something we were concerned about but in the end there was a plethora of choices for us.  Most of the information for the restaurants and other activities are included in the app – so you have to download the app to access most of the information; we were not aware of this until the second day so it would’ve been helpful to know this information when we arrived.  Also through the app you can request housekeeping, additional items for the mini-bar, etc so it is extremely important to download the app since this is mainly the way to communicate with staff.

The Paradisus was also a large property so there were plenty of spaces, chairs, and beds available next to the pool and beach.  The Reserve pool is a separate area where it is adults-only and it is supposed to be more exclusive – it was quieter than the regular pool but towards the end of our stay which coincided with the weekend, there were plenty of kids who joined the pool as the staff did not regulate who would come in.  For the Reserve pool, there are beds surrounding the pool which need to be reserved a day in advance and once reserved it is yours for the entire day until you give it up – so you can wander away but if you leave something of yours there or let the staff know that you will be coming back, then they will not give it to anyone.  While this is nice on one side, it does limit the amount of guests who have access to the limited beds.  Also, we were not informed upon arrival that the beds needed to be reserved a day in advance, we only found this out on our second day – again, information that would’ve been helpful in advance.  The large property provided plenty of opportunity and space to enjoy both the pool and beach, as well as walk along the beach and stay within the property boundaries.  

Other amenities on the property include complimentary wi-fi, which was a decent speed and allowed for email and Whatsapp but was slower for YouTube and streaming.   There is also a gym on property but it is a bit further away so we did not access it.  Overall, the Paradisus was a mixed bag.  The positives are the large resort space, the plethora of choices for restaurants, the Reserve lounge, and since the resort was so large it provided quiet areas so the noise wasn’t concentrated into one area.  The negatives are the lack of customer service, the somewhat outdated rooms, lack of a map or clear instructions/details as to what is available and when, as well as communication with the hotel regarding airport access.  Final note, I went for a couple of days and it was at the beginning of the week and left right as the weekend was getting started – there was definitely a different crowd, different vibe, and increase in noise level from when we arrived to when we departed.

reviews.author: James C
reviews.title: Excessive Charges for Added Children
reviews.text: It was meaningless even if they were charged an additional fee that was close to the room price for the additional child. I was very embarrassed by the charge for a different fee than before. I think next time I will have to look for other places and hotels.

reviews.author: dincauwright
reviews.title: Average Resort!
reviews.text: The resort was nice but was not maintained very well. The first room we were placed in (5004) had exposed breaker boxes by the front door, was supposed to be an ocean view and all you could really see was the top of cabanas. Instead of fixing issues they masked them, like in the spare bathroom they just covered the outlets so there were none available. The 2nd room we were moved to 5412 was nicer and had way better views but was kissing missing a shower door in the spare bathroom so unless you wanted water everywhere you couldn’t use it and the air conditioning didn’t work very well and the room would get hot. Overall the food was okay, to be expected at an all inclusive.

reviews.author: Storyteller823365
reviews.title: A little above average hotel experience
reviews.text:
Overall the stay was good. We stayed in the reserve that was supposed to have a concierge that took care of anything you needed. The 1st day Andres made our restaurant reservations and sent them to us on the 2nd day. After that we never really heard from him again until I complained to a manager. So if that is the service you get by staying in the reserve, I would save my money and stay in one of the other towers. The food at Sal's steakhouse was the best food of the week and would highly recommend it. The food in the buffet was not very good at all and really limited on selection. The other restaurants were average at best. All of the servers at all of the bars, pools and restaurants were excellent and worked hard to make sure you had everything you needed. 
Overall a decent trip, but will not be going back.

reviews.author: Culture799712
reviews.title: Had a Good Time Many Changes Needed
reviews.text:
We stayed in the reserve 4 nights end of Feb. first part of March 2023. Went with my daughter.  
Pros: 
Beautiful resort inside and out.
Nice clean room with balcony.  
Nice restaurant overlooking the ocean for rserve guests only. Waiters were wonderful.
Clean beach area for reserve only.  Large palapas provide shade all day.  With drink and food service
Private pool with nice furniture, umbrellas and sunbeds.
No kids and private.
Snack/lunch area inside with deserts, breakfast/lunch food.  Nice variety.  Bar also, drinks and specialty coffee as well. 
Multiple restaurants.
Some entertainment.
Concierge service.
All staff were friendly and helpful.

Cons:
Lighting in the room was awful.  Couldn't find a spot to put on make-up no matter where I went in the room.
Weird shower set up.  Full glass window facing into the room.  It did have a curtain.  But you could see right through it.
On the beach the lounge chairs were very old.  None of them laid flat so you could not lay on your stomach.  Also, none were adjustable.  They did did not go far enough up for comfortable reading.  We saw others place rocks in the back hinges of the chairs which brought them further up.  That worked well for us.  But, not all chairs had that particular  configuration in the hinges so this couldn't be done with all of them.
The pool area had nice new loungers.  They need to replace the ones on the beach.

They did have several restaurants.  Reserve guests were to get priority seating.  But. that is not entirely true. They have 25 reservations per each restaurant each evening.  When those reservations are taken you do not have priority.  When we came in the concierge could only offer us reservations at 6:00/6:30pm or 9:00pm.  We were told they would take walk ins if there had been a cancellation.  We tried that the 1st night as he had no reservation available for us that first night.  That was not true.  We would walk in and were told they had no tables available although several tables were empty.  We later found out that they do not keep their restaurants to full capacity.  Finally we asked to talk to a manager Who was very apologetic and helped us right away.  He actually went to all the restaurants until he could find one to take us that first night.  He also was able to arrange the rest of the nights so we could have better seating times.  Not the concierge fault.  The concierge has limited seating available compared to the manager.
The food was good but not great.  The seafood restaurant was awful.

If you want one of the sunbeds by the pool you must reserve them right away the first day you come in or you won't get one the rest of your stay.  Guests would book them for their full stay and then not use them everyday.

I generally do not write reviews at all.  But, felt I needed to this time.  Would I stay there again? Probably not.  If they made these changes maybe. For sure would not pay extra for the reserve experience.  It's such a shame because the resort is beautiful.

reviews.author: H4969YVcherylp
reviews.title: Overall pretty good
reviews.text:
I am actually here now- party of nine …2 families -property is  very nice the regular rooms are pretty tight and small only one sink in the bathroom— You have to close one door to use another type of small… Service is very nice food is just OK …my main complaint is dinner reservations…when you have a party of nine it seems they can never fit you in anywhere except this place called the “lunchbox”  which is basically burgers outside -even my concierge could not get me better dinner reservations- my husband goes down every morning waits 45 minutes and still is told the same thing -“nothing available for a party of nine except for the lunch box OR a restaurant at 9 PM which means we miss the show and we don’t like to eat that  late… …that’s very disappointing… 
Bartenders at the sports lounge are so nice and great… They do need more bars and lounges not just sports bar and ginger for such a HUGE property

reviews.author: DEBORAH C
reviews.title: Was ok for price
reviews.text: The resort is nice and the beach was beautiful  . The buffet was ok for breakfast , The only specialty restaurant we liked was the Lemon fish went there 3 nights . Issues we observed there were not enough lounge chairs by pool and quite a few of the palapas on the beach didn't have lounge chairs . You need to get up at the crack of dawn to get a towel and reserve a lounge . The lobby bar is set up poorly they need to remove the bali beds and add more table and chairs . The resort was ok  for the price we paid . How ever we paid a reduced rate because we did an exchange on our time share . A friend of mine was looking to join us and the prices she was finding on line $2500 a week per person I feel was way out of line for what you get here

reviews.author: Nelson D
reviews.title: Terrible service
reviews.text: The concierge there are terrible lack of information about what activities was available and what was available for my three year old daughter to do I have stayed in serveral Meliá resorts this is by far the worst I doubt I come back to this resort

reviews.author: Sandie T
reviews.title: Gone downhill
reviews.text:
I have come to the paradisus cancun since it was called the gran melia, about 8-10 trips here. This was the worst experience.

-There was a day my room wasn't cleaned and it was 5pm and I had to call and ask for towels at least so I could shower. 
-there was no concierge and I could never find anyone to help me with questions. I tried to go to the front desk several times and the line was so long that I'd wait for 15 minutes and just leave. Finally someone asked my father in law how the trip was going and he said not good and to contact me. That was the only way I could get any assistance for my questions. She tried to tell me someone named Victor was assigned to me, I never heard from Victor, don't even know who he is. If it is Tuesday afternoon and I don't know who my concierge or helper is, then that's a huge problem. 
-I couldn't get any reservations. It's ridiculous that I pay so much money and can't eat where I want to eat. This was a huge reason why the stay was so negative. I ended up having to walk up to places and beg for a reservation so we didn't eat at the buffet.
One day (3/7) I waited at the reservation desk starting at 840 (opens at 9am) in an attempt to be the first to get any dinner reservations and nobody showed up until 9:20. The line behind me was about 20 people. Everytime an employee walked by id ask where the people at the desk are and they'd pretend to text and then kind of walk away slowly and just not help at all. 
The buffet was closed on night (3/9) for dinner. Just a sign saying it was closed with no advanced notice. There were many people of course that couldn't make reservations anywhere so there was a huge line at the taco place (the only other place that doesn't require reservations) 
-my husband wanted to try the morning mediation at 830 on 3/9. He went up at 820 and was told it was full. The woman was not friendly and did not tell him if there was a sign up or how to try to get in the class next time. Again, we pay a lot of money and can't do anything we want.

The resort itself is gorgeous, stunning,  if food or activities or getting help of any kind isn't important to you, then this is your place!

reviews.author: jmarion93
reviews.title: Only OK for the money
reviews.text: Since it was not the least expensive, we expected a more luxury experience.  Staff all very nice and accommodating.  Top shelf liquor included.  Was not able to book a specialty restaurant our entire trip.  All beach chairs reserved before 9am.  Bars and restaurant service seemed very slow.  It was a "nice" experience, but would try other options next time.

reviews.author: Marla G
reviews.title: Paradisus Pick Another Resort
reviews.text:
PLEASE READ ...I'm not really sure where to begin. When I originally booked the resort I opted for the junior suite. I discovered that because I did not upgrade to the "Reserve" that we would not have access to certain areas of the Resort including the swim up bar. To me, the swim up bar and the Adult Only area was what I wanted. In addition there were restaurants that we would also not be able to eat at. So I paid the extra money and upgraded. I'm not really sure it was worth it though. By the way. I was surprised to see that this multi million dollar resort only has five restaurants? The resort advertises 4 pools. This is totally misleading as one of the four are a private swimming area attached to the rooms and then a tiny one next to the adult only pool. We never did find the fourth one unless you consider the hydro spa pool a fourth one. 

The cabanas- you have to reserve these 24 hours in advance and most of the time people don't show up. The beach chairs, people will come down at 6 am throw their stuff on the chairs but you won't see them until 1pm in the afternoon. See picture below . 

When we arrived to the resort they took us to this special guest service area for the upgraded Reserve guests. Once we were checked in, I was told by mistake I needed to pay a balance of $3,000 plus dollars. What???? I bought the trip through Southwest Vacations and it was paid for in full way before I arrived. Once that was straightened out, we got our bracelets on and headed to our rooms. The room we got was really nice. No complaints as we got a room off the main level with a swimming area outside off the deck. I was told this was an upgrade from the reserve we paid for which kind of scares me that the extra money we paid for would have probably gotten us a view of a brick wall. The swim up bar which is an amenity you pay for as a Reserve guest still allows kids at the swim up bar. We were told that the adult pool was this private great thing and it ended up being this tiny swimming hole while the awesome pool area where the swim bar is has kids swimming all around it. See my photo. 

We were assigned a concierge which was really of no help. All reservations for the restaurants were late (9:00 at night). We would walk up to the restaurant earlier and typically they accommodated us at an earlier time than our reservation. Our concierge didn't really explain anything to us. We had no clue about any of the entertainment going on until after it was over. We had to figure things out on our own and by the time we did it was too late.  

Taxi vs Uber if you want to go down to to Cabo or San Jose take an Uber! It's half the cost. An Uber was $10 to $12 vs  a taxi being $35.00. The taxi was a recommendation from our concierge. So there you go. Ubers cannot go the airport though so get a shuttle service. 

The excursions in the hotel are too expensive. Go see Amanda at Cabo Blue. It's 65.00 a person. They are awesome! They feed you, drinks, snorkeling, etc. 

The Reserve upgrade was also supposed to include an aromatherapy every night when they turn down your bed. This was not explained to me when I checked in. Some of the housekeeping staff had no clue and I got this service one night out of 6. I asked for food delivered at the pool. One waiter said no another said yes. Lol 
You have to reserve the cabana 24 hours in advance. Half the cabanas weren't even being utilized but they still wouldn't let you have them. So they stayed unoccupied all day. Most of the staff was helpful, friendly, and very accommodating with the exception of guest services and the front desk. I don't like the fact that you have to tip everywhere and everybody. You can easily go through several hundred dollars. I think the resort should take care of this. 

It's a beautiful resort and view of the beach is nice but I think it's overpriced. The food is ok but not the greatest. The wine is blah. I have had way better wine. I would choose a different resort with more restaurant options. We still had a good time an learned what to do differently next time. We hope you will learn from this as well

reviews.author: loretta
reviews.title: good stay
reviews.text:
WE HAD A CERY PLEASANT STAY.  the staff for the most part was great.  The only set back was the drinks. SUPER SWEET, watered down and cheap alcohol.    we ended up making our own cocktails in our room!  The pool was really nice and the hotel was extremely x
clean!

reviews.author: Lis C
reviews.title: December 2022 holiday in Cancun
reviews.text: Overall over paid and underwhelmed. This resort is not luxury, hotel is 3 stars, beach is small and dirty. We were in Melia in Punta Cana, that hotel is much better. Rooms at this hotel is dirty and not consistent with amenities as we have 3 rooms and they were all different, one has no bathrobes, etc.

reviews.author: Sam944
reviews.title: Great option and appropriately priced versus the comp set, but older product and lack of attention to details takes away
reviews.text:
Pros
- Great place for a holiday to relax, especially for young families
- Some of the very best food we have enjoyed at any hotel property, anywhere
- Wonderful staff

Cons
- Property is dated, much of the room product tired and in need of modernization
- Lacks on the small details and touches that would truly make this a 5 star experience; more of a 4-4.5 star hotel

TLDR: Great option and appropriately priced versus the comp set, but older product and lack of attention to details takes away from making this a true 5 star experience.

Overall, we had a very positive and wonderful stay at Paradisus Cancun. While the weather wasn't great during our holiday stay, our main goals were to have rest and relaxation for our family, and this fit the bill perfectly. This property had some of the very best staff we have experienced at any hotel.
