2) Food is mediocre. There is a lot of selection and the servers are great, but it definitely feels like all-inclusive dining. At the sushi restaurant they served frozen sea scallops as sashimi rather than fresh scallops. 

3) Various other issues with management - room not made one day. One night the entire room smelled like paint varnish.

The beach is great, the facilities are nice, but it feels dated and there are definitley better ones in Cancun.

reviews.author: sarahbB5787XI
reviews.title: Paradissus use to be good
reviews.text: Paradissus use to be good , very dissapointed , they need mahor uodate , renovations and service was very slow and not motivated.... pool was damaged all arround missing bullnose , lots of broken chair on the beach , no service on the beach

reviews.author: Elocin
reviews.title: Lovely hotel, a few major drawbacks...
reviews.text:
The hotel and grounds are beautiful, the staff is helpful, and the all-inclusive package is the way to go.  We enjoyed the drink selections and the staff frequently checked in at the beach and pool to take our orders.  The staff were very friendly and accomodating.

 I recommend staying in pyramid 2 if you can, it is the main building and much more vibrant than pyramid 1 where we stayed.    Avoid a first floor room as well- the patio is easily scaled and I'm not convinced that the door locks would prevent a theft.  Apparently we had a "lagoon view"  bur on the first flooe or view was only a parling lot.   Further, we had people from upper balconies throwing cigarettes off of theirs and they often ended up on ours.  

We had two junior suites and they were quite spacious and clean overall.

We ate at two restaurants, Fuego and The Market Grill.   We found the food to be just o.k.  The breakfast spread at the buffet was great, however, and was my favorite meal there- plenty of selection, mimosa and bloody Mary station, a wide variety of breads, omelet station, and much more.   The fruit was delicious.   

The gelato stand and the Nespresso stand on the main floor were great and we really enjoyed them.  

Where this hotel fell short is in lighting, humidity and, well, sewage treatment.    To be clear, we were there for a very short time (48 hours) so we didn't bother bringing it to the attention of the management.   We also didn't spend much time in our room since the weather was so beautiful so it didn't affect our overall trip very much.

The room size was great, but one of our two rooms had an old couch that was impossible to sit in because it had no support.   We came to find out it was because the mattress in this sofa bed was missing entirely.    Miraculously a new couch appeared on day two, but it was odd.   We also didn't have a coffee table in that room, whereas our second room next door was much better maintained. 

The lighting (in both rooms) was a problem.   After sundown it was nearly impossible to see clearly- there were approximately 11 light switches throughout the room and bathroom, each linked to a tiny recessed light.    Even with all switches in the "on" position the room and bathroom were dim.    There is no way to properly apply makeup after dark and you have to walk around switching off each light before getting to sleep.

The humidity in our rooms was odd considering that we were able to control our air conditioning.    However, each night we got into a damp bed.   This never went away and was pretty uncomfortable, (though the mattresses themselves were quite comfortable).  No setting on the A.C. unit successfully rid us of the humidity, and we tried repeatedly.    I suspect it may be an issue with the ground floor rooms.  

Possibly the most concerning was waking up one morning to the overpowering scent of sulfur and sewage.   There was no leak or sewer backup, but the smell was overwhelming.    It suggests some type of sewer issue but we never figured it out. We were checking out that same day and simply told 'thanks for letting us know'.
   
Overall, the hotel was lovely but our rooms left something to be desired.   For such a short stay it didn't matter much, but if I was planning to stay any longer i would certainly have requested to speak with the Management.  I might come back...  but would insist on a room on a higher floor.

reviews.author: S9693JOadrianc
reviews.title: Fake cigars at Paradisus Cancun
reviews.text: Did not appreciate being sold and promoted fake cigars. Best for you not to sell them at all. This will hurt your reputation. If your hotel is dishonest about its cigar products what else are you not honest about

reviews.author: jmblackburn
reviews.title: Lovely Resort...Needs a Few Tweaks for Families
reviews.text:
First of all, we are a family of five with three kids, ages 13, 4, and 2. We do much research everywhere we go to assure that the properties are a match for our variety of ages, and the size of our family....So this review is written based on the actual resort vs. our expectations from information provided on hotel website and reviews.

Start with the positives: The resort is beautiful. It is clean, modern, and the rooms are comfortable. The beach is gorgeous - Clean, white sand, perfect water, nice cabanas and chairs. We loved the barista and gelato stand. The entire feel of the main inner pyramid is beautiful, with the vines, the coy ponds, the bridges, the lights and candles at night. The food is good, but not great. We mostly at the Naos buffet for the convenience of our kids and the variety was very good. We at also at Blue Agave, Enso, and Vento. They were pretty good. 

Two great employees: *Sophie, who booked our AquaWorld experience, was very knowledgable and helpful. *Our server Asuncion by the pool is Wonder Woman. She ran our drinks and never lost her sprint and smile.

It was extremely important to us to have connecting rooms (Not just side by side rooms with entrances in the hallway). Our kids nap at varying times, we go to bed at different times, etc. I called the hotel directly numerous times before our arrival and was repeatedly told that they couldn't guarantee connecting rooms. The day before our arrival, I was then told that there weren't any connecting rooms, as in, the hotel doesn't even have any. I spent much time on the phone that day explaining that we wouldn't have booked there if we knew that. Miraculously, they then told me that out of over 800+ rooms in the hotel, there are 6 connecting rooms. We stayed for 5 nights and they could not give one to us the first night. So the solution was that we stayed in side by side rooms the first night, moved the next day (had to be out by noon, had no room until 3pm - not the best situation with young kids), and had lovely connecting rooms for the rest of the stay.

Since we didn't have a room for those few hours, and honestly weren't sure if it would take even longer, we rented a lovely cabana on the beach at Coco's. It came with a delicious platter of lobster, shrimp, and crab, and a bottle of champagne....but it is extra to rent there. Unfortunately kids were not able to nap there because we were very close to very loud music.

One other big downside to the resort is the COLD pools. The outdoor temps are lower this time of year and cool at night. They only heat the one main pool in front of the Market Grill and it gets quite crowded. The resort has so many beautiful pools that stretch the span of the whole resort...and they were virtually empty because they are so cold. I tried to warm up and get used to them and couldn't. My kids couldn't even get used to the temps. And just to be clear, this included the kids' pool. NOT heated. No hot tubs either.

Paradisus Cancun is overall a nice resort, but I don't think we would go back with kids. There are too many resorts on the peninsula to choose from that cater to families.

reviews.author: brenth171
reviews.title: Beautiful resort, beautiful beach, but if going for food DON'T
reviews.text:
We got a pretty good deal for this resort and I like to choose for food, I want to eat well. I looked at alot of reviews and felt for sure I was in good hands. Sorry to disappoint, but no, the food was average at best. There is the Sunset grill by the pool which was pretty good during the day for the same thing every day, which is fine, but the buffet was not that great. If you like fish you may do ok, the restaurants have alot of fish, but from speaking to others who were visiting too, it wasn't just us. We went to Grand Bahia in Punta Cana the year before, that was fantastic food, this not so much. Market Grill was ok, that's all I will say about that.
Coffee place open from 11-5, that was great for a cappucino, ice cream bar was good too.
Kids zone, my 6 year old had a fantastic time, never wanted to leave, he was always in good hands, they took them to eat and were open from 9-9 which is good, we didn't use that long, but used enough that he loved it.
the beach is beautiful.
I had a tough time with the room cleaners, they have 2-3 different ones coming to the room, one for the mini fridge, one to clean and one at night to put a chocolate on your bed. I really wanted the girl that cleans the room to get the tip, i'm just not sure she did cause the money was gone and the fridge was restocked (we really didn't use the fridge that much so there wasn't much to do with the fridge) so that was a bit upsetting cause i wanted to make sure the right person got the tip. hopefully they all share.
Everything else was great, just the food, I wish I could say it was good, but I can't, very disappointing that side of it.

reviews.author: 宏彥 黃
reviews.title: Great view and comfortable environment
reviews.text: The hotel offers great view, comfortable environment including multiple restaurants, clean hotel room, amazing beach, and bar/lounge to relax. Food are above average except meat category which is more of pro quantity than quality, where you can see much left over of meats. Front desk is less helpful and attentive in terms of the efficiency in check-in process, lack of hotel facilities info, and activities around hotel/Cancun. Clerks/Waiters in the hotel however, are very attentive and show great hospitality. One note is that some restaurants are not in All Inclusive package.

reviews.author: Afshin N
reviews.title: Excellent Staff, Food, but no Entertainment
reviews.text:
No Pool Table, Ping Pong. Day and Night Entertainment was very poor. 
The rooms are not fully high Tech. There is not USB Output to charge the phones or ...
The rooms are not big enough.
Excellent Staff.

reviews.author: reesag2015
reviews.title: Mrs Glassman
reviews.text:
Still at hotel as I write;
Restaurants; all very good, wait staff is wonderful, timely and food is very good.
Breakfast; buffet only and on some mornings the lines were long 

Room: junior suite is what I’m in: which means ordinary room. It’s not a Suite. It’s narrow and average. Clean, could use more plugs ( for cell phones) and more drawers. No wow factor at all.

Lobby; has the wow factor. Very dramatic, but how much time do you spend in lobby.

Pool: this is where the hotel fails. There is NO ADULT SWIMMING POOL. For a hotel this size, it should have a “quiet” pool. The only one way to get peace and quiet is to pay $300 more a night for the Royal Service which has its own overly large pool ( 2 people were in Royal Service pool which takes up approximately 1/3 of the pools at hotel, while dozens and dozens of  regular guests were densely using the other pools). There is a kids pool that some adults were using to escape the tumult and loud music and noise from the main pool.
If you want to use a shaded “bed” they are over $100 a Day. There are many of these which has impacted and cut into the amount of “free” lounge chairs. Not nice.
Main pool: very crowded, very noisy. 

Beach: long deep stretch. Nice.

Response for room service: good and quick 

Response if something breaks in room; ok.

Hotel staff : very nice and friendly 

Basically all inclusive when it comes to the pool and beach is NOT all inclusive, it’s more like exclusive!

reviews.author: JJUNNYC
reviews.title: Not horrible but not great either
reviews.text:
Things to know before booking Paradisus Cancun

The Good:
- Beach was beautiful and clean.
- Service was fantastic and every single person who worked there greeted us with a smile and went above and beyond to make our stay enjoyable.
- We had good dinners at Vento and Market Grill.
- Drinks were surprisingly good, if you asked for double liquor.
- Minibar is stocked daily with water, beer, soda, and snacks.

The Bad:
- Food was hit or miss but overall not great.  Our dinner at Mole was terrible, Bana was just ok, and Enjo was also not good.
- Not really the hotels fault and I'm not certain it's always like this but the waves were pretty strong on the beach and not safe for young children.
- They don't have people who setup beach chairs and towels, it's self service.
- They don't serve food on the beach unless you rent a cabana.
- Rooms were dated and the controls for the lights were confusing.
- There were 2 elevator banks but only one elevator in each bank was working which made for long waits for the elevator.

If you want peace and quiet or like to sleep early then be sure to ask for a room in one of the end buildings vs the main tower.

reviews.author: RT23
reviews.title: Christmas weekend
reviews.text:
Royal service Pros:

cabana with drinks & food brought to you

Access to Self serve bar with small apps to snack on

Heated pool

Cons:

No music by pool

No swim up bar

Your assigned butler is hard to reach

Overall, you can save a lot of money by NOT having the royal service. The hotel has everything you need by asking the concierge instead of a butler.

reviews.author: Humberto C
reviews.title: Room selection
reviews.text: When we arrived we had to wait til 3 pm for a room due to their policy about checking in, which is understandable. When 3pm finally arrived after 5hours of waiting they told us our room wasn’t ready and we had to wait one more hour. This sucked completely because we were already exhausted from waiting 5 hours. Instead of offering a better room they tried to offer another room that was not even part of the royal service and in the family section. I had booked this trip a month in advance and I would had wish everything would had been ready to go as soon as things should had been. And for a butler I never even saw one and I found out I was suppose to have one. It was my first time in Cancun and I would try other hotels before going to this one again.

reviews.author: Blake S
reviews.title: Almost perfect, until I had a problem.
reviews.text: This resort is fantastic, the food is excellent, and the workers are all very friendly. However, I left this resort early because there was a water leak in the ceiling of my bathroom. I told three people about it and no one came to fix it. At that point I just decided to leave early since I was being ignored. I told the check out desk about my problem and they wouldn't even refund me or credit me, I consider that very bad service and this is the reason for the negative review.

reviews.author: carlos m
reviews.title: Great Hotel,amaizing people and location
reviews.text:
This review is regarding the Family concierge junior suite ocean view.

At the arrival on the hotel you can see this big open space and plants everywhere. We were greeted by several people and told where to go and check in. Since we were on the Family Concierge package we had a private check in and private check out.

The check in and check out area is great. You have access to beverage, alcoholic and non alcoholic, food and more. We waited maybe 20 min for the room to be ready.

The room was a Junior Suite with Ocean View, the view was amazing really. The room was clean daily and it was great. Enough space for my wife, my son and I. The bath was with a tub and a private area for the toilet.

The inside of the hotel: It is beautiful, full of great people, and, very clean.

The outside is as clean as it can be, some people just do not help on this. The beach is beautiful and from the pool areas you can see the beach.

Inside the hotel there are different small shops that will give you food and beverages for free, they are there for the client. Coffee and food are great.

The attention inside the restaurants is great. We when to almost all of them, we tried one each day. Our favorite were Fuego and Vento. For breakfast we did go for the buffet every time, the attention was great.

In front of the hotel there is a MacDonald, if you want it, we didn't go inside. There is a pharmacy and the bus stops. We did use the bus stops since we did ride on the bus system.

The bus systems was great, you can get around pretty much anywhere along the hotel line. The people on the bus, drivers and people who collect the money, were very friendly. They told us the stops needed in order for us to go to the places that we wanted.

The water at the beach and pool were OK. For me they were not really that cold. In the month of November the beach gets some wave, is due to the month and the water in the area.

Been part of the concierge Family has its perks. We had a little surprise every night for us. For my wife and I it was fruits with chocolate and champagne, and, for the little one chocolate milk and cookies. You have someone there for you pretty much 24x7 and they take really good care of your need, like booking the restaurants and taxis or trips. Pretty much anything. They helps us in several occasions. We had 2 concierges, Fernanda and Gabriel. Fernanda was Amazing, she used to write us, they communicate with us using WhatsApp, every day asking us how was everything and if anything was needed, she used to know what to do and pretty much used to tell us about our restaurant reservation or hotel activities. Gabriel was the opposite, we had asked for a taxi to be ready on a specific day and time, and, he was working so he told me that it was taking care of, the day came and no taxi, almost lost my boat to the activity that I had pay for, swimming with the dolphins. I talk to him through messages and request a taxi back, there was not taxi to get back. We did use the bus system. He also miss a restaurant reservation. My son painted a ceramic iguana at the pool the day before departing, the iguana was not ready at closing time and the person working on the store told me that Gabriel would pick it up before me leaving the next day, which was at 9am, well I forgot, and, remember when I was at the airport. He told that it was going to be mail to my house and that never happened. He did not reach to us during the day, or told us anything about activities. Really did not like the way that he worked and that is why I gave 3 starts to the hotel. When Gabriel was working it seems that i had to be in top of things in order for them to go alright.

The things i did not liked:

Some areas seem to be damage and not been taken care of.

To get service at the beach and pool area you need to tip very good, if not a drink can take a long time.

The kid area was great, but, it was dirty. Even when 4 employees were in the area. I asked them to clean the area and they did, a little.

Hotel night or day activities lack a lot. They do offer some during the day but maybe 1 or 2, and, at night there is maybe one show in a space where you cannot see very well.

I did love the layout of the hotel, the location and the workers.

reviews.author: kn0wles
reviews.title: A little disappointed!
reviews.text:
Booked a trip to take my hubby somewhere warm for his 60 birthday and being as it was out 10th trip to Mexico, I was excited about staying at the paradises as it had a golf course. This proved to be a small par three course and we never saw anyone one. Check in wasn’t great, someone took our bags as soon as we arrived, an someone else took us to check in. We were given keys, but that’s it. No info on where our room was or anything about the hotel itself.. Front desk staff were not friendly or helpful. We finally found our room and waited for almost an hour for bellman to bring our bags then phoned front desk and they said “ did you go tell them what room you were in? We have never had to do this before so we didn’t know. 
Then we found out we couldn’t go to the adult pool unless we upgraded to premium svc for $300 US a day. We went to main pool and found out we had to pay $100 US to use one of the many cabanas around the pool. This made us very mad because this was one of the reasons I picked this place, they had lots of cabanas around all the pools and on the beach. The beach cabanas are $130 US per day (which is about 170 for us Canadians!) i was very disappointed as I love laying in the cabana out of the sun and 
reading, so it made me so mad to see all the cabanas sitting empty all day and not being able to use one. We have stayed in many 5 star resorts, and some have been free, some have charged 10 to 20 $$, but their prices were ridiculous. Other than a less than great welcome, and the cabanas, the staff everywhere else in the hotel was great. The service in the resterants was great and the food was pretty good too. Also liked the little coffee an ice cream counters. We wish they would have put the show in a better place, as it was in the lounge area with all the beds, but unless you were in the front rows very hard to watch and you had to stand the whole time. There wasn’t much to do in the evenings, the lounge was the only place to go hang out but because of all the big beds in there, seating was limited. On a good note, the hotel was very nice and the beach was beautiful, water in the ocean was much warmer than the pool. We enjoyed most of the resteraunts, and our balcony was big and private ( they all seem to be like that, the design of the hotel was great).

reviews.author: Monica C
reviews.title: Good time in Family Concierge room with a toddler
reviews.text:
We came with a group of relatives (18 of us total) for a quick getaway to celebrate a 40th wedding anniversary. My husband and I were in a family concierge room with our 17 month old daughter and my mom and sister were in a family concierge room next door to us. It was our 1st visit to Paradisus Cancun and 1st time visiting Cancun with a toddler but we have stayed in several different all-inclusives in the Cancun area. Overall, we had a pleasant stay but wish we had known some things about the resort before coming, which I will try to emphasize in my review. 

Check in: good experience checking in in the family concierge lounge. We were not greeted at the entry with any cold towels or champagne like others have mentioned, but got the champagne when we requested it at the lounge. We saw the long line for check in in the front lobby so we were happy to avoid that in the lounge. Check in was very quick and they honored our request to have 2 side-by-side rooms, though there are no adjoining rooms at this resort.

Rooms: We had 2 side by side rooms (initially 3406 & 3407) in tower 3, the main tower. I would say that it was nice to be in the main tower because we were a quick walk to all of the restaurants, but it can get loud. Also, these 2 rooms were not renovated and appeared very old. The mattress was sagging and the room just felt very dated. The biggest problem we had was that there is a STEP UP TO GET INTO THE BATHROOM, which with a toddler was dangerous, she kept falling while running around the room. So, after 1 day we requested a room change and we got moved to rooms 3204 & 3205, which were renovated, but on the 2nd floor so closer to the noisy areas. The mattress was new and there was no step to get in the bathroom, so that was better, but there was no bathtub, only a stand up shower. So, it made bathing our daughter difficult, she screamed her head off for every shower and left a pool of water in the bathroom. I would recommend that family concierge rooms have bathtubs as a mandatory thing, because usually you're traveling with a kid and need the tub. Also, it would've been nice to have a bigger bathroom, perhaps with 2 sinks. 

Butlers/Service: Josue and Alexander were our butlers and created a WhatsApp group conversation so that we could text them from each of our phones for anything we needed. They were both kind and attentive and even responded to our texts after hours. They helped us get milk in the mini-bar, spa appointments, and restaurant reservations. Generally, the service was prompt and all of the staff at the resort were pleasant and appreciated tips. The waiters in the buffet, Naos, however, were rude and it was like pulling teeth to get basics like tea or coffee. 

Food: We ate at Mole, Enso, and Vento for dinners and Naos everyday for the breakfast buffet. For lunch, we typically just ordered food by the pool or ate at the snack bar. We didn't enjoy the food at Mole or Enso but Vento was very good. Also, my husband and I did a  date night at Tempo, which I highly recommend. Naos was not that great of a buffet, very basic; I would recommend they add some more live stations, like a pasta station or something more substantial. Room service was available and we tried it once but the food arrived cold and soggy. One thing people with kids should know is that THERE ARE NO STRAWS ANYWHERE AT THIS RESORT! Meaning, if your kid needs to drink from a straw, don't even bother asking, they say that they got rid of straws in an effort to be more environmentally friendly. Luckily, we had a sippy cup for our daughter, but a lot of times, we forgot it and she spilled all over her clothes. As other reviewers have mentioned, none of the restaurants have sufficient A/C (except Tempo) and are pretty casual so keep that in mind.

Spa: My husband and I went for an 80 min deep tissue massage and enjoyed it. I would definitely recommend the spa but don't bother with the hydrotherapy, it is nothing special and the water is too cold.

Beach/Pools: the pool water needs to be warmer! It was downright cold in the kids' pool, so my daughter didn't enjoy swimming around. The beach was clean and the water looked beautiful, but the red flags were up everyday we were there.

Baby Club: We took our daughter here once since we spent most days on the beach/by the pool and she had to be dragged out. This is definitely a huge plus for this resort!

Overall, we had a good stay but would recommend some updates and straws!

reviews.author: spegram45
reviews.title: Amazing beach, resort just OK
reviews.text: The resort is nice, but not fantastic. My main complaints are 1) the food (not as good as other resorts I’ve been to), 2) difficulty making restaurant reservations (you HAVE to make reservations but we had issues getting someone to answer the phone so that we could make reservations; also, our reservations were lost multiple times which was frustrating), 3) and entertainment (there was only one [mediocre] show each night. If the weather is bad or it’s nighttime, there really isn’t that much to do at the resort. I still had a good time and the price was reasonable.

reviews.author: Pooh328
reviews.title: Please Read if you are Planning to Stay at Paradisus Cancun!
reviews.text:
First, let me preface this review by giving a glimpse of who is writing this review. I am a 36 year old single woman who travels at least 4-6 times a year, domestically and internationally.

My review will be a little backwards as I am starting it with an incident that happened towards the end of my stay. My companion and I had an oceanfront room in the main building from Saturday, December 2nd through Wednesday, December 6th. We placed our cash and passports in the safe upon check in then quickly changed to hit the pool. Before we were leaving out, we both realized that we still had on our watches and placed them INSIDE of compartments in our separate bags. We only requested housekeeping on Monday. Tuesday evening while we were getting dressed to leave the property, my companion realized he hadn’t worn his watch the entire time we were there ( I mean who’s keeping time when you're at the beach?) He looks in his bag and sees that its not there. He looked everywhere which prompted me to look for my watch, which lo and behold, was missing as well. We go down to the lobby to inform management what happened. 15 minutes later, a manager and a member from security go with me to my room. They ask questions and security proceeds to search my room and all of our belongings. I found that quite odd to be honest but I let them search. The manager leaves while the “search” is still going on and another man enters. He begins to interrogate me as if I was lying about the theft. They asked me if I had a car on the premises, I replied no. Then he asked why do I have a car key in my bag? I stated that the key is for my car which is parked in the USA. He tried to tell me that I told him I was traveling with girls and that he saw me in the lobby getting out of a cab at 3am which was absolutely false because I was with a man and we never left the property at night. He kept asking me questions as if he was trying to catch me in a lie. Then he states “well you should have put them in the safe and the hotel isn’t responsible”. The end. No apologies, no nothing. At this point, I'm furious but I kept my composure because the power is in the pen, not the tongue. I have never felt so humiliated and violated while on travel. We were one of the few African American couples at the resort and probably the youngest during our stay so its hard not to think that we were treated this way because of our race and age. Was it a mistake to not place our watches in the safe, yes, but to completely dismiss us and not follow up with us as they so called claimed to do is unacceptable. I have stayed at other Melia properties and Im not sure that I will again. I will be sending letters to both the Melia and Paradisus corporate offices to inform them of how we were treated so hopefully no one has to endure this during their vacation.

Now, if you so choose to stay here, here’s my review of the property itself:

-	Check In: We arrived at 1pm. No drinks upon arrival. Maybe if you are Royal Service guests but don’t expect one if you aren’t. That was a little disappointing. Check in line wasn’t long but they will not allow you to get your room key until 3pm. Prepare for a crowd of people lined up at 3 to get their keys at the same time. The resort was nowhere near full so why they made us wait is beyond me. 

-	Rooms: We had an oceanfront room in the main building. It was a good size. A little dated but it wasn’t bad at all. Our balcony only had one chair. The bed had this cheap duvet that kept coming undone and the blanket under it felt like something from a bed at the Econo Lodge. Cant order room service from an ipad or TV so don’t look for that. There were no outlets near the nightstands to charge your phones so that was an inconvenience.

-	Lobby: To me, the décor of the lobby doesn’t give me that “tropical” feel. The lobby bar is great! Love the décor of the bar area. Has a sexy feel to it.

-	Food: The buffet is subpar. Breakfast is decent. Lunch wasn’t good. We never ate there for dinner because we didn’t enjoy lunch. The restaurants were quite tasty. Make it your business to make a reservation first thing every morning as they fill up quick. Room service was ok. It came pretty quickly.

-	Drinks: Pretty good. If you tip, the better your drinks will be lol.

-	Pools: The pools are well kept and nice sized. If you’re short like me and can’t swim, the main pool is over 5ft. I could barely stand up. It was little difficult trying to keep my head above water and drink my cocktail. The food at the pool is pretty good. Music isn’t loud enough. Its only louder when they have salsa dancing or Zumba. If you are looking for a place thats upbeat, even a little, this isnt the resort for you. 

-	Beach: GORGEOUS!!!! The water is so blue! The only downside is the locals walking up to you every 5 minutes selling stuff. Other resorts that Ive been to don’t allow that but Paradisus seems not to mind. The service on the beach was great. Never had to wait long for our drinks. No food service though.

-	Nightclub: The DJ is pretty good. He plays a mix of genres and takes requests. The waiters are very attentive. It wasn’t busy so don’t expect a full crowd.

Last but not least, I would like to thank Luis Cortez and Christan for taking GREAT care of us at the pool bar!!! Luis made sure our drinks were never empty and catered to our every need. We made it a point to sit in his area every day.

reviews.author: Dan S
reviews.title: Nice family vacation despite poor resort management
reviews.text:
We spent 6 nights at Paradisus.  Although we found the resort to be poorly managed, if we overlooked the related frustrations, it was a nice place for a family vacation.

Our frustrations started prior to arrival (which perhaps should have been a clue).  We emailed the hotel twice with various questions and the hotel never responded.

Check-In Difficulties
We arrived at 7am on a Monday morning after taking a red-eye.  We had booked two rooms, one with a king bed and one with two double beds, we had requested roll-away beds in both rooms, and we had requested adjoining rooms.  (We are a family of 6, and we wanted maximum flexibility as to sleeping arrangements.)  Our reservation was confirmed at check-in, but they told us no connecting rooms were available.  Instead, they offered us two rooms with one room in-between.  We realize the connecting room was not guaranteed, and this was a good option (and certainly we appreciated it).  We were put on a priority list for room cleaning, and we were told to check back in a couple of hours.

At 11am our rooms were still not available.  Not a big deal because check-out was at noon.  We were told rooms would be available at 1pm.  We checked back at 1pm and rooms still not available.  We were told to check back at 3pm.  At 3pm, the official check-in time, rooms were still not available.  We were told they were doing final cleaning, and one room would be available in 30 minutes and the other room would be available at 4pm.  We came back a little after 4:00pm, got our room keys and found that we had 2 rooms with king beds (instead of 1 king bed room and 1 room with double beds) and no roll-away beds.  I went back to the front desk, and I was told that the only double bed room was on a different floor, although there was a room with double beds on the same floor that would free up tomorrow (so we put a hold on that room).  They said they would have the roll-away beds set up.  

At 6:30pm, we still did not have roll-away beds.  We called the front desk and we were told no roll-away beds were available.  I complained and they said they would work on it.  I then went down to the front desk and asked for a manager.  I complained to the manager about no roll-away beds, not getting 1 king and 1 double bed room, and not having rooms available at the official 3pm check-in time.  His response was that room type was guaranteed only if we booked directly through the hotel (we booked through expedia), and that they could not guarantee room types sold through any other party!  He also said there was nothing he could do if all of the roll-away beds were being used.  He ignored my complaint about not getting rooms at 3pm.

In the end, the rooms worked out fine.  They found one roll-away bed which we used.  We ended up not taking the double-bed room that we had placed a hold on.  It was incredibly frustrating that they did not tell us about the rooms at check-in (that we would not be getting a room with two double beds) or that no roll-aways were available.  At check-in, they confirmed our room types and they confirmed we would get roll-aways in both rooms, and then they could not deliver.

Room Overview
The rooms were large, with 1 king bed and 1 fold-out couch (full).  One sink in the bathroom, with shower over tub.  Although the rooms were basically identically, one room did not have a clock, the other room had only one bedside lamp (instead of two), and one room had just a folding chair on the balcony whereas the other room had two folding chairs and a table.  So, a bit of inconsistency whereas we would have expected the two rooms to be identical.  We requested a second lamp for the room with only one bedside lamp, and housekeeping brought one up.  Note that the "master" switch turns off many outlets.  So, if you turn off the master switch to turn off all lights before going to bed, don't expect your phone to charge over night!   

Housekeeping
Housekeeping was pretty spotty.  One of the two rooms had a sticky, orange substance on the floor that we found when we first entered the room.  One day it was obvious that the shower/bathtub had not been cleaned.  We ended up putting four kids in one room (and it was very obvious that 4 people were sleeping there), and some days housekeeping left 2 towels in that room, and some days 3 towels, but never 4 towels (even though we called every day and requested extra towels and asked that they make a note that we would like 4 towels).  In general, when we called to request items be delivered (towels, etc.), the items were promptly delivered.

Room Location
We were on the 2nd floor of building 3.  Building 3 contains most of restaurants and bars, with restaurants on floor 1 and bars/nightclubs on floor 2.  Noise was fine/no issue, although it was a bit loud on Saturday night with music from one of the nightclubs (but not so loud that it kept us or our kids awake).  Biggest issue is that the stairwells smelled like sewage and you had smells from restaurants in hallways outside the room.  No bad smells in the rooms or restaurants though, so we just tried to ignore this.  Clearly the hotel is aware of this as they try to cover the smell with musky perfumed air on the first floor in the staircase areas.  This worked on the first floor, but as you moved up to the second and third floors, the smell got pretty bad.

Activities
Typical resort activities - Zumba, volleyball, etc., all of which were fine.  However, at least 4 times during our visit an activity did not occur.  For example, on the day we arrived we were given a schedule of activities.  Volleyball was supposed to happen at 11am.  Our kids went to look for volleyball, but it turns out volleyball had been replaced by soccer (with no notice).  Another day, there was supposed to be poolside games in the afternoon.  We saw the "entertainment guy" at the designated time, and he was leaving the pool.  We asked him about the games, and he said we was coming back.  20 minutes later, he still had not returned.  Another day, morning Zumba started 30 minutes late due to an issue with hooking up music.

Concierge/Butler
We had just basic level of service (not royal service or family concierge).  At check-in, a concierge was assigned to us.  He told us we would be working very closely with him the first couple of days as we learned the resort, he would make dinner reservations, etc.  He gave an overview of the resort, which finished with him asking if we were interested in the time-share presentation.  We said no, and he spent a few moments trying to convince us that we did want more information.  We held firm.  At that point, he basically wrote us off.  He passed us off to someone else to take us to the hospitality suite to change (as our room was not available and we wanted to change into bathing suits).  After changing, we went back to the desk and asked him to help us get dinner reservations.  He told us that he was not able to help us and pointed me to a phone so that I could call myself.

Dinner Reservations
The restaurants that require reservations book up very quickly.  You can only book two days in advance.  We wanted a 6:30pm reservation at Fuego or Mole the first night, but, when we tried to get a reservation the morning of our arrival, we were told nothing was available at any time.  I asked what dinner spots were open at any restaurant that night, and they said the only reservation was a 7:00pm at Bana (which we took).  At the same time we tried to make a reservation for Fuego or Mole for the next night, and we were told the restaurants also were booked the next day and the only reservation was a 9:00pm at Mole.  We pleaded (it was my wife's birthday the next day), and they found a 6:30pm slot at Fuego.  For the rest of the vacation, as soon as I would wake up, I would call and make a dinner reservation for the next night, so we had to plan things out two days in advance.  With that said, as we walked around the property at night, and as we ate dinner (usually at either 6:30pm or 7:00pm), most restaurants had numerous free tables, so we do not know why it is so hard to get a reservation (is there just not enough staff to support a full restaurant?).

Food Quality
Dinners, in general, were very good.  Mole and Bana were excellent, and Enso was solid (although no steamed rice available at a Chinese/Thai/Indian restaurant?).  Fuego can be easily skipped - the food was fine (nothing special), and, because the restaurant essentially is right next to Naos (the buffet restaurant), with an opening into Naos, you get a lot of extra noise and traffic - depending on where you sit, you feel like you are in an extension of Naos as compared to being in a nicer restaurant.  We did not try the Market Grill (Brazilian) or the Mediterranean restaurant.   

The buffet breakfast (at Naos) was fine but was below average compared to what we have had at numerous other resorts (for example, the way they cook made to order omelets results in the eggs always becoming very brown/burnt; none of the pastries were "worth the calories"; etc.).  The buffet lunch also was fine but was below average.  However, after two breakfasts and two lunches, we had had enough of Naos (which is not a good thing given no other breakfast option and another 4 days of vacation).

Sunset grill, by the pool, is basically unappetizing, bad kid food - pre-cooked hamburger, hot dogs, chicken patties/nuggets, and fries, sitting under warmers, nachos, a few things you could order, plus kid-quality pizzas.  Most of it was pretty unappetizing, although the guacamole, which was available 4 of our 6 lunches, was very good. 

Blue Agave, which was open starting at 11am and then all day each day of our stay is the street taco restaurant.  That quickly become our lunch venue of choice.  Nice atmosphere, and good tacos.  For some reason, the restaurant information we were provided at check-in indicated that Blue Agave opened at 4pm, although we found that it opened at 11am every day (another example of poor management oversight resulting in us getting bad information).

For dinners, we had some excellent waiters and some ok waiters.  Service in restaurants and at the pool and beach was uniformly good - no bad experiences.

Beach/Pool
Only two (very large) pools, and no hot tubs.  (We did not check out the spa or the gym.)  Both the pool area and beach area were very nice with lots of chairs, umbrellas, etc.  Plenty of staff around the pool and on the beach - asking us regularly if we wanted drinks or bringing us water.  On the beach you had the typical "locals" selling trinkets/cigars/braiding/etc.  In general they did not bother us, but we were surprised that they would walk to within a couple of feet of where we were sitting.  At other resorts, we have seen a rope line in the sand and they have to stay on the ocean side of that line.
    
Nightly Entertainment
There was one show each night, and we went to the show each night while we were there.  One (Michael Jackson) was entertaining and equivalent to what we have seen at other resorts.  The rest of the shows were all below average, and at least half of our group of 6 people left each of the other shows early out of boredom (except the circus show, although that also was below average - we kept hoping the next act would be better but the show never improved).

It's easy to leave a review with lots of complaints.  Bottom line though is, even with the frustrations, we still had a nice family vacation.  With that said, due to overall lack of management oversight at the property, I cannot rate the Paradisus very good, and therefore am giving 3 out of 5 stars.  It is a shame - with stronger/better management, and specifically more management oversight and a bit better training (housekeeping and front desk), this could easily be an excellent resort property.

reviews.author: Vh36
reviews.title: Does a lot, but none of it well
reviews.text:
We stayed for a week at the Paradisus Cancun as a family of 4 that travels frequently across the world.  This was our first time at an all inclusive resort, so maybe my expectations were too high but we found this hotel at best mediocre.

The hotel itself is very pretty with beautiful landscaping and a stunning beach.  But there is a lot to be desired in the details.  The rooms show a lot of wear with terrible beds (the “queen bed” is full size at most), broken latches in the bathrooms, finish pieces that randomly detach, etc.  Sometimes housekeeping will give you clean towels, sometimes not, sometimes you get 4 towels, sometimes 1.  They will knock on your door for turndown service at 10 pm, call you at 8 am, but if you need an umbrella at the pool, it’s basically impossible to get one. Staff are nice and seem to be trying but are overstretched.

The food is wildly inconsistent.  Some things (blue agave tacos) are delicious and sometimes you will get a plate of fried rice with absolutely no salt or seasoning.  We didn’t have a single meal where the wait staff didn’t forget part of our order.  We ended up eating off property for some dinners because the food was so bad.

The hotel felt very crowded and incessantly noisy.  There was pumping dance music at all hours of the day, and well into the night, at the pool, at the beach, and in the central area.  Since the door to your room is not even remotely soundproof, that means you will have to listen to the music (like techno violins) day and night.

We still enjoyed our vacation, but it felt like it was in spite of the hotel.  They would do a lot better to tighten up the focus and do less but more consistently.

reviews.author: Char F
reviews.title: Frustrating!
reviews.text:
I am writing this review as we are still here at Paradisus Cancun - we have been here one week, and have 3 days left.

The welcome on arrival was wonderful, really great staff and had a full explanation of how the hotel works, facilities etc. Again great concierge who took us to our room and explained things further. Room is ok. We have a junior suite with lagoon view. It has two beds which are pretty small, not a lot of space for two adults! Room decor is ok, a bit dated, but the room is clean.

Now the frustrations!

1. Despite signs saying you can't reserve sun loungers for more than 30 minutes, you basically have to get up before 7 to hold them. No one enforces the rule. The first day we went to the pool, I got two loungers next to one of the cabanas that you have to pay for to be told that 3 loungers are per cabana - and most of them not used! If you aren't down there to mark your territory at 7am you have to wait for someone to vacate one during the day.

2. Restaurant reservations. These supposedly can only be made between 7-7 for the following night. One morning I called at 7.15 and was told the only times they had were 6.30 or 8, nothing in between. I asked how that was possible when it was only 15 minutes since reservations had opened and was told some people book early! Today I called at 1015 and the restaurant I wanted was full though was given a time if 9.30pm which will be fun with a 4 and 5 year old...

Not a totally relaxing holiday - I didn't expect to have to be up so early every day. So much for a lie in.

reviews.author: Edna B
reviews.title: Not a big deal
reviews.text:
The hotel is very beautiful and has very good accommodations. 

We went there in our honey moon and initially it was not a very good experience since we had to sleep the first night in a room with two single beds. 

The staff is very kind, specially the waiters in the restaurants who make their best to provide an exceptional service. 

In general, is a good all inclusive hotel, but the expectation was higher. It seems all the good things are for the royal service. For example, some days there weren’t chairs available in the pool and in the beach, however they were renting places for abusive prices (tents rent by 170usd at the beach with food included).

reviews.author: Elizabeth K
reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text: After staying at LaPearla this was quite a let down. We requested two rooms close together and were put on two different floors; this really makes a family girls trip feel fragmented. Royal service was not quite as royal on this trip.

reviews.author: kgr1789
reviews.title: It was ok
reviews.text: The pool and beach were very nice. The dinners were nothing special. The lobby was very nice but hot (No AC). If you are looking for any night life even with low key, music and bar there is not much ever going on. I would not run back to this hotel. I stay in Royal service part of hotel service was nothing special.

reviews.author: Flightattendantk
reviews.title: You can find a better place for the same price
reviews.text: There's 5 parts in this resort. We were staying in the first one, it was about 7 minutes of walking to get to the main pyramid where all the restaurants are. The room was okay, nothing fancy. The balcony is small but we had a hot tub on it. Housekeeping was usually good except the last days they forgot to put new towels..we called and they delivered it within 10 minutes or so. The restaurants are not the best, service is not consistent and food is great at Market Grill. For the rest it's not exceptional for Mexico, I had better food in other resorts in Cancun. You feel the gap between Royal Service and regular guests. You have to book your a la carte restaurants a day in advance and not all the restaurants were open. They ask for your room number and then tell you if they have availability for you. We had a few waiters who did not speak english at all and freaked out because we didn't speak spanish very well so they didn't serve us until we called the manager, then they came back and screwed up the order even if I showed them the menu to make sure they really understood what we wanted. On a better note the beach is clean but there is a big step to get to the ocean due to the strong waves so be careful. Service on the beach is great if you tip well, around the pool you better go to the bar yourself it will be quicker. Ask for brand alcohol, if not they will use the cheap stuff. Towel service doesn't required a card which is great. The hotel is close to the bus stop if you want to go downtown or to la Isla Shopping.  I wouldn't recommend going to this hotel unless you take the Royal Service.

reviews.author: O1773QEluiso
reviews.title: very nice property, excellent beach but rooms very mediocre
reviews.text: feel we got value for our money but i don't feel the upgrades i paid for were worth it. Beds were very uncomfortable and rooms were very small. the property itself was very nice comparable to the nicest hotels in the area. Also need to be careful with the charges as they try and double bill.

reviews.author: Francisco P
reviews.title: Nice looking hotel, great Beach, not an all Inclusive
reviews.text:
Just stayed there last week because of a Congress. The hotel is beautiful with great scenery and landscapes, beach is outstanding! However to be sold as an "All Inclusive" when you have to pay extra to get a bed by the beach or by the pool, then is not really an all Inclusive. We had to pay from $105-$150+ to get a bed by the beach (and of course, you get a bottle of champagne and food delivered), but the mere fact that you have to pay extra to get the better things of the hotel is definitively a bad thing. I have stayed at many other All Inclusive type of hotel, and when you say All Inclusive, is really all. Don't advertise like it if you are not ready to deliver... 

The other bad thing that was although my room was very nice, my mattress had an inclination on the head side. I didn't realize that for a couple of days, and as result, i had gastritis and reflux. When i noticed what created the problem, i tucked in the cushions from the living room under the head side of the mattress and problem solved. Good sleep (actually the mattres could have been better), but the best of it, gastritis and reflux were gone. 

Bad place to stay if you are an smoker. I don't really care that much about that, but certainly having to walk outside of the hotel to smoke or just having one single area for smoking by the beach is not a good thing if you want to relax and enjoy a cigar.

reviews.author: Atti S
reviews.title: Big hotel in CAncun
reviews.text: This is an ' all inclusive ' hotel but that is a bit misleading because not everything is included. Good beach and pool and average food. Rooms are good especially the ones facing the ocean but the registration, checking in/out is a disaster, be prepared for long waits.

reviews.author: Caldeira Bertoli
reviews.title: Very good if you are on vacation mode and mood
reviews.text:
My stay was pleasant and you cannot complain about the all-inclusive fare. The food is quite reasonable, the drinks are server non-stop and the people nearby the pools are pleased to serve.

The inconveniences I found were on the instructions for the use of the  safety box - do not match with what you have to do to use it - and the not pleasant smell inside the drawers which prevented me from putting my clothes inside.

The pool and the beach are very pleasant to stay and I found it weird that the guest has to pay for the use of the bungalows by the pool.

If you are in a vacation mode and mood you will enjoy it.

reviews.author: naughty2000
reviews.title: All Inclusive in Cancún
reviews.text:
Just returned from Cancun where I attended the Alacero 58 Congress.

The large hotel complex has already seen it’s best days. The style and lay out (pyramid style) is outdated. Especially the lobby and the center of the pyramid are too dark and hot. The room (pyramid 4) was behind expectations. Bathroom boring, the room in white, average furnitures. However, the TV set was modern. 
What was really good is the beach aerea including two large pools. The beach very nice and clean.

It was my first time staying all inclusive but cannot understand the advantage of such concept. The lobby service was more or less missing. Especially during the day many outlets were not open but idle. Sometimes no chance to order an espresso or somehing else. Most staff had problems speaking English and/or were not motivated at all. Nevertheless tip exspectations were always evident.
May be for the many US tourists no problem but for many others.

The all inclusive concept together with many other things were not according to my taste and therefore do not plan to check again into this hotel or other hotels having the same concept. In my opinion all inclusive hotels should be excluded from common star ratings as it easily could be misguiding.

reviews.author: RICHARD A B
reviews.title: Good 3 star resort
reviews.text: We have stayed at several Melia resorts and this was similiar to most of them.  Pool lacked slides and other self play activities for kids.    Uffets was ok and some of the restaurant meals were very good.  They are in process of remodeling building 5 which caused no problems.  Pool area is not the easiest area to access with no rooms (or few) having access.   Work out area better then most.

reviews.author: Amanda T
reviews.title: Wasn’t really impressed
reviews.text:
We stayed here for an anniversary trip.   Check in was very nice, and we were upgraded to Royal Service. I commented to my husband about how amazing it smelled in the check in/lobby area.  

We arrived way sooner than check in time, but were given our bracelets and told to check back in a couple hours for our room.

Right after check in we were approached by a man that wanted to invite us to a welcome breakfast and gave us a list of all these upgrades and discounts we were getting just to attend.  Obviously it was their Club Melia presentation.  My husband said he had read they didn’t pressure to buy and that the incentives were worth it.   We agreed to attend the next morning.  

We then decided to get some drinks and eat lunch and then come back and check on our room.  We decided to dine at La Palapa, for Royal Service guests.  It is open air, overlooking the ocean.  We got great service here and great food and strong drinks.  Loved it here!!

Our rooms were not ready at this point so we decided to check out the resort.  It was at this point that it appeared the resort wasn’t really up to standards one might have expected.   In different areas of the different pyramids, I would smell a strong musty, moldy smell.   This persisted throughout the stay.  The hallways and common areas are also very dark!

I told my husband I didn’t really feel comfortable traveling the dark hallways alone. 

When we got our room, we had two double beds but had booked a King.   We didn’t care either way, honestly.    The balcony is very spacious but they need pub height chairs and a table out there because the beautiful ocean view is obscured by greenery growing there.

Our room also smelled very musty and a terrible odor came from the drains at times.

There was a smoke detector right above the bed with BRIGHT flashing green lights.   It was disturbing!  Once during some “adult” activities at night  the green lights came on and stayed on which freaked me out a whole lot.  Not sure what the deal is with that!!

Dinner reservations were always a hassle!  The first night the only restaurant we could get into was ENSO, which is kind of like Chinese.    I got chicken tandoori and my husband got duck.  Both ours were dry and overcooked.

The second night was our anniversary.   We called for reservations right after our “Club Melia” presentation and again they said the only thing available was ENSO! We just decided to go off property that night for our anniversary dinner.

DO NOT DO THE CLUB MELIA PRESENTATION!  The “free” vacation they promise comes with a 50.00 fee and according to the fine print, you have to attend another presentation.   We were also a discounted spa service we never received and Two free excursions that took pretty much demanding to get them to honor.   Plus it was very high pressure to pay 43,000 for a 50 year timeshare.  

We did get reservations at BANA the next night and it was just ok.  The sushi didn’t seem fresh.   We are sushi fanatics so they had a lot to live up to.

We spent a lot of time at the beach area in the Royal Service area.  It and La Palapa were our favorite places during the day, then a drink at Coco’s Beach club at night.

Our last night we decided to eat at Blue Agave.   No reservations required, and this is pretty much just tacos and quesadillas.  It was very good but my husband and I felt sick the rest of the night.  

Overall it wasn’t a terrible time, but it wasn’t the best either.   I enjoyed being in Cancun and their beach, drinks and pool area was good.   The food needs some attention and inside needs some updates, cleaning, etc.

reviews.author: Nortoa
reviews.title: Amazing Staff
reviews.text: I will start this review to say we stayed at the Hyatt Ziva last time so it may not be a fair comparison.  We did the Royal Service and paid more using Booking.com and paid more because it came with $550 in hotel credits.  The hotel credits are anything but. They are coupons to use example $20 off a bottle of wine however drinks are included. The resort is beautiful however music sucked by the pool bring own speaker, need more activities and beware every two seconds we were being upsold on timeshares, Massage’s, etc was hard to relax when constantly getting asked for things. The pool staff on royal side were amazing, they truly made the resort. Food was mediocre at best...

reviews.author: Omar R
reviews.title: So so vacation
reviews.text: Well the place was nice along with the staff , one of the few downsides is the air conditioner, only your room has air , no ac in the restaurants . The other one is that someone came in my room and stole my money , once I called the security they came to my room asked me questions , they searched my room as well as my luggage making sure my money was not somewhere else in the room . They checked the electronic door mechanism to see who came in my room and and according to them no one but me enter the room ( figures ) . The next day I went and talk to another security staff member to tell them to check on the people that comes in to the hotel and sales you the excursions because they are the only people that have your hotel name of course and your room number so they know how long you will be out of your room , the guy looks at my face and said no that is IMPOSSIBLE , I laughed then as I tell him that it sounds like an inside job he assured me that they have a security system that no one can crack , I laughed some more and went back to my room , then I realized they are sitting on a gold mine , cause here in the US we have one of the best  secured systems and Russia , North Korea and China were able to crack it so I hope they take advantage of this situation LOL ! Little to say I will never go back to that hotel ever again .   PS I know they provide a safe in the rooms and my money was taken from a drawer , still an inside job so be careful  use the safe specially if you are going to an excursion .

reviews.author: Michael L
reviews.title: Average resort to enjoy the climate and beach of Quintana Roo
reviews.text:
This past weekend I had the chance to stay at this resort for work from Monday through Friday. The resort was fairly empty, I would guess around 50% occupancy. Upon arriving the people at that front desk were very nice and helpful, with the customary cooling towel. I was checked in and given my wristband, a sort of colored nylon fabric with a wooden token intertwined with the fabric. 

I was taken to my room with the help of the bellboy. The room was very clean and nice with a King sized bed. The air-conditioner worked very well, which was really helpful as there isn't a ceiling fan, which made me sad. The mini fridge is stocked with water, snacks, and a variety of malt beverages. There are no liquor spirits in the room at all. I am not a fan of this at all, though I didn't consider calling anyone to see if that could be changed. The bathroom is a good size, and is elevated about 4 inches off the room floor, which my big toe repeated found throughout the trip. The shower has great pressure and heat, but is also again elevated a bit off the bathroom floor. If you have arthritis, or bad hips, etc, etc, I would consider finding a different resort as you will have difficulties getting in and out of the tub. 

The property as a whole is a smoke free environment, save for a few designated areas, though I did see quite a few people smoking in various outdoor areas without consequence. The buildings are very pretty inside, but the common areas are either not air conditioned at all, or are so poorly done that they feel as though they aren't. The restaurants were all comfortable except for The Market Grille, which is outside so this makes sense. The restaurants are all next to each other, and in a few instances we were seated in closed restaurants to eat in in a restaurant that was open at the time. This is how close they are to each other, which made for some confusion. I never had the opportunity to make a reservation and eat at a nicer restaurant because I forgot pants and didn't want to break the dress codes. It didn't alter my experience at all I believe. The room service is actually some of the best I have ever had at an all-inclusive resort. It was also delivered about 20 minutes after it was ordered, which is far and away the fastest I have ever had. The gym was nice, A/C'd and a great place to get some exercise in with cable machines, free weights, treadmills, and ellipticals. I was very happy with this amenity.

The Pools are all nice and clean, there aren't any floaties and I didn't see too many people who had brought there own actually. The music was never too loud and a good vibe. The beach is kept very clean and is pretty expansive and deep for Cancun. I did not at all appreciate the bars near the pools closing before the pools close. Not a fan at all.

Overall this was a pretty nice place. If you are in decent enough shape to get in and out of the tub, and love the hot weather, this may be a good option for you.

reviews.author: Flor Dalisa Q
reviews.title: GREAT BUT did not reimbursed my money...CHARGED ME TWICE.
reviews.text:
The hotel is great, breath taking. The services is excellent. The food, OMG, the food. 

However, THEY CHARGED MY RESERVATION TWICE. I forgot to bring the credit card with which I paid (booked online) and they didn't honored it even when the reservation was already charged and money was withdrawn from the credit card. Because I didn't show the plastic credit card at check in, they asked for another payment method promising they would reimburse the money from the original credit card. It's been almost two weeks since then and I am still waiting for the reimbursement. I even had to request a dispute with my credit card company to get my money back.

reviews.author: nunezeri
reviews.title: Paradisus Cancun 9/2017
reviews.text:
This was A honeymoon trip.   Check-in was great, prompt and quickly given our room. 
The room left much to be desired. The furniture was dated, and there were dirty curtains in the room and in the bathroom with stains that were so noticeable but have not been tended to.  The mirrors in the bathroom and behind the door where rested and the paint falling off the door. The rails to the sliding doors how much accumulated grime dirt and dust which was hard to look at and shoukd be steam cleaned immediately. 
 The hotel grounds were neatly kept up every day, there was lots of foliage which made it look beautiful, but all over the hotel it was warm and humid as it is open and AC vents should be added and turned on in the hot weather to help with comfort level of guests especially in the indoor restaurant Bana. We sweated through our dinner that night.
The restaurant food was good. We did not get sick throughout our stay. On Wednesdays the buffet has seafood and the lobster was amazing. We tried all of them except two restaurants which were part of the Royal service side. Outside pool area bars and snack bar had a great service and staff was friendly.  The Cocoa bar staff however ran things a bit differently, we were only given top shelf liquor which was on the shelf and clearly available if we bargained tips. This was odd because we were given the same type of drinks or liquor such as Hennessey at the pool bar and other bars around the hotel without a request for a tip before providing it.
The beach was amazing. This is the best area for water in all of Cancun, the hotel zone which ones all the way from down south beach palace to the top point- so any hotel in most of this area is great . Some seaweed in these months at different points in the hotel zone beach stretch doe to the tides and it being rain/urricane season but it was not much even on this trip.
 Overall this hotel is noted it self to be a five star. It felt more like a 3.5 or four people, and the room felt like at three. We would recommend it for the beach and the staff, However comfort level and room we would not recommend. We do not see ourselves returning to this hotel, hopefully they update their rooms.

reviews.author: W8997OMmielr
reviews.title: Hot and hotel of no!!!
reviews.text: Great hospitality but everything is no no no. No to sitting you if your party is not complete no to moving a chair for an old lady to sit on no to connecting room no to late checkout and we went during low season can't imagine what it's like during peak season. Every place in the hotel is hot and humid. I thought I wouldn't mind when I read other reviews but can you imagine having every meal in a sauna??? That's what it's like. And kids zone is filthy!!!! I understand it gets dirty with kids but it hadent been cleaned in maybe weeks!!!

reviews.author: Alex_723312313
reviews.title: beautiful hotel but???
reviews.text: Paradisus Cancun is a beautiful hotel i would give it a  5* if the staff wouldn't lie from the time we enter the hotel , as soon as they gave us our room key they were pushing us to do a couple minute presentation during breakfast time of a next day , they said that we are going to enjoy our breakfast and they are going to talk a bit about hotel and as complementary gift we are going to receive a 3 nights free stay for the next trip.(we thought you cant go wrong on that )so me and my wife we agree , it was all presented by the front desk by the guy name Mario and after by his manager Pamela , to make a long story short ,when we showed up next day on the breakfast i found out that we   signed up for 90 minutes presentation (not like they said before couple minutes) which ended up 3 hours nightmare with Rafael and his rude manager(dont know guys name)  presentation (we lose 3 hour of our day of beautiful sun ) of trying to sell us a timeshare and convincing us its best deal of our life paying 500$USD/ month for 50 years (or 170 000$), and we can stay 7 days a year  in Melia Hotels in VIP section ( where nothing happen ) in a room with the kitchen ( in all inclusive  hotel (what a joke)) but i first i need to purchase all inclusive which is 89$ a day/person (its not included in this 500$/month lol)and of course you need to purchase  a flight ticket on your own, Im telling you guys what a deal lol , after all of this happen they said because we didin't sign a deal for 50 years with them we can't get a 3 night free stay for next time lol :P ( and you know what i don't  want it  ) to all the travelers out there my review is hones truth and im not saying that i dont recommend this hotel i only dont recommend getting being fooled buy some of the staff member.  On the other hand waiters from Naos restaurant Andrew and Gabriel are 6* waiters ,very friendly ,helpful ,honestly really nice guys .The rest of the stay was great , its very nice and clean hotel , with great food and bars also a night club , its solid 5* hotel , just this second day experience made me so mad that i had to write what ever i wrote on the beginning just remember if you dont wanna waist your vacation time ,( there is nothing for free ) just dont go for any  presentation which you really dont  need, Have a great day every one

reviews.author: Clare W
reviews.title: Paradisus Cancun
reviews.text: I deal with the Melia White House in London so knew what to expect of the brand. On entering the hotel it is distinctly Melia, but this is where it ends. For what is advertised as a family Hotel I cannot believe that pretty much all of the main pool is nearly 6ft deep with steps down into it that are not marked, the last one is a large drop down. At check in no one mentioned that there would be maintenance work ongoing throughout our stay (mid August) and there where no warning signs around the hotel either. We would have to use a different staircase to the pool side, hearing banging from the room next to ours as it was renovated, the Sunset Grill not open for the first few days. One day we walked in to our room and it completely smelt of paint.  My husband went to reception and they said they would send a maintenance person up. A cleaner was sent to our room! She did not speak English, (I do not have a problem with this but when you have clearly been to reception speaking English you expect someone to come to you who will be able to communicate with you) in the end the cleaner put me on the phone to talk to someone who said they would send a maintenance person!. They never materialised and the only reason we did not complain again is that the smell did go by the time we was going to go to bed. The last few days all of the sunbeds by the shallow end of the pool was shut off but with no screen to the pool, meaning that although children could use the shallow part of the pool dust was constantly blowing across this area. The restaurants are not geared towards children at all. If you have a fussy eater it is very hard to find food that is plain! Turn down was erratic. The beds are ridiculously small! My husband and I are not large people and to have a more comfortable nights sleep my husband slept on the couch! We where in pyramid 3 for our stay which is convenient for being near the restaurants and reception but if you want to be able to get your children to sleep at a reasonable time I would suggest you avoid this pyramid as there is regularly loud music late into the evening. On the last day we had a cockroach in our room!  Thank goodness that was the last day as I would not of been comfortable staying after that, there may be a lot of plants but I still don't expect one of those in my room. Kids Zone was the best thing about the Hotel, the staff here are lovely and made my children feel very welcome for the hour or two they spent there a day.

reviews.author: Paula A
reviews.title: Customer Service was Excellent. Hotel Installations, not so Great.
reviews.text:
We are repeating customers to the hotel, this is our fourth time here. 
We, as always, have experienced great customer service. However, this time, we found the hotel installations lacking a LOT of maintenance. Tons of water filreting through the walls, bathroom showers, etc. Saw many roaches as well. We changed room twice because of the water filtering issue.
They've taken a great amount of "free space" in the pool and the beach area that used to be available for the guest's enjoyment, and have converted it into Bali beds for rent, ranging from $85-$150 per day.
Also, we used to love the Mexican restaurant, Mole. Not anymore, food was bland and with lack of character. It is more like "International Mexican" food, not taste whatsoever. 
Music through the hotel was awful. Although we come to this hotel every year to relax and enjoy the beach, we also come to Mexico to enjoy its ethnicity. Music was more like to put you to sleep. Not even in the Mexican restaurant we found a Mariachi.
Of course, not everything was bad. The Market Grill and Bana restaurants were DELICIOUS. Managers and waiters/waitresses were attentive and very accommodating. Jose at the coffee shop was beyond attentive. He was smiling every time we went there, very nice and a customer oriented guy. The ladies at the ice cream place were also great people, very attentive, and smiling all the time.
Food at the buffet was also very good. The tacos restaurant wasn't really impressive. It was okay overall.
And last but not least, the view of this hotel is MAJESTIC 😍😍😍

reviews.author: Victoria Miller
reviews.title: Love the employees
reviews.text: We loved  the staff they work so hard to try to please the guests. Daphne our conceiger was wonderful. The room was ok the food options not so much need some more variety. Perhaps vining a couple of the restaurant in to one and adding some more variety and family friendly menus so that we are not forced to eat at Naos every night.

reviews.author: Emily L
reviews.title: Trip with friends
reviews.text:
I will start out by saying that my husband and I have stayed at some 5 star resorts that definitely earned their stars.  We sort of consider ourselves "hotel-snobs".  This resort did not live up to our expectations.  The lobby was grand and beautiful.  The rooms were completely ordinary and plain.  Granted, we stayed in the lagoon-view king bed room, but it felt no different than a Holiday Inn.  This hotel is old, but they try hard to make sure things are fixed up.  Ongoing maintenance all over the resort.  The restaurants were nice, great food.  You had to make reservations the day before and we didn't get to eat at all of them.  Buffet got very crowded in morning hours, but the food was all delicious.  No one on our trip got any food sickness :)  There were lots of kids in the resort, so if you want to get away from them I would not recommend coming here.  We would try a different resort next time. 

Pros: food, lobby and indoor areas decor, overall appearance outside, entertainment, rooms clean

Cons: pool too deep- 5 ft everywhere, stone walkways too hot on feet, beach dropped off and waves strong, rooms ordinary decor, no open bars inside during the day to hang out when it storms, missed out on restaurants because we couldn't get reservations, hard to get chairs around pool

reviews.author: kimhT1665IZ
reviews.title: Not satisfied
reviews.text: Location is ok. Beach is always rough. Kids can only play in pool not beach too rough. Restaurant has to be reserved 2 days ahead. Spa services prices are tripled from US. Not much family friendly. Entertainment was so boring. No originality at all.

reviews.author: Kara1114
reviews.title: It's an Ok Hotel
reviews.text:
I travelled with my mother to the Paradisus Cancun July 21st-27th. This was our first time in Cancun and overall we had a very nice vacation. We stayed in the regular section of the hotel and did not get the royal service package.

Pros:
- The hotel grounds are extremely beautiful and well maintained
- The wait staff in the buffet are super friendly. Omar was our favorite waiter. I have an allergy to sesame and one night during our stay it was "Asian Night" which meant I could not eat most of the food since sesame oil was used in it; our waiter was Pablo that day and he was kind enough to let the manager of the buffet know about my allergy. The manager allowed me to eat from the royal service section where there were more options that did not include sesame.
- The beach is beautiful!! The sand was nice and powdery. There was a lot of seaweed in the water and on the beach for the first few days of our stay but, I know that can't be helped sometimes
- The hotel is pretty clean. Our room was fairly clean as well. 
- Our room had a really nice view

Cons:
- The check in process is so lengthy and disorganized. If you're like my mom and I and like to relax in the room for a few minutes after your flight, I would suggest that you try and arrive to the hotel after 3:00pm so that your room will be ready upon arrival. We arrived to the hotel around 11am and did not get into our room until about 3:15pm. Check in is at 3:00pm and there is no way they will allow you to check in earlier. BRING A PRINTED COPY OF YOUR RESERVATION! When we gave our name to the women at the front they said the they had no reservation under our name. We showed her the copy of our reservation and she brought it to another woman who was able to locate it after a few minutes.

-We stayed in the main building where all of the restaurants were and the Wifi is kind of non-existent on the first floor of this building. I would suggest getting a room on a higher floor for stronger wifi.

- Buffet is extremely basic. We didn't end up eating at any of the restaurants because it was nearly impossible to make a reservation so we ate at the buffet the entire time. The food was either over salted, did not have enough seasoning, or had too much oil in it. There were several occasions when even the rice was in a pool of oil.
