Don't expect there to be any authentic mexican food because they really dull the food down to try and fit what they think the guests like. Even something as simple as the guacamole didn't taste good. The cloth napkins at the table were almost always dirty and stained every time we sat down. BEWARE OF THE FISH LABELED WHITE TUNA! It is not white tuna, it's escolar and it made my mom sick for the first few days. Escolar is an oil fish which caused my mom to have really bad diarrhea and caused oil to leak from her bottom!! Whatever you do, stay away from anything they label as white tuna because it's not.

- BE CAREFUL WHO YOU BOOK YOUR EXCURSIONS WITH! Upon check in they assign a concierge to you who is supposed to explain more about the hotel and answer any questions you may have. Our concierge was Marta who tried to force us into a timeshare/royal service presentation. It took about 30 minutes of us saying "no, we are not interested" for her to finally stop trying to pressure us to attend. After she was done with the timeshare pitch I asked her where we could go to book excursions. She walked us over to an Expedia excursion booth and told us that we could book here. We booked two excursions, one to Isla Mujeres and one to Chichen Itza. We went to Isla Mujeres two days before Chichen Itza and had a great time with no issues. However, Chichen Itza was a disaster. We were in the lobby by 7:00am just as we were told to be. We waited for 45 MINUTES and OUR TOUR BUS NEVER SHOWED UP. After seeing that we were out there for almost an hour without the bus coming, one of the guys at the front desk in the lobby offered to call the tour company for us. He called and they said that they had no record of our reservation. The man at the front desk who called for us suggested that we go back to the booth where we booked the excursion once the staff arrived and see what happened. Later on that day as we made our way to the expedia booth from our room, we were stopped by a man who worked for Otium, another tour company within the hotel, he had recognized us from standing outside earlier that morning. He explained to us that Marta should not have brought us to the expedia excursion booth and should have brought us to Otium instead; he said depending on what travel agency or website you book your vacation package through, you have to go to the according excursion booth inside the hotel. I have no idea how they expect their guests to know that if no one tells us! Also, it should be up to the concierge to ensure that we are at the right booth!! Fortunately he was very kind and was able to get us on a tour bus to Chichen Itza for the next day with their tour company and we did not have to pay any additional costs. I am not sure if Marta brought us to the wrong excursion booth on purpose because she was annoyed that we weren't interested in the timeshare but, it certainly discouraged us from asking her anything for the remainder of our stay.

-The pool is always crowded until probably 6pm. There were never any chairs available no matter how early we got up. The water in the pool is so warm too. It was easily over 90 degrees everyday we were there and the pool water was anything but refreshing.

- There are cabanas called bali beds that you can rent out for the day by the pool or by the beach. At first the concierge Marta, told us that it was $50-$100 to rent one for the day. After a few days we decided to rent one since we could never find seating at the pool but we we were told they were all $120. We decided against renting one because we wee skeptical since the price keep changing for whatever reason.

Overall it is a nice hotel but, I would not say it was worth the money that we spent. The hotel advertises itself as a 5 star luxury hotel but, I would not agree with that statement. This is probably just an extremely basic all-inclusive, I'm sure there are better options out there if your are looking for luxury.

reviews.author: 585aliciae
reviews.title: Not enough air conditioning!
reviews.text: This resort needs more air conditioning especially at the places where you eat!  Main pool is to deep to walk around and to many young children hanging around the bar.  Location is great!  Service good!  Cooler air in rooms too!

reviews.author: mc20172017
reviews.title: Not sure it was worth the price tag
reviews.text: I think the number one thing my husband and I could not get over was how hot it was everywhere in this hotel.   I understand it's hot outside and they have all this foliage inside but we shouldn't be uncomfortably warm inside the restaurants and in our room.  The food was okay.  Some of it was really good and some of it was just okay.   The rooms were not anything fancy and you can see the wear and tear throughout the hotel.  For dinner, they said reserve the day before in the morning, but when I called they were already booked for most of the restaurants.  If you go, make sure you just reserve all your dinners for the entire time you are there the first day you get there or you won't get in, and will be stuck doing the buffet or tacos again.  The beach was beautiful.   The swimming pools were incredibly hot as well.  The staff were very nice.   We tipped everyone because we could see how hard they worked.  The entertainment was pretty good.  They work their butts off.   I wish there was a better space for them to do the shows because it was crowded and they were smashed into unconventional places to perform.  Overall, we enjoyed ourselves.  This was our honeymoon and they did do flowers and champagne and fruit the first day which was nice.  Will not stay be staying at this hotel on our next trip.

reviews.author: Becca R
reviews.title: Nice time, but wouldn't come again.
reviews.text:
I've visited the Paradisus in Punta Cana before so I definitely had certain expectations. This resort exceeded my expectations!! It is GORGEOUS, and you can tell that they put a lot of thought into their decorations and design of the hotel. It is also huge. There's 5 pyramids in the whole hotel, the lobby is in the 3rd pyramid. This is where my sister and I stayed, which was good because it was remotely close to everything. We had an ocean view room and we requested a room on a high floor, since we didn't want to be close to the pool area or the lobby area at night since we wanted to be able to sleep.

When we first entered our room, we were stunned by the beauty of it! The balcony is HUGE and gives you a beautiful view of the ocean and the pool area.

 The only con about the room was the door that connected to the next room. We called the front desk and requested that someone come up and lock the connecting room so that it wouldn't be able to be accessed by the family in the next room. They assured us they would and we waited and waited for someone to come up. Maintenance finally came and told us that there wasn't a key to lock the door and they weren't sure why the front desk told us they would lock it. (Lack of staff communication) We explained our safety concerns to the maintenance worker, and he understood and told us that the only safe option he recommended was for us to change our room. We were super annoyed because we had already settled in and unpacked and loved our room! We headed to the front desk to change it and they didn't have a room until the next day. So we headed back up to the room and a few minutes later, maintenance was knocking at the door and told us that they would replace THE WHOLE LOCK for us so we could lock it ourselves and be safe!!! We wanted to cry we were so happy! I loved how accommodating he was and assured us that we would be safe. Thanks Andres!!!!

This hotel isn't for people who are strict about air conditioning. There are definitely cooler areas in the hotel, but there isn't actual air conditioning until you get back into your room, which we didn't mind since we were used to this at Paradisus Punta Cana. 

Also, their entertainment is lacking. We came on vacation to relax, yes, but we're also in our 20s so we wanted to have some measure of fun. They don't have a specific area or room for shows; just the stairs by the pool and it's really uncomfortable to sit there, especially for 2 hours at night. 

THE FOOD IS DELICIOUS!! There's an array of restaurants to choose from, and all of the food is great! Vento was our favorite!! The only annoying part was having to make a reservation for each restaurant a day in advance because of the crowds - we traveled in late July.)

The part that really bothered us was the segregation of Royal and non-Royal service. We paid a lot of money to stay at this hotel, and Expedia did not offer the Royal Service option to us. Therefore, we weren't even aware it was available. Considering we paid so much for our stay, we assumed it would just be a frivolous extra. Boy were we wrong! At other resorts, we weren't really able to distinguish between Royal Service and regular guests. It was mainly the quality of the rooms and the discounted spa packages that they received. However, this ENTIRE RESORT is segregated. Regular resort guests and Royal Service guests almost never interact. There was a separate beach, separate check-in, separate pool, separate bar. One waiter was even instructed not to give us water bottles unless we were Royal Service. It was ridiculous, and made us feel like our money wasn't worth the same as the regular guests. 

There were several people that made our stay great! 

Andres in maintenance, Telma & Magaly in Housekeeping, and Benito the waiter. Thanks guys!!

reviews.author: skeith405
reviews.title: Beautiful Place But A Bit Quiet For Me
reviews.text:
I took my daughter on a "Senior Vacation" before she starts college.  We stayed in the adults only section with Royal Reserve.  Our room was fairly updated and we received a ocean/pool view upon only booking a lagoon view, which was  a nice surprise.  The room was very nice and seemed fairly updated.  The shower was full glass which was only covered by a thin white curtain and fully visible in the room  which was a little embarrassing for myself and my daughter.  Our butler Carlos was very nice and attentive.  The staff at the hotel were amazing and super attentive, especially in the adult only section.  
I thought the hotel was a bit boring.  It all depends on what you are looking for on a vacation.  The only swim up bar was in the family pool.  The adult only pool should have an accessible bar.  The adult only section inside and outside were dead!!!!  The adult only section pool area was under construction.  I cannot fault the resort for this.  It was unfortunate for us, but when you are open 365 days a year, improvements have to be made.  The restaurants were VERY  hot and I am coming from Oklahoma were it is extremely hot in the summer.  Also, I thought the evenings were a bit boring.  Basically, the only entertainment at night were cheesy shows from 8:30-9:30.  I would have much preferred some casual bar areas for mingling  and perhaps some music to dance to??  Again, I think it all depends on what you want out of a vacation.  If you want a serene calm vacation, this is your place.  If you want lively, fun............this is not your place.

reviews.author: Carianne F
reviews.title: Paradisus Cancun
reviews.text: Spur of the moment vacation with Hubby. Rooms were nice through Royal Service. We stayed on adults only side. The spa services were worth the value. The food mediocre. Nice service. Too many others to choose from. Hotel is being renovated. So lots of construction going on. I would not recommend staying their unless you choose Royal Service-comes with a butler.

reviews.author: BoomerTs C
reviews.title: Paradisus -Small rooms.  An 'Ok" resort.  Friendly Staff.   • Club Melia - No Good!
reviews.text:
ROOMS: Not good!   We are RCI members and expected a nice room.  We were told all the rooms are on the small size.  We got a parking lot view in a very small room. It was kept clean except the floor.. they must mop with dirty water.
CLUB MELIA:  Terrible.   Terrible check in and service. They do not care much. They do NOT return any calls either.  Took us almost 2 hours to get checked in and to our room. would NOT go back.  They offered no assistance in relocating us to a better room..  the actually don;' care at all.  They push you to go to a presentation.
FOOD.   Tempo restaurant is GREAT!!!!     The buffet restaurant is good BUT go to Blue Agave right across  from it. Better omelets and not crowded.
POOL AREA.  Pool area is good.  Good service etc.  I wish people would keep their KIDS away from the Pool Bar!  DUH.  They sit their with their 3-6 kids circling them in the water and taking up a lot of space.  NO TOWELS the first day by 4 p.m. and the men's room there was a disaster and they had to shut it down.  The rest of the week seemed better.
POOL:  about 70% of the pool is deep.  I am 5'8 and had to stand on my toes with the water at my chin.
BEACH is clean and great.
HOTEL:  Very dark hallways.  Very clean hotel .  Friendly staff.
RETURN?   It is an okay resort but we wouldn't go back because the rooms are to small and the pool is too deep and the chairs etc around the pool are can get congested to walk through.  
TIP: BEACH CABANAS   Don't waste money renting one!  There are many and they never once had more than 2 used for 1/2 a day.  By 10-11 a.m.  you can just go use one.

reviews.author: felix s
reviews.title: isssues
reviews.text: Has issues with reservations and theft while I was there.  Neither issue was solved to my satisfaction.  It included being lied to which I do not appreciate.  For what I spent on this Hotel and, I expected far more.  I would not stay there again.

reviews.author: nikkifay15
reviews.title: Family trip
reviews.text:
So my stay at this hotel was OK ! 
The check in service was horrible . Room wasn't available not to mention I paid for an  ocean view room upgrade ended up with horrible view of a huge motor attached to my balcony .  Other than my check experience service was great at this hotel .. room service takes about an hour so order ahead . Staff is super friendly .. food was great.. I'd like to say a special thank you to Mr Joseph from the Enzo restaurant. He went above and beyond for me and my family . Thank you . I'd like to also say a HUGE thank you to the girls in the baby club who took great care of my kids Michael and Rafael. They fell in love with u guys and thank you for allowing me to have piece of mind -Monse , lilli, Yeni - you girls are amazing! We miss u .  Just another thing I'd like to mention is that there is practically no AC in the common areas due to the live plants in the hotel .  (These are some pics from my balcony )

reviews.author: Neero D
reviews.title: Great location ,food but service was okay
reviews.text:
We stayed at the royal service which is an adults only building. The food ,drinks are excellent.
Our favorite restaurant was market grill. But they have lots of good option. great view at the la palapa.
Our butler  wasnt  responsive .We had a hard time reaching her and making reservations for restaurant.

reviews.author: Boti C
reviews.title: Paradisus is not much different from average resort
reviews.text:
The rooms were well maintained and the customer service was excellent all around. The servers do go above and beyond to help, and obviously tipping them helps as well. The pools were also very clean and in good condition. The food was just average and the only restaurant the only good restaurant was the Sushi restaurant. Restaurant reservations were very difficult to find. We spent quite a few days eating at the buffet that was also always busy, and we could never get a preferred seating area.
I did not appreciate the up charge every time we tried  to make additional requests. For example the pool and beach beds are an extra $10 per day. 
The beach was really rough the weak we were there. Obey the red flags and this means bathing is dangerous.
This is a family friendly restaurant and there were crying children at every turn. This is something I could not avoid, and would not recommend this resort for families with older teenage or adult children. Frankly, this was really a damper on my vacation.
For a day trip I would recommend going to Isla Mujeres. Take a taxi or a bus to Playa Tortuga. From there you can buy a ferry return ticket for $19. On the Island you can rent a golf cart for around $40 and drive around the Island. Stop at Playa Norte, which is the best beach on the Island.
We are Club Melia members and considering the amount of money we pay for the meal plan, the food options are really not worth the money.
All in all we did have a great time at the resort.

reviews.author: falciano5
reviews.title: No one to speak to regarding a bad room
reviews.text:
I have stayed abroad and to many different hotel atmospheres. I will say first the hotel is beautiful but the service is horrible. I checked  in on June 29th, there was a terrible odor in my room and complained. We had 2 rooms next to each other as we had 3 children, 13, 11 & 10. They moved out room finally on the 5th day being promised that they would move us right next to them. By 12 that day they locked us out of our room and gave us the room they promised us away and we had to move a hallway and a half down. Nothing at all upgraded or given to us in apology. People working here are no  accommodating or even sympathetic. I have stayed in the Paradisus in Punta Cana and have found their was resort was impeccable. Sadly I will not be back here. Please find another hotel in Cancun if toy want staff to be friendlier and more accommodating.
Btw the coffee bar guy was the best

reviews.author: Skitime 54
reviews.title: Overall a great Family Vacation but......
reviews.text:
First let me begin by stating that it rained, almost non stop, for the first 4 days we were at the resort which obviously made it difficult.  We had 16 people, 9 adults and 7 children so it was a big group.  I'm attempting to write an objective review despite the rain which the Paradisus has no control over. This is a very nice property but I would rank the food as very average.  I would have expected a little better.  We had 6 rooms with the Family Concierge package and albeit we liked the private check in area it seemed to be pretty dysfunctional.  All the rooms that had kids were supposed to have robes and slippers when we arrived but only 1 of the 3 had it, and then it took 2 days to get the rest of the rooms.  The adult rooms were supposed to have slippers and robes and again they only showed up in 2 rooms with adults.  These may be small things but it is the small things that we are paying extra for.  On the 5th day we woke up to no air conditioning in our room and now I will say they had someone come up and check it quickly it was obvious by later that evening it was not working again.  So they sent two maintenance folks up again the next morning and they worked for a couple of hours and got it almost working.  Thank goodness we were checking out later that day.  Because of the guys working we had to go to our daughters rooms to shower and get ready for checkout.
We typically take our family on a annual vacation to a nice resort or a cruise (Disney was over the top) and I can say we probably wouldn't consider this resort in the future.

reviews.author: Rebeca C
reviews.title: Might not be what you expect given how expensive it is.
reviews.text:
This hotel is beautiful but old and there are few things that make it nice but not worth the money you pay for.

Rooms: the rooms are ok but nothing wow. It was nice that we had ocean view but the buffet was below and it smelled like food all the time (not good). Also the AC installations were right outside so it was pretty loud. 

The beach: It was beautiful white sand and we always found a place to  sit and relax. However, the ocean was very  aggressive and the wave would pull you in.. can be very dangerous. Thanks god the lifeguards were there all the time! The servers at the beach were very attentive; they did earn their tip. 

Food: we went to almost all restaurants. Tempo was amazing as well as the mexican cousine restaurant. The rest not so good. The buffet was not that good, it did had a lot of variety but it wasn't delicious in general. Couple of times they did have one dish here and there that was ok.

Customer Service: I think this is what we liked the most. The staff, the servers were sooo nice , helpful and humble. We enjoyed talking to them.

The pool: the pool was nice but most of times very busy. It was hard to find a spot. I will mention that the hotel grounds and facilities were very clean all the time. A lot of workers!

Entertainment: they did had something every night and it seemed ok.

For me  it was an "ok" experience, hanging out with my sister and her family made it nice because that's what mattered to me but when it comes to the overall experience it should be cheaper given what it actually is.

reviews.author: M C
reviews.title: Average hotel with bad food.
reviews.text:
My sweetie and I always go to the ME Cancun for Memorial weekend. Unfortunately, they are currently undergoing renovations, so we decided to go to another hotel in Cancun. Lets just say the toilet and I were best friends because I had abdominal problems from the food.

Hotel Grounds- 
This hotel needs to be renovated. There was always dirty towels on the floor throughout the hotel to soak up the leaks from the roof. Hotel looks old and the elevator smelled like mildew. However, there were always multitudes of workers tending to the vast array of plants and flowers inside the hotel. 

Room - 
We had an oceanview suite with a Jacuzzi. However, the Jacuzzi did not work. We called maintenance and they had to change the motor in the Jacuzzi. You mean to tell me no one knew the Jacuzzi was inoperable?

Housekeeping - 
Below par. It appeared that the bed was the only thing that was tended to in the hotel room. 

Pool/Beach - 
Since we had the Royale Service/Club Melia, our Butler reserved the Bali Beds for us everyday that we stayed there. I preferred the Beds by the Club Melia side as opposed to the Royale Service side because it was much livelier. Very quiet by the Royale Service. 

Restaurants 
Naos - The buffet was awful and gave me stomach problems. Below, I will discuss each restaurant that I had the opportunity to eat at:

Tempo - Michelin star, contemporary, formal/elegant restaurant. Hands down, this was the best restaurant that this resort has to offer. Although, its not included in the all-inclusive, its an absolute must to dine here. The food and service was impeccable and I had no stomach issues afterwards. This restaurant actual carries this resort.

La Palapa - This restaurant is located in the Royal Service VIP and only Royal service guests can eat here. The food here is good. I enjoyed their breakfast as well.

Mole - service was good, but the food was not. Mexican cuisine.

Toiji - Asian Cuisine. Located in the middle of the hotel. Very nice restaurant and romantic. We ate here several times. 

Entertainment
The Red Lounge was popping. In fact, this is the first resort in which people actual went to the lounge. Had alot of fun there. The DJ was great because he catered to the crowd. Drinks were great as well.

Shows - We did not attend any shows at all.

This resort was ok, but this is a one and done for us.

reviews.author: Hardygrl
reviews.title: Would not stay here again
reviews.text:
Just came back from a week at the Paradisus.  The resort is very pretty but in VERY serious need of a makeover.  Our room had chips and cracks in the floors and throughout the hotel it was very obvious that this was an old building that needed a lot of updating.  There are hardly enough outlets in the room for charging and some didn’t work at all.  

The views are spectacular and the turquoise water was perfect.  We had two rooms with an ocean view that were incredible! 

Check-in – long lines and took forever.  Gave us resort coupons but never explained how to use them. The way they work – they were not even worth it.  For example, one of the coupons was for $10 at the store.  So I had picked out a few things.  Unfortunately, they advised me that I had to spend $100 to get $10 off. Ridiculous - so we never even used any of them.  Also, we had a reservation for a king room and a double room.  They could not honor our king size room which was terrible and I was very disappointed to find out that a reservation made months in advance could not be honored. 

The lobby is very pretty – but it is extremely HOT! The air-conditioning is close to nothing throughout the entire lobby.  It was extremely uncomfortable walking around at night and just trying to “hang out” as it was so hot and humid. 

Food:  Food was very good.  The presentation and taste in the restaurants were great – but if you have picky eaters you may have some problems. The restaurants were not crowded or busy yet we seem to never be able to get reservations at the restaurant we wanted.  Every time we went to eat there were always empty tables so I am not sure why it was always a problem.  Service in every restaurant was phenomenal and we always tipped our waiters as it was well-deserved.  Our favorite place was Blue Agave.  Loved to just grab some chips and guacamole or some delicious tacos or quesadillas.

Bars:  There are not enough bars or places to get drinks around.  We recently went to the Hard Rock Punta Cana and loved that there were places all over to get drinks.  Never a problem finding drinks.  There were bars everywhere and even martini and vodka bars set up throughout the resorts.  This was certainly NOT the case at the Paradisus. Aside from the main bar, and the pool bar there were not many options.  Definitely could use more bars throughout the resort

Entertainment:  LACKING – I never saw anything but one singer by the pool at night.  No activities around the pool. At the Hard Rock Punta Cana there were tons of poolside games, activities, foam parties, etc.  Lots for young and old adults.  Nothing happening at the Paradisus.  Never saw the non-motorized sports either and no one told us where they were.   Finally, on the day were leaving we saw parasailing offered at the beach. 

Shops were nice – typical resort and hotel merchandise.  However, the resort does not accept American dollars (unless you are tipping of course).  Only pesos or credit cards.

In a nutshell, we had a great time with our friends but along with the cost of staying of here and lack of entertainment, amenities, and outdated facilities  ---- we would not stay here again. I don’t think it’s worth the price and there are many other resorts with more to offer.  The service and staff were GREAT but it's just not worth it.  This resort is definitely no more than an average 3 star.

reviews.author: lucilap491
reviews.title: Rooms were not cold enough
reviews.text: Beach, pool, staff, service awesome. Downsides were that our room was not really cold. Just tolerble with the air con blasting at the coldest setting. Drinks not very strong. And mini bar stocked with only four cans of beer daily. Food at restaurants was good except for asian cuisine.

reviews.author: Hortensia M
reviews.title: Kids and Husband Birthday Vacation
reviews.text:
As a Melia Club member I was expecting a better stay. To start the Consier assigned to us we only saw him 3 times out of our 6 days.  We had an unconvinced with the person that fill the fridge he came in the room with out giving us time to answer the door and cut my husband trying to get dress. Just because the DO NOT DISTURB sign is not on the door does not give you the right to open it with out knotting and waiting enough time for the person inside to Answer😡😡 
The pool was not an all members area only nor the beach everyone was together. 
The food in the restaurant Enso  was not good at all it was extremely greasy and the service well.....  not all that great... 
the only restaurant we enjoyed was FUEGO, the service there was great and the food fenomenal.  Some of the others are ok . 
The kids pool area was good again it was for everyone but the pool service was great our server was excellent always asking if we needed anything.  
This Hotel did not meet my expectation will not come again and we rather  go to any MELIA / paradisus in Punta Cana  because is better in all aspects....

reviews.author: TeanaMartinez
reviews.title: Mediocre All Inclusive
reviews.text:
It is difficult to have a "bad" time in Cancun so the trip was good regardless, but specifically related to the hotel the pros and cons as I saw them are, 

Pros:  Great location, better than expected view based on the room type, the hotel did set up the room with flower petals on the bed because it was a honeymoon (very nice and unexpected), friendly staff, nice included add on at the aqua park across the street (kayaks etc.), property was clean and well maintained.

Cons:  Mini bar in room wasn't well stocked.  Room had a faulty dresser drawer that was reported and never dealt with. Building public areas were hot and not well ventilated. Despite being "all inclusive" the Bali-Beds were an up charge of anywhere from $50-$170 US depending on location and / or club status (I am a timeshare owner, and at the location where I bought the timeshare the Bali-Bed usage was free). The food in almost every location was over salted, and the Asian food in both locations that served it was absolutely terrible (my wife is Asian and we live in San Francisco so know "good" Asian food).  There was something weird about the fruit juices served also, almost like it was artificially sweetened with saccharine or something - bleck!  Finally, service dogs were not allowed.  We have a certified service dog who detects the presence of crustacean's in prepared food but she was not permitted on property.  The end result was that my wife had a mild hive breakout, despite the fact that each restaurant did ask if there were any food allergies.  Luckily it must've only been a minute trace caused by cross contamination, so the allergic reaction was mild.

reviews.author: Ally
reviews.title: Hotel was fine, beach was beautiful, service was ok
reviews.text:
My boyfriend and I stayed in a Ocean front room in the Royal Service side for 8 days, 7 nights recently.  Overall, I would say that the trip was good but a little disappointing.

The room was clean, large, great view, quiet, and had an awesome clear shower that faced the bedroom (a curtain is available if you do not want to be watched).  The mini fridge was constantly restocked.  We were big fans of the downstairs private Royal Service lounge, which had good food 24/7, a Nespresso bar, and a premium alcohol bar, which you could use to serve yourself or ask for drinks to be mixed by the waiters who were always nearby.  

The hotel property was large, pretty and generally clean.  The different pyramids did have strong scents but you get used to it after a while.  The roofs leaked after a massive thunderstorm during the first 3 days but hotel staff was quick to have buckets, mops, warning signs at the ready.

There were a good number of different restaurants available.  Yes, reservations were necessary at all except for the buffet and the Royal Service outdoor restaurant La Palapa.  We tried almost all of them and overall, the food was good.  We ate at La Palapa almost every morning for breakfast and lunch only because we did not want to deal with crowds and children.  La Palapa and the two Asian restaurants were probably my personal favorite.  There were reviews that complain about the food but I really think it depends on your personal preference and if there is something you don't like, then try a different restaurant until you find something you do.

The beach was beautiful.  As mentioned, it was surprisingly rainy, cloudy, and actually a bit cold the first 3 days.  That was depressing as it was heavy enough rain CONSTANTLY that you couldn't even sit by the pool or under one of the beach huts.  So we spent most of the first 3 days wandering inside the hotel, eating, and watching Netflix, which was a drag.  But during those moments when the sun came out, the water really was beautiful.   

Pool-wise, we spent most of our time in the Royal Service pool because it was less crowded and quieter.  We ventured over to the main pool a few times as the pool bar is there but to be honest, it was surprisingly smelly every time we were there.  Not sure if it was due to the weather or what was going on but it actually stank so bad that we didn't even want to sit on the stools surrounding the pool bar.  

Butler service was good.  Our butler was Giraldo and he was lovely.  Very helpful, somehow always managed to run into him once a day even though the property was big, and surprised us with champagne and rose petals on the bed one night.

The one thing that let me down was the cabanas.  We were guaranteed 2 days use of the Royal Service cabanas out of 7 days.  We only got 1 day.  On 2nd day we booked, we showed up in the morning to ask for our reserved cabana, only to be told that they didn't have our name down.  This was despite the fact that we made the reservation days ago with the Royal Service front desk and double checked.  We asked to be put on the wait list (you come back and check at noon) but of course there were none available.  So that was a downer.

reviews.title: First vacation with 1 year old
reviews.text:
We traveled in May with our son who just turned one. My husband and I have been to Mexico and Punta Cana many times. We tried to stay at the Iberostar Cancun again, however they were fully booked and we had to look at other options. Paradisus Cancun was recommended to us by Apple Vacations and Cheap Caribbean agents. 
Room- We requested not to be in building 3. Upon arrival, we upgraded to ocean front and were placed in building 3. That evening, we had to move rooms. The singer downstairs was so loud that you could hear her over our noise machine our baby sleeps with. The beds were comfortable. Pillows very flat. Room is small, nice balcony. Our air conditioner also broke several times and we had to have someone come service it. 

Pool/beach- Ocean was beautiful! Very big waves though which made swimming very difficult. The main pool was busy. We didn't like that it was so deep and we couldn't touch. We enjoyed using the smaller pool in front of the buffet restaurant. We had no trouble reserving chairs by the pool and beach around 9am. Definitely reserve them though, or you won't have any. The music is very loud. The singer on the beach was loud too. This is not a very relaxing resort. Also, the bali beds are useless. No one rents them, so they are all empty. The price isn't cheap for a daily rental. I would have liked to let my little guy lay down to take a nap, but it  wasn't worth the price to us. 

Food/drinks- We were very satisfied. Because we had our little guy with us, we only ate at the buffet and Blue Agave for tacos. All waiters were wonderful!! There is no pasta station at this resort as there is at many other all inclusive resorts. Drinks were great! 

Baby club- We took our son to play a couple of times but stayed with him. He enjoyed playing with the toys and watching Mickey on TV. There isn't a little water park at this resort, which we would have loved to have. They call it a kid's pool, but it's just shallow with loungers built in. 

Bring lots of small bills to tip. The service is great! We took the public bus to La Isla for shopping and dinner one night. Highly recommend getting out of the resort for a little bit. We enjoyed our stay but won't return. Cancun is very busy and while we picked this resort because of how close it is to the airport, we would rather drive down to the Iberostar complex or Playacar.

reviews.author: N5061YPkarenk
reviews.title: Vacation
reviews.text: Had high expectations but was disappointed first day room wasn't ready we got checked in at 9a.m. did not get a room till 5 PM . It seem like when we declined the  orientation.The level of  Service declined. We did not come there to buy a timeshare I don't know why that when we declined to listen to the presentation  our service decline also.

reviews.author: Haitham A
reviews.title: Most beautiful beach I've seen, but property leaves a lot to be desired.
reviews.text:
The Paradisus Cancun has one of the most beautiful beaches I've seen. The beach doesn't benefit from shelter like a bay, hence the waves (and riptides!) here can be very strong (something to keep in mind if you have small children, or can't swim very well). Red flags (no swimming) were up on the three days that we were there, but the lifeguards did let you wade into the water for the first 10 meters or so from the beach. The water also did have the occasional seaweed like some reviewers had mentioned, but its the sea not a swimming pool and did not bother us at all. 

The issue with the hotel was that it was built in 1991 and was really starting to show its age. The rooms finishing was quite dated, and there also seemed to be minor pest problem during our stay there (found two small roaches inside my room on two separate occasions, plus a larger one outside on the way to the lobby).

Food (and drink) were overly abundant, but what they had in quantity they lacked in quality. The Market Grill (Churrascaria style restaurant) was great, and Vento was alright as well. The buffet style restaurant is to be avoided wherever possible (alas its the only option for breakfast). Drinks service at the beach was sporadic at best and was limited strictly to drinks, no food.

reviews.author: ca2556
reviews.title: Honeymoon
reviews.text: It was okay wouldn't recommend not that it was bad it's just that I've been treated better at other hotels.one day the electricity went  out and no ac that day so that sucked didn't get the room I had asked for so we had to change rooms three times !!! Smh!

reviews.author: Christina G
reviews.title: Was just ok
reviews.text: We stayed here for a week. We would not go back. It's too hotel like and doesn't have a nice resort feel.  There is nothing family oriented to do in the evenings. Just a bar that you seem to be able to hear from every room (although some rooms are worse than others).  The pool is nice and the beach is nice.  The shows...well who knows if they are good because they have such a poor set up you can never see them.  The food was good but other than the buffet not great for kids.  We found it not very entertaining for our kids but our standards were high as we had previously been to the now jade and honesty we don't think it gets better than that place. We will not venture outside that chain of resorts from now on.

reviews.author: Vika P
reviews.title: Good old - fashioned hotel
reviews.text: Have spend 7 days in that lovey hotel!Yes exactly -  hotel is really lovely,nice design with jungles inside of piramide,but it has really old managment!Food isnt good,from all la carte restaurants - brazilian was good!Others was awful!Beach is pretty good but sea is very wavy!Entertaiment is poor.Very talanted people but cant show their own ability but make american clone!Was sad....

reviews.author: annay157
reviews.title: A solid 3 star average Cancun resort
reviews.text:
The property and common areas were lovely, as expected at any Cancun AI resort, the service was awesome, the pools were nice, although the kids pool is not really a kids pool (no fun slides), just a wading pool I would say but still my son loved it. The restaurants had nice modern decor, service was good, food was just OK. My problem with the food was that everything was room temperature, and this is not only for the NAOS buffet restaurant, it was even in the sit down restaurants. We were so disappointed with the tapas restaurant Vento, everything was room temperature, we had one bite of each tapas and left and decided to go to the buffet. BANA was a huge disappointment; the food did not taste Japanese, I would call it really bad wannabe Japanese/Chinese food. They had a speciality Udon stir fry, it was seriously inedible; the udon noodles were so overcooked, it was broke into one inch pieces, it was just bad. BUT the service at the restaurants were excellent. The only restaurant that we enjoyed was Market Grill, went there 3x during our stay, everything served hot! 

NOW for the cons: aside from the average food, the rooms are so outdated, they need to renovate ASAP. Door knobs falling off, cracks in the stone and patched up, the decor is old and dark. We actually paid for an upgrade and were shocked that this was the upgrade. We asked one of the room service people about the room and he stated that the was one of the nicer rooms...shocked!

SO overall our stay was good: my son loved the wading pool and beach, service was excellent, food was average, rooms were old= 3 star resort.

reviews.author: carolynw377
reviews.title: Holiday
reviews.text:
We stayed at the paradisus Cancun for 7 days we had the all inclusive, we had a good time,
The negatives are 
1st : the drinks package is ok ( there is only about 2 types of beer, wine is average and I am a southern comfort drinker and they do not have it)
2nd : do not stay in reception tower I think this is the 3 rd tower it is way to noisy we could not sleep we had 2 rooms 4 adults we had to shift after 1 st night we could not get 2 double rooms again so 1 couple had to have single beds for rest of trip.
3rd : They let people get very drunk. First experience of hotel we stood outside and a girl beside us vomited on the ground beside us, it was 4.30 in afternoon.

The positives are
1st : The food was really good.
2nd: The amenities were great to.
All in all it was a good holiday

reviews.author: Rachel M
reviews.title: It's not great and it's not terrible.
reviews.text: I don't have anything bad to say about the Paradisus. The staff was always wonderful, especially Jesus at the pool bar. But I have stayed at several resorts in the Cancun area (Rui Peninsula, Now, Secrets) and all are relatively close in price range and all are better in quality. The beach is gorgeous at this resort, but the beach is gorgeous everywhere in Cancun. I never had outstanding food but I never had bad food, it was always just ok. The mixed drinks were very weak but the bartenders were very happy to provide alcohol when asked. It appears to be an older resort that some of the newer places are just passing up in respect to modernness. For the price it's nice for a few days.

reviews.author: craftysue62
reviews.title: Been to better
reviews.text:
After staying at the Paridisius Palma Real in Punta Cana and having a wonderful time during a 7 day stay we decided that we would book the Paridisius Cancun and stay for 10 days this time. We where greatly surprised that there could be such a difference between two Melia resorts.

At the Palma Real we did not have royal service and still had a great time as the resort had such beautiful grounds open to all and events on the beach a few times during our stay.

We decided to go for royal service this time as there is a issue with specialty restaurant reservations without having royal service.Check in was quick and staff was excellent. Our butler Maria was top notch and assisted us in making all our dinner reservations. The room was nice except for view low floor lagoon view huge balcony but hardly used.

Servers at all restaurants were excellent, please tip these people they work so hard for so little pay,it does get you more personalized service but did notice they were very nice to those who did not.

The water is beautiful at the beach but was rough most days.when the wind died out and the waves calmed down its breath taking. Our biggest complaint about the beach is that the tide never seemed to go out any so long walks on the beach were difficult as the water is almost up to the shore line and there is a drop offf from the sand level.

Pools where plentiful from quiet in the royal service area to swim up pool at building 3, royal service is building 5. Nice beach service at the royal service beach where a bucket of bottled water was supplied at your chairs. Beach chairs on the beach are horrible no padding and just two positions. Come on for what they charge for royal service padded chairs should be the norm as in other resorts we have been to.

Food was good at the buffets with many choices. Specialty restaurants was ok have had much better with very poor desserts at the specialty ones. We would skip desserts and return to the buffet after dinner for deserts.

Our biggest complaint is the lack.of a theater for the entertainment shows. They are held in a bar lounge where there is club type beds were people lay down trying to whatch a show that is visible to only those that get on these ridiculous beds and couches. There is limited couches with any kind of waitress service where one can have a drink and chill though out the resort.

If you have trouble walking up stairs this is not the resort you should go to. You must walk up stairs almos everywhere. To the beach, to the restaurants, to the pools. Oh yes all the pools are deep over five feet so walking in pools are not easy.

If you want to do Melia resort go to Paridisius in Punta Cana there is no comparison between the two when it comes to entertainment and grounds.

reviews.author: kevinC8560AN
reviews.title: Best location Hotel
reviews.text: Power outage 4 times a day. some restaurant had high room temp setting. we have kids and have to leave early to take a shower. other place are ok. food selection were limited as most of the place must have reservations and we are not coming in peek season.

reviews.author: Debbie & Jose R
reviews.title: Average resort
reviews.text: Our butler Maria was excellent. She was very attentive and accommodating. Service from  servers Carlos at Vento, Arturo, Armando, Pasquale, in Naos was excellent. The room was very nice, although I would have preferred an Ocean view. The beach was gorgeous, but must get there early to reserve lounge chairs. Would have been more comfortable if they had cushions. Too many stairs to climb all over resort. Even the beach had quite a few steps to walk up and down. Entertainment was limited and not enough comfortable seating at the Avenue bar where show takes place. There is no theater like most resorts have. Although everyone was nice, I don't think I would return.

reviews.author: Jenene J
reviews.title: Lots of good things about this place, but also some not so good
reviews.text: There were lots of good things about Paradisus Cancun, but I found two things not so great.  The grounds were lovely and well-kept.  The pools were huge and well-kept.  The service staff was excellent.  The room was comfortable and quiet.  So sleep was no problem.  What I didn't like was the food.  This is an all-inclusive with 9 restaurants, and they had real chefs who tried.  But the food was just odd.  I believe they have a lot of European and Asian clientele, and they seem to cater to those people.  While the food was nicely prepared with attention to detail, it is for the adventuresome person.  I thought I was adventuresome, but guess I'm not.  What you see on the menu and what actually appears on your plate is about 180 degrees different.  Example:  my hubby ordered a Steak salad, and out came a bowl with black slimy stuff (I think it was seaweed), which my husband couldn't eat.  They had two or three Asian-type restaurants, Mediterranean, but there was no restaurant that we ate at that had anything remotely American-like.  There were two restaurants which required extra charges, so maybe they had America food, but I don't think so.  Even the Mexican-style restaurants were not what we are used to in America, but they were at least more tasty.  Their buffet restaurant came closer to serving some American-style food, but even it seem to cater more to other countries.  I think a child would likely starve trying to find something he/she would like.  I've never been so glad to get American food when we got home.  Also, this trip cost a pretty penny, but they have set aside one gigantic pool and pool area for their "Royal Service" guests.  I felt like a second class citizen with all the areas we couldn't go to.  So you had way too many people trying to enjoy one pool and hardly anyone enjoying the other pool.  And the only place you could get a sit-down breakfast was in this same area and off limits.  I felt a little cheated with the way they remind you that you didn't pay top dollar.  But all in all, the place is nice and has a beautiful atrium.  I wouldn't go there again simply because of the food though.  Also, regarding children, the kids pool was a very small section of the big pool.  For the most part the big pool was nearly 6' deep and not suitable for children.  The room had the most private balconies I've ever seen because of how they designed them.

reviews.author: prplbunny
reviews.title: Amazing Staff, Mediocre rooms
reviews.text:
I started out my visit wanting to move somewhere else. Our room wasn't very clean (crawling baby found multiple pieces of garbage/random stuff on the floor to chew), it was absurdly loud (as other reviewers have commented), and our "Lagoon view" was the roof of the building next door and a McDonalds.  The pillows are, in fact, horrible (again, as others have said) and the food at one of the restaurants (Enso) was so bad we left and went to the buffet to try and find something else to eat.  The drinks may not actually contain alcohol, though they were delicious. 

However - the staff was seriously amazing. Friendly, helpful, went the extra mile EVERY time.  So the more we stayed, the more we ended up liking the place.  Market Grill was AMAZING - we ate there twice.  The main buffet (only place for breakfast) had a huge variety of foods - we always found something we liked.  The views on the beach were awesome, the kiddie pool (where we, admittedly, spent most of our time) was beautiful, and the staff working there were attentive, friendly, helpful, and a pleasure to work with.

All in all - 

Pros - STAFF STAFF STAFF. Beautiful beach and pools, Market Grill was delicious, Buffet had wide variety

Cons - So loud. Could hear everyone in the halls/rooms around you. A/C sounds like a plane taking off. Pillows/beds were not great, room not that clean, worn, dated, and limited options for breakfast/lunch.

Not sure I'd recommend, but enjoyed our stay for the most part.

reviews.author: Procaresteve
reviews.title: "They spoiled us in Playa Del Carmen and let us down in Cancun"
reviews.text:
We have experienced both Paradisus in Playa del Carmen and now Paradisus in Cancun.  
I spent the entire week comparing the two resorts and I feel the need to share my opinion. 

First off my wife and I have 4 kids ranging between 9 and 16. We are the typical NJ family, we make a decent living and have spoiled ourselves with some really nice high end family vacations.  
The Paradisus Cancun wasn't even close to the Paradisus Playa Del Carmen experience, I'll explain.

At first glance the Cancun resort was huge with an impressive 9 story opened lobby lined with gift shops and attractive looking restaurants.  
The rear of the hotel looked out to a beautiful beach and blue water.  There were large pool areas, a swim up bar area adults and an area for young children.  The rooms were not large but clean and updated. 

So far so good. At first glance we were feeling pretty good.  

As we got settled we realized there was no a-la-cart menu lunch service.  The lunches were all buffet style, dried out chicken and hot dogs and over done burgers.  Immediately I was missing my fish sandwich that I was served in Paradisus Playa Del Carmen(PDC).

We immediately rented a Bali bed which had a great ocean and pool view for ~$100/day that included a pretty nice shrimp and lobster tray and a little extra waitress attention.  After doing so we figured out that menu service came with the Bali bed rental as well.  We were excited until we ordered off the menu and received dried out food.  Still no fish sandwich.  Lunch was a bust.

The dinner restaurants looked great and they even had the same names as the Paradisus in PDC but they were not even close in quality and lacked the luxury feel and service you got in PDC.  By the end of the week we were not even excited to go to dinner.  The restaurants lacked quality and luxury.  My dirty martini had green olives with PITS, Really? 

The pool area had a great view but was showing its age.  The concrete around the pool was beat up, there were a few tiles missing from the swim up bar, and the poolside bathroom lacked ventilation.  One day two of our lounge chairs would not recline and it became obvious that they had broke and were fixed via bolting the reclining  mechanism, just very annoying.
The little kids(kid zone) was led by an attendant but I have three teens and there was no activity director getting teens/adults going.  In PDC Jonathon, the activities director, rallied up the teens/adults and played water polo for two hours every day.  Cancún lacked someone like Jonathan and his fun enthusiasm.  Furthermore, the entire pool was over 5 feet deep throughout which was annoying for those of us that aren't 6ft tall(especially when you are treading water with a drink in your hand).

This place just lacked the high end luxury that PDC had.  They fell short with so many little things. Maybe bc the hotel was much larger or maybe the typical Cancun crowd doesn't look for luxury service and food.  

We spoke to a few other vacationers there that previously went to Paradisus In the Punta Cana and they loved it, calling it much more luxurious with great service. (they were not thrilled with Cancun either).  

BTW we had cashed in some Melia rewards points for butler service. The butler botched more things than they got right.  What a waste!

All in all we paid up for butlers and Bali beds but even with that we weren't thrilled. We hunkered down everyday in our Bali bed relaxed and made the best of it.   

In closing, just before leaving for our vacation I read a startling review saying "don't be fooled by the beautiful lobby" now I see what they meant.  We had a great week of weather and laughs with the family so I can't complain but I do COMPARE.  Player Del Carmen out classed Cancun. 

(If you want to read my trip advisor review on  Paradisus PDC just google 
"where's the beach Paradisus")

reviews.author: Stacey J
reviews.title: Satisfied but may not go back to this specific location
reviews.text: The hotel is dated but the staff was extremely accommodating. I wish there were more activities during the day and the shows that were listed on the entertainment board were consistently wrong. Also the pool was too deep, I couldn't stand without being on my tippee toes (I'm 5'1")

reviews.author: jjloar
reviews.title: Family vacation
reviews.text: The hotel was beautiful and the food was good. However, on the second day, my wedding ring of 17 years was stolen from the room. Granted I did not have it in the safe, but I put it in a container with other belongings and put it under my clothes in the drawer; therefore, someone had to really be going through our belongings to find it.  My husband went to the manager, and they did nothing. They didn't even say they were sorry. Needless to say, it put a damper on our trip.

reviews.author: NCE
reviews.title: Don't visit the spa!   Stick to the buffets!  Call your handyman before you go!
reviews.text:
Expensive trip for our family of five with 3 rooms and continued problems.  We arrived late and the sink was stopped up and the electricity in our bedroom was not working.  We called maintenance and it took two trips for them to discover that yes,  the master switch was on but the circuit breaker was tripped.  Also, the electrical switches in the room are very confusing.
The next day we visited the spa and were treated rude and condescending by Nallely and cancelled 3 spa appointments.  It is really too expensive anyway for the treatments but it would have been a nice treat for my daughters.
The a la carte restaurants are really not very good.  They try to create international dishes and really don't quite get it in taste!  Stick to the simple buffets and check for the warm food.  Lots of food in the buffet but temps are really not maintained very well.
My husband really dislikes buffets so we go and make his plates and pretend to be his waitresses after we try and eat at the other restaurants!
I have written many comments before on the Paradisus house wine selections as I have stayed at other Paradisus resorts but I guess they don't listen.  The house wine included in the all inclusive sucks!  And I mean it is really bad.  It probably cost $2 a bottle.  We instead purchase the overpriced wine on the menu and pay $100 for a $30 bottle of wine.  They serve top shelf liquors but the wine is horrible.  
Our one dinner which was enjoyable was at Enso and Edwin, Carlos and Alonso were outstanding!!!!  Also, Eddie, one of our beach waiters was fabulous!  The waiters do their best serving you and overall the service is great with what they have to work with! And of course, the beach is fabulous!!!!  Beautiful!!!!  Cancun is nice but resort is not as nice as other Paradisus that I have stayed at.

reviews.author: HeatherL1674
reviews.title: It was average
reviews.text:
We stayed at Paradisus last July. My husband, My 13 yr old daughter and myself. I had researched a lot hotels that resulted in choosing Paradisus. It seems the newer and more modern hotels are mostly Adult-Only, so our choices were limited. We didnt want to stay at a family resort with a bunch of young kids running around either. 

Overall, the hotel is nice, its just a little dated. Its unique in its architectural features that are reminiscent of mayan pyramids. The rooms are nice and updated and fabulous view of the ocean if you choose that. I would definitely recommend to upgrade to ocean view. 

Restaurants are ok, which is to be expected of an AI resort. The ceviche buffet by the pool is delicious.

The pools are nice but deep and a bit too warm. I like my water warm but i think it was a bit too warm like close to 90 degrees.. so not refreshing at all. The ocean being beuatiful and inviting is a bit rough. Although I enjoyed the thatched umbrellas and scenery. 

Not much to do in the evening, the lounge has daily shows but they are kind of lame. It gets crowded too since theres not much else and its open for all ages. We ended up taking a taxi/bus to the local shopping La Isla Shopping Village. 

The resort is located midway between the north/south part of Cancun, you can easily hop on the bus at the entrance to the resort. It wasnt scary at all, and a lot cheaper then taxi. We actually took the bus to the ferry to Isla Mejeures which is on the north end of Cancun, that saved alot in taxi fees. 

Some excursions and activities I recommend. 
Take the ferry to Isla Mejeures and rent a golf cart. You can drive around the whole island in half a day, see the sights - gorgeous coastal views, stop at a beaches to swim or snorkel, and grab a bite to eat in town. Also, we did ziplining, Swim the cenotes, and 4 wheeling with Selvetica. Worth the trip if your looking for something to do, but skip the 4 wheeling unless its muddy b/c you just drive down dusty dirt roads, nothing exciting. 

One note - Check In and Check Out are little disorganized and long waiting.

reviews.author: claudia007-2017
reviews.title: Bad Customer Service for Members
reviews.text: Yes, I am one of those fools who bought a membership for Melia Hotels & Resorts. My experience with Paradisus Hotel is like this: you areprepaying for a service and once you get it ... they give you the minimum and they try to charge you for the minimum of extra for anything. I wanted my cousin to visit us at the hotel, maybe purchase a day pass or maybe get a little discount for being members. All I got from the Fabiola at the front desk for the member NO NO NO you need to pay a full pass. Instead of giving me options all I got was NO NO. I made my point clear to her and Carlos that according to the Hospitality classes you should not say NO to a guest but instead give options. I got out of there as fast as I could and went to the front desk for NON Members and I got treated better and they offered me different options to get my cousin and her family in to the hotel to visit. I AM REALLY DISAPPOINTED WITH THE SERVICE THEY OFFER TO MEMBERS AT PARADISUS CANCUN

reviews.author: Jkrob2013
reviews.title: Not for us ....
reviews.text:
Jan. 21st 2017 -2 weeks.
Hotel lovely, staff very pleasant and food first class.  
Swimming pool freezing, and sea very fierce!
Upgraded Hotel suite in Pyramid 3  -  FAR TOO NOISEY, day and until very, very late!!! 
Poolside FAR TOO NOISEY 
No where quiet to relax and rest !!!

reviews.author: johnsU9749XA
reviews.title: Not really 5 stars
reviews.text: Pleasant enough stay but little things like jacuzzi not working and room furniture not really 5 star quality compared to other hotels.  Annoying loud DJ music on the beach also spoilt the beach experience.

reviews.author: I3353CMandreaw
reviews.title: Stay Was Fine
reviews.text:
Requested a quiet room. Check in clerk gave us a room next to the construction next door.Also, the room was so terrible, it should have been detonated. Dank and unremodeled with a sofabed whose springs almost poked through the mattress cover. The second room was great but the AC wasn't working. Required several calls over two days to fix. Food was lousy. Stick with the buffet and you might be able to pick through and find something, but the sit down was scary (think pre-prepared tepid food just waiting for a food-borne illness to happen). The hamburgers at the grill were unidentified meat (worse than Mc Donalds). Lack of lounge chairs almost forces you to get the cabanas to the tune of $125+ per day. Never experienced anything like it.
Ask for a room in section 2 or 3 and away from the disco. Beds were comfy, bathroom really nice, clean room (It's a miracle they can clean up all of that sand) and minibar well stocked.

reviews.author: carolnyc2003
reviews.title: Singles vacation
reviews.text:
I was at this property last week for five days.  The rooms were quite dated but clean. We had a room overlooking the lagoon which is basically the parking lot so beware.

We upgraded our service which was worth it, especially for the "all" adult pool.  To the families looking to book here, there is a family/kid pool so not sure why you all insist on staying at the main pool (sans bar).  This in itself was worth the additional $80 p/day. 

Restaurants- It was difficult to get reservations but the older crowd seemed more concerned with this issue. Mole got the best reviews and it was just average in our taste. There were men singing and playing instruments throughout the meal and it was 
really annoying. I understand they want to give you the whole dining experience but 
dinner doesn't need to be almost two hours with loud entertainment. 

The buffet for breakfast was great and by far our favorite meal of the day. We didn't notice the activities board until three days in when we walked by the party pool. We wanted to take yoga but didn't get a daily pamphlet or notification when classes would be. I would say it would be helpful to slip under people's doors like most resorts do. 

Beach/Pool ~ Difficult to find chairs. I get that everyone wants a seat so they leave their towels while they eat or dos whatever, but if a waiter notices unoccupied chairs for hours they should give the chairs to someone else.

Staff- Very friendly and tips go a long way, especially at the beach/pool.

I was in Cancun this past November and it's by far worth it to pay more money for a nicer property, like Secrets the Vine.

reviews.author: Lauren B
reviews.title: An AVERAGE at best hotel.  Not a 4-5 star by any means!
reviews.text:
Our experience started off poorly.  We booked our reservations then 2 weeks later it went down $500 a room, they wouldn't credit us the difference or work with us. We repeatedly contacted them and were ignored us every time.  Don't bother trying to contact the hotel directly or Melia customer service. I called the hotel and asked to speak to a front desk manager and was told they "didn't have one".  I asked if this is the poor service that we can expect upon arrival, he responded with a "Yes".  

THIS IS NOT A 4 or 5 STAR HOTEL...DON'T BE FOOLED.  The $1500 resort credits are a complete joke.  

Let's start off with the hotel rooms:  we had 2 double/double rooms.  Beds are truly double sized beds, not queens, and were comfortable.  We asked for adjoining rooms since we were traveling with kids, did not get it. DO NOT use the pull out couch, absolutely disgusting!  The furniture is old, stained and beat up, doors to patio and bathroom were missing handles.  Caution with bathrooms - there's a step to enter, tub is at a higher level then the floor and the door to the toilet can't be opened or shut unless the door to the bathroom is closed.  You need to request daily to have your refrigerator refreshed.  The last day we were there the air conditioning was barely working.  Two days with no hot water for showers!

Restaurants:  If you don't make your reservations 24 hours in advance enjoy eating at 9:30-10pm or be subject to the buffet AGAIN.  Service is extremely slow as well.  We walked out of 2 of the restaurants because food was so bad at one and too slow at the other.  You cannot walk in the restaurants without a reservation either.  There was a buffet at the pool a few nights.  We thought it was for private events but turned out to be for hotel guests.  Overall the food was okay...some restaurants better than others, that's to be expected in our eyes.

Hotel:  TIRED!  Needs a major renovation.  ALL the lobby and lounge furniture is worn and torn.  The hanging plants cause a mildew/musty smell so they over compensate with overwhelming air freshener machines all over the hotel - migraine central.  

The staff was very nice and accommodating.  Make sure you find Oscar in the check in area...he'll take great care of you.  The pool and beach were very nice, location is nice, public transportation ($1) was a great way to get to the shopping areas.  There was entertainment at the pool but only on the weekend and the nightly entertainment in the lobby lounge was nicely done.  

We enjoyed our vacation, not because of the hotel but rather cause we made the best out of it.  Would not go back, would not recommend staying at this hotel and will never stay at a Melia property again.

reviews.author: Brooklynite_Abroad
reviews.title: This places is improving, but slowly
reviews.text:
The setting:  You are 20 minutes by car/shuttle from the airport.  This is a rebranded Gran Melia, now a Paradisus.  This, however, is not at all like a Paradisus you may have visited in the DR or even Playa del Carmen.  This is a spacious complex but one without the modernity of a Paradisus resort.  The main lobby is located in the middle pyramid, which is the third pyramid to be exact.  The lobby opens into an incredible, large space with hanging plants everywhere.  It’s calm and soothing to enter the hotel.  Complimentary parking valet will take your keys upon arrival.  Check-in is tastefully handled to the left of the lobby in a glass enclosed area, with plenty of seating.  Check-out can be done at the regular reception counter, to the right of the entrance.  If you are a Club Melia member, like I am, your lobby and check-in is done in Pyramid 1, which is similar to Pyramid 3, but smaller in scale.
The room:  Whatever you do, make sure you spring for a sea view room.  Cancun’s beach is incredibly beautiful, and the water is many shades of blue.  Having this view is definitely worth it.  Your alternative is the back view of the hotel, towards the inland lagoon.  Looking out at the parking lot and lawns, rather than the beach and sea is a drastically different experience.  Our first room was a master one-bedroom that faced the parking lot, room 1312.  It lacked a Jacuzzi on the balcony, and even a mirror above the vanity in the bathroom.  After some persistent and bitter complaining, and although we were initially told nothing was available, we were allowed to switch to a ground level master one-bedroom, with a sea view.  This Club Melia room had a living room and kitchen, with its own full bathroom and a balcony with a Jacuzzi.  The bedroom with a plush king size bed was its own room and also came with a full bathroom.  Both the living room and bedroom had large, flat screen TV and the Wi-Fi worked great.  The kitchen has an electric range and microwave, a small fridge, a coffee maker and basic utensils.  There was a safe in the closet off the kitchen.  The shower in the bathroom off the bedroom had good water pressure, but the rain shower head was attached to the wall and not hung from the ceiling, defeating the purpose of the rain shower.
The grounds:  This is a large property, with Club Melia area at one end (Pyramid 1), and Royal Service/adults only area at the opposite end (Pyramid 5), and three pyramids of regular all-inclusive rooms in between.  There is a large pool in front of Pyramids 1-4, and a separate smaller pool at the Royal Service area.  The Royal Service area has better service than any other part of the hotel, separate a la carte breakfast and lunch restaurant, and a child free pool/beach area.  Unfortunately, the beach cabanas (Bali beds) are limited at Royal Service.  Although free to RS guests, there are only four cabanas that face the sea, and many more that face the pool, but these are booked up in advance, and are only available for two days of one’s stay.  Chances are, once you arrive, you won’t be able to land a cabana until a few days into your stay.  There are plenty of loungers by the pool and beach, many under thatch umbrellas.  There is now an exclusive beach club, Coco’s, in the middle of the beach at this hotel.  For $50/day you can rent a cabana at Coco’s.  Lastly, is the Club Melia beach area, which has been much improved.  I was surprised that I could rent a sea facing cabana at the Club Melia beach or pool for only $10/day.  The main area and Club Melia pools are loud with children and occasional drunk adults.  The beach was wonderfully peaceful, but beware, March is the windy cooler time of year in Cancun, which means big waves and dangerous conditions for enjoying the sea.
The food:  As we were part of Club Melia, we had the option to add an all-inclusive plan for $100/person/day.  We didn’t take advantage of this because we were without kids and wanted to enjoy the excellent restaurants that Cancun offers for dinner.  The breakfast buffet here is $25/person/day, and the lunch buffet is similar.  There was a large selection of Mexican and continental options at breakfast.  Although, all the food looked great it did not taste as good as it looked.  The same can be said of lunch.  For dinner we headed out to eat.
All in all, this is a good hotel, though slightly dated, with a wonderful beachfront.  Stay here if you get a good rate.  If possible, avoid the all-inclusive and go out to dinner as outside restaurants exceed the quality of the hotel’s restaurants.  Do not skimp on a sea view room, as the beach and sea are strikingly beautiful.  Lastly, this is much below the quality of other Paradisus resorts.  It's not comparable to the Paradisus resorts in Playa del Carmen or in Dominican Republic.

reviews.author: Mist24
reviews.title: Please do not mistake this for a five stars hotel
reviews.text: Omg I am so sorry to say but this place sucks!!! We checked in today and it's just heart breaking. The rooms are tiny, the first upgrade to another tiny room is $120 per new night. The buffet has hardly any options, not even pasta station. All the restaurants are booked and when I called to book for tomorrow they are also booked and you can't book for the following day. There rule is book only one day in advance. So I have to wake up at 7 am tomorrow to book a restaurant for the day after tomorrow . I can't imagine that we have to stay here for a week !!!! Based on other reviews I was really looking forward to this Vecation but this is so bellow our expectations.

reviews.author: Jose R
reviews.title: Staying Here Now: Family Vacation
reviews.text:
Staying here while writing this review.  This hotel has more negative than positive attributes:

We arrived early Saturday morning for a 7 day stay & our son had 102 fever.  The staff made us wait for hours for a room.  They would not give us a room unless we paid $80-$250 more per night for an upgrade & could care less that our son was ill & needed to take medication & go to bed.  

Not enough shade in children's pool area.  People place towels in the few shaded spots by 7-8 in the morning & than the resort forces you to pay $50 daily for Bali beds if you don't want to roast in the sun.

Same situation in the beach area.  Also, no staff to help you with chairs on the beach unless you pay more for the Royal service.  Difficult to do with children & all the things you have to carry with you.  The only way you get any service as a family with small children is if you pay $200 a night extra for the Family Concierge package.  I already paid $4000 for this stay to begin with.  I expected better service & compassion since we have 4 year old twins with us.

We're not foodies but the food is just ok.  However, we're not picky & have never found anything we thought was great.  The variety is excellent though.  We're not drinkers so I can't comment about the alcoholic beverages.

The staff at restaurants & bars are excellent.  As a whole, workers throughout the resort are very pleasant.  

I have traveled the world & have never been segregated in a hotel based on what I spent to stay there.  If you go into the Royal Service or Family Concierge area by accident, you're asked to leave instantly.  My wife took my children to the nearest bathroom by the beach & was asked to walk to the other side of the resort because it was the Royal Service bathroom.  Try explaining that to 4 year olds when they need to go to the bathroom right away.

I would never come back to this resort.  However, we have 5 days left & will make the best of it.

reviews.author: Sylvia C
reviews.title: Could have been better
reviews.text:
Please note that this is an older hotel. My husband and I had our wedding at the amazing Paradisus in Playa Del Carmen last year and were expecting the same quality. The initial check in was a pain as we asked to switch rooms; the first room was right by the central building and we could hear people and music going on in the atrium. The second room was very old and didn't feel the same so we just accepted it and went on with our vacation. 

The quality of the food was mediocre, nothing special from any of the restaurants here. The drinks, pool-side and beach-side servers were great!  The pool was too cold to enjoy as we visited in early February. The beach was FABULOUS, a little cold but nothing you can't get used to .

During our visit, the waters were too choppy and the red flags were out. Unfortunately, someone drowned one of the days were relaxing on the beach; please take caution!

All in all, either stay at a different hotel in Cancun that has a better value in price and experience or visit the Paradisus in Playa del Carmen.

reviews.author: H8447DLjulies
reviews.title: Spring Break with a Large Group
reviews.text: I was part of a Spring Break group of 14 moms & their daughters plus extra friends who were Seniors in high school. The Paradisus was what we expected for the price and location of an all-inclusive hotel in Cancun. The hotel was clean, the rooms spacious with nice views, and the property was nicely maintained. However, the food was just mediocre, especially the buffet breakfast and lunch grill. There's little kid-friendly food besides bread or rolls, and no cheddar cheese anywhere so "nachos" were a plate of thick tortilla chips with a scoop of pico de gallo and guacamole on top. It was difficult finding a single chair or group of chairs after 8:00am at the pool or beach....unless you upgrade to the Royal Service Side. We were never able to secure large group dinner reservations before 8:30pm at any of the restaurants, despite calling each day at 7:00am as recommended by the hotel. The beach was picturesque, but service was slow and there were people peddling their wares all day long. The chairs at both the pool and beach were extremely uncomfortable, and there weren't enough chairs (although there was enough space) for peak times when the hotel was at capacity. The drinks were very good - and Christian was an outstanding waiter for our group of moms who would stay by the pool while the girls spent the day on the beach. I personally would choose a more upscale, non-all inclusive hotel if I travel to Cancun in the future.

reviews.author: KellyBurgATX
reviews.title: Nice But Needs Some Work
reviews.text:
We had an amazing time, the service was impeccable and the grounds are nice.  We stayed in a regular room.  Our friends upgraded to the Royal Service.  Their room had been updated and was more modern.  

Pros:
-Lots of restaurants to choose from
-Beautiful beach and view of beach from pool
-Not stingy with pool towels - no keeping up with a towel card!
-Service was top notch
-Pool side entertainment was good
-Pool snack bar had pretty good food for a snack bar
-The service with the poolside cabanas was awesome and came with a better food menu
-The onsite nightclub is fun and kept us from going downtown (saved money!)

Cons:  
-The main pool is too deep - I'm 5'4" and had to stand on my very, very tippy toes to keep my head above water - not ideal for hangin out in the water or standing around drinking in the pool (it is shallower at the pool bar, just too deep in the rest of the pool)
-My room had bugs
-The pool tiles needs some repairs
-The evening entertainment started too early.  They should have 2 showings.  You need to go to dinner pretty early to see the show.  Our dinner reservations were at 8pm each night and we always missed the show
-The check in and out line SUCKED!  Everyone was trying to check in and out at the same time and it was slow and hot and frustrating
-While the menu with the pool cabanas was more expansive, my chicken tenders came out raw - GROSS!
-My favorite meal was lunch in the Taco restaurant.

reviews.author: Julian F
reviews.text:
We just came back from a 6 night stay at this hotel. 
Pros:absolutely amazing property. Rooms are clean and spacious. Upgrade to ocean view. The view is amazing

Con:One of the staff Alex you guys need to be aware of him. First when we checked in he was like meet me tomorrow and we will go over dinner reservations etc. we told him we need help getting a cake for our son's birthday and balloons in the room. He took the information and promise he will help us out. Alex did not help with the cake because we didn't go to the timeshare presentations. We took a cab and went to Walmart. Beware of ALEX, he is a con and a horrible staff. Another weird thing that happens on Saturday march 11th the entire phone system was down in the hotel. However the phones at the front desk and concierge works. Another incident i have is that we miss the dinner reservations at market grill for our sons birthday by 30mins.
