They will actually follow you around while you are trying to go from place to place.  Stay clear when you see a staff member approaching you. 
The main buffet is decent.  Dinner there fair.  Breakfast and lunch are much better.  Make sure to make reservations for the other restaurants the night before because they book up quickly.  The pool is beautiful, and well maintained.  The swim up bar is a lot of fun and they offer kids non-alcoholic drinks, including milk shakes!!  The beach at Pardisus is nice but the water is very rough.  The shore is rocky so wear water shoes if you can.
The rooms are in need of updates.  Make sure your safe and electrical outlets are working!  Our room had faulty electrical outlets and safe.  Our bath tub was also clogged!  One day, when we came back to our room, we found an old paint brush which had not been there when we left.  That means a worker was in our room when we were out, and without our permission!  Wonder why?!
Finally, if you book this hotel on-line, double check your reservation!  We accidentally booked for 6 people even though there were only 5 of us.  I called the hotel manager and was told that they would not refund me.  When I arrived in Cancun, I was told I would not receive a refund.  So I asked for an upgrade to butler service and they said NO!  They are very quick to take your money but they will not give you a dime for anything!  
The only way to obtain resort credit is by attending one of their time share presentations.  My family and I went there to relax, not to attend a sales presentation or to be hawked by their staff!

reviews.author: Stephanie N
reviews.title: Hotel was good, but needs work
reviews.text:
Myself and my husband, along with our 2 kids (11 year old boy and 6 year old girl) stayed at Paradisus for 6 days. There were many things we really enjoyed at the hotel, but a few things that were disappointing. 

Pros
-the staff members were really friendly
-the food was very fresh and there was a really good selection
-great beach and pools
-quick and easy check-in and check-out

Cons
-we paid for an oceanview room, but we didn't get one because there were no chairs on our balcony until the last 2 days after many requests - we only enjoyed the view if we stood outside
-other balconies had 2 chairs and a table
-the family concierge told me that a supervisor would contact me, but that didn't happen
-the t-shirts for the kids were really small (even for our 6 year old)
-a lot of tiles are cracking - definitely needs updating

Overall, our vacation was good but we I think we would try another hotel if we go back.

reviews.author: Anna S
reviews.title: Could've been better
reviews.text: This is our second time to Cancun. The first time we stayed at an adults only resort, Secrets The Vine, which we absolutely loved. We wanted to bring our 15 year old son for his birthday and for Spring Break so we picked Paradisus based on some the reviews. We had a basic ocean view room in tower 3 on floor 5. It was actually perfect, close enough to the restaurants, but far away from the noise. The view was the best, although you had to stand up due to the plant bed. Room was clean and comfortable, AC worked fine. Safe didn't work, but maintenance was able to fix it right away. And we had to call for housekeeping because they didn't clean room for 2 days. The grounds overall was nice, but it was so humid. And there were towels and leaks everywhere. Loved the beach and the huts even though it was a battle every day to get chairs. Laura was the best server! The buffets were not good. Breakfast was ok, but after the 2nd day, it was getting redundant. Enso was ok. But the Market Grill for dinner was the best! We really enjoyed it and they even sang happy birthday to my son. Lunch was fine, we mainly ate the taco bar and sunset grill at the pool. If you do not have kids, I would highly suggest an adults only resort. Entertainment was ok, but short. My teenager was bored. The location was great, we took cabs to the mall and walked across the street to Aquaworld. Overall, we had a good trip, but the resort definitely needs some improvement.

reviews.author: mustafa
reviews.title: Nice hotel and location, disappointing service at times.
reviews.text: The Paradisus Hotel is quite nice with nice pool and beach. The service pool side and in restaurants is nice. The food was generally quite good. The service was not as expected and the beds in the room were uncomfortable.

reviews.author: 296leighc
reviews.title: Don't look up!!
reviews.text: Food was good.   Gluten free options available which was very nice.   Most of the staff was very nice.  The building is old and needs a major renovation.  Everything is cracking and leaking.   Our room had an electrical issue and the power kept going out.   There is no night life at this resort!!  Not a lot of activities during the day either.

reviews.author: Mary A
reviews.title: STAY AWAY!!  Go somewhere else...
reviews.text: I have never written a review before but I felt compelled to now because of the horrible experience we had at this hotel.  My family of 5 just returned yesterday from Paradisus.  I wanted to hopefully save someone else from booking here and having the same terrible experience. I chose this hotel based on the good reviews and I am shocked anyone would enjoy this place.  First of all, the min you walk in the hotel they pressure you for the Time Share sales and if you don't want to sign up you basically get treated like a second class citizen.  Secondly, the food was terrible!  There are several restaurants on the property but good luck at getting a reservation.  Ever day we called for a reservation and were told that they were booked.  The only time we could eat was at 10:00 or 10:30pm; unless we wanted to go to the nasty buffets.  Blue Agave is nothing more than a taco bar, Naos is typical buffet food that is terrible, Tapas was the worst I've ever eaten!!  Market Grill was the best out of all but it wasn't great.  The staff was less than helpful; there are LOTS of people around but they all tend to the new arrivals and appear to be focused on getting you to do the time share session.  This was our first all inclusive and what a disappointment.  I highly recommend looking for another resort if you are considering this one.

reviews.author: Zakato70
reviews.title: All Inclusive should not mean you have to sacrifice the basics
reviews.text:
I try to save writing a review for when I receive outstanding service, or when my experience was below my reasonable expectation.  In the case of the Paradisus Cancun, unfortunately my review will be because of the latter.  I have been to a Paradisus property in the past, and I feel that the quality of this one was below par, and I can not see myself spending the money to stay at this or any Melia resort again.  The bottom line is that for the money, you can get better.  If you're happy with average, and can get a discount, the Paradisus Cancun is for you.  Please note that we've traveled to Mexico many times, we all speak Spanish, and we LOVE Mexican hospitality.  It is second to none in the world.  

I reserved two rooms for my family of 5 as the maximum capacity is 4 people per room.  That's pretty standard, and for all of you who have more than 2 kids, you know the pain of having to get the second room.  We generally don't mind as we can put the kids in one room, and we try very hard for an adjoining room.  

Again, most hotels can not guarantee an adjoining room, but when you are traveling as a family, have 5 people in your group, and your youngest is 10, it would seem assigning  adjoining rooms would be a priority.  

When we arrived, not only did we not get adjoining rooms, but we had rooms that were several doors apart.  I was quite disappointed.  Apparently there is NOTHING you can do to ensure adjoining rooms.  The person checking us in worked extremely hard to find us two rooms that were at least next to one another, and finally succeeded.  We didn't get adjoining rooms, but I really appreciated her trying as hard as she did.  For the benefit of having our kids in the room next door, my wife and I had to sacrifice a king bed for two twins.  Could have been worse, and we made the best of our tiny bed.  Soon after we got ready to go to our room, we passed another family with three little children, all under 10 who were in the same boat as we were, and pleading for the hotel to help them.  I felt terribly for them.  

We opted for the family concierge level room.  After almost four days here, I can't really figure out what advantage this extra cost brings.  We had wine and cheese delivered to the room a few times (again this is an all inclusive property).  We were also assigned a "Mayordomo" or personal concierge whom we could call on a little phone they gave us.  He was helpful in getting us information for excursions, getting us restaurant reservations, and other little things.  He was very nice, but I can't really see needing this service if I were to come again.  A couple of times, we asked him to reserve cabanas for us (extra charge of between 100 and 185 dollars a day), and both times, we had to wait around until people figured out who were were, and why we were there.  I don't know whose fault that was, but it was a bit annoying.  I could have just gone up and picked a place on my own.

The other feature of the family concierge is a special family concierge room that has a few snacks and some candies available throughout the day.  Since this is an all inclusive resort, the fact that there is a bar and more drinks, seems like a benefit for the few.  If you have very small children, there is a romper room and a place for an exhausted mom or dad to let their kids run around, so I can see that being a bonus.  There are also video came consoles there for those kids that don't want to go to the pool, beach, or hang out in their rooms.

We had ocean view rooms, and I must say the views did not disappoint.  Make sure to request higher floors, otherwise, you could be staring at people by the pool, and the tops of trees.  We were on the second floor, and that was barely enough.  The size of the rooms were nice, and they were mostly clean.  I say mostly, because our bedding was gross (stains on the duvet) and many of the fresh towels (they are white) had stains on them as well.  I feel like a good dose of OxyClean or Chlorine would have solved that issue.  The dirty sheets and towel issue was a harbinger of things to come.

The most glaring and unbelievable problem at this resort was the utter lack of clean towels available for the guests at the pools and beach.  When I say a lack, I mean there were hours throughout the day, when there were no clean towels to hand out.  The hotel does not even take the responsibility to have hotel staff stand in the towel hut to tell people there are no towels.  Instead, there is a person from a separate company that sells tours, and uses the same hut, who has to notify all the wet guests looking for towels that there are none available.  I spoke with several staff members, and they confided in me that the hotel is aware of the problem, but they are unable to address the issue quickly enough.  It is plain to see that management is unwilling to purchase more towels.  They may have enough for off-season capacity, but during Spring Break there are literally hundreds of guests who have to wait up to an hour to get a towel to use at the pool or beach.  When the clean towels did show up, they were piled into a large mountain in the back of the hut, and handed to the guests without being folded and moist in many cases.  There was no staff to help.  The lady selling tours would hand out towels.  She tried to fold them in some cases, but there was too much demand so she gave up.  It was so surreal and unnecessary for the Paradisus to show such a lack of class on such a simple issue.  As someone who has worked in a service based industry, I couldn't fathom such a glaring issue.

Food.  Food.  Food.  I'm happy eating at a cheap buffet or France's finest restaurants, but the food at this resort left me longing for anything better.  The daily buffet for breakfast was good, but the dinner at the buffet was below average.  Also, the special restaurants including the Japanese, Brazilian, Asian/Fusion, and the Latin one were simply not that good.  I have  very open mind and an accepting palate, but the dishes were uninspired.  The meats were overcooked, and because of the humid temperature, everything became soggy in a matter of minutes (think seaweed on sushi rolls that chewy).  Even a simple order of nachos showed up at my room without the cheese.  At the Asian restaurant we ordered pork Gyoza and the waiter served us shrimp Gyoza.  We asked about the pork ones we ordered and he tried to insist that no such item existed.  We showed it to him on the menu, and then he explained they were out.  They tried to serve us "Nan" as in Indian bread, and it was just an overcooked pita bread.  I could literally write a book on how average/disappointing the food was.  I can pretty much guarantee that given a choice, most of the staff that works at this resort would rather eat at home or a local restaurant than the foods served here.

Finally, let me talk about the service and the staff.  The service at this hotel is what kept this review from being a two star review.  The employees of this hotel make the best with what they have.  That is simply the truth.  They work so hard to make the experience great.  Almost all of the wait staff was super helpful and respectful.  As I mentioned, we speak some Spanish, and that was appreciated, but almost everyone could speak a little English as well.  The housekeeping staff was terrific, and the people taking care of the resort were awesome.  Everyone greeted us with a smile, and a hand on their chest.  It was a great touch.  I love the spirit of hospitality that I feel every time I visit Mexico.  I was not disappointed by the great staff at the Paradisus Cancun.

Maybe I was expecting more, and I shouldn't have.  Overall, I can't recommend this resort to my friends and family, unless there are some changes in the food, the way the rooms are assigned to families with young children, and unless they can get their act together with their laundry.  I have a feeling that the dirty towels, lack of towels, and dirty linens are all somehow related.

Sorry Paradisus Cancun - thank you for sharing your wonderful staff with us, but management needs to know that short term gains will result in long term losses.

reviews.author: Candiebeninga
reviews.text: The hotel was extremely humid. Was uncomfortable when we ate at the restaurants. We mainly ate at the outdoor restaurant to stay cool. The service was wonderful. Ceaser was the best waiter ever!!!!:))

reviews.author: C C
reviews.title: Older Hotel needs face lift
reviews.text:
Overall experience was OK - the hotel looks good in the main areas but the rooms are small and dated needing upgrading badly, Avoid rooms that overlook the center area where restaurants and LOUD shows occur every night till late at night.
The food was ok most seafood was not fresh and most of the restaurants while not full seemt struggle to keep with flow of people. A few exceptions of good service the majority of staff while pleasant was also very slow and often taking way too long to do basic tasks.
the beach was very nice and the people serving the pool and beach area were very good.  Overall must say way overpriced for what you get.
Just a last comment nowadays good wifi is a necessity and I must say the internet service was atrocious.

reviews.author: Al K
reviews.title: A four day nightmare -- but great staff
reviews.text:
This was a family holiday with our children and grandchildren. We have also been long standing members of their vacation club. The hotel has deteriorated over the years --in its ambiance and the quality of some of its guests -- as it has changed its business model from a classy Gran Melia to an all-inclusive Paradisus. We had booked our rooms and vacation about four months in advance. It was a "guaranteed" booking backed by credit card etc. After the first week we were told that we were going to be moved to a different hotel ( in our best interest apparently) for four nights as the hotel was fully booked for a convention attended by siding and window salesmen from the US !! We refused to move -- with young children ( 4 & 2 years in age) --and six adults. We lived through days of uncertainty not knowing whether our stance was going to work. It did--but we had to change rooms several times--and lived through a nightmare of Donald Trump followers--heavy duty drunks and parties with blaring music and doors banging until the wee hours of the morning.
To make matters worse the dining areas and restaurants were packed to the brim --and had to be expanded over to the atrium is with the fish ponds. As a result, we were squeezed dangerously such that some of the chairs and tables were placed dangerously at the edge of the ponds; resulting in my fall backwards and injury to my skull--six stitches. Not once did any of the hotel management inquire about my wellbeing nor any apology was ever given. I talked to my attorney about it and he said good luck –in Mexico !! They are a money making machine with really no regard for their guests. They rely on the adage "there is always another sucker around the corner". After almost 16 visits to Cancun I will move forward to some other hotel and location. We were not on some cheap package--we spent a lot of money for a family vacation--it was a damn disaster. Too bad they have some wonderful staff --if only their management could learn from the real people who slog during the day – as the management guys stay cool in the air conditioned rooms!! If you are a party animal –do visit the hotel. It is your scene. If you are a family or a couple wanting a classy holiday—save yourself. Don’t go.

reviews.author: NatashaKanji
reviews.title: Incredible staff, but poor management
reviews.text:
If you're planning to go during Christmas break, make sure they don't have any conventions going on at the same time. The management tried to kick us out of the hotel and then when we refused to leave, we spent almost a week of our vacation room hopping to meet the demands of their convention guests. This convention took over the entire hotel (imagine loud heavy techno bass music blaring into your ears through your pillow at 3 am type takeover). 

BUT the staff were AMAZING! Once the convention was gone, it was back to a peaceful, family-friendly environment, and we really valued the care of the staff, especially Anores Contreras at Nespresso wanting to make sure we had the best coffees every morning, Martin Sanchez at the restaurant who took care of us every morning and afternoon for breakfast and lunch, and always made sure we had a wonderful experience, and Juan Jorge Garcia Soto at the pool who made sure we always had our cabana. Thank you all sooooo much!

reviews.author: HollisterRanchGirl
reviews.title: Nice hotel but not 5* service
reviews.text:
We were a family of nine and had 3 rooms at the Club Melia (timeshare) side of the hotel.  The hotel is huge and generally clean, but lacks a certain charm.  Felt very sterile in places and showroom-like.  There are some areas that look like they are unfinished (like maybe they are trying for minimalistic zen garden but felt like a corporate apartment) and others are really beautiful and well-done.

THE STAFF was usually really nice and helpful; some wait staff were superb including all of those we encountered at the breakfast buffet and at lunch at Market Grill.  Ordering drinks from the pool near Club Melia was easy and consistent (tipping helps).  We inquired with guest services about a spa menu and were told that they couldn't provide because they changed the prices and we had to walk to the other end of the hotel to get it (no offer to bring us one); another desk printed it out for us.  

THE FOOD was decent at most places.  The breakfast buffet was standard breakfast buffet.  Lots of options from an omelet bar to churros; nothing tasted amazing but it was all okay.  At busy times the line for made-to-order eggs took 10+ minutes so best to get there early if possible.  Fuego and Vento were fantastic, Market Grill, Enso & Bana were good and I didn't care for Mole.  We noticed that many restaurants didn't give us menus and just brought out a tasting of everything; this may have been because we were a large group of nine.  We were were very diligent on making reservations early so we could sit together (even booking with the hotel for the 1st 2 nights before we arrived).  One night we wanted to go to Blue Agave and they do not take reservations.  We took the extra precaution of calling Guest Services to make sure they could take a group of 9 w/o reservation and they said we would be fine.  We showed up and there was a sign out front that Blue Agave was closed that night and the next.  There were other groups milling about and scrambling to make other arrangements so it appeared to be a surprise to many.  We were never notified of the temporary closure and at the very least we should have been told when we called Guest Services.  After trying to squeeze into a restaurant, we were turned away and ended up having to eat at the buffet which we did NOT want to do.

THE DRINKS were consistently inconsistent.  Sometimes you'd get a fantastic, well-made mojito and sometimes it'd be sickly sweet.   

THE ROOM was clean and spacious.  We stayed in three rooms in the Club Melia, Pyramid 1.  Two of our rooms were the 1-bedroom suites, which was actually a sliding room divider in one large room; our room was a studio.  Strange to have a stovetop and full set of dishes at an all-inclusive resort, but that may be helpful to some.  The refrigerator was very loud and turned on throughout the night.  There was a jacuzzi tub on the patio, which would have been nice except we faced another set of rooms so we would have been in full view of others.  Two of the rooms faced a parking lot so also not a very romantic setting, but that was due to our room price point.  The pull out couch beds are extremely hard.  They offer mattress toppers upon request, which make them decent, but they ran out so my sisters had to sleep on very uncomfortable surfaces for most of the stay until the hotel got more.  We don't think they're made to sleep on without these toppers.  It would be nice if they supplied drying racks for swimsuits as there was nothing (not a pull out line in the shower, either).  We had to drape them over the chairs on the patio and as it was very humid or raining they never really dried.  The room setup was fine, but plugging in electronics was not easy (had to pull out bedside table and unplug lamp).  There was no signal on any of the TV channels, not that we wanted to watch much TV on our vacation, but it would have been nice to turn on the news for a bit.  

HOUSEKEEPING was usually decent although replenishing supplies in the room was very inconsistent.  One day we'd get 1 shampoo/conditioner/soap and another day we'd get 5 of each.  One day we'd get a lotion and for the next 4 days we'd get none.  Some days we'd get 2 towels each and others we'd get 1 and they took our bathmat and didn't replace it for 3 days, and so on.  The toiletries were Thierry Mugler, but honestly didn't seem better than any generic hotel stuff I'd used before.  On one occasion a soiled washcloth was set out as clean on the counter.  I threw it on the floor under the sink and when we got back after the "second cleaning" of the day, that same soiled washcloth was set back on the counter.  On the last day we paid hourly to stay until late afternoon as we had a 9pm flight and I was sick with the flu.  Despite putting out the do not disturb door hanger, housekeeping came in on me, waking me up, which was an annoyance.  

THE GROUNDS were nice and generally clean.  A lot of the air conditioners drip and throughout the trip we all ended sitting somewhere getting dripped on and having to move.  The common area near our rooms had some issue where the ceiling or wall was literally chipping off.  The bar area looks nice in the evening with the lights, but the seats are ripped in many areas and some pieces looked like they had literally fallen off the wall and just leaned there.  There was no jacuzzi at all at the hotel, which would have been really nice to have as the weather was a bit stormy at times.  It was warm out but the pool was really cold.  We rented a bali bed for the duration of the stay.  We didn't realize it, but it was right next to the kids pool so we had to put up with annoying song/dance routines by the staff throughout the day.  We moved down the way and it was fine.  As it was stormy many nights/days, the bali bed was wet on some mornings as they didn't protect it during the night.

WIFI was free and ok most of the time, but it wasn't working in our first room.  There was a known issue and we were told to use "common areas" instead.  We had to put up somewhat of a fight to get our room changed to one that didn't have problems.  It was spotty in the other two rooms, but not much time was spent there so it wasn't a big issue.

ISSUES.  At 1:40am we were awoken to a stranger entering our room.  He quickly saw us and apologized, leaving but not stating who he was/why he was there.  The next morning we reported it to security and after investigating they found it was a staff member that had mistaken our room number.  Mistakes happen, we understand that, but the man should have notified someone so we didn't have to spend our morning dealing with security.  They weren't very apologetic and didn't seem to care much.  Same with when our key card stopped working (happened to my sister also).  We were told we had to go to reception (quite far away) and wait in a line to have it fixed.  They told us it was probably due to us holding it next to a phone.  If this is the case, they should inform people of this at check in.   

Overall a decent hotel, but it's not comparable to other 5*s we've stayed at (Shangri-La, Ritz-Carlton, Four Seasons are far superior in amenities, service and detail).  Lots of kinks to work out and consistency needs to be addressed.  Would recommend, but expect more of a 4* experience.

reviews.author: Bridget C
reviews.title: Nice but could use some updates
reviews.text:
The resort is nice but a few things are showing their age.  The brick pavers around the pools are starting to fall apart. I can't tell you how many times i tripped on them.  
The hotel hair dryer burnt my hair the first night we were there. I couldn't get any help from the manager on that night.  I wanted the hair dryer replaced (it was shooting out sparks) and asked for some conditioning cream for my hair from the salon.  I was told that they would just give me more conditioner that is already there. Not good enough. My hair was still falling out and my scalp was throbbing. Finally had the woman who was in charge of our group to go and get it straightened out. That next afternoon, I finally had a new hair dryer and a small container of conditioning oil.  The manager of the rooms, Abraham came to my room and apologized for the mishap. He said he wanted to make it up to me. I told him I didn't want it to happen to the next person who gets the room. I just wanted to condition my hair so it would stop falling out and help my scalp feel better and not peel. He offered me a free service at the salon, which was very nice but I didn't take him up on it because I wasn't looking for free stuff.  He was very nice and because of Abraham, I would come back. Knowing that someone was concerned for me and my well being, makes me happy. I only wish that the manager who I first spoke to could have been as accommodating. She never did any of the things she said she would do.  Anyway, enough of my story...
The food was pretty good. The service was great everywhere we were. They really hustled at the pools to get you drinks.  We brought a bunch of singles to leave as tips for the servers. The more you tip, the better service you get!  
The beach is beautiful! Water was great, warm and clean.
If you are looking for night life, this may not be the place for you. We found that for the week we were there, everything became very quiet after 9pm. Only one night club in Pyramid 3.

reviews.author: Julie H
reviews.title: Definitely not a 5 star
reviews.text: The resort is very tired and in definite need of a re-fresh.  The front door could not be locked, the bathrooms are needing a total refresh and just does not meet the quality standards we have experienced at other Melia resorts.  On the 2nd floor of the Royal Service tower as an example   (premium priced luxury - highest price class room), guests come out to the floor to see planter boxes full of dirt but no plants or flowers.   In the day we arrived jacuzzis did not work but later were operating but you could see the water level ring mark due to the decade of wear and use and poor maintenance.   Activities schedule was not accurate- wasted time showing up to a published activity we were excited about only to be told that the schedule was inaccurate and staff could not even confirm what was the rescheduled time (perhaps sometime between 6 and 7 pm but "we really can't say....").  Service was generally good to very good but not excellent, not in accordance with our experience at other Paradisus resorts such as La Esmeralda or Le Perla in the Rivera Maya area. I saw many royal service pool guests get up and walk to the bar to retrieve their own drink at the Royal Service pool because there is no swim up bar and there were long lapses between waiters coming around for what should have been an experience in stellar service.  Food quality was best in the Royal service area which was only available for breakfast and lunch but mediocre in the other common areas and for dinner and service was extremely slow (2-3 hours in duration) in restaurants which purposely limit seating with advance reservations required.  While the nightly entertainment was very good the venue is extremely poor - poor visibility, uncomfortable, crowded, forced to cozy up with strangers etc ( not a Royal experience at all).   An actual show theater with individual chair seating should be put in place.  After the show is over at 830 pm there is absolutely zero entertainment -not good if you have teenagers who you would like to engage beyond the drinking experience that 7 or 8 bars have to offer .....Butler service benefit equated to an ability to secure a cabana (which is only guaranteed for 2 days of your stay ) and get restaurant reservations.   On the plus side the Royal Service liquor quality is very high and the view of the Caribbean Sea is absolutely gorgeous but I assume there must be other resorts along the coastline that offer equally great views as well as better overall service, consistent food quality and activities.   I have been a devoted repeat Paradisus customer in the past but may not return to Paradisus resorts and with certain will not return to the Paradisus Cancun resort.

reviews.author: Jamiejamie77
reviews.title: My moms birthday trip
reviews.text: I have stayed at several all inclusive resorts in Mexico and the carribean. Riu Palace, Sandals, Barcelo. It was my moms birthday trip. I wanted her to feel spoiled and amazed by a luxury resort. She had never stayed at an all inclusive or even been to Mexico. So I payed the extra money to upgrade to Royal Service and an ocean view room. I called ahead from the US the day before our trip to make sure we would have 2 beds and to request a dinner reservation on the night we arrived at Bana. I knew we could only make reservations once we were there so I didn't want to get stuck eating the buffet our first night. I told them on the phone we were celebrating my moms 60th birthday, I put in our reservation comments I was traveling with my mom for her 60th birthday, I told our butler it was my moms 60th birthday. It was not once recognized...Yay! We're finally here. Ummmm no. We were greeted and told we were Royal Service and escorted into a lounge to wait to be checked in by our butler. After no one acknowledged us for 30 minutes I said please just show us to our room- no it has to be the butler. An hour later and 5 more people to talk to we were shown to our room. The worst possible upgraded room in the hotel. With a king bed. On the 1st floor, right outside the Royal service concierge area. Really? Live music, a bar and buffet right outside our door. Our ocean view suite was clean but not a view to be paying extra for. Could we see the ocean yes. A view from the first floor was not what I had in mind. I was told the hotel was a capacity so we could switch rooms to the zero floor with 2 beds and no ocean view. Not a great option. Our butler was friendly and made us our dinner reservations but we never really saw him after our 1st day. The food at Bana was good, our service there was great. We had the breakfast buffet- lots of fresh choices. Mole was good also with great service. We were lucky to get a Bali bed on Saturday because it rained. Our server out there was nice but kept forgetting our drinks so I had to go to the bar anyways. The ocean is breathtaking. The pool was not heated and there is no jacuzzi on the entire property that is hot. Even in the spa. Very disappointing. Bubbly pools of cold water- hmmmm? We ate at the market grill our last night, really good and great service there as well. The other problem here is the nightly entertainment. The entertainers are amazing and really talented but the venue it awful. They threw a show in a lounge bar on a tiny stage for hundreds of people to watch. Only about 25 could sit down and have a view. I booked this hotel because of the reviews the food, Royal service and entertainment. My mom doesn't drink so I thought she'd love the shows at night. She would have if we didn't have to stand up among all the other guests josteling for position to catch a view of a dancer or singer. I'm turning 40 in January and was using this trip for my moms 60th to check out this property for my upcoming trip with friends and family. We won't be back- I am really disappointed in this hotel. Our servers were all so friendly and nice but the management system needs lots of work. The check in process was infuriating and ridiculous. Not a great first impression. And our room and the cold pools and entertainment situation didn't leave a great last impression either.

reviews.author: jchoi104
reviews.title: The Good, The Bad, and the Ugly (Missing/stolen items)
reviews.text:
First the good - The hotel itself is pretty nice. Open layout, big but not too huge that you need transportation to get around. You can pretty much walk from one end to the other in about 7 - 10 min. We had an oceanfront suite, which was not really a suite. Just 2 full sized beds in a smallish room with a balcony. The oceanfront view was really nice though, not a fake oceanfront where you have to peer around a corner to get a glimpse of the ocean. 

The breakfast and lunch buffets had a lot of options. Loved the fresh juices for breakfast - they had green, orange, melon, grapefruit, etc. They also had a smoothie bar. Lots of fresh fruit, an omelette station, smoked salmon, cold cuts, etc. The service was pretty good. Nice waitstaff. 

The kiddie pool was great for our 2 small kids. Hint - a lot of people get up early and reserve pool chairs by putting towels and some personal items on there so if you get there after 10 or 11, no chairs for you. 

Now the bad - The dinner restaurants were mediocre. We ate at the Asian Fusion one on our first night. It was pretty bad. I'd rather eat take out chinese food than what they served us. I guess they took the word fusion and applied it literally. We had dumplings, fried rice, shrimp noodle salad, chicken tikka masala and some crispy naan. It was like they fused all the Asian foods and served them in one meal...weird. The 2nd night we ate at the tapas restaurant which was decent but not anything to write home about. The 3rd night, we ate at the Japanese place which was pretty good. Definitely the best out of all of them. The sushi and sashimi were average but their seafood salad and seared tuna were pretty good. The 4th night, we ate at the Mole, the Mexican restaurant. Again average but their tamarind margarita was really yummy. Definitely something to try. 

Now for the ugly - There are THIEVES in the hotel!!! After getting off the shuttle, the bellhop took our bags to be brought up to our rooms. Now, I guess this is partially my fault for not paying attention, but my husband gave him our backpack with my personal belongings. But we were tired, had 2 cranky kids with us and all we wanted to do was check in and relax. The check in process took really long, about 45 min. After we were done, we got showed to our room but our bags still werent there. We were told it would be up shortly. After it arrived about 10 min later, I looked through my backpack for my phone and couldn't find it anywhere. I was CERTAIN I had put it in there before getting off the plane. Still, I guess there was a miniscule chance that it may have fallen out or something so I didn't complain. I did ask the hotel if they had found a phone with my description but they said they hadn't. I let it go for the remainder of the trip. On our last day, my husband was cleaning out our safe and discovered a $100 bill MISSING. I know it was there because I had seen two $100 bills in there a couple of days before and there was no way either of us used it. So there, now we were missing a phone from my bag and a $100 bill from the safe.  This time, we definitely complained to the concierge upon checking out but all they said was to fill out a form, which we declined to because we were leaving and it would probably do nothing anyway.

So overall, the hotel was nice, very nice service, mediocre food, and thieves in the hotel.

reviews.author: Lynn M
reviews.title: Beautiful but not 5 stars
reviews.text: My overall impression of this resort is beautiful and well kept but not 5 stars. The staff is very friendly and there was always someone there when you needed something and they aren't "in your face". Our room was large and spotless. There was a nice variety of food in the restaurants. However, there were enough little annoyances that made me give the resort only 3 stars. Our room in pyramid three was very humid which I assume is because it was on the ground floor. Our clothes, the bedding and the towels always felt slightly damp. The hair dryer only worked on low. Several of the nights we spent there, we had no washcloths. The food was ok but nothing special. The one exception was the Japanese restaurant, Bana. It was excellent and we had a lot of fun trying all the different kinds of sushi. The pools are clean and attractive and the beach of course is awesome. However, there were too many cabanas that you had to reserve and not enough regular lounge chairs. It's kind of disappointing when you just want to sit in the sun and there are no chairs. We had a wonderful time because we wanted to get away and spend time together. But unfortunately I would not go back to this resort.

reviews.author: Sdccowen
reviews.title: Never mind your blow drier...bring your own robe if going to the spa bc one size does not fit all
reviews.text: If you have never been to an all inclusive, you would probably give this place a 5 but we have been to all inclusives in Riviera Maya, Cabo San Lucas and Puerto Vallarta before that far exceed this place. The hotel is huge (really too big)! The breakfast and lunch buffets both inside (Naos and Bana) and out were both cold (sausage, French fries, hot dog, pizza, etc.)...there were very few things at breakfast or lunch that I would consider good bc most was cold. By the time we left , I longed for a hot meal. We did have a good dinner at Vento (tapas) but they brought out things so fast that you couldn't enjoy the experience of trying new stuff. The same at Enso and the Market Street Grille. The rooms and bathrooms are ok (standard room) but we have had bigger/better/nicer elsewhere. They have huge balconies on the rooms but nothing else on them (no chairs or tables; you have to ask for chairs). The spa is ok. Again we have been to nicer ones. Not all the jets work in the spa pool. The room with the couples spa pool is not very appealing (black walls and panes above beds with either paint or bird poop on them). The robes at the spa are small. I put on mine and thought that, having been to other spas were you normally have to roll up the sleeves. The men's robes were REALLY small for the average American male. You have to make reservations to eat at most places but you cannot do it more than 1 day in advance and before 11 am. Their computer system cannot accommodate earlier and if you wait until after 11 am the day before, you are unlikely to get into most places. The ocean was rough. The pool on the right is not heated and if you want a drink before 11 am at the pool you have to go get it yourself. If you like sushi/sashimi you probably will like Bana. I did not, the wait staff there at dinner was the most friendly and funny!!! The red lounge (disco) is awesome if for no other reason then to people watch!! They played great music!! We watched part of a show in the Avenue Bar...could not see well...for a place this big they show have a big enough area to have chairs out front so all could see. It rained the day before we left and many rooms, hallways and stairways had towels thrown on them that were still there the next day.

reviews.author: James l
reviews.title: An English review
reviews.text:
If your into faceless hotels with no continuity of staff or service then this is for you. The ocean view junior suite with club room benefits is a Virgin holidays upgrade and  only worth it for the service on the beach and the room. Be aware that because of your different band it allows a constant sell by Club Melia reps to target you every day. We were targeted the moment we checked in by a Club Melia rep who while giving us information about the hotel (made it over complicated about moving around the hotel) wanted us to sign up to a Club Melia upgrade over a hard sell breakfast of 90 minutes which we avoided. You are then targeted throughout your holiday by reps looking to upgrade you. 

Ok the hotel is pretty impressive but is too big to have any atmosphere. Trying to book your restaurant for your evening meal is impossible for the same evening ( even thou you see empty tables ). The food for the masses restaurants where you don't have to book is rubbish and mostly cold. Even the Blue Agave Mexican restaurant is hit and miss especially with drinks and service. The Market grill is novel  but food not up to five star quality. 

The pools are cold as well as the jacuzzi even in the Royal service area ( the sea is warmer). To sum up, the hotel is showing its age and leaks everywhere when it rains. Hit and miss service and not 5 star quality food.

reviews.author: SILVIA G
reviews.title: The grounds are beautiful!! BUT....
reviews.text:
The room was not up to par for the price. The sofa in our room had large stains. I found a contact in my outdoor hot tub.  The furniture on the balcony was cheap & plastic. The room decor was not layed out well. 

The restaurants were inflexible when seating larger parties. We were there for a wedding and our groups were large and they were unwilling to sit us all together or add more people. 

You have to pay for the beds by the pools something that is standard in most other resorts.

reviews.author: DaveSC_7
reviews.title: Cancun vacation
reviews.text:
We stayed at paradises Royal service, comparing it with the paradises ponta Cana and Costa Rica was a little bit disappointing.
we arrived at 8.30 at night they checked us in without giving us a tour of the hotel and what we could expect from the Royal service also offered us water in champagne glass instead of a refreshing cocktail (seriously).
Our Butler didn't do much at all accept making restaurant reservation which we could have done it through the Royal service personnel ourselves, he did not offer us any suggestion as far as hotel amenities concern, for example we didn't know on Wednesday there was a sea food buffet or there is facility cross the street from the hotel that we could use for water sport activity and so on, he was a nice guy but obviously he wasn't trained that well.we still tipped him$100 for each couple because we know that without the tips they can't make a living with $5 a day. Royal service itself and all the staff from house keeping to the server and the cooks were fantastic and absolutely first-class worker.
our favorite was Alexandra he was at the Royal service bar at night and server at Royal service restaurant by the pool,also Valeria was amazing lady who served us lunch  every day at the Royal service restaurant.
The only restaurant for Royal service was opened for breakfast and lunch only and is located by the pool area, without a question that was the best eating place in  the entire resort, we tried all the restaurant for dinner, Brazilian restaurant was a joke all the meat was tuff, Thai restaurant was beautiful but food and service was awful, Mexican restaurant was better than the others with very limited menu and no traditional Mexican food, i must say I have been in restaurant business for 30 years and I know about food and service , in general they can improve  their restaurants and foods, I can't believe you couldn't find a fish taco or plenty of fish dishes in any of their restaurants.
Spa facility was great Angel at the reception was very helpful , Ana was my message therapist she was great and my wife had Lulu for therapist and she loved it. We also played golf 3 times and it was nicely maintained
Royal service beach is great but the ocean is always Rugh and it's not a snorkeling beach .

This is my suggestion for the management.

1- when your Royal service guest arriving treat them like royalty and have knowledgeable staff to greet them and show them around .
2-Royal service concierge should be smiling , happy and helpfull.
3-you should have one restaurant for Royal service guest for dinner time.
4- improve the quality of the food on all restaurants and have more seafood in all menus.
5-give more Training to Royal  service butler so they can service the  guests better.

reviews.author: Mike M
reviews.title: Nice place, but not the best
reviews.text:
This was our first visit to Paradisus in Cancun.   We have previously visited 3 other Paradisus resorts, all in Punta Cana, DR.  The Cancun resort was nice and the service was good.   My wife and I liked the Punta Cana resorts better.   The two main reasons were the food and the resort's layout. 

Mole was not very good, their menu was much too exotic for our tastes.  Bana, the sushi restaurant was so-so (tiny pieces of sushi).  The room service food is terrible.   

But, the food we had in the Paradisus resorts in DR was out of this world. 

The layout of this resort is 5 connected pyramids.   It is very maze like and very easy to get confused.   

It was a nice 5 day trip,but I doubt we'd return to the Paradisus in Cancun. 

Upside is the service was good.   Even though tips are included In the all-inclusive, I think many of the service staff gladly are hoping for tips.

reviews.author: spadre99
reviews.title: mid winter vacation
reviews.text: we have a timeshare with melia properties, we booked a room for 6 days, not 7 and got a gulf view room, we requested an oceanview room and were told they couldn't honor that request.  i also don't mind tipping for good service, but find that it is ridiculous that you can't get good service without tipping at an all inclusive resort, we didn't feel right not tipping our waiters after a nice dinner either. Also, that they don't mention anything about it to people when they're booking the resort so they can plan their cash accordingly.

reviews.author: Piperkid
reviews.title: Pretty Mediocre - Not a great choice for adult only
reviews.text:
My wife and I are pretty frequent travelers and visit three to four all inclusive properties a year. This gives us a pretty good basis for reviews. I have really mixed feelings about this resort. There are a few positives but a number of area's for improvement. 
Positives first, room was pretty nice (we were in the Royal rooms), there was a seating area in the room but only one TV by the bed, grounds nicely maintained, the bars did have premium liquor and the beds were comfortable. Very friendly staff. The Atrium in the center building very impressive. 
Now the negatives, check in was not a good experience. Most properties here in Cancun will greet you with a welcome drink and a cold towel, that did not happen here. Many of the rooms have twin beds rather than king or queen and they wanted to put us in a room with 2 twin beds - on valentines day weekend. Wouldn't work and it took a couple of hours to get it sorted out. The room we did get didn't have any view. The balcony only had 1 chair and I called multiple times to get a second so we could use the balcony. I was lied to and told that all rooms only had 1 chair, when you could clearly see that others had 2 chairs and a small table- we finally gave up! UPDATE – on our last day (raining) a chair magically showed up (only took 5 day’s)
There are a number of palapas on the beach so you can find shade while out there (many properties have none and you're only option is sun all day ). Royal service does get you access to the adults only pool, but there really isn't any shaded places to sit, other than the day beds which were an up charge. Pool is really cold and none of the Jacuzzis work (all cold). There is a section of adults only beach (Must be Royal to use it).
Service was spotty, rooms were not always cleaned or turned down. Drink service on the beach is slow and limited (at most 1 person serving the entire Royal section). The atrium in the Royal area is a nice touch and it's nice to have a quiet place to go for a drink.
Restaurants require reservations (except buffet and Mexican) and even if they are half empty they will not seat you if you don't have a reservation. You have to make reservations either the day before or up to 4PM the same day if available. Since check in is pretty late your only option one day 1 will be the buffet.
Food was pretty mediocre except for a dinner at the Market Café, which was an interesting concept and the sushi at Bana was quite good. Virtually everything I got at the Buffet was cold, eggs in the morning pasta for lunch, etc.
Another thing that we have been accustomed to at other resorts is the bellman giving us a tour of the property while accompanying us to our room with our luggage. Here we were given the key and left to find it on our own. This is a pretty big property and the signs to direct you are limited. They do not have a good map of the property and the list of restaurants and bar's was a barely readable copy from a copy machine.

There was some entertainment at the main bar each night. The entertainment was fairly good but amateurish. There is very little seating at the bar so most had to stand around to watch.

In conclusion – we went here because they had an Adult only product and found that if you are looking for an adult experience don’t go to a family resort with an adult section. Yes you do get an area of rooms and beach that are kid free but the whole property is designed for families. The restaurants are designed for family, as are the menu items. It is a real compromise when compared to properties that truly have an adult only product. (Try having a quiet romantic dinner on Valentine’s day when the next table is a family) Bars were limited as was any nightlife (not that we are partiers).

As noted in other reviews, building does leak big time when it rains

There are a few properties (adult) that we go back to somewhat regularly, but this will not be one of them!!!

reviews.author: DGSNYC
reviews.title: Not as advertised - room for improvement
reviews.text: The quality of the rooms are not as advertised. The first room they gave us was a horror show. The food was just - could be much better quality.  Tempo and Fuego (we went 2x) were the standouts.  Our waiter Aldo at Fuego was great as was everyone at Tempo. Tempo was pricey but a worthwhile experience. Overall it's a good 3 star hotel but just average and in need of renovations.

reviews.author: Cassia R
reviews.title: Average
reviews.text: The hotel is well located and huge, but breakfast and decoration could be improved. Dinners need to be booked but experience was better and food too. In the pool if you are not a member of the club you cannot use chairs facing the ocean, a pity, as chairs should be allowed to all guests no matter where...

reviews.author: tgdr4
reviews.title: Sun... Sand... Recouperation
reviews.text: My husband booked our trip so I could recouperate from a double mastectomy.. I was sooo nervous because I was still weak walking wise.. The pictures I saw looked like I would be walking a million miles.. The hotel is nicely laid out. The lobby is a lush tropical paradise, an instant feel of relaxation. The pool was amazing .. Although chilly it was refreshing. One thing it was very deep except for pool bar, so i would suggest a small float or a noodle.. The best was the seats under the palapa by the pool although that great hubby of mine had to go down very early, to catch a spot it was soooo worth it .. The view of the ocean was amazing as there was a clear  railing.  We have been to cancun 16 times and this was the best pool view.  The food was  well resort food.. We did not do resturants as we never seem to want to leave pool time to make reservations and don't like to be stuck to a dining time.. The food I had was good but seemed the same selection at the buffett except for seafood night when they did have small lobster, shrimp, scallops, mussels, washed down with a merlot yummmyyy.. The shows were good but you need to get there early, the show is in the lobby that barely sits 75. The rooms were nice but needed updating I hear there are towers that have updated rooms  .. We were obviously not in one  tower 4 ..

reviews.author: Jacqueline N
reviews.title: Pick and choose your battles
reviews.text: The distance from the airport to the hotel was perfect (15 minutes).  Check in was seamless.  Staying the main building is definitely a great location.  The hotel and rooms are very clean.  A couple of hiccup in the room; safe did not work and the bathtub would not drain.  Other than that the room was always well cleaned.  The pool area was not hosed down every night so if someone dropped a drink the day before it would certainly be there if it doesn't rain.  Pool service was by far our best experience.  In my experience going to all-inclusives for many years, the bartenders tend to be slow and inattentive at times.  NOT hear, all the bartenders at all the locations were friendly and fast.  We had the pleasure of having Sofonia, Carlos and Jesus cater to us by the pool the whole time we were there.  They were so kind and knowledgeable on the different tequila.  We are both not big tequila drinkers but they introduced us to a few different ones and were quite surprised that we did enjoy them.  Our massages were incredible; we had a couple massage (unfortunately I only remember one of the two names of the two women, Caroline and ?) but I do think they work as a pair so it would be easy to find them  It was one of the best ones I have every received.  Negative - The omelet line in the morning was slower than a snail.  You can never get the same name or type of red wine when you have dinner nor can you call the same vodka brand at different bars.  We had an ocean view room but if you are sitting down on the patio chairs they provide you, you are unable to see the ocean.  The whirlpool in the spa was cold and some of the jets did not work and if they did work I would need someone to press the button on for me because it is too difficult.   The tennis courts needs to be repaved and new balls should always be readily available (dead balls) were given to us.  We decided to golf and rent the clubs from the hotel.  You should be a shame of yourself for even charging $30 for those clubs... they were not worth $3.00

reviews.author: Anna H
reviews.title: We only stayed one day but found it just nice...
reviews.text:
After spending an amazing week at the Hyatt Zilara our flight back home was cancelled and the Hyatt was sold out...so we spent one night at the Paradisus...it was nice...but HUGE and it felt that way...the food was nothing like the zilara and of course all the restaurants were full so we had to eat at the buffet, the food was not hot and they layout was confusing.   
The hotel is beautiful, like a rain forest and nice lounge areas.  We needed money for tips but they wouldn't give change for a $20 without our passports and the elevator took so long we didn't bother.  The main building is VERY noisy but the beds are Very comfortable and the AC worked well.   Beware there are bars not included in all inclusive as well as restaurants. 
It is advertised as a 4 star resort but felt like a 2.5-3 at best.  A nice place if you don't mind LARGE resorts.

reviews.author: aam154
reviews.title: Great Beach Average Food
reviews.text:
The beach was amazing and the facilities were great. Everything you could possibly need for our stay was provided. 

The service was also excellent. The only problem I found was that the food wasn't worth the price paid. If you like to travel to eat then this probably isn't the right place.

reviews.author: MPeg39
reviews.title: Butler Ramon was a STAR but resort didn't shine!
reviews.text:
We stayed as a family here Nov 2-7 and enjoyed it but a return trip is unlikely.  The butler staff were exceptional and deserve a 5 STAR rating! Ramon, Josheu and Rodolfo were key to making our trip a success. They went above and beyond with service and were fully engaged in what they do. They are over qualified in customer service for the calibre of this resort. If you do visit here, please request them. Since I'm taking the time to write this 2 months later, you can see how impressive they are!!

This resort needs a transformation. The rooms are very dated but have lovely views and balconies. I liked that it was a small resort and would consider coming back if they upgraded the overall decor and amenities as it's so convenient to the airport and the setting is beautiful.  The food was good for buffet style but decreased in quality throughout the week. Our favorite was the Market Grill  - the big hit for us and the boys (12 and 14). We had a cabana which was essential. The same depth pool made it tough to just hang out in since I'm not tall. I ended up doing some work and the wifi was horrible. I couldn't work in my room and had to move around the public hotel areas to try to get a consistent connection.
The golf was a joke and was actually a factor we booked this resort so the boys and husband could have some fun together. As per other reviews, the evening entertainment doesn't have adequate seating. There was ongoing construction and on the day it rained everything was leaking. My limited interactions with the front desk were less than stellar. The family concierge area is dark and dingy which is not what people want to see on a sun vacations. It should be bright and inviting. The  game room needs some serious investment.
Apart from the super butler service (thanks again)  I don't have anything to say to encourage travellers to book and stay here when there are plenty of better options unless they make major improvements.

reviews.author: Kirsten
reviews.title: Great Beach but property needs to be updated/upgraded - disappointed
reviews.text:
I had a room in tower 2 near kid zone with parking lot view :( which I did not mind since I was here for work purpose and not on family vacation. 
The thing that really bothered me was there was no hot water at all in the shower - it was only lukewarm - no matter how much time I let it go to get hot water. I guess because my room was at lowest level. 
Another biggest disappointment was there was a hole in the bathroom roof which had a leak, yikes…

Do I need to say more?

Also heard from my other friends who had room in the main tower was that it was very loud even at 4am and they could not sleep.

I will never choose this place for family vacation.

reviews.author: carrie2play
reviews.title: Not my jam
reviews.text:
I will preface this review with sharing that all-inclusive resorts aren't my thing. My standards are VERY high if I were to find myself needing to be at one, think One & Only is almost all I could stomach but not sure my bank account would appreciate that! I was at the Paradisus for a large work event, which absolutely needed to be at an all-inclusive resort, which I understand for efficiencies and ease of use so to speak with so many people - so that's my context.

All that said, I will start with the good news. Folks that work here couldn't be more gracious and sweet. Customer service is EXCELLENT.  There is no dig or knock on them!

Now, for the bad news. I'll start with one of the most important things for me, food. I could write a whole review on that in and of itself. There was no Mexican food to be found (a few sad tacos and some guacamole at time scattered around the resort buffet options) for the majority of the day's meals. I love Mexican food, so this was disappointing. There are a few nice restaurants for dinner, but otherwise, you're doing the all-inclusive thing, meaning lots of pre-made greasy food for unhealthy American tourists - fries, hamburgers, random buffet things, you get the picture. I love food, and when it's not good, it doesn't make for a great trip. 

Unfortunately the accommodations weren't all that either. I was in the 'regular' part of the resort, not the fancier part so take that into account. My room was huge, which is nice for spreading out and feeling spacious, but the lights weren't easy to use and were annoying (I like dimmable lighting). The light outside the patio door could not be turned off, so there was no leaving the doors open for fresh air and the sunrise all because of a glaring fluorescent light right above the sliding glass doors. Bathroom lighting was also terrible (all downlights) which don't work well for putting on makeup or really seeing your skin or face (probably more important for most women).  There is a fire alarm right above the beds that flashes a bright lights sporadically throughout the night - not sure how anyone can stand this?

The shower took 10+ minutes running to get hot. No joke - it really did. I took cold showers until one day I figured this out somehow, but I'm a conservationist, so this is just not acceptable. 

Every chair and table or desk in the room wobbled.

There was no patio furniture for sitting outside. Really?  I'm in Cancun, I'd like to sit on my patio.

The doors on the TV / entertainment system furniture were falling off the hinges. 

I could hear people loudly walking down the hall at night b/c the floors are so hard and the sound just goes right under the doors.  I was woken up multiple times by folks coming back to their rooms after being at the bars or clubs.

All in all, as I said, not my thing, but even if it was, this wouldn't be where I would return to spend my money or my time.

reviews.author: debbie s
reviews.title: somewhat disappointed
reviews.text: Thought it would be a good value - kids club awful, used for 1 hour, restaurants not great - buffet is best food but if you don't like buffets you are disappointed. Massage at spa was GREAT - pool and ocean amazing - Martin Sanchez in main restaurant was so service oriented and on it....he was awesome!

reviews.author: EUROPEU
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.text:
In a point of view of architecture , views , loacation and atmosphere the Paradisus deserves a high note.
The problem is that a hotel it's not only walls, ceilings,furniture an. swimmingpools.
The quality of service of the human side is perhaps so important or more than the nonhuman conditions, and in this area Paradisus is very bad.
Service in bars and restaurants  are very bad , slow and without any kindness.
A glass seems to be any unknown thing.
If we order a beer or water comes the bottle but never the glass.. This is a 5 stars  hotel?
The concierge service is a complete joke.
Our concierge apparently knew nothing and didn't give some useful orientations.
Our concierge even , told us, that in Xcaret thare was no dolphins!!!
I think that she wished to sell not onli Xcaret but also Xe La.
As I have been 4 times in Cancun i Knew that her information werw wrong and I went by my own where I wanted.
But remain the question : Concierge for what? 
Also de food it's not compatible with a 5 stars hotel.

reviews.author: Akemi I
reviews.title: So-So
reviews.text:
My mom and I stayed here for one week and we have to say we have mixed feelings. When we checked in, there was no special greeting. We then got in line and waited 15 minutes. The check in employees seemed tired and to our surprise, we were not upgraded to the room we booked.  They said to come back the following night to check for availability but when we did, they said the upgraded room features would be the same. The next day, we didn't get a detailed orientation to the hotel but it was clear that a lady who kindly explained a few things about the hotel was more interested in selling a timeshare. In regards to the room itself, it was clean. However, we had to remind the staff to bring towels, washcloths, and toiletries. Plus, they didn't clean/restock the rooms until late in the afternoon. The food was alright. We ate at the buffet most of the time and we can't deny that the food was varied and fresh. The servers were always kind and very attentive! It would be nice if the coffee station near the restaurants would open earlier. The entertainment was fun but there was never enough room for the guests to enjoy the shows. Most of the crowd had to stand up. Be careful what you lean on because one night, during a show, a pillar meant for decorative purposes fell on another guest's head and nearly hit a few other folks as well. We didn't see the staff rush to check on those guests which was worrisome. On a side note, the dancers and singers were fantastic!
The pools are nice but one of them was too deep for us. The beach was gorgeous and the accessibility was one of our favorite parts of the whole stay. However, there should be more beach chairs. 
About half way through our stay, it was time for our scheduled massage that we booked during the 2nd day. It was a wonderful 50 minute massage. The staff also let us know that we had access to various hydrotherapy areas. My mom wished she could have stayed longer than the 1 hour time limit. 
Bottom line, we are not sure if we would come back to stay at this hotel.

reviews.author: katiesim99
reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text:
I can't honestly say we would come back. I read many reviews on trip advisor before selecting our hotel accommodations. With rave reviews from friends about the food and service coupled with the positive words of trip advisor recommendations we booked at the Paradisus Cancun. 

Things happen that are beyond the control of the person behind the desk giving you the news. But how they handle it is important. To start things off we waited in a long and slow checkout line. Unlike other resorts no drink is offered upon arrival. We had requested two doubles beds and were given a king. Our "ocean" view was a small sliver of the ocean and the roof top of some facilities. The next day we were told to let them know before 11am if we wanted to switch rooms. We did. They said come back in one hour. We returned, waited in the Long check out line again and were told in another 30 minutes our room would be ready. Watching the clock tick on our sunny day as we sat in the hotel lobby we finally were given our room. We questioned what they were doing to make amends of the situation and they upgraded us to royal service. This meant we could enjoy some of the bars and dinners exclusive to Royal service. The view in our new room is gorgeous. 

Then we went to our first breakfast. Everyone had raved about the staff. We didn't have a single server address our table. (Which means you can't request bottle water). 

Off to enjoy the day. Lasted that night we went to make reservations for dinner and were put on hold for ten minutes. The only way to make reservations is over the phone. One nice thing is you can only book dinners two days in advance. This prevents people there for a week from filling all the spots. 

Lastly, I went to grab my glasses from the room and they wouldn't work. We went down to the lobby and explained it's a battery issue in the door and could someone call maintenance, the concierge said the only person who could do that was the main check in desk. Really? You mean to tell me I need to wait in the line where the average check in takes 15 minutes all to ask you to call maintenance because nobody else can.  I'm not faulting them for the door not working---but how you handle the issue is important. They sent a service person and 30 minutes later they arrived. I just wanted to meet my friends for breakfast....not wait for service. 

All in all, the service staff tends to be good. Bartenders try to take care of you. Although, the bars all close staggered from 10-12 until all that's left is the club. If drinking past 12 and not being in the club is what you are looking for your options are limited. Dinners are good and food is tasty. Even the Mexican that does not require a reservation was excellent. 

I can't recommend this hotel. Not because there were issues (that's life and travel) but because of how they didn't handle the issues. Of the three other hotels I've stayed at in Mexico, and one other in Cancun. I'd go back to the Iberostar in a heart beat. I actually looked at canceling day two and leaving. To spend all this time and money and feel like you can't get your issues resolved. I'd give up the good food for being able to enjoy my vacation from somewhere other than the hotel lobby standing in line.

reviews.author: HunnyBunny2014
reviews.title: Not what I expected
reviews.text:
Will go back to Cancun but will stay elsewhere.
Hotel dated, needs maintenance. Had a really really crap check-in experience which is too long to write about, Virgin refunded me 10% to apologize.
Staff ok in general. Most came across rude and obviously wanting tips!
I take my hat off to Samuel on the beach, he was friendly and assertive.
We opted for the extra cost of the beds on the beach everyday which we were made aware that it was rare for people to do. We went all inclusive but still spent a lot on extras and would expect to be treated nicely (not special treatment)
We didn't like any of the restaurants there - wasn't anything like I was expecting. So we went out and ate elsewhere most nights which was extra cost - not really what you expect for an all inclusive holiday.
Also the GM had friends staying so all the staff had to rally around them and make sure they were fed, watered, got their favourite bed first etc etc VERY POOR
Also lots of group large bookings which were disruptive. Wi-fi is not good.
Room was ok - my friend paid extra for a junior suite - and there was NO difference between my standard room and hers! housekeeping didn't top up fridge or cleaning products daily. One day my friend didn't even have towels!
Will be returning to Cancun but staying elsewhere.
I'm not a moaner, we did not let this ruin our holiday, still had a great time.

reviews.author: Carol K
reviews.title: Family Christmas Trip
reviews.text:
Trip with our kids and friends the day after Christmas. We had decided at the last minute to upgrade to the family concierge level.  I am not really sure it was worth it. Our butler, Ramon, although very nice and helpful when we asked, we expected and wanted more. We asked for chairs to be brought down to the beach,to put next to the beds we rented for 3 days, that took more than 2 hours,We actually carried them down ourselves the other 2 days, we ordered room service for breakfast and it never came, when our rooms were cleaned daily we daily had to call for towels which were forgotten or the mini bar was not restocked. The restaurants were great, food delicious,( except for Venzo- newly opened and they have yet to work out the kinks) the staff at the Bana especially Gaudacio was excellent, he always greeted us and he was warm, friendly and kind. Sammy our waiter on the beach worked his tail off and always had a smile on his face. 
The beach was beautiful,clean and heavy surf, so much fun.
Our rooms were clean,a little dated, we would have liked to sit out on our balcony which overlooked the lagoon but there was no furniture .
The weather was awesome, 85 degrees, sunny with some clouds, and always a breeze.
Wifi very spotty.
The staff at the pool bar and Coco's were great.
The biggest problem was at check out. We were told by our travel agent who spoke with the staff at the hotel that out upgrade cost would be 100.00$ per room per day and with coupons for our more than 4 night stay the overall cost would be 340.00$ We were charged twice that and they "forgot" to give us a big book of coupons with money off renting the beds, wine, activities, spa use etc. Our check out turned into a disaster and we were late getting to our prearranged travel to the airport which included another family who almost missed their flight as a result. We so enjoyed our time away with friends and family but the ending certainly changed our feelings about the vacation. When you pay the money to upgrade we should not have to beg for beach chairs, towels and services .

reviews.author: Vijit W
reviews.title: Huge Place
reviews.text:
Huge resort. Nicely kept. Beach wasn't that good. Lots of sea weed and the water goes deep within a few feet from the beach. Pools were good. There were guests bringing food into the pool and some were eating it standing in the water and washing off the grease on their fingers in the water. There were security people around but they either did not care or was scared to point that out. 
It looked like the management was a bit confused sometimes. There are two pools and all of a sudden, they would close off one pool to the regular guests so that their exclusive club members could use it. There were only two couples in that section the whole day and lot of kids and parents were very disappointed as the other pool was deep and kids could not use it.
Good entertainment in the evenings but after 9.00 pm, the place is dead. There is a disco place which is a joke. Some guests go out to the night clubs etc in the City but there is nothing for people who want to remain in the hotel. Shopping is close. You can take the public transport. 
Most of the staff were friendly. Food was good and a lot of variety. Did not like the Japanese restaurant much.

reviews.author: Elio L
reviews.title: Mixed emotions- hot and cold
reviews.text:
I will say that despite my review, the staff and facilities were good. I spent 7 days as part of my Melia membership at this resort over Christmas week. The restaurant options were good and I specifically want to call out Jose (concierge), Jorge (Bali beds), and the Blue Agave staff (Grissel, Alejandro, and Emanuel). These guys took great care of us during our stay and made great conversation as there was a huge lack of planning from management during that week. The facility, for the years it has, was not bad and to be fair it was good. Internet sucked and was slow. Food was good at any restaurant option we chose.

Now the good stuff. I am a Melia member. We booked our trip for many months in advanced. We take one long vacation a year and Melia messed it up as I booked the Playa del Carmen resort and apparently it was sold out. We settled for Cancun as it was booked. As we arrived we were told about a US company totally booked the facility. The dining options were limited, there was no entertainment during most evenings. One of the nights the company had a concert beach side which you can hear in your room and after it was done, the crew diassembled the stage and made noise all night. No entertainment and no sleep, great. The managers, directors and who ever is in charge have no respect for long term paying members and just showed no lack of loyalty for members who have paid a lot of money for a lifetime membership. This was our first time use of the membership and Paradisus Cancun made it a bad experience. 

My experience was bad, we made it the best we could as we were there already and invested our money. Outside of this incident, The facilities were good and all around great.

reviews.author: L M
reviews.title: Two weeks too long and too many weddings
reviews.text: We booked two weeks at the Royal Service (adults only) section of this property with friends who joined us from Europe.  We were not advised at the time of booking that the hotel was undergoing multiple (needed) renovations – not ideal but manageable if you could overcome the barrage of weddings each day (painful).  The swim up bar which one would guess would be at the adults only section was actually in the family section and it closed at 6:00 PM; enough said. What saved and made this vacation was truly the staff.  They were warm hearted, very courteous and attentive to our requests.  Hats off to Josue and Catzin working at The Royal La Palapa and our butler Juan; they did a fantastic job.

reviews.author: Lamont M
reviews.title: Hotel needs a ton of work. Average at best.
reviews.text:
When you first walk in the hotel it has amazing beautiful views with a great ambience. It appears to be a great pick.  However, when we stayed there was a ton of rain the entire weekend. The rain exposed this property for the worse. This property has leaks all over the building. Towels and wet signs were placed throughout this property. This hotel is gigantic. They simply dont have enough staff or finances to up keep this tremendous property. This hotel has been worn down. We had puddles of water in our hotel room. We had to switch rooms. The second room had mold on the ceiling. The water spa only like 4 out of 60 water jets worked within the entire experience. This property was not built to last. Spring breakers have definitely taken its toll.

The food didn't settle well with my stomach nor my GF. After the second day we had to go elsewhere and eat off site. Restaurants off site were amazing.

This hotel does provide incredible views. The beach is amazing. We had the Royal service which was a semi plus as the staff is very courteous and professional. They provided us with a mobile phone in which we could call our butler 24/7 which was a great feature. If you are a drinker you can certainly take advantage of the full bar and try to get your money's worth that way. We are from FL, I wouldn't recommend eating on site. Im not sure if they cooked with their own water as opposed to bottle water. It took almost a week after this trip till my stomach was back normal.

reviews.author: Laura A
