If your looking for a more upbeat vacation this may be it, if you want a more relaxing vacation so you don't need a vacation when you get back, try Cozumel.

reviews.author: 440marcelop
reviews.title: Not as good as advertised....
reviews.text: Expected staff to be much more efficient....don't waste your time with the rewards program.. the discount coupons are almost useless... expect a sales pitch to buy a timeshare from the moment you walk in...housekeeping was not efficient...missing coffee, towels, etc....had to call daily.  Very difficult to get a chair by the pool...people seem to think they can "reserve" a space overnight.  Overall, good quality of food, but restaurants are packed unless you are fortunate enough to be able to make a reservation.   Excursions booked through the hotel are good...recommend Xcaret and snorkeling at Puerto Morelos--best reef.   Good location....somewhat difficult access to the beach and pool as you navigate through a maze of pyramids (5).   Check out was the worse--did not even acknowledge our stay or say thanks.  Will not be going back.

reviews.author: Charm0521
reviews.title: 3 Star Resort at Best
reviews.text: My family and I, which included myself, husband, 11 year old daughter, and 5 year old son, visited the Paradisus Cancun for 5 days during the 2nd week of July 2015.  The Paradisus was nice BUT it was not worth the money.  Starting from the top, before you can make it curbside from from the airport, you are bombarded with timeshare offers.  Normally, I try to avoid them, but I did get a very good deal for Wet nWild water park and Dollphinaris.  The price for both is regularly $149 us per person, but I got it for $100 us total for 4 people for signing up to do a presentation at the Beach Palace.  The ride from the airport to the Paradisus was about 15 min.  The check in process was very smooth.  My kids were able to play in the family lounge while my husband and I checked in.  We were given a cell phone to have direct access to our butler, Fernanda, who was great!!  Our room wasn't ready yet, so she gave us a tour of the resort and escorted us to the Market Grill for lunch while we waited.  Once our room was finally ready, i was terribly disappointed.  It was very small to be a family concierge suite.  At first glance, the room looked very clean, but once I started looking closely at the AC vent, the floor, and little corners and cracks around the room, I saw stains, hair, cobwebs, and everything that suggest that the room is poorly kept.  I read reviews before about it being difficult to get a chair at the poolside.  This is very true.  I noticed that people left towels and flip-flops on pool chairs to reserve them and never came back.  This was totally unfair and when I mentioned it to the staff, I was told that I could rent a bali bed for $50 to avoid this.  Most of the pool area is not for kids, because its too deep.  Most of the pool was between 5-7 ft deep.  There was a small area for kids that was about 2 ft and it was always crowded.  Also, I noticed that a lot of people would rinse the sand from the beach off their bodies in the pool.  Disgusting!!  You could actually feel the sand at the bottom of the pool.  No one stop this from happening either.  The beach is filled with seaweed, so much that swimming in the ocean isn't an option.  On top of that, the water was so rough that you could barely even stand in it.  The food was descent.  Mole for dinner and the Market Grill for Lunch are the best choices.  Oh yeah, reservations are required for all of the restaurants for dinner except for the buffet.  A reservation is required even though the restaurants look pretty empty.  There is nightly entertainment at 8;30 in front of the Avenue Bar.  This was my favorite part of our stay.  The performances were great, especially the Michael Jackson performance.  However, other guest make it a bad experience.  People show up late and still try to push their way to the front to see, ultimately blocking your view.  The kid zone is for younger kids, my 5 year old loved it, but my 11 year old hated it.  The final straw that made me really wish I chose another hotel was at check out.  They tried to charge me $40 for not returning the card that they give you to get towels by the pool.  Come to find out, lost towel and room cards is a $40 charge.  Wow!! I was done..  Ultimately, I wouldn't recommend this hotel, unless they are having a serious sale on the rooms.  It is not a 4 1/2 star or 5 star hotel, it is a 2 1/2 3 star.  it is not worth the money we paid and I would not return.

reviews.author: niteflite
reviews.title: Overcrowded and Hot but Great Staff, Good Food
reviews.text:
We stayed for four nights leading up to the 4th of July.  Was placed in suite in 3rd tower.  The room was adequate...the AC was extremely loud, the TV doesn't get many channels, and the TV inside the bedroom got even fewer channels than the one outside.  It got pretty loud here in the evening with the entertainment going on nightly but i guess the loud AC offsets that noise from outside.

Here is the good:
- Food overall is good.  Even at the buffet, i enjoyed the made to order smoothie/juice bar.  They have two grills working at breakfast, there's fresh fruit (papayas, mangos, watermelon, etc).  One restaurant in particular was very good - Mole.  The quality of some of the menu items we got were on par with what you would expect at a real sit down restaurant - sea scallops that were huge...short ribs tender. decent sized shrimp.  The tacos at blue agave were excellent, as was its soup and some other stuff.

- The staff overall was great.  Other than the lady trying to get us to attend a breakfast sales meeting for timeshares, others did not seem pushy and were very helpful.  Never did they look unhappy for not being tipped or did they actually look at the tip amount.

- The location is good....but i think this applies to most hotels in the hotel zone.  It was a 5 minute walk to the city bus station that took us into town.

- free wifi

As for the not so good or bad:

- The place was very crowded.  At some times of day I saw a line of people trying to get into the buffet.  That's not my idea of a relaxing vacation.  The pool and beach areas were ridiculous.  People have to come out before 7 am to place a towel on a chair to call it theirs for the day.  The pool and beach areas are simply too small for the # of people that can be vacationing there.

- Inside the hotel a lot of the lobby and common areas were hot and humid.  There was no AC running...same thing in the elevator.  It was rather uncomfortable.

- The reservation required policy for most restaurants for dinner is a hoax.  It's a cost saving tactic for the hotel.  Upon arrival when trying to make dinner reservations for that night i was told everything was booked, and that i need to call at 7 am on the day of to make the reservation.  The funny thing is when I went to the restaurant with the reservation, the place was empty.  Even two hours later only a couple of other parties walked in.  It's not that the restaurant is filled to capacity, it's that they simply want to serve so many parties on a given night.

- The front desk failed to give me or offer me the x dollars of resort credit I was promised in the reservation.  I did not ask for it since based on my research i found out it was just discounts adding up to x dollars, but i am disappointed they didn't think to present it to me.

All told i do not plan on going back here if i return to cancun.

reviews.author: Eduard B
reviews.title: It was ok!! Nothing Special!!
reviews.text: Just came back from Paradisus Cancun, and overall was ok, just as far as restaurant service so-so. They don't follow reservation time giving you some stupid excuses, only one restaurant I was pleased "Vento" definitely recommend, La Perla and Market Grill nice but outside and it's really hot and humid that you can't sit and enjoy. Room service was ok, I guess it's depends on who's does the cleaning(every day different housekeeper).  Beach was dirty. Overall do I want to go there again-NO.

reviews.author: travelcat080
reviews.title: Beautiful but hot and crowded Jun 26 - July 4
reviews.text:
This hotel has a lot to offer because it is beautiful and has lots of amenities including several excellent restaurants as well as fabulous swimming pools and coastline.  Our 2-year old daughter had a wonderful time.  I hesitate to recommend it to others because the whole place was just so crowded the entire time we were there and also very hot and humid.  I usually write rave reviews about hotels but I really can't do that this time.  I was disappointed by this place repeatedly.  We came after hearing rave reviews from two other families that loved it, but visited at low season.  If I could do it again I'd just avoid this place at the high season and come back another time when it is less crowded.

Here is a laundry list of things that they need to change.

1. Staffing/Human Resources
The staff were clearly overwhelmed, overworked and undertrained.  Each person we talked to told us they had only been working there a few months.   The management needs to hire more staff to increase the ratio of staff to guests and stop overloading the ones they have.   Maybe that will reduce the high turnover.

+ Checkin
Check in was abysmal. We waited for an hour in the supposedly premium family concierge service area and were finally led to the room. The delay was largely because the person checking us in was in training and had to keep checking with her manager because only he had the permission to access certain data.  In the end the room they brought us to was not what we had reserved, it was a standard room in the back and we had reserved a family concierge suite with an ocean view.  We had to do it all over again to get the right room that was closer to our original reservation request.  We said we would like tower 1 or 5, not 3 and sure enough the only room left was in tower 3.  Online reservations are manually copied from the website into the hotel system and whoever does this leaves things out apparently.  Not a great start.

+ Club Melia sales people 
These people were the worst.  They try to get you to sign up on your first day and just waste your valuable time.  So annoying and pushy.  They were completely unhelpful answering any of our questions, and were telling us we should stay at a different Melia resort that is better on our first day!  She just kept asking if I liked massage and other stupid things so I walked away.  My husband tried to get her to spit out what they were selling and in the end it sounded like some timeshare with unclear benefits.

+ Family Concierge/Royal Service
This is an added benefit but was sold to us as some sort of VIP treatment which is a bit of an exaggeration.  Our butler Maura was totally nice and all, but really did not provide any real helpful service other than arranging our dinner reservations.  The fact that reservations were that hard to get is a whole problem in and of itself.  When you go on vacation you shouldn't have to worry about this.  He gave us some candy and aromatherapy pillows, nice.  The few things we asked him for - reserving a cabana at the pool, arranging our luggage pickup- he screwed up.  That was also due to the fact that noone who works at the hotel talks to anyone else.  They would all say "We'll talk to Maura and tell him XYZ" but it never reached him or vice versa.   Apparently if you don't sign up for Family Concierge or Royal Service you get completely screwed at these high traffic times as certain things are reserved only for those groups (like beach chairs and towels).  Without these services the all inclusive service is really limited.

+ Nightly shows.  
We loved the nightly shows, but we literally showed up each night 1 hour in advance to reserve seats.  The shows are in this nightclub lounge setting with beds and pillows and barely any real chairs.  It seems like they decided to put on shows AFTER they built the place because the setting really doesn't accomodate more than a small group despite the massive number of people at the hotel.  Each show was totally packed and incredibly hot.  My daughter loved the shows so we sweated through them each night.  Maybe they could add some more fans or chairs to this area?

+ Beach Chairs
The beach chair situation was outrageous.  Each morning we woke up to see towels reserving every beach chair.  Given our vacation plan was to relax around the pool/beach and we had no chairs we were really frustrated.  There were just too many people there and not enough chairs.  What we learned is the trick is to get up before 7 AM (ideally around 6) and stake out your chairs.  My husband figured we could just leave our towels at midnight and sleep in.  Sure enough it worked.  Ridiculous, right?

Unfortunately the week we were there there was a lot of seaweed on the beach and in the ocean.  We saw the hotel had hired someone with a tractor to clean up the seaweed.  I was optimistic this might fix the situation and improve the beach, but I was wrong.  The tractor guy just raked up the seaweed and dumped it into the ocean so it made the ocean even less appealing to swim in and all of it just ended up back on the beach again shortly thereafter.  We told the staff which reacted with surprise but seemed helpless to do anything.  Who is managing this place?

+ Baby Club
The thing we liked most on our first day was the Baby Club.  The staff were the first really nice and professional people we'd met since we arrived.  My only criticism here is that they seemed to lack fun things to entertain the kids.  They had a TV on and were usually looking at the computer while the kids entertained themselves with a handful of Megablocks and some stuffed animals.  They could really use a play kitchen, some toy trucks and trains, push toys, books, puzzles, etc to make it fun.  My daughter was bored quickly and lost interest after her first visit.  I am guessing others agreed and that was why it was practically empty the whole week even the whole resort was completely packed.  It was basically TV babysitting, which, lets be honest, you can just do in your own hotel room.

Despite all this we had a fantastic vacation, but we'd warn anyone from this hotel at this time of year.  Even though we paid the extra for supposed VIP service through Family Concierge we found ourselves too often frustrated about lines and crowds for things like food, towels and places to sit.   We talked to others who were repeat hotel guests who told us it use to be much better before they changed to the All Inclusive Package model.  It sounds like when they made the change the crowds increased and the service and quality went down.

reviews.author: Vanessa F
reviews.title: Not Nearly as Nice as Paradisus Playa De Carmen
reviews.text:
First the negatives:

The layout is obnoxious.  The pool is way too deep in most areas so you can't casually walk throughout it and its too spaced out. There aren't enough ladders or steps to get in and out.  The kids pool is very boring. There is no pirate ship or floatation jumpy like there is in Playa's Paradisus.

The resort itself is more rundown.  The electrical outlets don't all work properly. The rooms are not very nice. They are ok. The bathrooms are tiny and the layout and decor is super boring.  The outdoor terrace is boring.  

The food is  good not excellent. The clientele is okay.  The place is too crowded. The waitstaff is not as prevalent. 

The positives:

Nice music in the evening
Beautiful Ocean right by the pool unlike Playa
Great Waves - very strong and fun for the kids
Nice Spa

reviews.author: thetruthbetold123
reviews.title: Solid three stars!  The good, the need for improvement, and tips for making your stay pleasant!
reviews.text:
We spent one week at this hotel recently.  I give it a SOLID three stars.  I read thousands of hotel reviews before selecting this one.   Plus, we stayed at this hotel several years ago when it was the Gran Melia and were familiar with the layout.  

 The bottom line is that it is nearly impossible to get everything you want in a hotel.  I have to say that Paradisus for the most part met my expectations.  I will also gladly recommend the hotel to family and friends.

  I should also mention that we purchased the general all inclusive package.   

THE GOOD

-The staff are extremely friendly and always of service.  From our check in to food and room service, all staff were professional and courteous.

-The hotel is not only big, but it is long, which means you have access to a long stretch of beach.

-Buffet food is always fresh, full of flavor and area is kept clean and food is replenished in a timely manner.

-The Vacation Club Melia staff are friendly, not at all pushy if you aren't interested in joining vacation club.

-The decor and and the overall ambiance of the hotel is stunning!  I enjoyed walking through the main pyramid and smelling the soothing aromas, hearing the calming zen like music, and appreciating the unique decorative pieces throughout the hotel.  I also enjoyed hearing the fountains and the ocean from my room everyday.

-If you want to relax in the comfort of your room or don't want to face the crowds at the buffet, order room service!  We planned a day trip to Isla Mujeres and opted for room service for breakfast.  Within 30 minutes of ordering we received our order.  The presentation was nice and the food was delicious!

THE ROOM FOR IMPROVEMENT

-The policy for reserving beach chairs either needs to be enforced or thrown out altogether.  If you go out at 630 am to reserve chairs, nearly all are taken!The policy is such that if you are not at your lounge chair for 30 minutes staff can remove your personal items so that other hotel guests can use the chairs.  Make up your mind Paradisus management!   

-The kids club feels like an afterthought.  On paper, there is a nice, balanced schedule of activities, but we did not choose to leave our kids there for several reasons: 1) kids 5-12 are lumped together in the same not so big room with about 6 activity/toy stations and a jumper.  I walked in twice.  There were 2-3 staff there with as many as 40 children!  
2) There is an iffy system of identifying children who are part of the kids club for outdoor activities--there was an outdoor treasure hunt activity one afternoon.  When I asked staff how children from the kids club would be tracked as they walked through the hotel grounds I was told that the kids were identified by paint on their face.  How about a matching bracelet for kids and parents?
3) A majority of activities are indoors, and the kids zone room is dark with no windows.  We are in Cancun!  Have activities outside!  There seems to be a large underutilized space where the playground is.  Put a big palapa over this area and create a fun outdoor space with a water tables, water slides, etc so kids aren't enclosed in the existing claustrophobic space.

-The nightly entertainment needs to be offered in a larger space!  For a hotel with nearly 700 rooms, there has to be a larger space to accommodate several hundred people. The bar lounge area comfortably accommodates not more than 100 guests. 

-Activities throughout the day and week should be posted on the hotel TV channel.  The only way we knew about events was by asking staff or looking at the activities board in the pool area.  

-As big as the hotel's oceanfront is, you can't enjoy swimming in the ocean as the ocean is rough. The  red warning flags were up the entire week we were at the resort.  Based on tripadvisor reviews the red flags have been up since May.  Not fault of hotel..its Mother Nature..but something for you to consider if you enjoy swimming in the ocean or you have small kids.

-The $1500 resort credit needs to be scratched.  Basically if you book through the Melia or other travel websites, you are lured in to secure your hotel with Paradisus with a $1500 credit.  Here's the lowdown- it's an expensive card stock  booklet of coupons ..for golfing, spa services, towards wine, champagne, or Bali beds.  We only used a couple of coupons for the Bali bed rentals.  A majority of the coupons were not relevant, or would be too expensive to use ie get $10 off at the convenience store for purchase of $100 worth of items...the coupon book is just a big waste of paper...why not list all discounts on one sheet of paper and staff can document unique guest code when redeeming?

TIPS

-Lounge chairs-as long as the lounge chair policy isn't enforced, have someone in your group reserve chairs in the early am--as early as midnight for the next day.  Place Paradisus towels, cheap flip flops, beach bags on your chairs.  The lounge chairs next to umbrellas and palapas go first!

-Make reservations at Fuego and Mole.  These restaurants, in particular, have amazing food and exceptional service!  Be curious!  Try food you'd typically never order and you'll be surprised at how delicious every item on these menus are.  (Make reservation the day before ).   Skip La Palapa-underwhelming cuts of steak, and Bana-not any better than your local sushi joint.  

-Go to the Market Grill restaurant for lunch.  The restaurant has an ocean view, no reservations are required, and the food is fresh, healthy and made to order.  The kids loved the pasta and pizza.  The adults enjoyed the salads, the shrimp skewers and the sides.  

-Be persistent!  We purchased the junior oceanfront suite.  The room we were given was in the 3rd pyramid and had a view of the roof of the Market Grill restaurant.  After seeing this we asked the hotel staff for a complete ocean view room, as we had purchased.  The hotel management offered us another rooms but these had issues as well- one room had outdated light fixtures and decor, the other had a leaky air conditioner.  Needless to say, we ended up staying in the room with the partial ocean view for one night.  The next day we were given another room in the 3rd pyramid which had a complete ocean view and updated furniture, fixtures.  For the inconvenience the hotel management made dinner reservations to 2 restaurants for us.

-Go to breakfast early!   Anytime after 10 am you'll have to wait in line to get seated, wait in line for the omelet station, the juice bar...and lines get long!

-Check out the view hotel atrium from the 8th floor of the 3rd pyramid.  After dinner one night we took the elevator to the top level and absolutely enjoyed the views of the atrium from above.

reviews.author: golobos
reviews.title: Nice hotel, but Family Concierge was a HUGE letdown!!
reviews.text:
We traveled with friends, and in large part picked this hotel (and Cancun in general) due to the Family Concierge option.  We were very excited about what was offered with the concierge option, and also the fact that we could get essentially a one-bedroom suite for some more room while traveling with small kids.  In total there were 8 of us- 4 adults and 4 kids aged 2,4,7,8.  We each booked the Family Concierge Lagoon View Suite, and ended up being in the main tower- tower 3.  I had read many reviews prior to going that stated this tower can get loud at night during shows, and I asked about this when checking in.  I was assured that on floors 6 and 7 where our rooms were, that noise from the nightly entertainment wouldn’t be an issue.  What a lie! In our room on floor 6, it was so loud that you would have thought you were AT the show.  Luckily my kids didn’t have a problem sleeping through it so I didn’t bother to try and change rooms to another tower.

A few comments on specifics-

The Hotel- The hotel itself was very nice.  Great common areas, nice rooms, nice pool, and most of the dining & bar options were great as well.  We ate at Naos, Vento, Bana, Market Grill (twice), La Perla, and Blue Agave.  We had some picky eaters with us, but everyone was able to find something they liked at pretty much all these places.  The only big disappointment from a food standpoint was Naos, the buffet.  This is the only option for breakfast, and it’s total chaos.  Adults, kids, and servers all running around and long lines everywhere.  The breakfast menu didn’t really change from day to day from the looks of it.  For dinner at Naos, while the food offerings did change, the “kids” section was terrible.  You would think for the kids it would have been burgers, pizza, chicken fingers etc….but it was more fancy fish, pasta with rich sauces, and authentic Mexican dishes.  Not really food that would appeal to most kids.  Not to mention they didn’t let you take food out of the buffet.  One night we ate at Blue Agave which is literally 50 feet from Naos and they wouldn’t let us prepare a dish for the kids and bring it to Blue Agave for them.  They made us leave the dish we had prepared at the buffet.  

Kids Club- This was hit or miss.  The first time the kids went here for a few hours they had a terrible time.  No one working there that day seemed to speak English, and our kids just sat there and were miserable since they didn’t know what was going on.  They didn’t want to go back, but after a few days they were willing to give it another shot.  Luckily they did, since they had a much better time after that and had fun the few hours they were there.  

The Beach- While this obviously isn’t a fault of the hotel, the beach was a total bust for our week there except for 2 days.  There was a tremendous amount of seaweed both on the beach and in the ocean which made going into the water extremely unappealing.  I’m not sure if this is common or not, but there was really nothing being done to clear the seaweed from the sand by the hotel.  The waves were also pretty rough for little kids, so keep that in mind if you are looking for a beach where little kids can have a little independence in the water.  

The Pool- Being with small kids and the fact no one wanted to spend time on the beach we spent about 90% of our time in the family section of the pool.  As everyone mentions, there are very few chairs to go around and they seem to be snatched up very early in the morning.  After our first day there we decided to rent a Bali bed for the rest of the trip which I think was worth it.  Service at the pool was also hit or miss.  Some days it seemed like people were coming up to take drink orders every 5 minutes.  Other days it seemed they would come every 30-45 minutes.  They also seemed to constantly run out of towels at that section of the pool, which didn’t make a whole lot of sense.  Other huge disappointments were that the pizza oven at the pool snack bar was broken and wasn’t working the entire time we were there.  Also, the help-yourself smoothie station inside La Perla disappeared a few days into our trip which made us more reliant on the waiters and longer wait times for drink orders.

Resort “Credit”- I was wondering how this worked before we arrived, and as some have posted of late, it’s just a coupon book.  Not entirely a waste since we did use coupons towards a Bali Bed (which made it $35 a day instead of $50) and we used some coupons towards the kids spa.  Mostly it’s just coupons towards money off the spa, Bali beds, premium alcohol etc.  

Family Concierge- I saved the worst for last.  After meeting our concierge the first day, he was basically no where to be found after that.  When checking in we specifically told them which restaurants we wanted to eat at so he could book them all at once for the entire week.  We were told our concierge person would book them and contact us to let us know when they were made.  Well we never received a response.  We used the “butler cell phone” we were given and we left him multiple messages but never heard back.  We had to constantly go into the Family Concierge lounge to check on the status of our reservation. And on the nights we ate at Bana and our second visit to Market Grill, we showed up at the wrong time since the reservation ended up being for a different time than what we were told by the Family Concierge lounge. Our butler was supposed to slip a reservation reminder under our door each night with a confirmation of the time of the reservation but we did not receive one of these reminders on any night we were there. We also only received the milk and cookie turndown service for the kids on 2 of the 7 nights we were there.  Not sure if it is standard per night but some people’s reviews mentioned the kids receiving nightly gifts as well. Our kids only received a note and a little trinket (Mexican candy, food to feed the koi fish) on 2 of the nights. The worst part though is that our friends were celebrating their 10-year wedding anniversary while we were there.  Our concierge was made aware of this on day 1, and actually wrote it down.  Well their anniversary came and went and nothing was done.  We complained at the family concierge lounge about this and 2 days later rose petals and cake were left in their room.  Basically anything we needed we ended up having to go to the lounge to request.  So the idea of a “personal” butler was completely lost on us.   

Overall the Family Concierge aspect seemed like a huge letdown and really a waste of the extra money we paid.  But the hotel itself was nice and all of the employees (outside of our butler) really did seem to go the extra mile.  It just seems that for the number of guests staying at the hotel, there isn’t enough staff to fully handle everyone.  The staff does their best, but at times I think just fall short due to the number of guests they must service.          

I would probably go back for a couple’s vacation, but don’t think I would go back as a family.  Last year we also went to Cancun, and stayed at Club Med.  From a family perspective that seems to be the more family friendly property and where I think I would choose first to go back to.

reviews.author: jwiebusch78
reviews.title: Fun time with some challenges!
reviews.text: We stayed at Paradisus June 24-July 1. We found that it was a very nice resort, however it was a bit disappointing at times. We had a mindset of excellent service and chose the resort because it was supposed to cater to kids as much as the adults. We travelled with our 3 kids and found it disappointing for the family portion. When we first arrived we were told our butler, Charly would be by in a bit to introduce himself and bring the kids their kids bags (toys, toothbrushes, etc). After 2-3 hours we had to call down 3 different times for him to show up. When he did they weren't full kids packs and we were not happy. Also we were staying in the Family Concierge area (pyramid 3) and that is a joke if you have kids and want to try and sleep. VERY LOUD! so we asked to move but no rooms were available until Sat. 6/27. Once we moved it was MUCH BETTER (pyramid 1 which is the Club Melia area). it was much quieter. We enjoyed the nightly shows and the kids loved the Casino nights. Food was good and there was good variety, but the reservation system was a joke. We reserved all dinners but there were a couple times the reservation got mixed up and we had to switch. Not sure the point of reservations if you have to continually call down to Family Concierge and verify the reservation everyday. The pool was huge, but a bit disappointing that it was mostly all about 5.5-6 feet deep. There was a kids area where it was shallow for my almost 2 year old though. We rented Bali beds daily at the kids pool and that was great. Pool staff was great and very accommodating. We had one night where we let the kids come back to the room themselves while we finished dinner and they forgot to shut the door behind them. So we came back to our room to find security there. It took almost an hour to get that sorted and review the door log to our room to ensure no one entered while we were gone. They were helpful and it was great knowing it was a secure resort. As mentioned in many other reviews the beach was filled with seaweed and ironically they were cleaning the beach the day we left. Otherwise the ocean is beautiful but the tide was a bit rough. I would say overall a good trip but would have been much better with better service from our butler.

reviews.author: JB M
reviews.title: I got a great tan!
reviews.text: The drinks were cold and wet, the food was just ok, the beach had lots of seaweed but the waiters Guadencio and Arturo in the Naos restaurant in the Vento section were world class.  They made our trip so much fun.  They were so kind to our daughters...even giving them fish food for the koi.

reviews.author: ddpmp
reviews.title: Paradisus vs. Oasis Sens
reviews.text:
I purchased a Melia Vacation Club membership on the resale market. I stayed at Paradisus Cancun from June 20 to June 27, 2015. We h. ad a beautiful 1 bedroom suite. The air conditioning worked great as well as the plumbing. We had no issues with our room. Unfortunately our room was the best part of our vacation.

We made an appointment to meet with our vacation concierge on Monday. She was not available during our appointment time. We had to go to the members service area 4 times on Monday before finally getting to meet with our vacation concierge. We asked her to make dinner reservations for us for the remainder of the week. We never heard from her again until I complained on Thursday afternoon. Then I received a note on my door blaming me for never being in my room as the reason why I was never notified when and where my dinner reservations were made.

Even though though the hotel has a policy not to reserve pool chairs, all chairs were claimed by 8:00 AM and you never saw the people that claimed them all day. The pools are between 5 and 6 foot deep throughout except one small area for children in front of Tower 1 (the timeshare tower). It would be better if there were more shallow areas so you are not constantly swimming or treading water. 

The seaweed is not cleaned from the beach every day like it is at other resorts. The waves are rough. The red flags were out most of the week we were there. When they did put the yellow flags out, the waves were rougher than they were when the red flags were out. You are constantly picking off seaweed while in the ocean.

There are several restaurants on property. All are beautiful and serve delicious food. My complaint with the restaurants is that they do not have a very good variety on the menu. For example, they have a restaurant called Mole. I expected to see several dishes made with mole. Nope, only one dish on the entire menu made with mole.

Overall we had a good service. We did have two servers at the pool who were not very attentive and took what seemed forever to get our drinks. 

The worst part about this resort is the unruly children that were not being supervised by their parents. I'd like to enjoy dinner at one of the nice restaurants but that wasn't happening while unsupervised children are running through the restaurant and yelling as they passed my table at least 4 times and the parents ignored them. The hotel staff should be able to ask the parents to control their children or leave the restaurant.

I have stayed at 2 resorts in Cancun, Paradisus and Oasis Sens. Overall both resorts are pretty equal. Paradisus excels in the beauty of the rooms, hotel interior, and air conditioning. Oasis Sens beats Paradisus in pool design, beach cleanliness, calmer ocean, service, and peacefulness. If I was not a MVC member I would not return to Paradisus. I would go to Oasis Sens.

reviews.author: Joe Rivas
reviews.title: Mediocre at Best
reviews.text: Before you book please read this. My family and I visit Cancun 1-2 times per year and regularly stay at all inclusive resorts. This was the worst one we have been to yet. This is a nickel and dime resort. The very basics were covered but that was it. The bars were barely ever open for drinks. The liquor was labeled top shelf but Don Julio did not taste like Don Julio. When I went to get ice cream from the little shop I was told it was not included. I was told there were two restaurants I could not go to because I was not family concierge level and the other was $120 per person extra surcharge. The best tequila they had was a $30 surcharge. Higher level wine was an extra surcharge. Late checkout was an extra surcharge. The golf was free but bag rental is $25 and golf balls are $4 each. If you plan to go golfing at least bring your own tees and balls. The beach is okay but has a 1-2 foot cover of seaweed to walk through to get there. When I printed my boarding passes from the computer there it was 8 pesos a sheet. They don't have to go boxes from the restaurant it buffet. All good stays in the restaurant. The room service menu was limited but adequate. There are water leaks from the ceiling all over the resort. We stayed with friends and 1 room's air conditioning didn't work and in another they had a water leak from the air conditioner. The gym though is one of the better gyms I have been to a my a Mexico resort. One shout out is the honesty of the staff. One day we forgot to lock the room safe and the maid came In To clean while we were out. Not a thing was missing. I had $400 in the safe our phones passports tablets everything was still there. I was very impressed by that. The pool service for drinks was great. The actual people that work there are the best part of the hotel. They do their best to make the best of the harsh policies but in place by management to save a few bucks. Enrique and Sergio at the pool are great servers. Try to get in their section and they will treat you right. One thing that really stinks about this resort. The restaurants require reservations and they are tough to get. You can't walk in either. You either get a reservation or eat at the buffet or Blue Agave. Every restaurant is hot so be prepared to sweat through every dinner. 2 restaurants are completely outside and the others have POOR air conditioning. The only one half way cool is the buffet and I don't think that is an accident. I believe that is where they would prefer you eat. The shows are terrible because they don't have a proper viewing area for the show. It is at the avenue bar and it is not large. After reading this review you can make your decision whether you stay here or not but trust me, for $100-300 more you should consider another resort. You will save a few bucks but you will wish you had stayed somewhere else. We only stayed here because our friends wanted to try it. Otherwise we would have never stayed here. However, it still wasn't miserable. Like I said. The basics were covered but that was it. Pool entertainment was terrible and there was no Pool Volleyball. Only beach volleyball. Good luck in making your decision. Oh one more thing. The $1500 resort credit is a coupon book for various things like $100 for a room upgrade but you still pay between $320 and 640 for the room upgrade. $50 towards a $200 Spa service. $15 towards a Bali bed rental that reduces it to $35.

reviews.author: Ms T
reviews.title: Average...
reviews.text: This is a decent resort with one of the best things being the variety of restaurants to choose from. You do have to make a reservation for dinner but if you do this a least a day in advance there is usually a spot available.  Not the case for the Bali Beds near the pools or so they say.  I tried to reserve one the day I arrive and was told they were all reserved for the next 3 days.  Yet several near the pool by the kids play area were never utilized.  This was frustrating since I was willing to pay for use of a bed yet was unable to do so and after lapping the pool a few times was beyond pissed to find there were no lounge chairs available as early as 10am in the morning.  Several people had already placed towels on the chairs and in one case the family never returned to use them until 4hours later. Thankfully Eduardo took time away from his post at the towel hut to locate some lounge chairs and place them near the pool for me.  Yes, I showed my appreciation for him taking time to do so.  I also want to comment about the renovated rooms. I requested and was assured I was getting a room that was renovated.  A fresh coat of paint and new caulking does not a renovation make.  The rooms are decent but I'd hate to see what a room that's not renovated looks like. What others say about the staff at this resort is correct.  For the most part they're very customer service oriented. Would I come back...probably not on my own dime.

reviews.author: ivanritbound
reviews.title: Didnt meet our expectations.....
reviews.text:
**Beware, this is a long review**

My family and I have travelled to Paradisus Palma Real and Paradisus Punta Cana, The Reserve, the latter 2 times.  We have also travelled to Paradisus Playa Del Carmen.  All of these hotels are top notch!  Service has always been spectacular and the hotels themselves of beautiful quality.  

When I was ready to book Paradisus Cancun, I prepared by reading the reviews and looking at pictures, there was no doubt in my mind we would have a great time. 

Dont get me wrong, we did have a beautiful time.  The weather was amazing and the people at the hotel are great, I will take this moment to give a very special thanks to Martin at breakfast in Naos who acted as if we were the most special guests in the hotel.  I highly recommend a delicuous frozen mochacchino he makes.  We also appreciated service by Pascual who worked outside during brekfast time also, he was very attentive to our needs, constantly checking up on us.  

Something we love about Paradisus is that their hotels are meticulously cleaned!  This hotel did meet our standards in that sense.  

Our dissapointment came when we walked into our room.  It was not the biggest room in the world....narrow entrance which led to a couch across from a dining table and a king size bed.  The bathroom was a huge dissapointment!! No walk in shower?? AHHH!!!! we had a TUB....one that was painted over and had a bubbly floor.  The shower head shot water so hard it hurt.  Then water would not drain as fast as it came out so here we are taking a shower with our feet in dirty water.....yuck!!  We called about this inconvenience 3 times.....they would come and say "its fixed", yea right, no it wasnt.  I'll never forget the showers in Playa Del Carmen, it was all laid out in beautiful tiles and I seriously think 10 people could fit in there.  Here, we had one sink and a toilet in a seperate little room.  Also our walk out patio was so less than stellar....it was not at all a place my wife and I desired to be..  The hot tub was pretty sad looking, there was one chair out there....so I guess I would have needed to sit on the plastic table out there.  Also the planter along the whole length was just full of dirt...no plant life.  Not my kind of oasis.  

Out of the 7 nights we stayed here we only received turn down service 4 times.  For some this may not be a big deal but we have kids, we'd come to the room mid-day to put them down for a nap, so maybe a little sand would come back with us, we'd use towels and stuff, so for us to be able to go out to dinner and come back to a clean room that had tidy beds again and fresh towels was important.  One of the times we complained only resulted in a crappy job that night....all the pillows and the decortaive piece on the king bed were thrown on my little boys bed. Also not ONE towel was left.  I dont understand!!! I think I paid for the service....I want it! 

We were frustrated also with making reservations for dinner.  If you call in the morning which you can as of 7am, likely you will not be able to make any reservations for that night, if you try to make one for the next day, likely you wont get one where you want at the time that you want.  Its truly ridiculous, once we called at like 7:20am to make one for the next day, everything was nearly booked.  Seriously? In 20 minutes everything booked up?  Then when we complained about it to the front desk...poof...suddenly slots were opened.  Hmm....

The hotel itself has from what I heard, only had the Paradisus name for 2 or 3 years.  It was a Gran Melia Cancun.  I think it shows.  Some parts look old and just overall it doesnt live up to the Paradisus name. The pool right outside of Market Grill was nothing special, , it had cracks in it, ugly attempts to repair cracks, no pool beds ( you know those hard beds that are literally in the pool that you can lie on) neither does the other one with the bar.  No fountains to go stand under or relax in.....just boring pools.  I truly hated the fact that EVERY bali bed, beach or pool, needed to be paid for.  Some people have said "oh, only 50 dollars? not a bad deal...."  Well when Im used to being able to get a bed on first come first serve basis at other Paradisus hotels, its a very bad deal.  So we needed to be content with folding chair/beds under an umbrella.  

Food was just OK.  Very much the same thing again and again.  The same fish, chicken, disgusting looking chicken patties and nuggets for the kids.  I recommend Market Grill for lunch, its a la carte so, a little more attention is given to your food. I wouldnt overall say the food was bad....just OK.  If I went again, id eat at Bana every night....WOW!!! amazing Sashimi and Sushi!!! 

Kids Zone is miserable.  My child who is 3 (who I would never leave in a kids zone alone anyway) was not permitted into kids zone, rather he would need to go to Baby Zone.  An ugly basement like room with no windows with napping children in it and useless toys and an unanimated "nanny" who was just organizing the whole time....umm...arent you supposed to engage the kids?  We spent ten minutes in there and left.  

The only reason I booked this hotel was because Playa Del Carmen doesnt have the nicest beach.  But Paradisus Cancun doesnt either necessarily.  LOTS of seaweed to swim among and the red flags were out the whole week we were there which meant no swimming in the water.  If I would have known this I would have reserved at Playa Del Carmen in a heartbeat.  

Shows here were great.  The few that we saw.

My in-laws were there that week too and their refrigerator stopped working and toilet clogged up.  They were offered either an upgrade or free massages or a free dinner at Tempo ( a not included retaurant)  I thought, hmm....I wonder what I would get.  So I complained and got "we offer out most sincere apologies"  HAHA....whatever, its ok.  It was worth a shot.

Anyway, I personally will never go back. But, if you want a good time in a definitely decent hotel thats clean with so-so food with friendly service then go for it!

reviews.author: bhi77
reviews.title: Clean and nice....next to the beach and ample pools.
reviews.text:
The rooms are spacious and clean. The room service is shoddy at best. I ordered a cereal at 4 am and it arrived at 6 am. Though it is said to be available 24 hrs. We were in the all inclusive deal. That they really mean. The food and drinks were included all over the resort. 
The staff is friendly and helpful. You just need to keep tipping them for continuous attention. 
The property is situated in the middle of many many resorts next to the beach. 
There is easy access to water sports and other activities.

reviews.author: Rick L
reviews.title: Great property, staff not so much
reviews.text:
Was given 2 rooms in tower 3. Noise was intolerable. Spent the whole night asking for a different room. Reservations for dining are all booked and staff is rude making the reservation and when you get to it.
After all the time wasted in changing rooms and speaking to a manager about it we did not get a simple I'm sorry for your experience. It was dismissed as something that was our fault. That pretty much started our vacation on the wrong foot. The staff should be aware that many of us plan these vacations way ahead of time and we invest a lot of money on them. If you want to be great service, pampered and relaxed this is not the resort for you. Instead be ready to negotiate and be on your fighting game to get dinner reservations, and drinks.

reviews.author: isyan2015
reviews.title: My experience at the pool bar in Paradisus Cancun Resort, MX
reviews.text: I really liked the pool bar in this hotel. One of the employees by the name of Rey was very professional and greeted guests with a smile and made conversation. Overall everyone at the pool bar were great, fun and made amazing  yummy drinks. Santiago was also very fast in making his drinks and a great multi-tasker. My experience at the pool bar was positive. :)

reviews.author: catinparis
reviews.title: Overrated
reviews.text: We spent a week here in June 2015 in a family concierge room.  We chose the hotel based on the overall reviews on tripadvisor but I think the hotel is overrated.  We have been to Mexico 10 times stayed in many all inclusives.   The family concierge package is definitely not worth the extra money.  First the positives of the hotel and package:  Nice updated rooms and bathrooms, good view of beach (higher the better), beautiful lobby, good spa and gym, nice kids backpacks.  Negatives:  spotty service, poor family butler (took 5 days to get free backpacks though our butler told our kids about them the first day and we asked him about them everyday), fancy restaurants but mostly very average food, guys at pool bar who ignore your kids (had to speak with them when they ignored my kids several times),  beach full of sea grass that they don't clean up and rake  ( we just were in Belize and our hotel cleaned the beach every morning), horrible evening show facility (no where to sit and worst ever at any all inclusive) and they really push the vacation club.  The concierge called us everyday day saying they had special gift for us as part of the family conciege package, but when we went to pick it up the gift, it was a free visit to the dolphins IF you go to the vacation club sales presentation! What a joke!   Overall a very average all inclusive experience, not worth the extra cost or the high reviews on Tripadvisor.

reviews.author: treece404
reviews.title: pros and cons of this location
reviews.text:
This is my first TA review so I will try and be fair and thorough as I have been most grateful for those types of reviews. 
Pros include: the aesthetics of the resort. It is gorgeous from top to bottom. We had an ocean front suite and found it quite comfortable. The bathroom was well supplied with toiletries and hair dryer, and there was an iron and ironing board and small coffee maker with supplies. The restaurants were all quite good. I am a picky eater and was able to find something at each restaurant that i was willing to try and did enjoy it. My back up plan was always to go to the buffet which had a good variety of fresh and tasty items. Breakfast was at the buffet each moring. the only restaurants we didn't try was the Tiempo (which was a pay extra place) and the latin place (which we simply didn't have enough time to try). The Market Grill was my favorite which was a brazillian bbq type. Each meat item was EXCELLENT!!!.
Now for the cons: I was not happy with the concierge who greeted us on arrival. She was lovely, but took it upon herself to schedule all of our restuarant selections for dinner. They will tell you they do this to save you the time, but we found they are just trying to get an even distribution amongst all of the options. Look closely at this on arrival and if you are not happy with it, make sure you change it early. Even after our changes were made AND put in writing, we had confusion the first two nights and had to complain about our concierge for messing up. We also found out several days later that she was supposed to have provided us a coupon book which included discounts for many of the pay extra ammenities. Fortunately we found out BEFORE our scheduled massages and consequently was able to utilize the coupon. ASK FOR THIS COUPON BOOK!. The liquor was extremely watered down. At the pool bar, I saw some absolut vodka behind the bar and asked for a flavored one 'on the rocks' no mixer. I still barely tasted the liquor and had no liquor 'buzz'. I'm not an alcoholic, but like to indulge as many do, on these type of trips. If I travel to an all inclusive again, I will bring my own liquor to 'supplement' as needed. Finally, if you go during rainly season, BEWARE if you get an ocean view room. We were there for two days of the recent tropical storm Bill, and he hit the resort hard. Not only did the expansive atrium areas leak like a sieve, but the rooms with balconies had water entering constantly during the heavy rain. It hit against the slider and couldn't drain fast enough. During the first day, the staff promptly came by with squeegies, mops and towels to absorb. However once it kept coming, those towels needed replacing. In no time, we were out of towels so the water started running throughout the room. Then it became difficult to get towels. By the second day, the staff kept telling me they would send someone, but no one ever came. I think the resort literally ran out. I'm sure this was an unusual occurance, but they could have just told us they were out of towels instead of continually telling us they'd send someone - who never came - or at least not for several hours. 
Wifi wasn't bad, seemed to be better further away from the ocean.
So there you have it. If I were to try an all inclusive again, I'd try somewhere else

reviews.author: nickyedisonnj
reviews.title: good food, nice hotel- leaks like a screen in the rain
reviews.text:
7 day stay last week- all was well until rain storm friday afternoon- sunken bedroom had 2 inches of water and took 3 and 1/2 hours to get another room- halls flooded as well- should be better insulted from rain in this area.

servers and food were good.

reviews.author: Richard B
reviews.title: Royal service not worth the extra dough
reviews.text: 7 of us in 3 rooms the 1st week of Dec. The hotel was ok but none of us thought it was worth the extra money for the royal service. Our butler was non-existant during our week stay. several calls never answered. There was 3 staying in our room but 1 bed with a pull out sofa bed. We booked 2 bed unit. Sofa bed was awful. Food, drinks , bar staff were all at a level you'd expect. I don't know if we'd stay there again. It would have to be a great deal and we'd probably stay in standard rooms.

reviews.author: shelley11112015
reviews.title: Great Vacation!
reviews.text:
We had a great experience with Melia and Paradisus Cancun! However, it does need some upgrades with the plants and cleaning of the open water areas where the coi fish are are located.

BUT we did enjoy being upgraded to the Royal Service ( with a fee of course) and Rode was FABULOUS!  He was our butler for the 5 days and 4 nights we stayed!  Our wish was his command!  This was a choice we were offered once we checked in and it made a huge difference! Especially being told we could not get a room until 3 p.m. and we arrived at 10 a.m.

We did have issues with the tropical storm on Saturday and Sunday Jun 13 and 14 and out of TV service in our room for two full days.  It would have been nice to have more TV's or a sports bar with other games on besides soccer in the main bar that was already packed and no place to sit and very loud with music.

It would have also been nice to learn more about day trips in our daily newspaper.  We would have done something on Saturday, light rain or not, if we knew what the weather was really going to be like the day before but no local news and tv was hard to really get and idea.

Overall, a good experience, great beaches and service in the pool area for adults only and great food outside in the royal service pool restaurant.  This was better than the buffet by far. 

The food in most of the restaurants was good not great and we had issues with it being really dark and not being able to see our food, etc.  It is also really humid outside of your room with no real air breeze, etc.

If you are a picky eater...be warned....VENTO is not the best tapas, but room service is great and also the Blue Agave was great with tacos and mexican fair.

reviews.author: Kristine W
reviews.title: Ok resort
reviews.text:
Best part of the resort is the staff...very nice and hard working people.  If you are looking for a truly 5 star, this is not the hotel for you!  Beach is beautiful as are the pools and lobby, atrium....stunning and scent in this hotel is so nice!

Hotel transfer was awesome, food is good but sometime cold.  Blue Agave and the Brazilian steakhouse was Super good and AMAZING service in these 2.  we stayed May 28- June 4 and the beach water was a lot of fun with huge waves bit strong currents.  The lifeguards did 5 rescues during our stay due to people going out to far and current would take them out further....unbelievable how good these lifeguards are....AMAZINGLY GOOD!  If you understand ocean currents you can get back to shore but for those who panic, not good.  So much fun in the large waves.  I had a small child with me and I explained how to ride the current in so do not be discouraged by the current just make sure you explain to children how to get back in and stay with them, you will be just fine.  Room was ocean view and the views are beautiful.  No patio furnature, dead plants in pots, AC not good, beds not comfortable, shower worked some of the time, electrical outlets did not work, getting wash clothes was a struggle...you would think they were made with gold, buffet at times cold, reservations were tiresome, wifi terrible, music in building 3 at night was loud especially with children, entertainment area seats about 10 if you get ther 45 minutes prior you will get a seat but sitting in a room waiting for the show, bring a towel as you will sweat as no AC.  Here is the good, beautiful atrium and smell scented is really nice, blue agave and market grill is really good, staff very nice, bus to town is nice, beach service is great, pool side lunch is really good for children.  Overall it was not a great vacation but not terrible either, just average.  Not a 5 star in my opinion only as I have stayed in some really great 5 stars.  Not much attention to details it appears this hotel may look and smell pretty, a true 5 star is in the details and focus on a no hassle stay.

reviews.author: davidlQ6079YD
reviews.title: Family Trip to Paradisus
reviews.text: OVerall nice hotel great location but not enough restaurants or seating to do things on the fly. Beach location is great, not a fan of their day pass/night pass policies as we had other family in the area. So instead we went to moon palace where they were staying, which has much better restaurants only the beach there is not so great, but the pools make up for it.

reviews.author: vocalgirl1
reviews.title: After Paradisus Playa Del Carmen La Esmeralda, a bit of a Down grade here
reviews.text: We decided to split up our time between two Paradisus properties. While both properties have pros and cons. This hotel has the best stretch of beach and the water is beautiful. I feel this hotel needs improvement. I realize this is an older hotel, but a big difference in the rooms and bathrooms. One piece tub / shower combo. Very small bathroom. The beds aren't the quality of the resort in Playa either. We have a lovely large balcony with no seating on it. Very strange. There are plenty of restaurants, however we did notice identical restaurants had different menu items. Not as exotic as La Esmeralda. The waiter staff are very friendly here and accommodating. My biggest issue with this hotel and most is the smoking around the pool area. They need a designated area, so non smokers don't have to keep moving to get away from it. And please use ash trays. I hate to see cigarette butts on the pool deck when I'm walking barefoot. That's nasty. Clearly people aren't going to clean up their own messes, so the staff needs to sweep the pool area frequently for this problem. The pools need to be cleaned more than at night, especially the one by the swim up bar. Bags and band aides floating in the pool. I guess most people just don't care and throw trash everywhere. extra staff needed for cleaning throughout the day, outside.

reviews.author: Elissabetta A
reviews.title: Not at other Paradisus standards
reviews.text:
Not at the same level of other Paradisus hotels, laike In Punta Cana or Riviera Maya.
Poor food quality...no entertainments at pool or at night, no music at pool bar...
need to bargain to get the right price for any kind of upgrades.

reviews.author: jgoldie
reviews.title: Gorgeous Resort, Honest review
reviews.text: Resort, pool, rooms and beach are beautiful one of the best in Cancun. There is sun all day it is not blocked by the resort building like many other resorts. There is plenty of shade if you want shade. Getting shade/umbrellas at other resorts in Cancun is often a problem. Staff around the pools were wonderful. We've  used USA transfers from the airport for the last 16 years and have always been happy with the service. We do not like the food at this resort. They do not have many options and there has always been at least one restaurant closed every year that we have visited. They do have one highly reviewed restaurant that is not part of the all inclusive, we have not tried this restaurant recently so we can't review it. Do not leave anything unattended at this resort. We have had something stolen on numerous occasions and the resort does nothing except take a note of what the missing item is, this is a common problem in Cancun no matter where you stay, but some resorts do make an effort to discourage their employees from stealing and do try to find your missing items, it is clear that this resort did not care and blamed us for leaving anything where someone could take it. They made it clear it is a common problem there. I am sure there are many honest employees, but it only takes a few. They do have entertainment but it is in the nightclub and unless you are one of the first ones there you will not be able to see it. Very bad location for shows. Cancun is safe to walk around and you can take the public bus for $1 each way where ever you want to go There are bus stops on the street.. Do not stay on the bus past downtown thinking it loops around. It ends up at a depot in an area that is run down. There are many excellent restaurants in Cancun, Lorenzillo's, Thai, Harry's, La Habichuela. There is even an excellent bakery in the new supermarket in the Kukulcan plaza Soriana is on the second floor, excellent chocolate empanada . Soriana is better than Walmart. This time we flew in earlier than our reservation and paid for an extra day, we were made to check out of our room in the morning and were told we could not check into our new room till evening. The hotel was not full and our original room still was not cleaned in the evening when we were in the second room. So why make us get out?? We thought we left something in the room so we know it still was not cleaned. There has been a convention every year we visit that takes over the Hotel and is given priority. There are numerous steps to get to the street from this hotel so it is not good for anyone out of shape. We were given the 3rd degree from the sales staff on numerous occasions when we were walking to the street from this hotel, They sat in a golf cart or stood on the sidewalk by the bottom of the stairs. They wanted to know where we were going and accused us of leaving to do a timeshare presentation and said they didn't believe we were going where we said, there is no excuse for that.

reviews.author: Bobearmy
reviews.title: DO NOT GET MARRIED HERE
reviews.text:
First I will start by saying if I hadnt gotten married here and it was based on the resort stay only I would have given it 4 stars. Property is beautiful from the beach to the pool. Very well kept, most of the staff is very pleasant and helpful and the food is pretty good considering it is an all inclusive. We did have a butler, Juan, who was awesome. Took care of multiple issues on very short notice, couldnt have been more pleased with Juan. I will also say in terms of the wedding we had an amazing time due to the people we were with and the fact that we were in Cancun. The major problems were setting up the wedding. Throughout the planning, do not expect to hear from your contact until about 2 weeks after any email. Leading up to the wedding we could not get in contact with anyone we needed to for weeks at a time. This was beyond frustrating to say the least. I should have known better once we got our deposit in however. After emailing what we wanted we were told everything we wanted could be done. We wanted the ceremony and cocktail hour at the gazebo, and the reception on the beach. Approved, deposit sent. I then went to meet with the planner for details and planning. After finding out that "turtle season" was around our wedding date (not being told by the staff), I asked to make sure this would not be a problem. For a second time I was informed the reception could be on the beach for the time and location we originally requested. You can see where this is going. About 6 weeks prior to the wedding we were informed we could not have the reception on the beach due to the turtles at the time we requested. We could either have it by the pool, or 3 hours earlier on the beach. I did not want a beach reception at 5 in the afternoon, sun still blazing and having to end the party at 8pm which was required. I completely understand the turtles and having to protect them, but as this has been happening for decades, we should have been informed WAY prior to placing our deposit that we would be unable to get what we had planned. I have no doubt this information was kept from us intentionally to get our deposit and leave us no choice but to change our events. We decided on the pool area which they did set up nice. The next major problem was the DJ which they contract out. However, if you contract with this company, it might as well be Paradisus in my eyes as they are representing you. We spent countless hours coming up with about 15 songs we wanted played at the reception, the rest would be left to the DJ. We had maybe 4 of them played. After noticing time was winding down and we had only heard a couple songs, I approached the DJ who had the list in hand, and asked him to only play what was on the list. He proceeded to play the next song from the list, then go off it once again. 11 pm hit and we got 4 of our songs. I didnt let it bother me as it was our wedding night but was very upset after the fact. As for the wedding planner, I wont mention by name but if she reads this shell know exactly who she is, might as well should not have even showed up. Seemed as if we were bothering her with any questions or concerns we had. She was also the one who would take 2 weeks to respond to simple questions that would have taken less than a minute to answer. 

If you are going to stay just to stay, the resort itself was very nice. I WOULD NOT suggest getting married here however. Check out staff was not very nice either, tried to overcharge us then got "bothered" when we pointed it out. They did correct it but took some time. Also skip the sushi place, small group went and most of us felt sick the next day with one person puking and pooing himself all night. Buffet and Blue Agave were very good though. 

Other than planning the wedding itself with Paradisus and the stupid DJ, I would stay here again for vaca only. Great pool and swim up bar, nice rooms, great beach, mostly good food.

reviews.author: Vivian_MIA
reviews.title: Beautiful hotel
reviews.text:
Pros: 

Beautiful location with turquoise waters

Top shelf liquors!!! I've been to several All Inclusive Resorts but this one takes the cake with the liquor selection...Patron, Don Julio, Johnny Walker, etc. for no extra charge

Amazing service at the pool bar by Carlos!

Overall, the staff was polite and helpful. Audberto, who we guess must be the food & beverage manager, was truly a life saver when he booked dinner reservations for us when we were on our way to dine out due to lack of reservations

Rooms are spacious with a great balcony (although balcony didn't have any furniture)

Fuego restaurant was by far the best food we had at the hotel

Cons:

Spotty Wi-Fi

They ran out of pool towels by 1PM on a Saturday!

Reservation are required for most of the restaurants and must be done at least 1 day in advance which can be a bummer. We try walking in but, even though you can clearly see empty tables they, won't seat you. We were turned down at the sushi restaurant due to lack of reservation and 15 minute later, and with the help of Audberto, we were seated! On that note, the sushi place: nothing to write home about

Food is ok, not bad not amazing...just ok

We had an incident at one of the stores that required the intervention of the hotel manager (Alberto) who did NOTHING to help at all, even when the store clerk was being disrespectful to us in front of him. This incident alone will make me seriously consider returning to this hotel in the future

In summary, this was my 3rd time in Cancun, but my 1st time in more than 10 years and I was a little disappointed with the customer service experience. My memories of Cancun were always those of amazing customer service and this time, and based on the service at this hotel, I would rate it a 3 out of 5, tops

reviews.author: Eduardo Lara
reviews.title: I was expecting more ...
reviews.text:
I was expecting more from this Hotel, even though the service in general was very good, there were some dark points. 
The room doesn't have furniture in the balcony, we were told that "the rooms are in remodeling" so our experience was bad in this sense.
The thing that most bodered us was that even though the hotel says that is an "all inclusive", there are several services that are not included, such as wines at dinner. Also there is a "nice" beach area where you need to pay US$75 per day per person to get access, otherwise you can use another beach area further and where you cannot get food service, only at such "VIP" area!!! That was unpleasant and uncomfortable!!

reviews.author: J S
reviews.title: Lovely Resort
reviews.text: The resort is gorgeous and has many restaurants + a buffet  if you are looking to get the "Royal Service" I would add it on when booking due to when we got to the resort we were unable to add it on due to a large convention at the property. We had a blast on the beach and in our pool it was not over crowded to have to even need the royal pool. The beach amazing the water is crystal clear and felt like swimming in bath water they have covered beach beds and chairs that can be reserved at a extra cost as well but there are uncovered beach chairs that are not at a cost but you should clam them early in the morning before it gets busy. The pool bar was great! we loved the swim up section. We went with the Amstar company to book our excursions we went to Xel-Ha & Tulum and both were fantastic go to places that I would recommend we also took a short walk down the street to the right in front of the resort to Harry's Prime Steakhouse & Raw Bar Restaurant and oh my god this place is a MUST go it was the best place I have ever eaten the steak was like butter so good! the service was on point (www.harrys.com.mx) , The ONLY down side about this resort was the fact that the beach and pool close @ 7:00pm and the fact that our ac unit did not work 3 out of our 4 night stay it was rather hot.

reviews.author: Deb C
reviews.title: Company incentive trip
reviews.text: Food for all the group functions was very good, not as good in the restaurants but fine for all inclusive.  Rode our butler was great, but we had to move rooms to get a butler even though we were supposed to have Royal Service the entire stay.  The pool service was great, premium alcohol and Cadillac Margaritas are a must have.  Lights in the smoke detector were totally annoying but they can take the battery out and the lights will stop.  People were great, no storage in the rooms, public areas could use some updates.  Tons of fun!!!

reviews.author: Michael M
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort, Generally Great Service (yet inconsistent), Poor Management
reviews.text:
This is vacation day 6 of 8 here and I can't wait any longer to post a review. This is my fifth time in Cancun, first (and last) time at the Gran Melia Paradisus Cancun. Day 1 was great, but It has just gotten worst with each passing day - the inconsistencies with service and problems that arise on a daily basis keeps deteoriating the experience here. 

Let me just state that the general overall customer service here is great, from bell men to front desk, to servers & house keeping. Rooms are very clean and comfortable. The resort is beautiful. However, there were a few instances that just just odd but unacceptable.

 Midway through our stay we received a letter slipped under our door stating that maintenece needed to be done with the balcony, showing dates two weeks prior to our arrival. Thinking it was a mistake I ignored it, however, returning from the beach one afternoon, our friends 2 doors down, returned to their room with a crew of 3 doing rennovations on their balcony. They called the front desk and asked for the manager to come to the room to handle the situation. The customer relations manager (Sergio) arrived and asked what the problem was...as if it was normal to do rennovations on a room that was occupied with no maintenece request. When asked why that is happening he said it was "normal protocol for them to do that here" to guest rooms that are currently occupied. He had no sympathy nor empathy for how it affects guests. I was alerted to what was going on and had to vacate the pool, dripping wet, to go to the front desk to tell them that I got the same notice with dates that passed and that it was unacceptable for anyone to renovate my room during my stay. The front desk handled it perfectly well and advised that no one will be renovating my room - at my request. 

Tonight, day 6, I went to confirm my dinner reservations at Fuego Restaurant... The manager (Alejandro) gave me a card with a phone number to call for reservations. I reiterated that I was not looking to make a reservation, I wanted to confirm my reservation. He apparently was not used to people wanting to confirm reservations as he seemed incoherent and kept on repeating that I needed to call for reservations. I kept on reiterating that reservations were made and I wanted to confirm since the front desk manager made them for me. A server had to come by to explain it to him. It was baffling to me since he is supposed to the the manger and I'm sure that was not the first time a manager of that restaurant has encountered someone wanting to confirm a reservation! He eventually said that the reservations are no longer there but will reappear the next morning - whatever that means, if it even makes any sense. 

I've stayed at 5 resorts and the Paradisus was chosen for this trip because the Dreams Cancun was closed for rennovations - what a mistake this decision was. I started out with "this resort is nice, I like it, but it's not as good as dreams" to "I will not come back nor would I recommend it to anyone I care about having a great experience in Cancun"

This is sad as my review title says: Beautiful Resort, Generally Great Service (yet inconsistent), Poor Management. It's unfortunate that a few bad seeds in management can ruin a 9 day vacation experience. Perhaps those who can't embody the resort's customer service culture should be replaced so they don't lose future customers.

I still have 2 more nights and can't imagine how much more downhill it can go. Upside: the food is good, the coco's beach cabanas are amazing, the nightly shows are wonderful, the location is central, and the majority of the service is great. In a place with so many resorts vying for guests to stay at - this will not be a place I would return to.

reviews.author: Cahyani F
reviews.title: Swimming pool is the best
reviews.text:
The most highlighted great things from Paradisus is their huge and nice swimming pools. They also have very huge place and the main atrium lookings is nice.
The restaurants is many but for dinner, 90% needs a reservation and the place with better food is always fully booked during 4 days we've stay there (La Perla). International Buffet offers many variety of foods but for me the taste is not going anywhere.
Wifi just fine but the lift is super slow and small.
The staff are nice but some of them are too active I would say. I've got 2x they insist to enter my room while I'm already said they doesnt need to come (tag "do not disturb" was on the door too). If looking on the price and compare with the things you've got this resort is just ok in my opinion.

reviews.author: LJlovetravel
reviews.title: Nice, but the service could have been better.
reviews.text: We upgraded to the Royal Service when we booked, and it was nice to have someone assist you when needed. Our butler's name was Rodrigo, and he did an excellent job. You would think if you had Royal Service that you would have no problem getting into restaurants that required reservations. This was not the case, and we ended up having limited options of where we could eat, and on top of that we had to eat at times later than we wanted to. I would rate the places we ate at the resort as just average, nothing was really great. We also had some problems with our travel and needed to stay a day later. Although there were vacant rooms that weren't booked, we were told by the hotel that they were saving them for incoming guests, because they might need them due to overbooking in other parts of the hotel. Well, thanks for trying to take care of us! We ended up having to pack all of our things up and book a room next door at the Marriott.

reviews.author: Travel D
reviews.title: MIxed Reviews
reviews.text:
My husband and I (both mid 30s) traveled together to this resort.  We have been to many all inclusive resorts and we are not hard to please and we like to party.  I give this resort 3 stars only because I have mixed reviews about this place.  Making reservations to restaurants were a breeze.  We did not do the royal service and we did not feel like we missed out on anything.  All of the staff were extremely friendly and they were not pushy for tips.

Check In:  This was the longest check in that I ever experience on ANY vacation. It took 45 minutes and we were the only ones checking in at that time.  It would have taken an hour if she had given us our resorts credits book.  We received this book the next day as I realized they didn't mention it. 

Atmosphere: If you are looking for relaxation, this is the place to be!  This hotel is BORING!!!!  No music by the pool.  Also the main pool is 5.9 feet deep. Really!!! Hope that you are taller or know how to swim.  One night the club (Red Lounge) was weak with a overwhelming smoke machine (Friday) and the other night (Saturday) it was popping with a overwhelming smoke machine.  They set up a casino night at the Avenue bar, where they had table games.  This same bar also had a Spanish style dance show  and a Michael Jackson show.

Beach: Didn't use it.  Another couple that we met paid for a Bali Bed ($100).  They showed us a picture of a huge lobster that came with shrimp and steak.
