Your resort credit booklet has a discount for the beach and pool beds.  We order a pool bed ($50) and used a $10 dollar off credit.  Bed came with an option to use some of their sunscreen.

Room - Clean with a nice ocean view and AC. Bed, pillows, and flower box needs updating.  Mini fridge had soda, beer, 1 bag of chips, 1 package of cookies. Our balcony did have 2 pool chairs compared to other reviews I have seen.

We stayed in the main pyramid.  This is good and bad (you can't have it all).  The good: Main pyramid had the restaurants, shows, shops, entrance to beach and pool.
The bad: You can hear boom, boom, boom all night long from the club and the Michael Jackson show.  In addition to this noise, outside our room was two weddings on one night and one on another night.  So the weddings of course had a DJ.

Housekeeping:  They kept the room clean and ready for us.  However there is always the towel game on some days. 

Food:  So disappointed.  The buffet NAOS, everything was cold. Even the food that was supposed to be hot.  Vento was fancy (menu), food was ok.  Mole, my husband loved the grouper, my sea bass was plain (no taste).  La Perla was closed the entire time we were there.  We did not eat at Bana (sushi).  We ate at the Market Grill for dinner.  It was the best meal. Lunch there was not good. We did not try Fuego (didn't like the menu).  Went to Blue Agave twice.  The Tacos were ok for a quick snack.  Food by the pool was ok. Nachos, chicken wings, burgers, etc.

Excursions: We did the express trip to Chichen Itza that is offered on Tuesday and Thursday only from 7-3pm.  It was $79 per person.  Enjoyed the trip.  It was extremely hot so take a hat, sunscreen, and a umbrella for shade.  Its a 2 1/2 hour ride there and back.  On other days this trip is from 7-7pm. To long. On that trip you go swimming in a cave.  The express trip does not provide lunch.  They tell you to get a box lunch from the hotel, however its $23 for a ham and cheese sandwich with a few snacks.  You can not take food out of the restaurants. There is a snack bar at Chichen Itza and a restaurant.  They also have vendors that sell souvenirs (not credit cards).  They will work with you on prices.  The bus stops at a million other hotels before you hit the road.

We did parasailing (sky rider) with Aqua World.  You can sign up at the hotel.  Two options.  Either do it at another hotel next door over the ocean or across the street at Aqua World over the lagoon (cost more due to a docking fee). This was fun.

Transportation:  We paid a dollar for the bus. It was probably less than that if you used peso.  Never waited more that 2 minutes for a bus. They come back to back.

Wif: Worked well.

Check Out: Less than 5 minutes.

Overall the trip was ok.  It wasn't Atlantis (Bahamas) lol.

reviews.author: Elizabeth R
reviews.title: Is Everyone Drunk When They Write Reviews?
reviews.text:
I am actually still here at the resort. ì leave tomorrow afternoon. If I am taking time from my vacation to review you know I am not thrilled. Let me begin with stating that this was my 25th anniversary getaway 4 days away. ì even mentioned on my booking form (I booked with Book It.Com) that I really hoped for NO mess ups on this special weekend. Well, my story begins...When I booked there was no option for the "Royal"service so I had to upgrade when I got here. I had read everyone that you MUST do ROYAL. Let me give you my non-drunk review.

I have come to Mexico (Cancun and Punta Cana) before. As far as ...
Accomodations: above average. ì had room 5601 overlooking what they said would be a `lagoon'but it was basically front facing street view and after the gas station, etc, you saw the water. There was a small balcony and the sun was great out there but who wants to face the street? Lagoon? Por favor!!  For a 'royal'service room there was nothing really royal about it. Typical hotel room.  You also have to walk these mazes to get to the main building (3) where everything is at. 

Food: eh. ì have to say like I told my husband, this is just the way it is in these resorts. You can't come expecting fine dining. It was all average. Sometimes cold food, sometimes not enough food. Again, not surprised since at most resorts this is the way food is in Mexico or Domincian republic.

Activities: Since we had 'royal'service we were away from all the loud stuff. But they did have some things. I saw dancers, zumba, etc. however, we did not participate in any of it. We went to relax and that we did. 

Royal Service: well, I have to say, this is much ado about nothing. You do get a 'personal butler" if he is ever around when you want something. You can get a phone to reach him directly but that will cost you a $100 on your debit card returned after you check out. We decided against it. He did try to please us but we don't drink so all the free liquor couldn't be used on us which ì could see why everyone would be so happy after a few drinks. There is also a private area for people on the royal service which was a plus because we didn't want to hear children irking us all weekend. ìt as quiet just like we liked it. THAT was the part of the royal service we enjoyed. And having our own bali bed each day. Royal customers also had a private lounge to eat in on the way to their rooms but the problem was that they never had enough food and it took way too long to restock the food (no manager watching to restock as soon as a plate empties) plus not much of a selection.   Also when ì asked to print my boarding pass, i had to save it as pdf and send it to an email that didn't even get emails. So they offered for me to do the entire procedure again çheck in'so that they can print themselves which is what i was asking from the get go. Err. I said forget it.  `cesar did try to please us so he gets the most credit for anything in this place!

All in all, my husband gives me a much better royal treatment every day versus these last 4 days. It was not horrible, don't get me wrong. We enjoyed our stay other than the no kids in our area, we don't really think the upgrade was worth it for us.

reviews.author: roccom714
reviews.title: Rough Waters
reviews.text: If you love swimming in the ocean , I would not recommend staying here. When we first arrived there was a PANDORA Conference,  Extremely way to loud for me . I love that the hotel moved our room to a quieter location . The staff are very friendly , the pool was nice .The hotel decore was absolutely breathtaking ( I love plants ). Only problem is we really couldn't swim in the ocean , the water was way to rough , so again if you are a ocean lover like myself I would stay here , but not the hotels fault.

reviews.author: josephmX4713HA
reviews.title: No Pinot Grigio and no seats on the balcony
reviews.text: The hotel was very clean and the service was great!!! But I would not come back because there were no seats on the balcony and the 24 hour room service did not give champagne or wine when you ordered it. Also the house wine was Chardonnay and if you wanted something else you were given a wine list and the prices on that list were higher the New York prices!! So an $8 Pinot Grigio was offered for $60 and in my opinion that's not all inclusive.  Also, I've been to many hotels with 24 hour room service and when they say 24 hour room service that means food, wine, champagne etc...

reviews.author: Jenna L
reviews.title: depends what you are looking for....
reviews.text:
After having stayed a many (smaller) resorts, my sisters and I decided we would give a bigger resort a try, to see how it compared; we all agreed, smaller is, without a doubt, better.
I'll start from the beginning...
Checking in....we stood in the lobby for almost an hour before we were helped and able to complete our check in process. The other resorts we stayed at immediately seat you, and bring you a drink....not this one, and nor did the others take this long.

We upgraded to the Royal service, which means you get the promise of a bali bed for 2 days of your stay, a butler and the Royals dont have to share their pool, nor their side of the beach with the non-royal service. We saw our butler upon check-in, and after that, we felt like he avoided us, never made contact with us again. The bali bed situation, although we were told 2 days, we were unable to reserve a bed for any of the 5 days we were there, as they were already spoken for. It was nice having our own pool/side of the beach, the other side was extremely crowded.

We saw room service ONE day of the 5....ONE...

If you call for anything to be brought to your room, grab a book and plan on waiting at least 45 minutes

Avoid Mole (for dinner) no beuno

All we planned on doing this trip was laying at the beach and reading our books...relaxing, this place was good for that. If you would like to do anything, have entertainment...look elsewhere. Even the "free watersports" that are included with your stay were lacking...nightly entertainment was non-existent. I am not talking club scene, Im talking something to do after you eat dinner besides go straight to your room...

As far as checking out, we had to take our own luggage down to the lobby, which is not usual for all-inclusive resorts.

Overall, although the building is nice (although huge, and difficult to navigate) there is something to be said for the smaller resorts. I compared the resort to a buffet..the more people you have to serve, the lower quality you provide, and that was definitely true of Paradisus.

Also, if you depend on an elevator, seek another location...or plan on waiting for an elevator most of your stay

reviews.author: SkiFlyDoc
reviews.title: Nice but disappointing
reviews.text:
My family has stayed six times at various Paradisus resorts, and I would put this one at the bottom of the list. The location is convenient to the airport but away from the hustle and bustle of the city itself, so that part is very nice. The resort itself sits on a strip of resorts so if you are looking to “get away from it all,” this isn’t the place.

The atrium to the hotel is beautiful, with a lush array of foliage that melds well with the hotel.  The layout is great, with restaurants and shops centrally located around the sushi restaurant, which, with its open concept and wood appointments sets the mood for a wonderful dining experience.  The food is excellent, as is typical of the Paradisus brand, and when live music is playing on the stage in the center of the atrium it permeates through the halls of the hotel and sets a warm atmosphere.

The pool itself is beautiful, and the family area is well thought-out with a cordoned off shallow area for little ones that is connected to the main pool so one does not get the feeling they are banished to the kids’ table at Thanksgiving.  However, adequate seating is woefully lacking, and despite the signs that clearly state that one may not set out personal belongings at the crack of dawn to reserve spaces, this is clearly NOT enforced…so forget the lazy morning and get ready to brawl if you want a good spot.  

Unlike other Paradisus resorts, there are few shaded cabanas, so even if you are staying at a level that allows for reserving them, often they are not available.  Idiotically, there is a row of cabanas along the pool that require $50 to reserve (so much for all-inclusive) so they typically sit empty all day despite the fact that there isn’t enough seating to go around.  Go figure.

Beyond March, the heat is often oppressive, and the sheer cloth panels on the cabana-lounges by the beach provide little relief.  The riptide undercurrent is downright dangerous and the caution flags are always on red (no swimming). That said, the beach itself is beautiful and the water is a vibrant aqua.

The rooms are well-appointed although the internet is not the best.  The spa is lovely, as is characteristic of the Paradisus resorts.  However, the Kids Club is depressing, and when we picked our kids up, there were four kids from Boston plus my two from New Hampshire, all watching the Lego Movie…in Spanish (ha!).  The hallway to in which the Kids Club is situated was also the one through which we traveled from our hotel wing to the main part of the hotel, and unfortunately it reminded me of an old depressing shopping mall from the 1970’s, with some empty storefronts, almost no decorations, and poor lighting.

The shows were great, and having them in the bar centrally located was great, although there never was enough seating (seems to be a theme at this resort).  The great sound system for the shows really stirred up excitement about the resort and made for fun nights.

Importantly, if you dare to rent a car, beware.  When we rented our car at the agency in the resort to drive to XCaret (which is awesome, by the way), I saw three cars pulled up for prospective renters.  I purposely drove at 1 Km/hr slower than the speed limit to minimize the risk I might get pulled over.  Despite this, not more than 200 yards from the resort we were pulled over for speeding (although locals were screaming by us going at least 20 Km/hr faster!), and after being given two unpalatable options for paying the fine, I was given the option to “settle” the matter right then and there.  After continuing on our way, I saw the other two rental cars pulled over further along the same road.  In the parking lot at XCaret, we saw many cars with no rear license plates (indicating they too had been pulled over), and in each case they were rental cars (complete with stickers for the respective rental agencies). Coincidence? Hmm…2+2=?

Finally, of all the Paradisus resorts at which we have stayed, the staff at the Paradisus Cancun were by far the least accommodating.  If you are paying thousands of dollars for a well-earned vacation, the last thing you want to feel like is you have to pull teeth for people to do their job…and even then I got the sense they were expecting a tip.

In summary, the Paradisus Cancun is nice, and in the crush of a New England winter it is a welcome relief, but don’t expect the same level of attention or accommodation that you may receive at other Paradisus properties.  Heck, travel one hour south and stay at the Paradisus in Playa del Carmen…now that’s a vacation.

reviews.author: papino2014
reviews.title: Mass production
reviews.text:
Jeez, honestly wasn't what we expected....   place is way over sized for the staffing... you wait around like cattle till your room is ready. ..,We arrived at noon coundnt get in a room till 3 and nobody told us what to do were to go, just move in circles . To overcrowded areas.
 
Acs. In rooms. Need updates. Systems do not cool down room that good.dont get a room to high up. 

All in All....they do have a few
Outstanding Resturaunts

Staff was pleasent enough, but honestly, overwhelmed themselves

reviews.author: J H
reviews.title: Beautiful resort but no night life
reviews.text: Extremely nice resort, clean rooms and beautiful facility but they have no evening activities after 9:30 other than the disco and a small band on two nights of the week. Only beach event-volleyball...

reviews.author: Anita
reviews.title: Housekeeping is a joke
reviews.text: The hardware of this hotel is fine - spacious junior suite as the entry room product; direct access to beach and not so big but with good numbers of food & beverage outlets.  But I was traveling with my 83-year old father and my sister as family vacation and had emailed them before to request for a room with 2 beds + 1 extra bed long before our arrival.  Still we only got 1 King bad + 1 extra bed when we arrived.  I understand it is Easter period and the hotel occupancy at its peak but it was very disappointing that this cannot be accommodated with notice well in-advance.  Then, housekeeping is a joke.  Every day there are things missing and everyday we have to call for blankets, shampoo and even towels.  Then we need to wait at least 30 - 45 minutes.  But the real joke is, even after 30 - 45 minutes, what they delivered were not matching with what we need and sometimes they had to go second round to fetch us what we need and it again took another 30 minutes or so.  And for one occasion, we waited and waited and nobody came, when we called again, they said "housekeeping had gone home".  Oh really?  Anyway, the restaurants staff were excellent and food was good.  One thing to mention, I think the hotel needs to review its policy for people to use towels to hold the beach or pool chairs.  We NEVER manage to find chairs but there were chairs with towels since 7am and nobody came back and used those chairs for at least half a day.  Hotel did say if the chairs are not attended for 30 minutes, they will remove the towels but I did not ever see this happen.  All these make our experience less of what we expected.

reviews.author: Brian C
reviews.title: A little slide
reviews.text: This is our 2nd time at this hotel the first time we thought found was good and service excellant. This time we felt the food was not as good and the service went down hill.  We upgrded to Royal Service as we did our first time.  We did not get muh from butlers barely knew who they were.  The first time we thought they were great, we were given a cell phone to contac tthem not this year. Overall we just thought it went down hill a little.  Manager in the Royal Service was very good and responsive.  The service in the restaurants was very good. The pools were great as was the beach.

reviews.author: Dawn E
reviews.title: EXCELLENT BARTENDER
reviews.text: My husband and  just got back from  our yearly vacation to Cancun Mexico. We stayed at the Paradisus all inclusive resort. It was wonderful except for no nightly entertainment and you had to pay extra to get the "royal service" ,  which I didn't know about until after we were checked in.  We went to the COCO Bar everynight and had the best time. I would highly recommend Enrique. He by far was the best bartender we have ever had in all the years we have been going to Cancun. His english was very clear and tried to teach us some spanish! He is  truly an amazing person.

reviews.author: Missy C
reviews.title: Service issues!
reviews.text: My husband and I just arrived home from a week all inclusive at Paradisus Cancun. It's a shame to have to give this very beautiful resort such a low rating but we had a tremendous amount of service issues during our stay. Without going into too much detail I will say that I honesty do not know why the concierge is even there. They were of absolute zero help regarding any questions or concerns we had. They rudely sent us off to the front desk on several occasions (which is for check in/out). They messed up a reservation one evening and we were yelled at to leave the restaurant because it was booked for a private event. The last day of our stay our room was not made up at 2:30 pm, we called down for towels at 3:00 and they didn't show up until 6:10 pm. We were sent to three different places to get our currency changed up because we came to learn that they do not accept American currency (which is what we always bring to the Caribbean) they only accept pesos. When we were getting ready to check out and I wanted to get my pesos changed back to American, we were told they don't do it and we would have to do it at the airport! So expect that if you're planning on staying here as they do not inform you what so ever... And the list goes on and on. I usually don't dwell over tedious things BUT when you are paying for a five star resort, you expect five star service and that's that. We've stayed at much lower rates hotels in the Caribbean with much better service! The only help we had the whole week was from Ana at the help desk, she was great! The buffet was tiring after a while so we preferred the a la carte restaurants. Mole, Fuego and the market grill were our favourites, the food and service were amazing. The hotel and beach are gorgeous and kept very clean. The rooms are spacious but no patio furniture. We didn't not go to the nightly shows because that's not our thing. So to sum it all up, this is a gorgeous resort with really great food, but poor service. We will not return to this hotel or recommend it to any of our friends or family for that reason only. If you decide to stay here I truly hope the service improves.

reviews.author: tilly
reviews.title: Don't choose this hotel in peak season
reviews.text:
Choose this hotel if you like:
1. On arrival to be told your promised upgrade is NOT available because it's peak season
2. To have to get up at 6.30 am each morning to get a sunbed on the beach (4.30am for a pool bed) because it's peak season
3. To have a balcony but with no furniture on it because it has been moved to the pool because? it's peak season
4. To have very noisy bedrooms because if you are in the main pyramid all the noise is funnelled upwards and when this stops the beach party begins all in competition with the very noisy air conditioning.
5. You like your food luke warm
6. You like to play hunt the teaspoon at breakfast
7. You like dealing with surly unhelpful receptionists
8. You like to sit on the beach and have Gangsta Rap music? blasted in your ears for 2 hours hearing words like fu**ing, bitc*es and nig**rs, and this is a family hotel.
So if you like all of the above this is the hotel for you.
On a positive note Balan at the pool bar was great at mixing cocktails, you will need them!

reviews.author: Jekyllspot
reviews.title: Royal Service is overrated
reviews.text: We paid extra for Royal Service and have little to no idea why.  The butler that was assigned to us (Sergio) wasn't any help.  Our air conditioning went out in our room and on the second night, we called to complain again.  They finally agreed that it was broken (after numerous attempts to tell them this).  We then packed up everything and moved to another room a floor up which took away one of the only nice things about the other room-- the ocean view.  Food was okay--nothing special and as others have said, good luck getting a reservation at a sit down place.  They definitely try to push everyone into the buffets.  The most fun we had was at the swim up pool bar on the other side of the place!  Awesome bartender there went out of his way to accommodate everyone.  Entertainment at the resort was definitely lacking as was anyone that was helpful.  Getting around the place is crazy enough in itself--- after several days, we finally figured out the pyramids and the numerous stairs.  Elevators seemed to stay continually stopped.  We had a fun time but we did that ourselves--- definitely will not ever go back to this resort.

reviews.author: Tracy c
reviews.title: little overrated with no entertainment
reviews.text: After all the good reviews I read on here I was a bit disappointed with this hotel. The staff does a good job trying to keep the place clean. Unfortunately, this could not make up for other things.  As soon as you get to the resort a staff member from guest services wants to sit and talk with you and offer you stuff and try to get you to sign up for a timeshare meeting.  They don't give up even after you tell them no either.  I am on vacation and don't want to be hounded by timeshare stuff.  This resort is huge and does not nearly have enough chairs to accommodate people.  More than half the chairs they do have cost money to rent per day.  I thought this was all inclusive.  There was a lot of things that cost extra.  During the day this resort has virtually no entertainment.  Everyone around the pool had to bring there own speakers to the pool because there was no music. I talked to a lot of people who requested music from the staff with no luck.  A lot of visitors stated they would not be back because there was nothing going on during the day.They do have daily entertainment at night inside but good luck seeing it because it is in the smallest area in the hotel and there are very few seats.  Also, they have a beach party two nights a week that last until 2 am.  I could not sleep because it was so loud outside our room.  It faces pyramid 3 and 4, so if you stay in those pyramids you can hear the music all night on those nights. Our room was average. One of the big downfalls of the room was the balcony had no chairs, so it was nice but no way to enjoy it.  The food was just average food.  The buffet had the same thing for breakfast, lunch and dinner everyday.  One night we got sick off the food.  We never drank the water so we can't blame it on that.  The free WIFI at the hotel was very slow and didn't work very well, but then again it was free.  The candles they burned in the main lobby were too strong and did not smell good. Bottom line is that if this resort had entertainment by the pool bar and more seats and less paid seats it could be a nice place, but it was very boring with no entertainment. Unfortunately, because of these things and others we wont be back.

reviews.author: Vijaya Gari A
reviews.title: Average
reviews.text:
.Ask front desk staff not to bother customers by selling club melia.
. Add more options to dinner restaurants.
. add more dishes to dinner restaurants.
. Dance club on the property is not a good option .

reviews.author: Starling63
reviews.title: Beautiful Hotel and grounds with some issues
reviews.text:
Let me start out by saying that this hotel is absolutely beautiful. Each pyramid is stunning in it's own way. The pictures do not do it justice and the same goes for the beach. We stayed in the Royal Service section and I have to say that the food that we had in the RS Pyramid Lounge was some of the best we've ever had at a hotel. Drinks were also top shelf and available all day. All of the staff were friendly and helpful with the exception of one young woman at the Royal Service desk who exchanged money for us. She was clearly annoyed and I still can't figure out why. We are always friendly and respectful to staff. Who knows, not a big deal, we just shrugged it off. The rooms are quite dated even in the RS section. Ours was quite small, but again, not a big deal. We absolutely loved the Bali beds, especially those facing the ocean--heaven!
So this brings me to the one big issue that will keep me from going back to this hotel and that is Food Safety: I ordered the grilled Mahi Mahi at La Palapa one afternoon. I got 2 pieces of the fish. One was clearly spoiled and smelled very bad. Unfortunately I had taken a bite before realizing this and spent that night very ill. Luckily it was only one bite otherwise the outcome could have been much worse. We are very easy going people on vacation and never let little things bother us. This was a big issue though because this kind of thing can ruin your entire vacation especially in a foreign country should you end up in the hospital. 
All in all we loved this hotel and would have given it 4 or 5 stars but because of this one issue we would never go back. If you go just be careful what you eat. This could be an awesome hotel if they could get the food safety under control.

reviews.author: Chad G
reviews.title: Good Vacation... Could have been great with a little effort
reviews.text:
Pretty much what we expected.  Very nice hotel and the beach was awesome for the price!!!  A few minor issues with the hotel/service but overall nothing too drastic. We are not the type of people to let a few minor issues ruin everything.  However, I will let you know what to warn others about.

CONS-
1. We didn't have chairs on our balcony which was very disappointing.  We called everyday, sometimes twice a day, and still never were brought chairs to sit outside on our nice balcony.  They said they were full occupancy and they didn't have enough chairs???? That's just weird..  On the last day we b!tched so much that they offered us a bali bed, which was somewhat of a nice gesture because they usually charge 100 US dollars a day. 
2.  Also, continuing with the chair issues, I had to get up before 7am to go "reserve" seats around the pool with towels.  Otherwise, you wouldn't be able to find anything poolside.  And the beach chairs were gone by 11 am.  Just seemed very weird for such a huge hotel. And I was on vacation, I didn't want to get up at 7 am!
3. Making a reservation for dinner at the restaurants was  a bit of a pain.  I'm not sure when everyone else was calling but half the time nobody picked up the phone line.  And when we finally got someone on the phone, the only times they had left were like 8:30 and 9 o'clock for dinner.
4. Twice they forgot to give us towels after room service.  Obviously not that big of a deal, we just had to call down and someone showed up within 5 minutes.  But how do you not leave towels for your guest?
5.  The lock box was broken in our room when we arrived. Just annoying because it took someone 45 minutes to come fix it.  We just got off the plane and wanted to go to the pool and grab a drink but didn't want to leave our valuables unlocked.
6.  Because the resort is so big, it seems to cater better to larger groups.  And I don't think they are prepared to handle busy time periods.
7.  Being in pyramid 3 was a bit loud and noisy with music at random times.  Some nights we could have the balcony door open for the ocean breeze, other nights there was club music blasting until 2 am.  
8. Beds could probably use an update.  Not very soft
TIPS
1. Get an Ocean View room = amazing view…(just be prepared that you might not be able to enjoy it on a chair if the hotel is busy)
2. Beach was Awesome... Big and Sandy… Better than most other resorts in Cancun
3. Food and drinks were good for an all-inclusive. No complaints, except setting a reservation is annoying.

Like I said, nothing too drastic, and we had a good time.  Just some service issues that seemed weird.  Only thing that really pissed us off was not being able to sit on our balcony(all 5 days) and enjoy the view with a drink to unwind after a long day.  I would recommend this hotel to others but if we were to book another trip in Cancun we would try a different hot

reviews.author: Terri M
reviews.title: Not a 5* Resort
reviews.text: I have been to the Reserve Paradisus Palma Real in Dominican and this resort does not compare.  We were in the Family Concierge Rooms and again nothing like the rooms in Dominican.  My biggest compliant is there was NO patio furniture on our balcony!!  How can a resort advertise as a 5* without patio furniture!  Go and invest in patio furniture.  I am sure it won't break your bank account.  Totally unacceptable!

reviews.author: Steph
reviews.title: Middle of the road
reviews.text: I had high expectations of this hotel having read the reviews but boy I was disappointed on arriving after a 10 hour flight I was given the room key to a room that was a building site. A hole in the wall with a bag of rubble next to it bed on an angle and lamp at bottom of bed.  Went back to reception I who were useless.  Surely if this room was not ready it should be flagged up. I was given another room for the night and told my room would be ready by 12 noon.  The following day I went to see the Virgin rep Ellie she was extremely helpful and came with me to sort the matter out.  Yet more chaos the people on reception went into meltdown and could not sort the matter out only to say maybe my room would be ready that day or tomorrow.  I was then so angry as I was on holiday with my sister for her 50th birthday.  Her room was fine and we wanted rooms together as we had booked.  To cut a long story short they eventually sorted my room out and all was good even though I had wasted a days hols.  Ellie the rep was great she gave me and my sister a free trip on the dolphin experience.. Thank you Ellie.  Also the rooms were not ready some days till afterb4pm and then they came to turn the beds down at 6.30pm your having a laugh  I am trying to get ready for my evening meal and you want to turn my bed down!  On my last day my sister and I were sunbathing only to be told to move because there was a pool party and it was private.  You do not tell people on the day of the event to move you put a notice up 24?hours before to let us know,  would i return to this hotel - no virgin have classed this is 5 stars - not a chance

reviews.author: Lainesita
reviews.title: If you want good service have to tip first
reviews.text:
The hotel is nice, clean. Beach is beautiful, food is good. However, if you want to get good services have to tip first. If you don't (like we) some bartenders and waiters will just ignore you, specially in the pool area. It is almost impossible to get a chair in the pool area, and what is unbelievable is the the hotel personnel reserve them for people who tipped. 
Another bad thing Is that they are focused on selling their timesharing packages.

reviews.author: jbmatt
reviews.title: 3.5 is my rating. Great Vacation with Kids, but a lot of the reviews are spot on
reviews.text:
Overall, our kids and us had a very nice vacation.  We went with several other families for Spring Break and it was the right destination.
I have to say that after reading many reviews (both before and after the trip), the reviews are fairly accurate.  The rooms/bathrooms are nice, the pools are great, and the beach is the most outstanding part of the property.
However, the need to get up at 6:30 to reserve chairs was both annoying and aggravating considering it was a "vacation".  I have absolutely no idea why the property cannot purchase more chairs....especially after they have received this feedback from tons of customers. You cannot be a 4-star hotel and not have sufficient places to sit at the pool or beach.
Secondly, we went with a large group and had to spend a ridiculous amount of our vacation time making reservations for dinner.  We were very flexible with breaking up our group and times we could eat.  However, everytime we showed up for a reservation we had to beg, borrow and steal for, there were TONS of open tables.  It felt like the property was trying to "push" people into the buffets instead of sit down restaurants.  At the end of the day, the food at the restaurants wasn't very good, and the atmosphere in buffet wasn't what you want for dinner with friends.
Lastly, I am not sure what was up with the alcohol.  We drank and drank and drank and drank, and i am not sure that the alcohol had....well...alcohol.  Many of us went to straight to tequila and still.....nothin.   So so odd.  
All in all, our kids had a great time and we had a relaxing vacation.  However, it would be nice for the property (who usually reads and responds to these reviews) actually takes action with the feedback they receive.  Otherwise, why would they waste time responding to reviews.

reviews.author: Evamarie P
reviews.title: Easter vacation
reviews.text: At check in our room wasn't ready so we went to get something to eat at Naos.  The food is very good there however it's the same thing every day.  Never enough beds daily at the pool. No chairs on patios

reviews.author: Carole S
reviews.title: Not the Pardisus we expected
reviews.text: This property is beautiful but not quote what we expected. The Paradisus in Playa Del Carmen and also both in Punta Cana DR were more spread out properties. This is a hotel and the others were more secluded stand alone properties. The room was just average and the bathroom was small with very poor lighting.  we did get the Royal Service which is worth the money for sure, the staff is very good (we loved Juan our Butler). The food was not great, not impressed with the restuarants. The buffet was the best thing going. This hotel needs some serious work on the exterior, paint etc. But the property is well maintained by a friendly staff. not too much nightlife and the evening show is done in the main bar with standing only in the hallway.

reviews.author: Maria S
reviews.title: It's ok, but not for the price.
reviews.text: The place is magestic and beautiful.  The food is good, the big problem we had was a lack of chairs and towels.  In fact, the first day we arrived we did not have towels or chairs!!!  They simply ran out.  The rest of the vacation my husband had to get up at 6:30am, go downstairs, get chairs and towels and then come back up.  For what you pay, I would expect to have those things available to me.  Another thing that bothered us is that as soon as you check in, they want to sell you their time share- not very smart!!  We just wanted to come and relax!!!

reviews.author: Dan C
reviews.title: A mediocre (almost)all-inclusive
reviews.text:
First off, so that I don't sound like a crank with an ax to grind, I want to say right off the bat that my family and I had a great time here during our six-day stay. We went to Paradisus to have quality time together as a family and to enjoy seeing our young kids (5, 3 and 2) have fun, and we did just that. So, it was a great vacation overall. But in many ways, we had a great time despite the resort, not because of it. 

I'll start with the good. The women who work in the Kids Zone and Baby Zone were wonderful. By the end of our first day, if we walked in the door with one of our kids, they greeted them by name and made them feel welcome. When our youngest son got tired, we were able to drop him off there to get a break from the sun and to nap, which meant we didn't have to sit with him in our room while he slept. For our oldest, the Kids Zone offered a number of fun activities that broke up what otherwise would have been very long days of playing in the pool/sun. She made pizza, made cookies had an Easter egg hunt, etc. All of these services made it possible for me and my wife to sneak in a bit of either down time for ourselves or just more one-on-one time with our other kids. 

Other pluses: The beach is beautiful and the servers who tended to the tables at the beach and the pool were great — super friendly, fast, just really delightful. I even saw a few of them utterly refuse to accept tips, even after doing extra work like lugging beach chairs to a table on the beach that didn't have any.

OK, now for the long list of not-so-good points:
1. Do not waste your money on the family concierge service. We sprung an extra $700 for it and deeply regretted it. While friendly, we found the concierge staff pretty much useless. For instance, they were supposed to make dinner reservations for us and call to let us know where and when, but instead we had to sit with them at their desk for the better part of 45 mins while they made arrangements we could have just made ourselves. We were there over Easter and received a notice with our turndown service urging us to take advantage of "special Easter activities." So we asked the people at the Family Concierge what those activities were, and no one there had a clue. Luckily, we overheard on Easter day that there was going to be face painting. We were able to track down where that was happening, and that led to our daughter being able to participate in an Easter egg hunt and other events she otherwise would have missed.

The food: Ugh. Do yourself a favor and don't waste time or energy making reservations at any of the restaurants. The main restaurant, Naos/The Market offers breakfast, lunch and dinner buffets, which are actually quite good. The food at the other restaurants was uniformly awful. And I'm not picky. Pretty much everything was bland. The flank steak at one place (I'm blanking on the name) was pretty good -- but good in the way that you might think the beef option at a wedding reception is good. Pretty much across the board, I would have much preferred microwaved frozen food from Costco to anything I ate at any of the restaurants. That's not an exaggeration. Nice servers, decent atmosphere, but pretty lousy food.

Other notes about food. If you like your food hot, look elsewhere. Pretty much everything we ate, whether eggs from the breakfast buffet or beef tenderloin cooked to order at Fuego -- it was all lukewarm to cold by the time it got to the table. After a few days, I actually started to grow concerned about how sanitary it was to be eating cool food from a buffet, but since the buffet food was the best available, I ate it anyway. 

A few other things: While your room might come with a balcony/patio, don't expect that balcony/patio to be furnished. We had two rooms and looked forward to hanging out on our balconies at the end of the day, but with no furniture to sit on, we couldn't do that. I asked on Monday to get some delivered, and finally, on Friday, we received one measly lounge chair per balcony. I asked what the problem was and was told all the chairs were needed at the pools. I said, "But we paid for two rooms with balconies. Shouldn't we be able to use them? Here's and idea: You're a hotel with balconies. Buy more furniture."

Lighting -- or lack thereof. There's mood lighting and then there's tripping-hazard lighting. Be prepared for the latter. At night, the hallways are extremely dark -- as if you've walked out of your room during a power outage and only the emergency lighting is on. This wouldn't be quite so bad if there weren't tripping hazards everywhere. There are these weird step/ramp combinations wherever the floor level drops -- a narrow ramp next to a set of stairs. But there are no railings to separate the two, and the tiles are all the same color, so it's very easy to step halfway on a ramp and trip (I did it twice, once carrying my sleeping 3-year-old). Likewise, at restaurants, be prepared to use your phone's light to read the menu. It's that dark.

If you are staying in building number 3, the main building with the beautiful atrium in the center, know that there is live music in the atrium area nightly. If you're not as exhausted as we were and you find it tough to fall asleep, this will drive you nuts, since it's incredibly loud even with your door closed. We were so tired, we passed out every night by 10, so it didn't keep any of us awake.

Two last random things: Weirdly, spoons and salt and pepper shakers are in as short supply as patio furniture. Tracking down a spoon at the breakfast buffet was a daily challenge. And getting salt and pepper shakers felt like winning the lottery -- temporarily. Whenever we managed to snag some, a waiter would invariably come by shortly after to ask if he could take them to another table.

Overall, here's my take: This is fairly pretty place that really wants to be a four-star resort but is stretched beyond its abilities. I get the impression (and this is just a hunch) that whoever is running this place is cutting every corner possible in order to keep up appearances without shelling out what it costs to truly run a four-star resort. You get the impression the staff are more worried about screwing up and getting in trouble than about doing whatever it takes to make guests happy. At really good all-inclusive resorts (The Excellence Playa Mujeres, for instance), if you ask for something unusual, your server will automatically say, "Of course!" and make it happen. Here, you get a look that says, "Oh, crap. I'm not sure if I'm allowed to do that. Um, OK ... I guess." 

Finally, I want to be clear that it's quite possible to have a fantastic vacation here. Our kids really had the time of their lives -- and for me/us, that was priceless. But if you're fantasizing about having the best of both worlds -- a place for the kids to have fun and for you to live in luxury -- you might want to tone down your expectations for yourself. Go in expecting so-so service and mediocre food but fantastic weather and a beautiful beach, and you should be fine.

reviews.author: Clarissasuzanne L
reviews.title: For peaceful relaxation choose Royal Service
reviews.text: Poor food quality, too many people, however we upgraded to Royal Service at the end of day 1 and were better able to enjoy relaxing peace and quiet.  The Royal Service staff at the pool and poolside are extraordinary!!! Exceptional service there.

reviews.author: Cindy A
reviews.title: Seasoned traveler
reviews.text: The rooms are very nice clean and wonderful balconies.  The maids service was so so. They never filled up our water or coffee or replace towels. We were constantly chancing someone down for these items.  They cleaned the room made beds but seemed to forget to restock items.  Balconies would of been great to sit on in morning enjoying coffe or breakfast but no furniture and was told they ran out lol. The food is average nothing to rave about but edible. You won't starve. We did like that the buffet was close to the pools and that there was picky food close to the pool.  Water in pools very deep unusual.   There was very little music or entertainment during the day by pool.  So bring your own speakers for music bc basically you may get an hour of music each day.  The liquor choices were very good as was the free wifi.  Even at night there was not a lot going on.  We spent quite a bit more for this resort than usual. So we were pretty disappointed.  Also. They have scented candles all over which are too strong need to tone that down just alittle.

reviews.author: Jatink P
reviews.title: Paradisus cancun family vacation.
reviews.text: The hotel was ok.  The food wasn't that great.  It was usually cold and seemed like it was food from the day before. The service was pretty good.  The pool was clean which was the best par of our stay since my kids wouldn't get out of there.

reviews.author: Deena B
reviews.title: Beautiful but expensive
reviews.text: Upon check in, we asked for a room upgrade...there was no one to show us other rooms so they gave us a key and said we could look at 2 rooms.  We chose the bigger of the 2 because we have 2 kids and they needed their own space.  However, that cost an extra 100 US a night...The poolside activities were few, room service food was always cold and rubbery...you had to make reservations at most restaurants so we stuck to the buffet...tips are included however the staff had a way of making you feel you should be tipping...overall the beach and hotel were beautiful but it was very expensive and I have been on many all inclusive vacations and I don't feel there was much difference for the price...next time I would go for a 3 star and pay less because this was a 5 star price but a 3 star experience.

reviews.author: Yaisa0320
reviews.title: My vacation was to be a birthday gateway and it turn out hell
reviews.text: Hotel is beautiful  services by the bartender (joushe)coco bar was   excelente the nao buffet was ok wasn't the best food !!! service by the waiters whatt made you go back very friendly and attentive very disappoited overall our phone was stolen from our suit and to top it off we are meliaclub members they gave me $400 to  replace it we didn't feel safe and was afraid  for any other personal belonging. Being stolen We didn't allow no one clean wifi

reviews.author: Christine L
reviews.title: Over rated
reviews.text: Really the biggest negative was the room.  The "queen size beds" are full size and very uncomfortable.  There is no patio furniture on the balcony unless you want to pay extra when you get there.  Really? What kind of resort pulls this. The room had a table with two chairs and one area chair.  No sofa or comfortable amenities.  For the expense of the room it was VERY over priced.  This was a standard room and talking with other guests, their experience was the same. Wifi was slow and spuratic.  The pool was great and the ocean access was fantastic.  The pools were very clear.  Beautiful beach.  We have cruised, been to Maui, Cabo, Oahu, all over the states, Caribbean, by far worst room I've seen.  The food in the restaurants were okay.  The resort was generous with alcohol.  Very commercialized resort.

reviews.author: Joanne F
reviews.title: Truly relaxing
reviews.text: We've been going to the Paradisus for many years now.   We find it to be a great place to relax for a week, and the all inclusive option is the way to go.   We visited early in March this year (2015) and were a bit under-impressed by the staff and the quality of the food.   With one exception:  Sofonia, who took care of us when we were at the pool, was absolutely amazing.  He was friendly, attentive and actually anticipated our needs.  If it wasn't for him I would have given the resort a much lower this year.

reviews.author: tim h
reviews.title: nice but not great
reviews.text:
stayed for two days, the first day there arrived at 1:30 pm front desk was nice then on to the high pressure timeshare sale. I was not ready for this after paying over $450 a night! The food was just ok they were not able to give us reservations for dinner the first night saying they were booked till 10 pm we called at 2pm after getting to room. Off to the buffet "yeah"
Staff was nice, rooms were clean ocean view balcony not worth it. there is a huge planter in the view of the water plus kinda blocked by walls on all sides pluse dead plants in our planter. well off to the pool not bad,very clean, and big pluse warm with swim up bar again staff was nice. We stayed at a non all inclusive for 2 night before coming here and for the extra 250 per night I would never do that again. there is a bus out front $1 per ride per person will take you to any of the other resuraunts up the rd and the food is always great. The blue iguana is a hiden jem, small lunch or dinner food but great tacos and drinks.looks like a hole but good. some other guest told us about it.

reviews.author: TigerCanada
reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text:
The only great thing about this resort its a beach... We payid for Royal service, garden view room and ending up in the room with a view of tennis court. Have to rent a cabanas at royal service pool everyday, seriously? The "Coco" beach club is great, service there is really good as well but its not a part of all inc, even tho its part of the hotel, you have to pay for it. Love the japan ice restaurant, went there twice, awesome service, good atmosphere, delicios food. 
DO NOT FOLLOW FOR "FREE GIFT" INVITATION, ITS A TIME SHARE! Wasting two hours of my vacation, and salesmen get frustrating and angry when me and my husbnad decide not to go with the offer lol 
We have a great time tho, weather was perfect, drinks was yummy, wifi really fast, and beach just delightful. 
Would we go back to Paradisus Cancun? No.

reviews.author: newyearsday
reviews.title: It grows on you
reviews.text:
This was our 10th trip to Cancun (first one with our daughter - age 5) and I leave the resort (after a 5 night stay) with mixed feelings.  Off the bat, will we be going back? No...but most people we spoke with were really happy about the hotel.
Pros: Gorgeous beach, great entertainment/activities for adults and kids, beautiful lobby area, good room service, no problem getting a seat at the pool or beach
Commendations to Guadalupe at the front desk,Tabata and Oscar at Cocos bar, Luis at Market Grill, and Manuel at the gym
Cons: The resort is dated; is is well kept but you can tell it is older and has been renovated a lot, rooms are small (we had 2 full beds and a cot and this filled the room) - we had requested a king, the main pool is too deep, and overall, the food was average.
I almost feel bad we didn't like it more as it has received tons of great reviews but honestly, I'm surprised that Paradisus Cancun is so highly rated.

reviews.author: James M
reviews.title: Got moved from the ME by Melia in Cancun to Paradisus Cancun, no options given
reviews.text:
I have been a long time Melia owner, started with resort on Cozumel then upgraded to Puerto Villarta and then upgraded to a 1 BR Suite at the ME Cancun, then they decided that they didn't want me at the ME Cancun and just moved me to the Paradisus, I went there to stay for a week checked in and was given a room that was not a 1 BR Suite at all and it was facing a parking lot that was full of construction debris.  I complained long and hard to the highest level of management I could find, I was finally moved to another room with a nice ocean view but still not a 1BR suite, I was told there were none available but that was what I had reserved and that is what I bought with options.
I wrote to the owner in Europe no answer, I wrote to other management people and said I wanted out or my contract because they had forced me to make the move.  
I bought the new membership at Melia Puerto Villarta and a manager wrote to me saying I was welcome to come back to PV so I am going to try that.  I will never go back to Paradisus as they all lie and laugh about it behind your back.
I AM A MEMBER AND THEY PUT NON MEMBERS IN THE MEMBER WING AND TAKE THE ROOMS MEMBERS SHOULD HAVE.
I am still not happy with Melia the way they treat the Members.
I would still like to get out of this timeshare but probably will not happen, I threatened to stop paying the monthly payments, of course they said they would take me to court.  I should of tried it any way.

reviews.author: Doc58NewJersey
reviews.title: Primer for the non-all inclusive traveler
reviews.text: Note that we not the all inclusive crowd, so if you intend on taking that option, some of what follows might not be applicable.  We last visited this hotel the year before last (have been staying here every other year for over ten years); at that time it had just changed over to the Paradisus brand.  Being as Paradisus is marketing itself as a luxury resort, we had hoped the place had grown into the brand by now--not the case, as several things kept this place from being far from the standard of a luxury resort.  Paradisus is obviously catering to the “Disney Cruise” crowd; this has changed the vibe of this place from that of a relatively serine and peaceful getaway to that of a rather noisy, younger family with little kids environment--this is especially evident during meal times so be aware of where they seat you.  From the beginning, check in (we are club members) was laborious; it seemed no one person could complete the process (which took over one hour).  Check in ended with a hard sell attempt to upgrade; we declined since they could not give a simple quote to how much the upgrade would cost--instead they wanted an hour of our time to hard sell something.  After decling the hard sell a final time our “agent” asked me if a had some sort of problem--pretty rude to say the least--I let that one go and attributed it to her lack of English proficiency.  TIP: be prepared to not be able to get a direct answer to even the most simple question--seems that the default response at this place is “no”.  First and foremost, for the non-all inclusive crowd, things are not welcoming.  For example, after two days in, we were informed that the continental breakfast option (which had been available forever) was no longer an option.  So, although we preferred a very light breakfast, we were forced to either not eat or spend $50.00 (for two) for that meal--big rip-off.  And by the way, what happened to the great banana bread?  Seems I got the last piece on Sunday--never to be seen again!  We repeatedly asked to speak to the restaurant manager about the breakfast situation; he was always in a “meeting”, and never once did anybody ask to take our name so he could get back to us--not luxury resort behavior.  Next came room service.  We asked for a couple of bottles of water to be delivered on day two; much to our surprise this included a delivery charge; another rip-off.  TIP: walk across the street to Oxxo and buy supplies there.  We stayed in one night (due to illness) and ordered two margherita pizzas from the room service menu; what arrived were two small frozen pizza crusts with some sort of cheese--no discernable tomato or sauce and no basil.  TIP: don’t order room service if you can at all avoid it.  The room was okay; certainly not luxurious, but we had a beautiful sea view.  We battled with housekeeping all week to get two hand towels and wash cloths; they seemed to not get it--two people, two towels.  We eventually did get two hand towels by week’s end, but never received any wash cloths--certainly not luxury resort behavior.  The room had a ceiling fan--the fan worked but the chain to turn off the light was missing so the fan could not be run while we were sleeping since the light was always on.  The beach.  This is the best selling point of this place--white sands and “Corona commercial” water.  Interesting that the resort was even able to disrupt this by having the most obnoxious techno pop, new age, hip-hop boom boom boom boom blaring at very high volume (most days).  Funny how they can take one of the most beautiful settings on earth and turn it obnoxious.  TIP: get to the beach between around 8:00-8:30 a.m.; that way you can find a tiki umbrella and chairs as far away from the “Coco Beach Club” as possible.  Couple of other things; ATM not functional--I suggest using the one at the Marriot next door. Also, three out of the last four times we have been there have been accompanied by traveler’s diarrhea.  Now, I am not blaming this solely on Melia; instead, I think that some food quality control standards have dropped across the board, so be advised.  TIP: you are quite simply taking a chance eating anything raw in Mexico, so consider that.  Importantly take Cipro with you; at the first sign of any GI problem, take it!  All-in-all we were disappointed--love Cancun, definitely not in love with Melia Paradisus.

reviews.author: John S
reviews.title: giant cock roaches
reviews.text: my wife and I stayed in room 1603 which is located in tower 1 the 6th floor.  Giant cock roaches would visit us in the bathroom every night.  The room service food was delivered cold. The naos restaurant was pretty good accept food was not kept warm.

reviews.author: Canadian0102
reviews.title: Dissatisfied
reviews.text: This resort was good until I was feeling sick and was unable to go down to get food. We ordered room service (tuna sandwich and burger) and it took 2 hours and multiple phone calls before the manager came up with our order, which ended up being wrong. Prior to the manager coming up, I called multiple times. Initially they tried to make it sound like it was our fault that we didn't get the food. The operator said that they had brought the food into our room but no one was there so they just left the food in the room. The whole time after I ordered room service, I was doubled over in bed in pain and there definitely was no food in the room or outside the door. I called back twice after that and she told me the food was on its way. 30 mins later, no food. I offered to repeat the order but the lady said she knew exactly what our order was. When the food finally came, they got the order wrong (probably because they made the food while they were lying about it being on it's way). My friend has an allergy to gluten and we specifically said no buns on the burger but of course they brought the burger with buns. They did not do anything to fix the situation. This is not appropriate for a 4.5 star hotel, especially since they kept lying and tried to blame their mistakes on us.

reviews.author: World Traveler
reviews.title: Not such a great resort
reviews.text:
I had not very good experience at Paradisus resort in Cancun Mexico.  Most reviewers stayed at this resort paid for the all inclusive price.  I didn't not so my experience is from a non-all-inclusive point of view.

The resort was nice don't get me wrong.  The lobby was nice and the staff tried to great everyone as they come in.  I had to catch a cab from the airport to this resort since the resort  did not offer any free shuttle service.  I was on my own since I wasn't one of the guest who paid all inclusive price.

The AC from the resort couldn't keep up with the humidity and the Cancun hot weather.  There were sand on the floor in my room.  

Checking out was interesting:
1)  I had to leave the resort very early in the morning (like 5:30am) and there was a person at the lobby checking to make sure that I had a ticket which showed I paid the room.  They must have people stayed there and not paid???  This was the first hotel that I had to experience this level of 'trust' as I left the resort.
2)  Since I checked out the hotel so early, the person at the front desk told me that he couldn't print out the receipt showing zero balance and that he will email it to me after I wrote down my email address.  I need the hotel receipt for business trip expense report.  I noticed that the resort added some 'optional fees' to the bill without telling. I found out because I asked them to explain each line item.  I had to ask them to take it out.
3) Once I arrived home, I didn't see any receipt from the resort for a few days.  I had to make several phone calls; wrote several emails and finally received the official resort receipt for my business trip expense report.  The part that I found strange was that the amount listed in Mexico Pesos and not US Dollars.  The other thing I found strange was that for each restaurant I ate, instead of showing the final amount (price + tip) the bill had several lines.  From a business expense report, it looked like I ate at that restaurant multiple times during the same day.  I had to explain that to my company.

BTW, WiFi was terrible.  Try to do a speed test and see what you get from your room (not in the lobby of course)

Overall, it's an expensive resort.  It's not a good resort if you're not paying the all inclusive price.  It's not a good resort for business traveler, in my opinion.  I have been too multiple hotels outside the US and this was the very first place where it wasn't pleasant to do expense report because of the things I mentioned above.

reviews.author: WorldlyTravelers
reviews.title: Its ok, good value and nice location
reviews.text:
I spent 3 nights here before moving to the Secrets property, it was not to bad, its is strangely set out and easy to get confused in here, rooms are a little outdated.

Service and checkin was smooth but would much prefer and all inclusive property as this hotel is quite a distance from general touristy area.

reviews.author: Angela D
reviews.title: 5 Star view in a 3 star resort
reviews.text: The Check in was long and a bit disorganized. Couldn't tell if there was one, two or three lines - others would just walk up (and this was not the Preferred line either) Also had to wait for our room to be ready and this was after 3pm -  I must admit I Loved the room. View was AWESOME. Ocean front, nice sized balcony. Perfect. The resort itself was however rather large and required a lot of walking from one area to the next.  I took my mother for her 70th birthday and well, although it's a nice resort, great for families, children and young adults - not exactly what I was looking for on this particular trip and could be a lot of walking for the elderly. If you want to eat well, definitely go to the restaurants. The buffet was awful - food cold and bland - even for American standards! It took us a day or two to finally realize you have to call before 9 a.m. the day before to make reservations for a restaurant. We were actually ready to go of the property to eat because the buffet was that bad and we were that hungry!  The beach was beautiful - easy to walk on but the ocean water / current was strong and choppy. Every day was a red flag day. Could not enjoy the ocean at all. I don't know if this is the norm for this area of the beach or not. We were also there during one of their "coldest winters" with the highs being in the low 70"s! The pool with the pool bar is ice cold. The pool between the pool bar and preferred is not as loud and warmer. The warm pool is the preferred club pool and if you're not a member ' oh well to the cold pool you go. Staff were great. Excellent. I did enjoy not being hassled to buy anything. Wifi only worked 60% of the time. The gift shops only accept Pesos or you can charge to the room. Location is good because your on the main strip and can catch the bus. The best part of the trip was the room view and the Joya Cirque Du Soleil show in Riveria Maya - worth every dollar!  Stayed 2/18 -2/22.

reviews.author: 892shellir
reviews.title: Limited beach chairs
reviews.text:
If u are not royal service you feel it.  This hotel allows guest to save chairs with towels so late risers are left with no place to sit.  We crossed into a roped off area in front of building 1 just to find a lounge chair on the beach.  Luckily the wait staff didn't make us leave and served us as they would any other guest.  They should adopt a no saving chair policy.  I Would never wake early just to save a seat and leave another guest in the sun sitting in the sand while I am running around the resort doing other things.  

Cold buffet food...all the time.  Not just some dishes,  all dishes.  The only hot item was the omelette station which is obviously made fresh in front of you. 

Beautiful beach and fun waves.  This is the best swimming if you like wild waves (we do) it was a blast.  

Plenty of bars to grab drinks.

We don't have issues with stairs but if you do...there are a lot of them on the resort.  Just beware of u are traveling with a bad knee or something. 

Room was clean and nice.  We upgraded to the beach view but honestly I wish we would have saved our money.  Didn't spend much time in the room anyway.

We asked for royal service but were told to ask again the next day. 

If u arent interested in the club everyone is trying to sign up up for,  u are invisible.

Wait staff was really good and attentive.  No complaints at all.

reviews.author: Raf19
reviews.title: Overall good,  room for improvement
reviews.text:
I stayed for a week during presidents week/ carnival in mid February . The hotel was almost 100% full apparently. The general experience was positive, but some details can make a big difference and I do think they failed many times. 
Transfer – I had reserved through their website, but the transfer company refused to take me to the hotel because they just couldn’t find my reservation even I was carrying a confirmation voucher!  So I was standing  at the airport after a very long flight from South America connected in the US, under the sun waiting for them to find it, and after almost 45 minutes the answer was no. I ended up taking a taxi and paying myself (USD 68 for return trip). I reported it to the hotel later, they said they couldn’t do anything. Tough start. It wasn’t only about the money, but the situation.
Check in  - ok.  I upgraded to royal service at this moment for USD100/night. Let me tell you about this: I’d be the first to say Royal service is not worth it if it weren’t, but it actually is. And a lot. Actually for people without kids don’t even consider any other option, just do it. After arriving, try to go directly to people behind a glass wall, Club Melia people will already start to annoy you if you let them. 
Rooms – for Royal service upgrade, there was no availability for ocean view, so I got the last lagoon view unit which was nice, don’t automatically disconsider this type of room. I thought rooms could be bad by the photos, but they were much better. Everything worked well and was very well kept, including fridge, A/C, amenities, cleaness. Royal service Pyramid is quiet, so wherever you stay you’re fine. Room service used to take at least an hour, but good.
Butler service –  nice, but not essential. Our butler made reservations for us and everything, but seem to have a prepared speech  and an excessively standardized approach.  And he took some days off, so we didn’ t see him for a while.
Beach and pools – the beach is just like you would expect, gorgeous. The pools were nice, so here comes RS benefits. RS pool is nice and quieter, and heated (not 100%, should be more heated imo). They should heat all pools, as pools are one of resort’s main attractions.  I don’ t get this. In RS area you don’t have to rush for chairs, there is space for everyone. The awesome Bali beds (RS incuded) require reservation, but they can always find one for you. In this area waiters keep passing all the time, there’s absolutely no need to stand at the bar or restaurant and hope to someone take your order, as other areas.  Pools could be cleaner, threre were too many insects floating, leaves, sand and sunscreen, including the RS one. Main pool was even worse, cold and so many kids yelling I just wanted to be back to the adults area as soon as I could. 
In RS area there is a hot tub but not heated, actually very cold! There was also a spa style pool, with astonishing beachfront view, but guess what, not heated either and with an abandoned feeling. Service by the pool (RS) has nothing to be complained. Waiters also always brought us different drinks, whose names I didn’t know but were pleased to made us try them. Drinks are usually very weak, ask for double alcohol that it gets better.
At the main pool area, I saw many pelicans flying over plates to catch leftovers (and sucessfully landing at them!)  and staff would just return plates normally instead of throwing them away. 
Spa – if you’re RS you have one daily access to it and the “water ritual”. It is nice, but their pool is not heated, was not relaxed with the very cold water massage and plus not all of it were working. Didn’t  care to return.
Restaurants – didn’t meet my expectations, what surprises me ‘cause I’m generally open minded about it. There are up and downs. Sometimes I had that bad feeling that they were just serving buffet Naos food reorganized. Vento (tapas) was aweful, frosted food, tasted like plastic. Didn’ like the Mexican either. Brazilian Market grill doesn’t deserve to be at this resort, so bad I can’t even think of it again. I liked Fuego. Naos was chaotic, 40 minutes standing for an omelet.  Service in general was good though. I really miss an Italian and French place there. What’s the point to have a vulgar brazilian rodizio and not a place to experience classic cuisines? Lapalapa at the beach (only RS) worked for me. I had breakfast there almost everyday, perfect combination of view + fantastic camembert cheese omelet. They serve you efficiently at your Bali bed, good for lunch too. One day I chose to go to Naos, what a regret when I met all that crowd. What saved me is the fantastic royal service buffet at the RS Pyramid. It is just for snacks, but always included remarkable delicatenses like top notch cheeses, caviar, cavas etc.
Alcohol is a mixed bag. House wines are bad, but they had a reasonable offer of cavas  included (catalunian sparkling wine, from the land of the Melia chain), Freixenet an example. Just be specific and ask. Other liquors seem to be of good quality.
Night entertainement -  took place at the main pyramid – Avenue Bar. Shows were good, need to get there early. Neighbor bar Red held the disco scene later, was relatively busy when I visited. 
Club Melia hassle – they didn’t waste my time because I was warned here by other reviewers. Just ignore them, drop invitations for breakfast or to pick up welcome gifts. If you fall for them, you’ll  loose a whole morning.
I did report the hotel the problems I wrote here (dirty cold pools, bad restaurants etc) but they coldly ignored me. During check out they tried to charge me USD400 more, but later realized the mistake. The resort is nice though. But I think if you’re really into all inclusive experience, Punta Cana properties may deliver better value.  I hope the hotel improves related to my points here so I can return.

reviews.author: Oni J
reviews.title: Just Okay...
reviews.text:
I visited this resort from Jan 18-22 for my boyfriend's 30th Birthday. Not bad, it was clean but not extremely modern. The first day we arrived we offered an upgrade for a certain price but we were able to negotiate a lower price. The first morning I woke up I tried to order room service, after waiting almost two hours I recieved a cold omelet with raw onions and unmelted hard cheese. I called back room service they passed me on to several people only to have me eventually speak to the initial person that transferred the call, when I expressed my disappointment the woman pretended she didn't speak english. I was told I had to wait another hour to have it replaced. After waiting more than 1 hour I was once again given another cold omelet with uncooked ingredients. I didn't bother using room service for the rest of the trip. 

Other pro's and con's 
Pros
The room was clean 
Nice view of the beach 
Not a lot of noise on our wing 
Fridge was always stocked 

Cons 
Extremely old refrigerator 
Not a lot of food options (buffet food always cold)
Drinks were not strong (they reused soft plastic cups in certain locations, and didn't give you a straw)
We were being forced into viewing a time share (I was adamant about not going and I did not appreciate being forced) 
Not enough beach chairs  

One last thing, when I was checking out, the lady at the desk told me she could not change my $100 in US (so that I could pay for the cab to the airport) She offered to give me pesos which was pointless because I was leaving. As a courtesy, she could have changed my money into smaller bills because the hotel was more than happy to accept my payment in US dollars. 

If I came back to Cancun I wouldn't stay here again, simply because I would like to see what other resorts have to offer.

reviews.author: CandiceWinnipeg
reviews.title: Pyramid 4 is the best choice!
reviews.text: We recommend pyramid #4 as the best choice for a beautiful view and more restful, quiet night. We enjoyed the "quiet" pool and had excellent service from Victor! He was an excellent poolside server and even taught us a few words in Spanish!

reviews.author: Jannis S
reviews.title: Better hotels in the area.
reviews.text: We have stayed at 5 hotels in the cancan hotel district over the past few years. I would rank this hotel 3rd. or maybe 4th. for overall experiences. While the people who work here are nice and pleasant there was never the sense that they were willing to go over the top to accommodate us. When we arrived are group was told we were being upgraded to Royal Service. There was nothing Royal about the area except that there were no kids in one pool. That pool did not have a swim up bar, so us and almost all of the other guest spent our pool time in the regular pool. The pool area is nice, but there are no shallow areas in the pool except for maybe a 1' space on the outer edge. If  the swim up bar area was crowded you have to tread water to stay in the bar area. The best restaurant to eat is the Market Grill. Don't bother making reservation for The Steak House. The steak house was only a Mexican buffet. ( we were told that after we were seated) Our room in the Royal tower was small, I mean really small compared to the other couples in our group. There were no house coats or slippers or washcloths in our room. Room service is slow. There is only one elevator in each tower that is shared by workers and guest, so it is very slow. There are STEPS! A lot of STEPS

reviews.author: Slmonroe
reviews.title: So much potential
reviews.text:
Don't get me wrong....  We had a great time.   The hotel is very well kept.  Awesome service (from the wait staff and others who get tipped).  The front desk wasn't as helpful.   The restaurants were very good overall.  Feugo and Vento were are favorites.   Mole was the worst.  Two things really messed up our experience...   First, we reserved a King bed.  We wound up with two full beds.  Because they were at 100% occupancy my wife and I couldn't change.   Next, our room (3453) was two floors above the "Red Room", the hotels discotheque.   From 10pm to 2am every night we tried to sleep through pounding bass and music.  Terrible.  I recommend coming here, but stay in a part of the hotel not among the main atrium.  

Pools and beach are amazing!

reviews.author: James c
reviews.title: Great beach and drinks, average otherwise
reviews.text: Went for a business trip, stayed for the weekend when joined by my wife.  Sun and pool and sand and drinking are great.  Keep you expectations in check for other amenities.  Food is OK but hit or miss.  Nine hole par 3 course is fun, bring your own balls and tees

reviews.author: avpl
reviews.title: Not so good, won't be returning and can't recommend
reviews.text:
The good: The staff around the pool - Omar & Bernardo, and Jesus in the breakfast restaurant.  Our butler Hector was OK too.  They all went above and beyond to try and make our stay enjoyable. The staff (in general) are the hotel's best asset.

The bad: Food in the buffet was very poor; always cold (breakfast, lunch, and dinner) without exception. There also appeared to be a lot of nothing in terms of choice too. The other restaurants we ate in were merely acceptable, no stand-out meals in any of them

The other bad:  They closed Market Place on Friday night for a private party.  This is not acceptable when I've paid for all-inclusive for a set number of choices and restaurants.

The other other bad:  The rooms are not in great condition. Our bathroom mirror was eroding around all edges, the bathroom towel rail was held on by sticky tape, eventually falling off.  We also requested only coke and water in the mini-bar and to keep it stocked up, which took 3 days to get actioned.

Other gripes:  The resort is big, maybe too big and is a pita to navigate.  For example to get from 6th floor Pyramid 5 to the main breakfast area you need to go down to floor 2, walk through pyramid 4 to 3 and then down to the sub-ground level.

Compared to other 4/5* hotels in North America, Europe, and Asia this is at least 1-1.5 notches below.

I've started with three blobs, taken two off due to the above negative points, and added two on, purely because of the attitude of the staff members mentioned above, ending up back at 3 blobs

reviews.author: Sharon B
reviews.title: Interesting stay
reviews.text:
So... I'm on my fourth day of my eight say vacation at this resort and there's some good and bad. 

Good : nice looking resort

Bad : extremely cold pools (nobody even uses them), some of the restaurants taste so bad it's better off skipping dinner than eating at them (especially, fuego), when we first arrived everyone was willing to help us make dinner reservations and extremely helpful but they'd always end the conversation with asking if we had attended the timeshare presentation. Whenever I would tell them I'm not interested they'd immediately change their attitude. I eventually ended up saying yes to get a discount on an excursion and to receive a free four night stay (prolly won't be easy to get this) after being promised it would take 90 minutes max. I spent three full hours refusing the timeshare to the sales Rep that couldn't take no for an answer. After the presentation, I asked the staff to help me make a dinner reservation and all I got was someone pointing at a phone telling me to do it myself. 

They basically make you feel like you are here on some sort of free vacation because I am supposed to buy a timeshare. I paid 4000$ for this vacation and I don't owe them anything but I guess the staff were trained otherwise. 

The resort is nice looking and clean but if I were you I'd avoid ANY melia properties. The timeshare presentation was stressful and wasted three hours of my day

reviews.author: Michelle P
reviews.title: Fun in the sun
reviews.text: We stayed at paradisus for 5 nights. There were 3 of us and we requested 2 double beds, but I guess when you book the hotel states they will try to accommodate requests but nothing is guaranteed and we ended up with a king bed and rollaway bed for the first 3 nights.
