The first room we had was on an inside corner that didn't get much light or wifi. The room was kind of dank and nothing seemed to dry in it. We also had hot water problems. After 3 nights we moved next door to a room with two double beds (they are regular double beds not queen beds like you would get in the USA just fyi) this room was only next door but made a world of difference - much more sunlight, full wifi, things dried, no hot water problems. We were much happier in this room. The resort is beautiful and very modern. Gorgeous lobby, beautiful pools / beaches, excellent service, fun DJ at night. I was impressed with the food too - usually resort food is kinda blah but this food was actually good, especially the taqueria (blue agave was the restaurant name). We took a few of the gym classes which were fun and we were able to do outside on the beach. The day trip planner was extremely helpful and friendly in assisting us in booking day trips. The 3 things I felt this resort was lacking: an outdoor hottub for late in the afternoon when the sun goes down or if its a rainy / cold day out. Some type of towel rack or clothes line for the balcony to dry your wet clothes and also after around 3 pm the sun moves so it is on the lagoon side of the resort - so it would be nice to have an area to lay out on that side to catch a few afternoon rays. Overall we had a great time and were happy with our stay.

reviews.author: Karin F
reviews.title: Rules!!!
reviews.text:
Spent a glorious 8 days here, weather was pretty good even with the wind! 
Checking in was quick and efficient, and our bags were delivered to our room very quickly. The room itself was pretty large and the bed was two doubles pushed together.  There was no clock on the nightstand, but we did find it at the end of our stay. It was underneath the bed, as the nightstand was moved to accommodate the two beds being shoved together.There was the standard mini fridge with beers, some pop, chips and some cookies. There was also the usual coffee maker with instant milk powder. However disappointing was the fact that these items were not replaced on a daily basis, we had to phone for them if we wanted them re-filled. It was also difficult to get water re-fills.
There are quite a few restaurants here, but getting a reservation was a bit challenging. It appears that you must make a reservation 24 hours in advance, and if you try to make one after 5:00, you are out of luck. Most of our meals were taken at Noas, which if a buffet style overlooking the pool area. We went to this place and wanted a table for six, and were told by the hostess that we would have to sit at two tables. The tables are not nailed to the floor, so this sort of left us with an unwelcome feeling. Our waiter came, and seeing our situation, promptly put two tables together. The serving staff, no matter where we went, was amazing, not only professional, but also entertaining. 
One evening at Coco's bar, we had a server that we called "Ricardo Montalban", as he had an uncanny resemblance to this actor from Fantasy Island (hope I didn't age myself), and he was excellent at his job, as well as having a great sense of humour! We had many laughs that night. Job well done!
The restrooms are a bit sparse and all the restaurants on the first floor, all share the two public restrooms. So, you had to hike to one of them or go to your room.
We did have a cockroach visit us, and believe that it came up through the drain, but, this being the tropics, is not unheard of. Just cover or close the floor drains. We ordered a bottle of wine through room service one night, had about half the bottle. We had left the remainder on the dresser. The following night, we went to finish it off only to discover that it was gone :(  
We did go to the ruins, very, very well done, our guide was very knowledgeable, and then to the water park to snorkel. It was a fun filled day, even though it rained pretty hard!!
There are lots of walks to go on, one being the high end mall with Gucci, Armani, etc. 
The beaches could be a little cleaner as there are lots of cigarette butts, straws etc littering the sand.
Overall, our stay was pleasant, just found the rules a little bit constraining

reviews.author: Marc C
reviews.title: Bring a torch¡
reviews.text:
A mixture of the great, the strange and the dark at this hotel.  We stayed over Xmas & new year and I loved the Royal Service during the day, but at night things get strange.  Like the superb pool\beach side bar stops serving at 6pm.  So no evening drinks outside unless you are eating.  There is a self service bar area inside, but this closes at 10 pm.  So no after dinner drinks unless you go to the the only other bar and stand whilst being deafened by the music.
There are lots of great restaurants at the hotel, but you will need a torch to read the menus at many of them and to see the food.  You will also be very lucky if the food arrives even slightly warm. Which a shame as the food is very good, especially at the tapas restaurant (eat inside for great service and to avoid the noisy waterfall) or the sushi restaurant (use your torch to avoid falling into the Koy carp pond)!
And finally don't expect a gala dinner at Xmas and the hotel wanted 200 USD per person for a gala dinner on new years eve!  Not what I expected after spending nearly £3000 on my holiday.

reviews.author: Mary M
reviews.title: Great location .. Minor issues need correction
reviews.text: We stayed at Paradisus by Melia in Cancun in January and, for the most part, thoroughly enjoyed the resort.  There are lots of choices for dining and all the staff members were terrific.  The beach was right there.  However, for older folks, the constant, loud and unrelenting music from speakers at the beach and pool were inescapable.  It would have been nice to relax in peace and quiet, but that was not possible with the constant blare from speakers all over the place.  The rooms are good sized and comfortable but daily maid service was iffy.  We had to call for service very late in the afternoon on 2-3 occasions during our one week stay.  The balcony on our ocean front room was nice but we asked for a change of chairs and never got it.  We stayed on fifth floor and the ice machine was not working.  We reported that issue on our second day at the resort, and again on our third day and again on our fourth day.  When we left on our seventh day, the ice machine had not yet been repaired.  Lighting in the room was strange as well and hard to figure out what switch went to what light.  Other than the minor issues mentioned above, it was wonderful to be away from the cold winter weather and to a place of warmth and sunshine and friendly people.

reviews.author: Patrick G
reviews.title: Almost perfect
reviews.text: Imagine a gorgeous hotel on the best stretch of beach..great employees perfect sunshine..and then.. these geniuses turn up a sound system on the beach that would rival any rock concert...they play a heavy bass Latin rhythm that can be annoying 150 meters from the source..I am one who enjoys loud music.. this is truly deafening..the beach beds are not occupied due to this monstrosity..management seem oblivious to the fact that this music drowns out conversation and even the loud roar of the surf FIX IT.

reviews.author: whatmeow
reviews.title: Meh
reviews.text:
Overall the place is gorgeous and felt really tropical.  We stayed in the adults section and had the Royal Service, which was ok.  We enjoyed the snack/drink area set up for us often, which was good because the fridge restocking was hit/miss and after the first day no beer arrived again.  I got sick two mornings from the breakfast buffett,  all I had was some melon and coffee....we ate dinner at Blue Avage twice, everything was great there.

The bed was super comfortable.  We didn't spend as much time on the balcony as I would have hoped for, the only chairs available were lounge back chairs, and the concrete beam blocked a good portion of the view.

I would not stay here again as there are many other resorts to check out and enjoy rather than come back here and be underwhelmed.

reviews.author: Amaia M
reviews.title: Amazonic Mayan Paradise!
reviews.text:
I was taken aback, like other guests, by the amazon-like jungle decor from the inside of this gigantic five-pyramid complex. I was there with my colleague celebrating the publication of my book, but also we were there to work --to write. Both of us had deadlines pending so we decided to go to Cancun and work there. I had never been to the Paradisus before, and honestly, it was a matter of chance that I selected this hotel. I wanted to stay in Playa del Carmen, which is in the Riviera Maya but we decided last-minute and I didn't have a long time to select the vacation package. I decided to do an all-inclusive because I have done it before in Cancun and it's very comfortable no to have to think about finances when you're there (other than tips which I always leave, especially for the women who work behind the scenes but I'll get to that...). When we arrived we were upgraded to Royal Service after I told the front desk attendant that we were there to celebrate my publication. Let me just say WOW! Royal Service is amazing. First of all there are no children allowed and, no offense to people who chose to reproduce, that was very welcoming to me. No screaming, no running, no weird stuff in the pool, etc. That in and of itself was paradise. I concur with one of the reviews that though they told us the place was full, I hardly ever saw people in the pool or at the beach. This is due to the fact that they have five pyramids that are humongous so people are totally spread. I know that in the general area it was difficult for people to get a nice cabana by the pool whereas at the Royal Service, Bernardo and Arturo? who kept our reservations and we got a great place by the pool. The food was fabulous though after six days it starts to get boring... I really enjoyed the variety of restaurants although we were unable to go to two of them since they were always full. 
I appreciated the service at this hotel and the professionalism that all workers at this place have. They always say hello and give you the Paradisus ‘hello’ which is taking their right hand and placing in in their hearts (weird but it brings pride to workers because instead of them being invisible, guests acknowledge their presence and I liked that). So let's talk about labor: this hotel needs to be more balanced in terms of gender equity and workloads. On the one hand the waiters were always running around in all of the restaurants and the women in the buffets as well. Whereas the 'butlers' or others like the cabana boys in the Royal Service who spent most of their time chatting with each other and making reservations. Don't get me wrong they do work but the workload is definitely not balanced at all. The men waiters, bell-boys, valets, etc. make all the tips because they're all in front face-to-face with patrons whereas the women are in the background making your rooms, cooking, doing dishes, etc. This means all the tips go to the men and I find that horrible! That's why I'm giving this hotel only 'average' because they need to take care of their female employees way better than what they are doing now. Anytime I needed change for a $20 for tips guess who always had ones for change? the bell boys. So please when you go to the Paradisus be conscious of the women behind the scenes and TIP THEM! yes let me reiterate that TIP THEM! more than the cabana boys who make reservations, more than the guy who carries a couple of bags for like ten seconds, and take care of the smoothie woman at the breakfast buffet, or the woman preparing your eggs, and most importantly tip the women who make your room everyday! They have different shifts, so leave a TIP by the bathroom sink so they know it's for them or leave a note or something... be appreciative of the people who are working long hours for not a lot of money so that you may enjoy this amazing paradise. 
Having said all that yes, I recommend this hotel but I strongly advise the owners to re-structure their personnel so that women may be better compensated. They should have a tip pool and at the end of the day divide it among all of the workers. Just a thought.

reviews.author: ihatejjredick
reviews.title: Good......depending what you're looking for
reviews.text:
My buddy and I are in our early 30's and were looking for a fun spot to visit for a quick four day vacation. We stayed at Paradisus 1/16-1/19.

Pros:
- plenty of food options (note: room service for food included with all-inclusive)
- friendly staff
- buffet is good and available for all three meals for a quick meal
- great beach and pool bar
- very affordable
- very clean rooms

Cons:
- Very dated look and feel (included a 90 minute lip syncing Michael Jackson musical routine)
- Tons of amenities but you must seek them out constantly
- zero nightlife
- food is hit or miss
- Only four beers in fridge per day and they will charge if you want more

Overall I liked Paradisus but I wouldn't stay there again. Not because it is a bad place but because I'd rather see a different Cancun resort and see if I like it more.

Paradisus appeared to be perfect for older couples and families. Anyone looking for a party atmosphere or an ideal honeymoon spot will be disappointed.

If you want a relaxing, affordable vacation spot in Cancun you can do alot worse than Paradisus.

reviews.author: camp708
reviews.title: Nothing Special
reviews.text: Visited Paradisus for a 3 day business meeting with the all-inclusive package. Nice facility, but not new. In fact, while I was out at meetings, they actually did some painting in my room which resulted in a very toxic smell, strong enough to require me to change rooms. I travel a lot, never had a hotel touch-up paint in the room I occupied. Overall, the food was just OK with the seafood being the highlight. The beef steak I had at La Perla was a very thin cut and therefore not tender. The Japanese restaurant sushi was tasteless. The hotel was relatively empty yet it was not easy getting in the restaurants included in the all-inclusive deal because of the small seating capacity. The buffet did have a wide variety, but again, only the seafood stood out, while the rest was very average. The highlight was the staff - very friendly, spoke English well, and always greeted you with a smile. Paradisus is nothing special, but nothing real negative either other than the untimely painting of my room.

reviews.author: murdog
reviews.title: Just ok
reviews.text:
My sister and I came here for 3 nights.  We have been to Cancun many times, and have stayed at a handful of different places.  The service was good, and the hotel staff was friendly.  When we entered the hotel, we were led to a check in room as we passed by a large desk that looked as if it should be the check in area.  After waiting for around 20 minutes we were finally helped.  We got all checked in and went up to the room.  It was small.  We looked through the refrige area, looking for drinks.  Everywhere else that we have stayed has had top shelf alcohol in the rooms.  The bell hop came up with our luggage and said there was no alcohol in the rooms and that we would have to go downstairs to the bar.  
The accommodations were just ok.  The room never really cooled off.  The majority of the hotel was always very humid.  
The food was good at all of the restaurants that we went to.
We mainly went to Cancun just to relax by the pool and beach.  I must say that our favorite person in the whole place was Laura at the poolside bar.  She was very friendly and always kept our drinks filled- if we wanted them.  
When we travel together, my sister and I like to talk to other people, and maybe hang out with new friends for the duration of a trip.  There was really no one here our age (40's), with similar interests. 
We didn't find a lot of night life either.
Another con of this hotel is that they don't take US Dollars.  I found that very strange, and annoying.  Everywhere we have stayed is happy to take US.  I needed something from the gift shop and came in from the pool, wanting to just charge it to my room.  They said that I didn't have a credit card on file.  I know I presented it to them at check in.   I had to go all the way up to the room to get my credit card.
The check out process seemed to be odd too.  My sister had an earlier flight than I, so she left before me.  She had to get a check out card so that she could leave the hotel, although I was checking out a few hours later.  
After I had checked out, I was talking to the cab driver.  He said that there are some hotels that are marketed to Mexico City and other areas around Mexico.  Being from the US, I had no idea about this.  We won't stay here again.  I will stick with the Palace Resorts!!

reviews.author: riz513ca
reviews.title: Great service and grounds but...
reviews.text:
We decided on the Paradisus for a 9 night stay leaving out of Vancouver with WestJet Vacations. Total cost per person was approximately $2400 with a hotel stay over in Calgary while en-route.

The hotel itself was built in the early 90's and consists of 5 pyramids. Pyramid 3 is the center hub with all the night life and restaurants. We stayed in Pyramid 1 following the recommendations of other travellers for some peace and quiet. Pyramid 5 on the other end appeared to be where those who opted for the Royal Service resided. 

We were picked up by a shuttle which was quite convenient and dropped off at the hotel. Check in was fine with a welcome cocktail of our choice offered. Definitely a nice start. 

The Room - We had an ocean view junior suite with a large balcony and small hot tub on the outer deck. The room was spacious but dated. All the furniture was well worn and could have benefited from replacement. The bed was slanted on both sides which had us rolling towards the edges when we slept. Our final two nights involved a water leak coming from the floor above us that ran down through the light fixture in our bathroom. It made for quite a mess as the water would collect in the suspended ceiling and then drip down all over the floor. 

Staff did what they could and offered us a room change but given the late hour, the fact that it eventually tapered off and we only had one more night before departure, we decided to stick it out. Second night was a bit wetter and we were told that the water had to do with a leak in the upper suites shower. I think we may have taken them up on the room change had we known the problem wasn't fixed. Regardless, the staff were great and very apologetic. They supplied us with extra towels to mop up and all was good. 

The Timeshare Pitch - We were prepared for this and know it's very common. We were offered a free massage, a half price tour and a bottle of tequila to attend (never did get the tequila tho). We toured the property and were informed of the various properties around the world that are part of Melia resorts. It was informative but not nearly enough to motivate us to make a decision right then whether or not we wanted to spend $50,000 without doing any research on our own. We asked for a few days to look into things ourselves prior to making a decision but that's not how it's done. 

The Food - Paradisus has multiple a la carte restaurants. We visited them all. Again service was excellent but the food, at least for us, was simply average. We noted that with the exception of the buffet, all food was served in small portions so consider ordering a bit more than you normally would to share. Food was readily available either by dining within the hotel or ordering room service. 

The Pools and Beach - Beautiful pools that were well maintained. At time it was a bit difficult to get a seat as there was a common practice of people staking out their territory in the morning and then not returning until late morning or early afternoon to take up their seats. It was posted that belongings left for longer than 30 minutes would be removed but I'd imagine this would be difficult to enforce. With a little footwork though, you will be able to find a spot either by the pools or beach. Again, we found the service very good. One thing we noticed about the beach was that it was windy and the water quite rough. It had been red flagged for swimming a number of times. I'm not sure if this is characteristic to this side of the island or if it simply was the time we were there but we didn't experience even one day where the water was calm and the winds weren't heavy. 

The Final Say - Overall and almost without exception, the service was excellent. The staff were kind and cordial and very accommodating. The pool and beach were beautiful and appearance and decoration of the hotel in the evening was beautiful. Unfortunately for us, the room quality and food fell short. In retrospect, the price paid for the package just didn't seem to be a good deal. At $255 per person per night, I'd consider simply getting a room at one of the many hotels up and down the strip and spending a bit more time exploring and dining out.

reviews.author: Tristan S
reviews.title: Beautiful accommodation with inconsistent service and terrible operations management
reviews.text:
I stayed here for a full week with my wife and another couple. This was our first time staying in Mexico so I can only compare it to other international accommodation. We booked through RCI which the other couple had a membership in, so I cannot comment on the booking process except to say that the price was extremely inexpensive for the value we received. The room for a full week was less than $300 USD _total_ and the all-inclusive fee was $84 per person per night. We got that price by booking half a year ago before their price hike. I have heard that the all-inclusive fee is now around $200 for new bookings at this time of year, which in my opinion would be a very poor value.

First the good. The resort and beach are beautiful, assuming you don't mind some seaweed. The waves were complex, which made for great fun playing in the ocean, but it would not be good for people that want to actually swim, and there are no real lap pools. That was fine for us since we are not avid swimmers.

The buffet food quality was surprisingly good--probably the best I've had at a buffet (but I'm no buffet expert)--and the variety and quality of alcohol included in the all-inclusive plan was generous. There was also no push-back on quantity. If anything they had the opposite problem of occasionally overserving guests. (We ourselves had too much one afternoon and regretted it.)

We thoroughly enjoyed the trip, but there are a lot of things that the hotel could do better. Service was very inconsistent. Some servers and bartenders were eager to please, but many more tended to forget orders, disappear for long periods, etc. The table service at the buffet was particularly bumpy. We were never once seated at a table that was fully set-up. Tables were always missing something such as napkins or  coffee cups and sometimes even had dirty napkins. In one hilarious case we were seated at a table where every setting had two knives on the left and right and no other cutlery.

The main problem though was terrible operations management. The system for reserving the non-buffet restaurants shows it the most. Other than Blue Agave, all the non-buffet restaurants ostensibly require reservations, which can be made at most one day in advance and must be made either by phone or by physically going to a single desk in the center of the resort. This desk is supposed to be open from 9 to 5 and people line up before 9 to have first pick. The staff enter the reservations into a computer and issue a printed slip with the reservation details. At some point, someone transfers the information to paper reservation books at each restaurant. Obviously this is inherently error-prone, and one night we ended up with a printed slip that said 7:30 even though the restaurant was expecting us at 7:00.

In addition to the inherent ridiculousness of this process, on Wednesday no one showed up to staff the desk. It was over a half hour before someone in the know came by to inform everyone in line that the desk was not going to be open at all that day (information that was not communicated in advance anywhere AFAWCT). The hotel then placed a staff member at the desk to simply inform guests that showed up that the desk was closed! It was only at this point that we learned that the phone line to make reservations did not simply call that desk but rather went to a call center of some sort. However, calls we made were not picked up, and even the hotel concierge was unable to get through to anyone. We eventually managed to get reservations in late afternoon.

Strangely, the non-buffet restaurants were never visibly full, yet it was always hard to get reservations for the day and time that we wanted. Perhaps the reservation process is so frustrating that few people are willing to make the effort to cancel reservations that they no longer need. We did find that walk-ins are sometimes accepted (contrary to stated policy).

Another area of poor operations management is the cabanas/balinesas. They have an all-paper system for paid reservations charged to the room, yet there was much confusion about the price. One person told us $25 USD per cabana per day, one told us $20, and the actual bill at check-out was $10. On one occasion, we went to reserve beach cabanas for the next day and were told we could have cabana numbers 216 and 217. However, when we went to the beach the next day we discovered that cabanas 216 and 217 did not exist. Luckily there were still two cabanas available, although not adjacent.

This brings me to the poor maintenance of the beach cabanas. The beach cabanas (unlike the poolside cabanas) are open-sided structures with a fabric roof and fabric curtains that can be tied down to create a windbreaker, which works surprisingly well except when the curtains are torn or missing, which was almost always. Of the dozen or so beach cabanas, only a few had enough intact curtains to provide adequate wind protection, and when I asked the staff on one occasion for additional curtains they said they did not have any. To be clear, the poolside cabanas are a different design and were mostly out of the wind. Being at the same price, they were clearly preferable, and reservations for them tended to fill up more than one day in advance. I do recommend that you reserve at least a day in advance because there is a turn-up service that we didn't always get when we made a same-day cabana reservation. However, you would probably not be able to reserve anything before check-in. Even the spa was poorly set up to take reservations from outside the hotel. We looked in to booking spa services in advance and found that, although an online reservation form exists, the brochure of services and their prices is not posted anywhere.

Lastly I will mention check-out. It is 10 AM, which was a bit of a surprise given that check-in is 4 PM. My guess is they want to employ as few housekeeping staff as possible. But what ticked me off was that our bill was in pesos yet, without asking, they charged me in USD with a 3% currency conversion fee. When I asked about the presence of a USD amount on the receipt, the check-out agent said that that was just for my information and that the transaction would be in pesos. Only later when I read the fine print on the receipt did I see that that was untrue. It only cost me an extra $30, but it's the principle of the thing! If you know that your credit card gives you a fair currency conversion rate, I recommend that you insist at check-out to be charged in pesos.

So with so many problems, why 3 stars, you ask? Well, at the right price, all-you-can-eat-and-drink and a beautiful beach go a long way ...

reviews.author: IreneZCPA
reviews.title: Average hotel in Cancun
reviews.text:
Pros: beautiful design of the hotel. 
Cons: old, not well cooked food, rooms, service.

I have been in this hotel on January,1-6. I am New-Yorker. I have been several times in Mexico and before I was living in Secrets hotels.
Paradisus made a mixed impression. From one point of view, it is fine. From another: it is outdated and overrated.
Check-in. Instead of being welcomed by converge, we have been sent to the front desk area which reminds fast-food place. Nobody told us anything about the hotel. No information was given. We had to explore this hotel on our own.
Room. It is really old and small. Nothing to talk about. Due to high season we didn't get any chairs on balcony.
Beach. You need to wake up really early to reserve you beach chair. Without it you are going to lay on sand and be ignore by waiters. They have VIP Royal area as well. For additional charge you will get service that you are expected to get any way from a good Mexican hotel. People here said that it is hard to get a chair at the beach but once I saw that outside Mexican man not guest came and paid some money to guys and got two chairs to enjoy the beach. Along with chairs he got drinks and towels while guests were laying on the sand.
Food. Seafood smells like antibiotics or some chemicals. Stake house Le Perla is a joke. Do not go there under any circumstances. Food was average and really nothing to talk about. 
Service. I know it is a high season, but still service was not Mexican level. 

Summary. Comparing with Secrets this hotel is 3+ stars. It doesn't worth money they ask for. The only good thing is a beach, but beach is everywhere the same. I would prefer to stay away from this place.

reviews.author: Brooklynite_Abroad
reviews.title: Now a Paradisus, but the same old Gran Melia it always was
reviews.text:
The setting:  This is the former Gran Melia Cancun, recently rebranded as Paradisus Cancun.  If you have stayed at other Paradisus resorts, you will be quite disappointed.  I stay at this property every couple of years and there wasn’t a single discernable difference about this property from a few years ago to its current reincarnation as a Paradisus.  The lobby is spacious and impressive, although dated.  The rooms are standard issue.
The room:  We stayed at a Royal Service room, which appears as any other room at the hotel.  The only difference is that there won’t be any children staying in the Royal Service pyramid, which is the north most of the five pyramids in the hotel.  The only advantage to Royal Service is the adults only pool which is located where the Level beach was.  We stayed here at the end of September and the Royal Service beach was packed.  Finding a bali bed/palapa with a nice view of the beach was impossible.  The super discounted rates for Royal Service (@$200/night vs the usual @$1000/night at other true Paradisus resorts) meant that this property was packed even during the off peak season.  The butler service, which comes with Royal Service was subpar as well; ours fully forgot to reserve our bali beds.
The food:  The breakfast buffet is the sole decent offering at this property.  The Mexican restaurants are decent but definitely skip the Asian and continental options.  This is a shame as Cancun has great restaurants so the chefs do not have to approximate other cuisines, they can try quality Asian and continental food outside of the hotel and recreate the flavors.  The mandatory all inclusive at this rebranded Paradisus is a major negative, as I would have rather paid less for the room and enjoyed the dining options outside of the hotel.
All in all, I found this property to be a solid choice when it was a Gran Melia.  As a mandatory all inclusive Paradisus, it just doesn’t hit the product quality that I have experienced and have to expect from a Paradisus.  I hope the Melia chain truly upgrades this hotel.  My biggest gripe is the need to fight for a bali bed; that should never happen at a Paradisus, especially when there was never a lack of these at the Level, during Gran Melia times.

reviews.author: nora d
reviews.title: Tired rooms, not enough sun lounges, great buffet.
reviews.text:
Stayed in pyramid one, the rooms are very tired and the A/C is so loud. The lobby area is stunning, the beach is also great. 
The only problem is trying to gets sun lounger, the ones they do have on the beach are falling apart. There are Bali beds,$50 a day, loads around the pools weren't being used but people were sat on towels on the ground. Unacceptable. I have never had this problem at a hotel.
Naos buffet was great, fabulous selection and very fresh.
The kids club was fantastic, the staff were very patient with my 2 children and they had a great time.
I would love to return but don't fancy sitting on a sandy towel on the beach everyday.

reviews.author: rudy1428
reviews.title: Duet to Die For
reviews.text: Last night 12/29/14 my family and I ate at Bana.  The sushi and entire dining experience was mediocre at best.  Luckily midway through this meal we heard the most melodic beautiful voices I have ever had the pleasure of hearing.  The duet sang from opera to disney songs hitting every note pleasing even the seemingly most disinterested people at the bar.  My children were driven to dance my wife and I to tears.  An incredible duet who everyone should have the pleasure to hear.  Bravo, we are hoping for an encore tonight.

reviews.author: Joseph P
reviews.title: $12,000 for this?
reviews.text: 3 rooms with family concierge, don't waste your $ for perceived extras. Turn down service only 2 out of 4 nights so far. Asked for fresh towels over an hour ago and still waiting. Rusty light fixtures and AC that is barely "functional". Rooms need a major update. Forget getting beach or pool chairs unless you are up the crack of dawn to "save" your spot. Wifi soso. Food is OK. Beverages are OK. Major kudo's to the staff as service by beach/pool/restaurant is excellent. Last Christmas we stayed at the Fiesta Americana Grand Coral and it is 2 stars better; a real 5 star.

reviews.author: Doc Sam
reviews.title: Not what I expected
reviews.text:
Just got back from 8 day stay over Christmas at this resort.  Couldn't get Playa del Carmen for our family of 8 (9, 11, 13 and 17 year-olds) so settled for Cancun.  Have been a Club Melia Member since 2013 and usually go to Punta Cana but wanted to try the other Paradisus resorts.  This one is not in the same caliber as the others:

Service - more hit than miss.  The majority of the time, we received extremely friendly and attentive care.  Our best to Jose (cabana attendant) and Orlando/Hebert (restaurant waiters).  They made us forget about most of the misses i.e. unable to accommodate a party of 8 at the buffet most of the time so needed to split us up into 2 tables, waiting for our drinks half-way into our dinner.

Accommodations - this is where we were shocked by.  Since we were Club members, we were placed in Pyramid 1 where members typically stay at.  We booked 7 months in advance and the room that we got absolutely shocked us: ground level, "lagoon-view" but actually facing the parking lot and CONSTRUCTION right outside our bedroom window?  There was some loud banging going on throughout the day (some loose structure being blown by the winds and hitting the side of the hotel wall) keeping us awake for the 3 nights that we had to stay there until they could find us a more suitable replacement - which was much better with an ocean view!  Thank you Nikki!

Amenities - also hit and miss.  Great pool-side service and easy to get a Bali bed/lounge chair - no reserving with a book or towel allowed which is great!  No water sports really - the waves are too strong by the beach so all you can do is run in and out of the water before being pummeled by 5-foot waves.  They have free paddle boats and kayaks across the street at the Aquatic Center on the lagoon side (a lot of paid water excursions originate from here - try the "Fish Spa"!)
Not much night life nor kids activities for teenagers - ours preferred to play with their iPads in the AC-rooms when not at the pool!  

Ambience - must admit, very pretty resort but definitely some areas showing their age i.e. crumbling corners in the walls of some of our rooms, malfunctioning door locks, leaking ceilings in the hallways.

Food - more hit than miss also.  Best were Market Grill (Argentinian-style meats), Blue Agave (great tacos), room service (wings were the best) and Naos (buffet-style - only place for breakfast but changes just slightly enough every day to make it noticeably different).  So-So: Tempo (tapas-style but too small servings), Bana (sushi not great quality).  Horrible - pool-side grill (over-cooked burgers, tasteless pizza and a different type of Buffalo wings that were too dry).

Miscellaneous - we have always felt special at the Punta Cana resorts being Club members but in Cancun, this did not occur at all.  Although we wore different bracelets, there did not seem to be anything special about being a Club member at this resort.  They had a club lounge but there were no snacks/desserts/special drinks available for us.  Free internet use via desk tops but NO PRINTER.  Had to go 2 Pyramids over, downstairs to the Market and print it there and be charges 8 pesos per sheet!  I get my Boarding passes printed for free at a Holiday Inn Express whenever I happen to be in one in the states....come on!!!  

Bottom line - this resort needs to overhaul their rooms and amenities if they want to deserve the Paradisus branding.  Will be going to Paradisus Playa del Carmen in March - we'll see if they fair better.

reviews.author: 609jayr
reviews.title: More Fluff Than Substance
reviews.text: My husband and I had a lovely get-a-way with beautiful weather, buts lots of attention was given to the appearance of the hotel, rather than to practical usage. Examples: 1) Room décor beautiful and very spacious but much of the space was wasted and lighting was not very functional.  2) We are not gourmets, but the quality of the food in all the restaurants was uniformly disappointing. 3) None of the whirpool tubs were heated. 4)  All the common areas were beautifully decorated, but the hallways were oblique and it was hard to find your way around the hotel. 5)  There was no real entertainment to speak of.  6) The rooms were not soundproof and the heavy furniture scraped loudly on the marble floors when moved. 7)  The massage and reflexology were lovely, but the rest of the water therapy area was very disappointing.  All hotel staff were very friendly.

reviews.author: RachelSt.Louis
reviews.title: Nice Resort, Lacking Service
reviews.text:
I should start by saying that we have visited Cancun area resorts at least 10 times, but this was our first trip to bring our kids (6 and 4), as well as the first time we were there for a reason other than vacation (a wedding.) So it was a different kind of trip for us in general,which probably colors some of my feelings about Paradisus. It is a nice property, the lobby is gorgeous, and the beach is excellent. I have a feeling there are a lot of great things at this property - but the problem is no one explained anything to us about the resort. We had to ask other family members or stumble upon things (Kids Club!) on our own. I'm used to being told about amenities when you check in, but other than being told two of the restaurants were not included in the "all inclusive" we weren't told much. 
We never did find an indoor bar to hang out at, and when we did get to order drinks at pool bars/restaurants they seemed incredibly weak. I also felt like I was a burden to the bar staff when I'd order a drink. At least 3 times when I was at dinner/lunch I was never approached to be given a glass of water. I had to hunt down a waiter to get one. It was very odd - I've never felt like I was imposing to ask for a drink at other resorts! I definitely didn't feel "welcomed" there. 
On the upside, as I mentioned earlier the beach is beautiful. The sand and ocean access are great. The wedding was gorgeous as well, in a gazebo overlooking the ocean. 
So, a bit of a mixed bag on this resort - and I might have a different take if I'd been there without kids as well.

reviews.author: Christie B
reviews.title: Royal Service or don't bother!
reviews.text:
We just returned from our weeks stay on the Royal service side in a one bedroom suite as a couple plus one friend. This will be lengthy but honest as we travel to Cancun every year and usually stay at Riu resorts. I don't not recommend this hotel unless you are staying in Royal service or travelling as a family with small children.

Upon arrival our room was ready and it was almost what we expected. Two bathrooms, one king bed and one pull out, two balconies but no doors on the separate rooms like the photos show. The balconies are equip with one sun lounger each which we put together on the one balcony and enjoyed daily. We would order room service and lay out while waiting for it to arrive then heading down to the pool. The room was cleaned daily except for one day which I'm certain was the maids day off. We always had fresh towels and if we didn't they arrived within 5 minutes of calling, no different than any other hotel. The beds are comfortable but the pillows are small so you just have to call and order a few extra if needed. Our mini bar was stocked daily and we used several bottles of vodka in our room that was replenished daily by our butler.

The butler service was nice to have he made our reservations daily, made sure we had a bali bed reserved at the pool daily, replenished our vodka and cranberry in the room daily and retrieved ice for us. Our butler was Hector who was fabulous!!! We tipped him well on day one and day 7 because he earned it. He would catch us in the hall getting our own ice and demand we let him help and go get it. He found us at our bali bed every day to ensure we weren't in need of anything and to see if we wanted dinner reservations. He also confirmed transportation to the airport and bell boy service on our last day. He was awesome and a great help!!

The food...
As I said at the start I am used to Riu resorts. That means I'm used to huge buffets with giant fresh salad bars, endless fruits and countless choices of food from all sorts of countries. The buffet was small with minimal choices and not a lot of seating. We only ate there twice and we expected far better food according to previous reviews. I'm a huge buffet fan so this was rather disappointing. I stuck to the salad bar and the odd pasta dish. If you like seafood then this will be the right place for you. 

We ate at Blue Agave, Vento and Market Grill. Market Grill being our favourite and blue agave being our least favourite. Blue agave serves salty bland tacos with cheese on them and that's it. We added pico de gallo and gaucamole but it didn't help much. No flavour and overly salted but I found that was common in most areas...possibly because I don't use salt at home that often. The service was great though.

Vento is a tapas restaurant so you choose 6-10 different items and they come as very small portions. Most of it was average but the steak with truffled potatoes was delicious as was the onion soup. The service is very slow here so plan to spend some time waiting for food. It was average food overall. Out of 8 different selections I really enjoyed 2 and the drinks.

We ate at the Market Grill twice. The first night was ceasar salad, potatoes, vegetables and plenty of different steaks and other meats. This place is a meat lovers dream! They bring 6-8 different meats around hot off the grill and slice it at your table. You eat until your full and get seconds of everything you love. The steaks were great the first night but overcooked and some what dry the second night. The second night the sides weren't very good as they offered rice with beans, fried banana and some potato. We preferred the first nights choices and meats. Again, great service.

We ate breakfast via room service every day. Canadian Bacon is just sliced ham and the omelettes are delicious. We were happy to eat in our room every morning and the rest of the room service menu was great as well. We tried a bit of everything and the only disappointing order was the tuna sandwich as it was more like a tuna burger. The room service menu is great and they hardly every make a mistake. They forgot extra ketchup some mornings but were quick to fix it. The lady who takes the order over the phone is not very friendly and she sounds annoyed by every order. The food arrives within 30-45 minutes which I don't feel in unreasonable and it all arrives hot and with a smile. We always tipped a few dollars to whomever delivered it. 

La Palapas was delicious! This is a Royal service exclusive located by the pool and either delivered to your bali bed or you can sit at tables and watch the ocean. The guacamole and pico de gallo was my absolute favourite and the boys loved the burgers and flatbreads. I had them make the chicken wrap with guacamole and pico de gallo instead of beans and it was the most delicious creation ever. 

The royal service buffet/snack bar was lacking. The booze was great but they hardly ever had food out, usually just some lunch meat and a few buns. 

The service throughout the hotel was consistently great. All the employees say hello and ask you how your day is. The waiters are attentive at the pool and most brought more drinks without having to be asked. We always tipped a few dollars throughout the days as for quality of booze, top shelf is available when asked for. If you don't ask for it then you won't get it. I was annoyed by the avenue bar because I was told I have to pay $8usd for top shelf vodka....but every other bar it was included. Very annoying and the waitress there seemed annoyed by us asking.

The entertainment is done at the front of the avenue bar in the main building and there is little to no room. I don't even know why they bother. They constantly ask people go move out of the way so the performers can get by and then the onlookers can't see. They need to fix this. Even having it take place out by the pool or something would be better...anywhere with more room. We watched one show and that was it.

The royal service pool was warm and quiet, we loved it. There is a hot tub there but it is not hot...it's actually colder than the pool. I suggest making it an actual hot tub. There is also a small pool near the wedding gazebo with the beds built into it to lay out but it was also ice cold.

The main pool is crowded and cold, you can't sit comfortably at the swim up bar because the water is freezing and the sun doesn't get to the seats until late afternoon and it's very brief. The pool is also over run with small children screaming and splashing so you can't enjoy a drink without wanting to yell at a few disrespectful kids who have no regard for the people around them in the the pool. It's a large pool and the little ones don't need to hang out by the bar splashing everyone. I think all pools with swim up bars should be adult only as there is zero reason for kids to be jumping off the stools and playing around the bar. 

There was never any trouble getting chairs on the royal service side as out butler reserved us a bali bed every day and we would get 3 sun loungers with it. The regular pool you have to get up at 6am to get a chair by the pool and I'm so thankful we only had to deal with that one time. There are plenty of towels and the royal service side doesn't require towel cards so we got 6-8 towels a day for the bali bed, our sun loungers and to use after swimming. I don't know what it's like on the regular side.

The beach is huge. It's man made in cancun and I'm not sure if everyone knows that or not. So it does wash away eventually. Lots of sun loungers on the beach, just find some and pull them together. They have the umbrellas for use of drag them out near the water to be away from the crowd.

We were treated like royalty on the royal service side until our last full day when a huge group of "Power Home" employees arrived. There had to be hundreds of them and the whole hotel turned into one big advertisement for their company leaving us feeling very out of place. It was like the "regular" guests no longer mattered and we were only in the way. They reserved all the bali beds by the pool and didn't use a single one which was annoying to us who would've used one closer to the pool for the entire day. On the morning we were leaving they started blasting music at the pool via dj and 4 huge speakers at 8am waking us up well before we wanted to be and I'm sure we were not the only ones. I made a quick phone call to the royal service desk and it was quickly shut off but the damage was done and we were now wide awake. Very very annoying. We were then disturbed about 10-15 times by maids and other employees basically harassing us to leave the room well before check out time of noon so they could prepare our room for the power home people moving in that day. They had already plastered our door the day before with their tacky power home banners with the next guests names on them. It was extremely annoying to have to keep answering the door every 15 minutes as we tried to shower, pack and prepare to leave. The same maid entered our room without knocking at least 5 times. The maids also knock once and then open the door immediately without saying a word, they got a few glimpses of nudity as they invaded our privacy quite frequently that day. I found this extremely rude and uncomfortable. This happened a few other times on our trip, the employees need to knock once and wait more than 10 seconds before entering. As soon as noon hit we were bombarded with phone calls to leave the room while we waited for the bell boy to come get our luggage. The bell boy also stole $50 for one of our wallets in the time from taking the luggage from our room to the lobby. We were very turned off by how we were treated on the last two days because we weren't part of this huge power home group. I am SO glad we were leaving, after they arrived the service went completely down hill as soon as they did.

An important tip regarding the bali beds is that if you do not check in at the royal service pool by 11am then you lose your bali bed reservation and it's first come first served after that. If you don't like the bali bed assigned to you then you can switch to another come 11am, so don't sweat if you don't get a reservation as it's easy to get one come 11am. 

There is little to no nightlife at the hotel but we didn't mind as we wanted to go downtown anyway. The bars downtown are always fun but the men's washrooms are filled with drug dealers, just something to be aware of. The staff at all the nightclubs are helpful and ensure the tourists are safe. If you act stupid downtown then yes you will find trouble, just be respectful and don't get blackout drunk and you're fine. There is nothing like the nightlife of downtown cancun so no matter what hotel you stay at you have to experience it.

The location of this hotel is good, it's about 15 from the airport and 10 from the bars. $15usd cab ride to town.

The scents around the hotel are nice but some days they were really overpowering. You walk through doors sometimes and it's like a slap in the face, some days they were fine. The hotel is very clean and well maintained, it's up to date and there are always staff maintaining it. 

I wouldn't recommend this hotel on the regular side for anyone without small children. It's all young families with young kids. I would recommend the royal service side but expect to be treated like a basic peasant if they have a large group like this "power home" group show up as their money is obviously more important than the regular folk. We will continue to stay at the Riu resorts as the food and nightlife is far superior. We paid $1500 each including airfare for our trip to Paradisus but I wouldn't pay anymore for it just because of the lack of food options and the lack of activities and now they have left a bad taste in my mouth with the constant harassment on the last room to vacate the room...as well as the lack so respect for privacy some of the staff have.

We were also called each morning to come get our welcome package in the lobby which was also really annoying. I told them several times I wasn't booking excursions or buying jewelry and I had no interest in many thing else they wanted to sell me. Some days they called 3 times before 10am but I believe this was BD Travel not the hotel. But really really annoying. We never picked up the welcome package because we were so annoyed by being harassed to go get it.

Overall this hotel receives a 3.5/5 from me. I found the royal service to be great but our great impression was quickly ruined on the last two days due to being pushed aside and being treated like a nuisance once the large group of power home employees showed up. The food was average in most areas and lacking overall for options. The staff was great other than the disrespectful maid staff who disregard your privacy and just enter your room. I would suggest booking here for a large conference or the like but we will be going with Riu resorts for our future yearly vacations to Cancun.

reviews.author: fastFish55
reviews.title: Paradisus under new directorship
reviews.text:
First, the good part: they do have good food selections at the buffet: there were new offerings every day and excellent selection so eating in the buffet would probably be the best choice. Especially with kids.

Other restaurants are decent but if you are traveling as a large group (anything over 6), you better be ready to eat at 6 or you will be hanging around for hours waiting for your table, with nothing to do. They don't take reservations, so you need to send someone to get in line... Unnecessary aggravation you don't need on your vacation. 

The biggest upset for us however was almost complete lack of entertainment during the day. Fun latin music will only be played for a few hours a day, soft elevator kind after that. One or two activities at the pool on a good day, volleyball on the beach, same time, every day. We were excruciatingly bored. The beach is nice but you will have to fight waves to get into the ocean (definitely not a place for those who like swimming in the ocean). But that is everywhere in the hotel zone. It was explained to us that the resort received a new director recently who wants the theme to be a "complete relaxation". 

Another strange thing is entertainment in the evening: every day could not help but feel bad for the great dancers, singers and acrobats who perform there. Not even sure how to describe the location where they perform, it's a relatively small opening in front of a bar, so to see anything you have to either reserve the couches around the area or stand all around. Really strange choice, haven't encountered something like that in years of traveling to the caribbean. 

Overall, the resort wasn't a good match for our style and we would not rate it more than 3,5 starts.

reviews.author: darleytravel
reviews.title: The potential for 'excellent' is there, but NOT present
reviews.text:
The first impression, the lobby, is breathtaking.  I was mesmerized.  For a moment or two.  Our group check-in was swift, and the usual string bracelets Paradisus is known for were quickly attached for our 'branding' and we were set to head to our rooms.

I was in a double-bedded room with a small sofa, table, 2 chairs, and ample closet and drawer space.  The bidet in the bathroom was a treat to see as I'd thought that nice feature was a thing of the past.  Bathroom amenities were minimal, but all worked.  Every toilet seat I'd used in conference center, public areas, and my bathroom all were incorrect sizes, and as such, would capture the pinchiest bit of flesh with each use.  OUCH!  I did see that staff tried putting rolled up hunks of TP under them to try to mitigate this pinching, but it was pretty ineffective.  To KNOW that this issue exists and do nothing more permanent to fix it is really two marks off their scores.

Food was mostly buffet, and the foods were not heated adequately.  This was a concern, and something I do check whenever I do site inspections of resorts/hotels.  Desserts were lacking (Jell-o cheesecake?), and food, in general, was average.   One exception was the Agave eatery.  I thought the drinks, service and food there were excellent.

Maid service was erratic.  Disco - a JOKE.  There is no dance floor, and the 'dj' played various versions of 'Blurred Lines' at least 10 x throughout the day and evening.  

re: the Conference Center, it was adequate, but the placement of rest rooms in relation to some of the meeting areas was ridiculously far.  Also, there is NO way a wheelchair-bound person could negotiate entrance to the conference rooms.  No elevators, and the strangest array of stairs/escalators and obstacles one can imagine.

reviews.author: ebriganti
reviews.title: food was very bland, very little activities, no nite life what so ever.
reviews.text: the hotel was beautiful and very clean, not impressed with the food or activities, had a situation in the ocean called for help multiple times no lifeguard came to help! Also checking in took forever!

reviews.author: floridagirl2223
reviews.title: Not a great spot for a wedding.
reviews.text:
We hosted a wedding party for 40+ in-house guests last weekend. 
We intended to have a royal service room for my husband, daughter and I, but found out that no one under 18 could stay in that tower, so we opted for what we were told was the family option of a similar service; the "Family Concierge Service". It basically entails having a cell phone that connects you directly with your butler. We thought this would help us get dinner reservations since we had a large group, but upon arrival (and after it was paid in full) we were told their restaurants no longer accepts reservations, and it's first come first served. We found the family concierge to be a waste of money. They didn't always answer, the reception was not clear and their English was difficult to understand in person and almost impossible on a staticky cell phone. They were supposed to leave cookies and milk in the room for kids (we had to call once bc they forgot) but this is not really any added luxury since the resort is all inclusive and cookies and dessert are everywhere. Our reservation was for 3 and were were told the one bedroom jr suite would accommodate, but we found out upon arrival the jr suites all only had one king bed. If we wanted 2 beds we'd have to get a cot or a double room which wasn't a jr suite which we paid for... It would be a much smaller room with only one bathroom. So we opted to stick with the one bed and cot option which was turned into my daughter sleeping with us every night bc the bed was so hard she couldn't sleep in it. Seems like they may have offered us an upgrade since we're were misled to believe it would sleep 3 (and were hosting a wedding!) but that didn't happen. 

The structure itself seems old. Lots of AC problems (ours had to be repaired during our stay) there were puddles in many of the common areas and walkways from leaking AC units.  They were very nice and punctual repairing it though. Our balcony door was corroded and wind seeped through which didn't really both us, but I could see how if could bother those who need it quiet to sleep. The curtains were thick and darkened the room well, but ours were badly mildewed on the inside. The showers were a bit of a challenge - the handheld and shower worked but the water wouldn't come directly from the faucet to draw a bath, has to use the handheld to fill the tub. Our room had plenty of space and closets were large but only 3 drawers for 3 people was insufficient. It has 2 flat screen TVs. The thing that bugged us most about the room was on the balconies there are very large planters filled with dirt - intended for flowers/plants. Some rooms did have greenery in their planters but ours did not. It was very unsightly to have big containers of dirt diminishing our beautiful view. We were in building 4, which is a nice location - away from the noisy club and centrally located. It is next to building 5, Royal Service. As I mentioned were hosting a wedding and the majority of our guests were in the Royal Service building. I think royal service may actually be worth the extra money bc they have a private pool, keyed entry into their private building, as well as butler service. This is a very large resort and the beach is amazingly beautiful. I would not recommend having a wedding here however bc it's just too big, MANY things with the wedding did not go as planned - too many to even begin to mention. My step-daughter is an event planner in Denver so she knows what she's doing.  Our experience was filled with miscommunications.  

The food was mediocre, service was hit or miss - some places were fast, some slow. We ordered burgers one day at lunch and after 45minutes they finally arrived and were awful - processed meat and under cooked. Room service for lunch was the best bet: Tuna burger, chicken ciabatta, and key lime pie were our favorites. If you like good sushi, don't go to the sushi restaurant; you'll be disappointed. The Mole was probably our best meal. My husband had grouper and I had shrimp. 

We loved playing volleyball on the beach at 11 and 3 everyday. Nice court and plenty of players made it a lot of fun.  The tennis court needs to be resurfaced, I felt it was actually more of a liability rather than a value added feature, it's peeling up and unsafe for competitive play. 

The beach is beautiful, but there are not enough chairs on the beach or pool for all guests. It was a race every morning to get a spot - really hated this!  There was a lot of seaweed and other resorts had employees raking it up, would have been nice if this resort did that also. Workout room was very nice and  well equipped, but no one under 18 allowed so this again was an inconvenience for us. 

The staff was friendly, the shows were entertaining, the atrium is filled with beautiful greenery and tropical smells.  

One of our wedding guests was a late addition and didn't get in with our "group rate", and he actually got a better price than the rest of us online. That was a complete slap in the face for me who spent 10s of thousands of dollars at the resort during the week and our guests likely brought in even more.  I suppose we were expecting too much since there were so many great trip advisor reviews. We have traveled extensively and stayed at many resorts throughout the Caribbean and Mexico, and I feel this resort was not worthy of any more than 3 stars.

reviews.author: Sherry19841105
reviews.title: Disorganized and disoriented dinner!
reviews.text:
Their trick is to make you wait between 1 - 2 hours for a group of 4. This encourages you to eat at the cheaper buffet. Even though multiple tables are available.

No concept of joining tables to seat bigger groups even though multiple are available.

Portion size is surprisingly very small - especially the entrees.

Highly inefficient wait staff.

If you get a baby sitter to enjoy a quiet dinner - make sure you have the sitter for atleast 3 - 4 hours as it takes forever to get seated and significantly long for food to arrive.

Drinks are extremely watered down and not premium quality.

reviews.author: NerissaB451
reviews.title: After three days I have decided to leave early
reviews.text:
I should have read the hotel reviews more critically but we stayed at the Paradisus Palma Real in Punta Cana, and loved it! I really did not see a need to comb through traveler revews for this hotel - unfortunately.
The hotel itself is beautiful and humongous
The food is ok. There is decent variety 
The room is ok but nothing spectacular
The WiFi in room is good, the range is not great. Hence, it difficult to use devices in the pool area...
Definately not wowed by the service. Some of the cleaning staff actually seem BITER!
The place is overun with kids. Running everywhere! We probably should have stayed at the "adults only" location
The coffee (cappuchino) is great! 

I have had enough and we are checking out tomorrow.  We will check in at the Paradisus Playa Del Carmen - La Perla and give an update soon. Hopefully, we wont be dissapointed.

reviews.author: Carrie D
reviews.title: Nice Resort Bad Food
reviews.text: We really enjoyed our stay. The pools were excellent. The beach was in nice condition. The staff was kind and helpful. The food options are limited to say the least, especially for lunch. I ate one freshly cooked meal during our entire stay. The rest of the food was made in bulk and left on warmers.

reviews.author: Jessica B
reviews.title: Well....
reviews.text: It was great before I had about $200 cash stolen out of my room while we were at the hotel bar. Security says there is no cameras & no way for them to find out about the theft. So.... :( but overall the hotel is beautiful. The food options are abundant, the beach is picturesque, most of the employees are great help, it's big, great for events, & the entertainment is nice too. I don't like that randoms walk up to you selling stuff on the beach but that's any resort you go to. The front desk girl wouldn't apply my corporate discount to my room so that was also annoying

reviews.author: beerman
reviews.title: The golf course
reviews.text: This will be just a short review of the Par 3, 9 hole golf course located in the front of the Resort  which I am sure will be helpful to others. To begin with each hole is approximately 100 yards so the amount of clubs you need is minimal. I carried a pitching wedge a sand wedge and a putter. The course was in relatively good shape the greens were very true but could use a trim. There is no charge to play but I believe there is a charge to rent clubs, they give you a very large bag with a full set of irons....why??. there is no dress code, no club house , no score card and no reason to make a time, but they do have 3 sets of marker tees very close to each other. All in all we enjoyed ourselves . Each morning at 9 am we would play a round which would last about an hour or so then onward to the pool.

reviews.author: Lucky2Bme8
reviews.title: Paradisus is not paradise
reviews.text: My wife and I just returned from Paradisus Cancun and had a really good time. The beach could not be better and if you can get a palapa on the beach it is great. The beach chairs are old and in bad repair and not very comfortable. The resort occupancy was very low and we still had problems getting chairs. They have Bali beds for $100 a day and none were ever used, I don't understand why they wouldn't lower the price and get some revenue from them.After we were able to move from a very old room in building one into a little better room in bldg. 4 we were mostly satisfied. The resort common areas were very clean and in good repair, but all the balconies had planters which looked like they had not been tended to since the buildings were built. The food in the restaurants was very poor quality with Mole being the worst and the Brazilian style Market Grill the best. The large restaurant on the beach is closed and only one bar open during the day. This was our 7th trip to Cancun and we will return, but not to the Paradisus. J.W Marriott, Fiesta Americana Grand Coral Beach and Le Blanc are all much better options.

reviews.author: Christinem7787
reviews.title: Inconsistent stay at the Paradisus
reviews.text: Overall a pleasant stay but not sure I will be returning. Had multiple issues (sometimes multiple times daily) with our room keys.  Luis was gracious and helped us but after the 5th time I think a change to reprogramming the key is in order.  Hector was awesome at the pool,  making sure our drinks were always full!  Angel and Karla were great in activities, Zumba was good as well as the aqua aerobics. Had hit and miss service at the market grill, one day my salad came after my meal by about five minutes.  Overall a pleasant stay with some room for improvement.

reviews.author: Debbie R
reviews.title: We had prescription glasses stolen!
reviews.text:
We stayed for 6 days on October 2014. Hotel was nice, clean, food quality was the best part. However, we had a bad incident which in my opinion was not handled properly. While at the pool restroom, we placed my 10 year old daughter's $300 prescription glasses next to the sink while she changed her clothes in the stall next to it. Guests, employees came in and out within the 10 minutes we were there to find that when we were about to leave the glasses were gone! We turned the bathroom upside down and employees just seemed to make fun of us. I finally contacted the security director who said: we'll let you know if they show up. Seriously? My daughter needs them to see! can you check closely? guests? employees? security cameras? nothing. I asked for the manager to only gethe runaround. 
We were planning on another stay in 2015 but THERE IS NO WAY we will come back to this place. No customer service.

reviews.author: Gemma
reviews.title: Nice hotel...but our room flooded!!
reviews.text:
I visited the hotel with my boyfriend in October for 8 nights. First impressions...hotel looks impressive as driving up, nice lobby/check in area. Check in was very smooth and quick as we arrived at 11pm on the evening. Bell boy brought our luggage up swifty. The next morning we had card posted through the door, saying a lady called Rose had missed us on check in and she had a 'free gift' for us and that we were to go and see her. I think this was a timeshare ploy so we just ignored it.

Room: We opted for deluxe lagoon view. We were located in room 3625 - main building, 6th floor. Room was fine, nice comfy bed. We had to sleep with our air-con on every night to drown out the sound from Red Lounge blasting its music out until 2am. Maid visited daily to clean the room and also on an evening for turndown service. There was only 1 sun lounger on the balcony which was strange as it was a room for 2 people...it didnt matter to us as we didnt use the balcony during our stay. Bathroom was a good size, bath plug did not work - we had to stuff a flannel in the plug hole so we could have a soak. On our second to last day a huge storm hit, when we woke up the next morning the rooms floor was totally soaked everywhere, approx 0.5cm high. Our suitcases were soaking!! We caught the maid outside & she quickly cleaned the water up. We heard that it happened to alot of room around the resort. Surely if its a place prone to heavy rainfall they would have better seals on the balcony doors?!

Resturants: In my opinion, there was plenty of choice for everyones taste. Only place open for breakfast & lunch was Naos - an international buffet style resurant, lots of different food choices. Only complaint about this is sometimes dishes would be on the cold side. Our favourate resturant was Bana - a japanese sushi resturant. We ate here twice during our trip. Beautiful surroundings and great food!! On our 1st visit we found our waiter very obliging (think he was called Leo), he explained everything to us. On the second visit we had a different waiter and service was very sloppy, although he only had 3 tables to wait on!! We also ate at Feugo - a Peruvian themed resturant. Service and food were very good. Vento - a tapas resturant. Again, food and service was A+.   Blue Agave - a taco cantina. We chose to eat here before a night out downtown as we didnt want anything too heavy. Good food & service too. The worst resturant we visited was Market Grill. We got sat down and had counters placed on our table - one side green, the other red. We guessed it was similar to a resturant we know in the UK. No-one explained the concept to us. We had to ask one of the waiters for drinks after we had been sat 10mins without anyone noticing us. The waiters then came round with meats, salads, potatoes and veg (approx 5 mins apart for each other). The concept of the resturant is good but it just did not work when we visited. We constantly had an empty plate and was thinking of leaving and going to another resturant. We ate at Mole on our last night - Mexican resturant. Service was fantastic and food was really good too.

Bars: We used the pool bar during the day...Christian, Julian & Efrain were great fun and always ready to make up great tasting cocktails. We used Avenue Bar & Toji Bar on an evening...no complaints, bar staff very polite and accomadating. We didnt use Red Lounge during our stay - it was booming with loud music until 2am every night though.

Pool area: Good sized pool areas. Plenty of sun loungers - make sure youre down before 10ish if you want a lounger with a parasol. People tended to 'claim' sun loungers with their towels before heading for breakfast. Activities were a bit hit & miss. My boyfriend wanted to participate in beach soccer & volleyball...some days they would play as advertised, others they wouldnt play at all. On the 1st day we went to get a towel & the guy asked for towel cards...these were not given to us at check in. It wasnt a problem, he asked for our room number & gave us the towels. Upon return, he gave us 2 towel cards. 

Beach: Lovely beach, no problem getting a sun lounger with a parasol. Waiters on the beach very fast, always asking if you would like more drinks. 

Overall, Paradisus is a nice hotel. Many lovely staff whom are ready to help you. There was just a few issues which had let us down. Next time we return to Cancun i will be trying a different hotel.

reviews.author: Kelly R
reviews.title: Was expecting more
reviews.text:
I really wanted to love this hotel & the Royal Service upgrade which we opted for but I did leave feeling ready to go! We booked our package with Virgin & decided on this hotel purely for the Royal Service, we wanted to feel like everything would be taken care of...sadly it took a complaint to senior management to get the service we expected. 

Firstly upon arrival to the hotel after a 10hr flight from Gatwick we had to wait in reception for 20 mins for our butler & that was after reminding them twice we were there....we were assigned Erick who took us to our room via Royal Service check in, we asked for a mobile so we could contact Erick for anything during our stay. We decided to call Erick on day 2 to ask for details on the Spa & about a couple of other things, he didn't answer so we left a message asking him to call back...he didn't so we rang again & this time he answered & we asked that he could pop down to the pool to visit us...basically he told us to speak to the concierge down at the pool & that he would "pop" a price list for the spa in our room...not the personal touch we thought we would get.  We met a lovely couple around by the pool who were explains about their butler Hector & all the lovely personal touches he had been doing for them like run baths, champagne in the room, meal on the balcony, daily visits to them by the pool.  We suddenly felt short changed so approached management about how we felt & explained the previous phone call situation & the manager totally agreed that this wasn't acceptable....so we then ended up with two butlers! I have to say Hector pulled all the stops out & did make the effort to make our stay lovely & Erick apologised to us & did try & make amends for his lack of effort. 

The pool area was kept clean & if you tipped daily then you'd always get a great service from Javier or Octavier who were lovely. Drinks a plenty & snacks available, also breakfast in the RS area should you wish. 

We always used the buffet for breakfast which was fine & I'd say the food was the best thing about the stay, we tried all restaurants expect the Tempo & the sushi & all were nice, but I'd have to say you were never quite full after eating at any of them so maybe side orders of veg etc could be an option. 

Bali beds.....lovely option around the pool, we had reserved for our last three days, but were told that as new people were arriving we were basically being bumped off! This didn't go down well as you can imagine so a quick word with Hector sorted it, you shouldn't be made to feel that new people were more important- maybe a Bali bed per room would solve it! Clearly can't cater for all RS rooms in that case which is a shame.

The hotel itself is large & spread across 5 blocks, 3 is the restaurants & lobby & 5 is the RS so it always felt like a treck & I'm quite fit physically! One major disappointment for me was how dark the hotel was, literally people were using their phone tourches to read menus, not sure why it's so dark but it def needs to be lighter it made me feel so tired all the time. 

The Avenue Bar puts on a show each night, which is fine a bit of light entertainment by the same group of dancers, I will say the seating is strange as there are a lot of beds in the bar & pillars so the view can be restricted which would be easily solved with TV screens showing the show to those who can't see it. Lovely cocktails in that bar!

Rooms-we had a lagoon view which was fine but I've def stayed in better hotel rooms with out doubt, actually quite basic which surprised me. You got the usual safe, coffee machine, to etc but just felt it lacked that little extra, but I hear if you got an upgrade then your room was massive-seems a select few got this!

We did the Dolphin trip organised by the Virgin rep, was a good day & well worth it, the catamaran ride was good but take motion sickness tablets should you get sick as some poor chap couldn't cope.   

We went to Coco Bongos VIP service, def pay the extra for this or you'll be in the mosh pit & being VIP you get international drinks & a waiter, we got the bus there from outside the hotel the R1 or R2 it's 10 pesos each, each way & if you ask where to get the bus at the end of the night you'll be shown, takes about 15 mins. The show is good & although the same in places as it was a few years ago it has new sections. Give it a go!

Overall I probably wouldn't stay at this hotel again which makes me sad as I really looked forward to it, it just had a few to many things about it which disappointed me & my partner, but Mexico is good.

reviews.author: xz
reviews.title: Not for Kids
reviews.text:
The CONS:
I wrote to them ahead of time confirming there was a kids club, the answer was yes.  There is only a kids "lounge" that parents have to stay with their kids (and listen to 20 other kids) and even activities by the pool (not much) you have to sit in that little hut on a mini chair while they paint etc (really all they ever do).  Paid for the concierge, never got our Walkie-talkie (and seemed annoyed when I asked)--our concierge was not accommodating (female, can't remember her name) even though we never asked for anything.  Once we called to have our Bali-bed set up--no one ever came.  Asked the concierge about kids at restaurants, she would not give me a straight answer--but guess what, half the restaurants DO NOT take kids--Asian, and taco restaurants do not accept kids (and the fancy place which is understandable) but that's what we wanted to try--the Asian and taco places.  So we walked past these gorgeous Asian gardens in the lobby and could not eat there (or the other 2 restaurants).
