Also paid for kiddie turn down service--they came late at night after kids were sleeping to bring sugary boxes of strawberry or chocolate milk and garbage cookies.  Kids were already in bed.  Frustrating to get around, so many pyramids and only 1 floor actually connects them all (so you have to go up or down and then across and all times).  Also snacks in the lounge (that we paid a premium for with the concierge package) were hot cans of sodas sitting out, booze that you could make yourself a drink, and a few sweets from the buffet (usually empty).  No sandwiches or anything you'd actually want to snack on.

PROS:
Food is great (was only able to go to some of the restaurants)--especially the lunch at the grill on the patio.  Great margaritas (they are strong!) in real glass cups.  Buffet is a buffet (can't say I've ever wowed over a buffet).  And the lobby is beautiful.

Would I stay here again?  No, it is not worth the high price I paid ( especially for the 1bedroom concierge).  Service is lacking, and not a good place for kids (few activities and no real kids club).

reviews.author: sjykna
reviews.title: Paradisus resorts are not what they used to be.....
reviews.text: My review is not a good one,,,,Dissapointing is all I can say.....The food, the service slow and not impressive at all...I do understand it is all inclusive but I believe they fail in that department...The restaurant choices are poor.....The food is of poor quality......The breakfast was good, fresh fruit, and choice of many items....And I also feel the hotel was not up to par.......The beach however was beautiful........I have stayed at many paradisus prior to this, and I must say they have declined in the past few yrs.............

reviews.author: 874Lisa
reviews.title: Just another resort
reviews.text:
PRO's:  Beautiful beach and good location.
CONS:  Didn't get the room we paid for, mini-bar was only stocked if we left a tip, food was fair at best, hotel smelled overly strong like perfume, TV sound didn't always work, alarm clock was wired into the wall, not plugged in, and went off during varies hours of the night.  Only one lounge chair on balcony that they said they would get us another but never did. Bali beds are a joke.  You have to PAY to use them and almost all of them were empty.  The 1500 resort credit is also a scam.  It is not like the Palace resort credit that you can actually use it for activities.  Would definately not recommend this resort except for the beautiful  beach.

reviews.author: Sam R
reviews.title: So close but so far....
reviews.text:
I think this hotel is fine, but nothing special. For what we paid the service just fell short in almost all areas, for example...
1) wifi and service on beach great but service was slow, quicker to get yourself.
2) great food selection at buffet but food under lamps not hot
3) service in buffet hit and miss and salt and pepper never on the table and sometimes missing a spoon etc
4) rooms pleasant but we were missing towel/ flannels etc
5) room not cleaned on 2 occasions
6) balcony never cleaned
7) mini bar replenished but glasses not cleaned and plastic cup never moved. 
8) best restaurant was vento, but missed out eating there on last night because they all seem to open and close on different days which was not clearly advertised.
9) blueagave was the was meal of my life, left without eating
10) fuego was nic but service was terrible, waiter tried to rush us out together another table in by telling us the kitchen was closing at 10.15 when in fact we had till 11pm

reviews.author: Mbb82
reviews.title: Plus and minus
reviews.text:
We spent 3 nights in an ocean view room on the 4th floor of the main building, pyramid 3.
Plus:  Smiling and helpful personnel in all departments:  reception, bars, restaurants, etc.- Good size room - Very good food and  nice presentation -  Very nice restaurants - Free wifi
Minus:  Even if the hotel is very clean and well maintained,  the building shows its age:  pealing paint, stained glasses,  missing tiles,   stained joints _  Music all over the site,  mainly lounge and techno music,  sometimes pop around the main pool,  going from loud to very loud, we can hear the music of the main pool from the beach.   It is impossible to find  a spot around one of the pool where you just have the sound of the ocean.   For us this was very ennoying and except for this situation,  I would have agreed to 4 points instead of 3.

reviews.author: LisaJ002
reviews.title: Abs amazing
reviews.text:
I cannot say ANYTHING bad about this place.Says it in the name Paradise…..went on a girly holiday and paid for Royal Service,gees didn't we feel like Royalty,as soon as ,on arrival you get assigned your butler in the sumptuous surroundings, the smell as soon as you step in the hotel was amazing ,I even asked if I could buy it in an oil or burner!! Our butler was the best…Hector,he was always wanting to help us and gave us first class service ,it was sad to say bye to him and he even gave us a present!
We tried all the restaurants as Hector booked for us and were amazing ,the staff were always professional and helpful.Our fav was definitely Tempo ,which you have to pay a supplement as it is by a Michelin Chef,well it was worth every $,you MUST go ,sadly we went on our last night to make it special but was offered a different menu just for us if we wanted to go again but couldn't as we were leaving ,we are all in the industry and couldn't fault it ,it really was an experience!
I could go on and on about this Hotel,even the tours(booked in the office by reception Expedia,Teresa and Efren(think thats how its spelt)gave us amazing service and a fab deal on diving ,snorkelling and Coco Bongos trips ,so book all trips there and they will discount! Coco Bongos and Senior frogs was amazing night out to,like Vegas in Mexico!
Ok well I can't wait to return and I can't stop telling everyone about how amazing it was,lots of pictures ,couldn't take a bad picture,even my friends say how nice my pictures are!!! 
Miss the place already….they need to bottle that smell….oh go to the Spa (free in RService)sooo releasing if you need to be ANY more relaxed!!

reviews.author: Fever23
reviews.title: Family Resort and that's it...It just wasn't for me
reviews.text: I stayed at the Paradises from sept. 25th to the 28th. The resort itself is nice but for a person that's in there 20's and 30's I must say I had a pretty boring time to be on vacation. The resort pool closed at 7 pm it was still daytime. There was no DJ playing music or any type of pool activities. There was also no nightly entertainment to cater to people who wanted to stay out late on the resort with there friends or significant other. This resort exactly what they say it is a family resort NOT FOR YOUNG ADULTS

reviews.author: ava19
reviews.title: Beautiful but!!!!!!
reviews.text: I stayed Sept. 20-27.  The hotel is beautiful, pools great. They need more activities by the pool like all other hotels I've been to in Cancun.  The restuarants are average, buffet was the best. Servers were amazing!!!! Rooms were nice but cleaning service needs to get in corners and clean better.  Always called for towels which is unnecessary because they came right up it was just laziness on the maids part.  I enjoyed my week stay until the 6th day I found a cockroach in my room.  Now it made sense when they were spraying rooms including mine.  Got my room changed with some hassel but within 45 minutes new room.  Later that nite in lounge my family and I saw another roach.   I think hotel needs clean out.  Too bad everything else was great!!!!  I would of gave it a higher score but cleanliness is important !!!!!  Will not return.

reviews.author: jc1222014
reviews.title: 3.5 stars at best
reviews.text:
I did plenty of research before booking this resort.  Speaking as  a family of well-traveled individuals ( 5 adults and one child)  who are used to fine dinning and 5 star accommodations, it is 3.5 stars at best.  Here are my lists of pros and cons, but I have to warn you it is going to be mostly cons:
Pros:
1) room was clean and somewhat modern, oceanview was very nice.  Lagoon view wasn't bad either, you get a view of amazing sunset. (We had one room of each)
2) friendly staff, everyone was saying helllo's to my son, wait staff at the buffet went out of their way to get things for you, then again we tip well so the wait staff loves to see us.
3) we went first week of September, so not very crowded. decent size pool and great beach.
4) My husband wanted me to add that he liked the tacos in blue agave.
5) Confirmation phone regarding the room service items you requested, if you have not received the items, they will resent it.
6) close to airport, convenient to take public transportation if you don't want to take a cab.

Cons:
1) mediocre food, most things at the buffet are super salty even after requesting less salt on cook as you order items. If you are used to fine dinning and 5 star resorts and restaurant, don't expect the same.  All the food at the restaurants taste about the same. All came from the same kitchen pretty much.  I would say the only difference between the buffet food and special restaurant is presentation, or else pretty much the same food.
2) Food at the so call sushi bar, first of all, all they have is sushi, bad sushi.  The only thing we liked from there was the specialty drink of the night.
3) need to make reservation for all restaurants except the buffet, they grilled you regarding your reservation when there are literally no one at the restaurant at all.  They asked me who made the reservation for you, what is the confirmation number...
4) the pushy manager who tries to make you sign up for melia club, went through the presentation that went well enough then the manager guy came in and ruined everything.  My husband and I weren't impressed with the food or the services offered (which is a big part decision making when we decide on where to go for vacation), I told the manager that I am interested but the food is sub par and we don't want to lock in on going on vacations each year to places where I dislike the food.  He then tells me that don't worry, all the other melia club all inclusive resorts are better than this one, don't worry!  When I didn't reply, he started to offer me cheaper options to purchase, when I said it is not the amount of money (which it wasn't, it was more of whether we like the place enough or not), the manager replied it is always about money, and continues to offer cheaper options.  Starting from 35K option to 27K to 20K to 12K... At that point, I walked away from the table, he was insulting.  I have spent more money on bags than the options the managers were trying to push, it was NOT about the money.   
5)NO shows each night, just same lady singing different type of music each night.  So you either stay in your room watching tv or out eating mediocre food or drinking.
6) HATE the incense smell in the lobby, my mom got nauseous after 2 minutes in there.
7) AC blasting at full strength still wasn't not very cold.  Sweating during dinner time is not my idea of relaxing and having a good time. 
8) Children's play area is kind of dirty
9) Not a big menu for room service
10) Horrendous prices for the spa, I could get great facial and spa 
11) I was thinking upgrading to family concierge service at the resort thinking I can get a better deal, but I was very wrong.  They wanted to charge $90 per day per room, and all you get is butler that makes your dinner reservations as per other guests staying at the resort with family concierge. 
12) the 500/1500 resort credits are not resort credits, they are coupons.  The prices of the bali beds are different depending on the person you ask.  Never the same rate, I wonder if they just randomly say a number. 

Overall, don't go if you expect it to be 5 star, if you are expecting 3.5 star then you will be fine.

reviews.author: Shani M
reviews.title: Child care is from 5 and up not 4 years
reviews.text:
The picture of paradisus Cuncun shows that kiddie pool had slides but it is In their playa del Carmen location not in Cuncun. 
 Also AC does not work inside the hotel it was very hot. We couldn't sit at the show area because it was like 80 degrees inside the hotel plus the candles added more heat it was very hot.

reviews.author: Joy K
reviews.title: 58 Steps to Paradise
reviews.text:
The hotel was good however, needs to improve on a few things if, they want to make it to 5 stars
- Hire a driver to bring the clients up  - always counted 58 steps up, just enough to put you on a  verge of a heart attack but, not quite.( I was wondering why I did not see any seniors at the hotel and now I know why).
- Remove the musty smell from the drawers (that is not good) all the rooms have it and that is a total turn off.
- All restaurants should be all inclusive - Talking about the Tempo.
- Wine should be included in all the restaurants.
- More selections in the buffet restaurant 
- Maitre D to seat the clients in -  clients should not be forced to find their own seats, this is not good customer service, unless it's a 1-2 star hotel.
This hotel does not deserve to be a 5 star hotel
Just a quick hello to Bianca (concierge/hotess) was amazing and quite helpful during our star from September 5th to September 12th.

reviews.author: Judy F
reviews.title: Do not fall for their trap on timeshares
reviews.text: Overall, the resort was amazing. The customer service was excellent. Orlando, yovanni, and Julio were amazing. They were very nice and welcoming at the bar at Bana and at the all you can eat buffet for breakfast. Thank you for a wonderful experience.

reviews.author: Babiesjz
reviews.title: Paradisus needs to work on customer service
reviews.text: Traveler be aware! Paradisus is a beautiful hotel but it seriously needs major improvements in the area of customer service especially the folks that work in Tower 5, Royal Service.  Hotel is clean and presentable. It has a lovely smell as soon as you walk into the hotel.  Taking the recommendation from another Trip Advisor review,  my husband and I decided to upgrade to Royal Service.  With this service, you are supposed to have a butler that makes your dinner reservations, free WIFI, bali beds for two days, bed down, a scented pillow with a choice of the aroma you like, etc.  I got to Paradisus on a Friday and left on a Tuesday and never met my butler.  Needless to say I had to go to the concierge desk a couple of times and make my own dinner & spa reservations. The second day when I complained about the poor service we were receiving, I got a temporary (just for one day) butler assigned.  I received a bed down two days because I asked for it.  I received my scented pillow only one day because I asked for it and because I called at 9pm wondering where my pillow was.  I know all these things may sound pity but if you are paying money for these services why not be upset? I'm not sure about the other towers and rooms BUT the walls in the Royal Service are really thin.  I could hear my neighbor's TV and it was so loud that I couldn't even hear my own TV.  The following day, my neighbor woke up at 4:30AM and blasted his TV. This is not the hotel's fault but what I do blame the hotel for was their slow response to my request.  I called the front desk and it took them forever to call "the neighbor" so he could lower his TV.  It was very annoying.  On another note, several workers seemed like they didn't like working there.  Others like Rogelio and Gerardo (they both work by the Royal Service pool) were the BOMB!! I mean top notch service with drinks and food.  Thanks to them is why I'm not giving this hotel a lower rating.  In my opinion, the food was good.  Didn't really like Ibana (I think it's spelled like that) but it's a Japanese restaurant.  Fuego and Vento are pretty good.  The weather was good as well....sunny and then it would start raining but overall the weather was great.  If you are looking for a good place to stay I heard from a few people at the airport Secrets is the place to be. On my next trip to Cancun, I will definitely not stay at Paradisus and check out Secrets instead.

reviews.author: Mathew Z
reviews.title: It was a nice hotel but with some flaws
reviews.text: I stayed there during x-mas last year and i decided to finally write this review. Staff was friendly but my friends and I was harassed by locals at the beach trying to sell me cigars.  Food was ok but the location and beach was fantastic.  Entertainment was really good. The singers and dancers were gorgeous.  If wasn't in a loving relationship I would hit on every staff member there. but all seriousness. It's a good hotel but the cleaning lady didn't come to my room at some days which really upset me and my friends that we had to take it up to management.

reviews.author: Michael L
reviews.title: All Inclusive All the Way!
reviews.text:
Paradisus was my first vacation to a tropical destination and it did not disappoint.  The beaches and water were absolutely beautiful.  We booked our trip a couple months in advance for the last week of April - post spring break craze.  It was approximately $1K per person for flight and a 6 day / 5 night stay at Paradisus, all inclusive - a total bargain.  The only times we left the resort were for short daytime activities like the dolphin experience at dolphinaris or snorkeling adventures, so we had alot of time to experience the resort amenities and staff.  

The Good:

-The beach - beautiful sands, comfortable chairs (although if you've read other reviews about the war for good beach chairs, it's all true - they're typically all gone by 8-9am).  I believe Paradisus has one of the largest areas of beachfront in Cancun.

-The staff - generally very cordial and friendly.  I spent whole days on the beach drinking Miami Vice's, Mojitos, and Electric Lemonades.  The waitresses would be back before I finished my last drink most of the time.  Just be sure to tip them!  

The Bad:

-Room was poor - we were upgraded to a beach view room right above the bar in the central building.  It was pretty windy while we were there which made our room difficult to cool and 100% humidity - massive air leak through the balcony door.  Being right above the bar was terrible.  Constant stomping and extremely loud music until midnight every night.  The combination of noise and humidity made it difficult to sleep.

-Food was average - it is nice to be able to drop into the buffet for a snack whenever, but besides the buffet and the taco place (blue agave I believe), it was difficult to eat at the other restaurants in the resort.  We were told to make a reservation 24 hours in advance, but they wouldn't take reservations and insisted we try an hour prior to dinner service, so we did.  Restaurants were empty when dinner service started and we were still asked to wait an hour for a table?  It seems like they're saving tables for their VIP or Club Melia guests should they show up... more on this later.  The quality of the food, especially at the buffet, wasn't great.  Blue Agave was decent, the tapas restaurant was good, and the Brazilian steakhouse place was average.

-No Air Condition in the common areas of the hotel - not sure if this was specific to my stay.  It was bearable when just walking around, but if you have dinner at the sushi place in the center of the hotel be prepared to sweat.  It feels like sitting in the middle of a 100 degree rainforest.  One of the most uncomfortable meals I've ever eaten.  I wanted to leave rather than wait the hour it took to get the food to our table. 

-Preferential treatment toward VIP and Club Melia - this happens everywhere but is better disguised than at Paradisus.  I couldn't get a reservation at a restaurant without standing around a couple hours because of the color wristband I was wearing - unacceptable.  Roped off areas on the beach for VIP and Club Melia.  Earlier I said that I believe Paradisus has the largest stretch of beach in Cancun, but for normal guests you only have access to a third.  Two-thirds is reserved for VIP and Club Melia guests.

All-in-all the stay was pleasant - I've been through worse in my life.  The beach was so serene and beautiful that it overshadows the shortcomings of my Paradisus experience.  There was a pretty stark contrast between the service found near the pool and beach vs. the service and treatment inside the resort.  Should I return to Cancun, I would explore staying at a different resort, but wouldn't be disappointed if I ended up back at Paradisus.

reviews.author: Gan0829
reviews.title: Nice ...BUT.. Choices are not there.
reviews.text: Food choices are very poor. Some staff are really really nice .. while some doesn't seem to enjoy working. We tip every time went to the restaurants ..but the service is not up to standards. Internet very slow. Most disappointment was the food.

reviews.author: jdogger
reviews.title: Over-rated, Hotel itself has issues.
reviews.text:
We stayed at the Paradisus August 23-27.  All the talk about the strong, piped in scents at check-in are true, it did not bother me as much as my wife, but I would have preferred it was turned down about 80%. Upon check-in the receptionist told us they were at 80% occupancy that week, but had been at 100% for a month prior, this is the off-season, so the hotel must be popular.  Another factor could have been the sale, ME, their parent company was offering $200.00 off per stay through  Expedia, that effected our decision immensely.  Service at check-in and through-out our stay was acceptable, nothing great but is worked, we did tip on every service based occasion, it did not seem to help the service level, but it did help the consistency, I noticed some non-tippers did not get as many return check-ups from the servers that my wife and I enjoyed.

        As far as the rooms, we were not impressed, we stayed on the fourth level in building one, This is the building for time-share owners, they must use extra rooms for guests, we are not owners.  They did give us the black bracelets for owners, I think this gave us more access to the shaded beach chairs, they always had open chairs with palapa shade available in the members only area, even after lunch, but the regular guests had much less to choose from, it was confusing, we saw quite a few people sit down and get moved because they did not have the black bracelets, we did not like this, had we been asked to leave there were no shaded areas open elsewhere.  Back to the room, we paid extra for the ocean view upgrade, but we were in the back of the pyramid directly facing building 2, and did not have much of a view, 75% blocked, with a small partial view of the water/beach.  The balcony had no shade, and only one lounger, useless unless you want to get a sun-burn.  The room was somewhat small, the bed did start to hurt our backs after a few nights, the television only had 2-3 English channels, and it took two days to get hand towels.  The AC and other room amenities were functioning properly.  If you enjoy extra time in the room, it's not ideal.

Other issues were:
The heat in central areas/ restaurants.  We are from a desert climate, so I thought the heat would not be a problem, but is did get irritating, every time we would set down to eat, we would lose our appetites because of the heat and humidity in the building.
The confusion over hotel ammenities use, they have a lot of "Me club members only" and "Royal Service only" areas, it is stressful to find a place to sit without getting kicked off. 
Horrible wifi.  Don't come here if you need a lot of bandwith, my wife and I tried to watch Netflix and would get kicked out of  their wifi every 2 to 3 minutes, it was very frustrating.  It was slow and inconsistent, just good enough to check emails, banking sites, etc,  even then it was logging us out all the time.
Stay away from the hotel store, we forgot sunblock and had to pay $35.00 dollars for a $5.00 tube of banana boat sunscreen!

Overall we would not return to this hotel, service, rooms, and ammenities do not 
warrant it.  As for the food, we enjoyed it the most, we hate to wake up for a "chance" at a reservation. so we stayed with the buffet and Blue Agave, the food was presented well, colorful and full of flavor, smoothie bar, green drink, were awesome!  The only down side to the food, was the hot and humid eating conditions.  We tried room service one evening to stay in our cool room, the options were extremely limited, it did arrive on time, but was cold.

reviews.author: Tennesseegirls
reviews.title: Amazing service at the pool bar
reviews.text: We visited this past week for 4 out of 5 visitors first time to Cancun. It was a very beautiful place.  The service at the pool bar was exceptional. They went above and beyond to take care of us. As far as the resort there was a lot of steps and walking that could use improvement. The temperature in the rooms was not good at all and they did work on it a couple of times unsuccessfully I might add.  The shows where good and I do agree with an earlier review it was too crowded. Will I go back? Not sure as of right now.

reviews.author: mark b
reviews.title: location awesome pool staff boring
reviews.text:
The food was very good. All restaurants require a reservation ( make them in advance) except the Blueagave  ( only so-so)= Tacos

Pool staff had little excitement in them. Pool volleyball net was broken

reviews.author: Peridot0831
reviews.title: Wouldn't return but it wasn't a horrible stay
reviews.text:
I looked at several reviews before booking at this hotel. 
I would honestly say it isn't a horrible hotel. It smells so nice.
Whenever you request a service the reception will double check if you recieved your service (i.e. Room service, extra towels, etc)
Bana was definetly my favorite restaurant. I would request the server by the name Franchesco or something beginning with an F. He truly made our experience at Bana. Vento wasn't that bad. If you're a vegetarian you can manage, but it's okay options. Fuego was okay the presentation was nice. Blueagave was another one of my favorite places to eat. There's a place to eat near the pool and that was nice. La perla doesnt have any options for vegatarians and its a very limited menu. But they cook their food quite well.
Naos has amazing soups and it's better if you go there early. 
The food was pretty good.
Some of the waiters were unfriendly and sometimes forgot to give us our food/drinks.
The rooms. Well the wifi isn't the best in them. We stayed in a Royal deluxe lagoon suite and it was quite small... and the beds feel smaller than queen beds, it was quite an uncomfortable arrangement. The one night we requested an extra bed to sleep on, I got attacked by vicious bugs and insects so they had to spray the room down. The house keeping service is quite great. The cleaning lady helps quite a lot. The room is too hot.  The view of the sunset from the lagoon suite is just beautiful. The beach is also really nice and you have to really look for chairs to sit on. You should leave some stuff so no one can take them. The cabanas are so expensive we didn't get to really enjoy them. Also, the hotel is just very hot, and it makes you feel really lightheaded. The best place is the welcome lounge- it has a lot of AC. I wish there were more activities to do to with families. Overall it's an okay experience, nothing too bad, nothing extraodrinary. I travel quite a lot and this is quite an expensive hotel, if you find it for a decent price, i would check it out. If not, it's quite expensive and isn't worth THAT much.

reviews.author: Nikea G
reviews.title: Great hotel, but their customer service needs work
reviews.text: My family and i just returned from Cancun and we stayed here at the Paradisus. The hotel it's self is lovely,the drinks were good. When we first checked in our room we noticed the mini bar was dirty as well as a half filled bottle of water was left behind. When we went into the bathroom the tub was not cleaned and we had a broken iron. When we called the front desk they took about 2 hours to come and fix the problems. Besides those problems we had an awesome time.

reviews.author: Das889 S
reviews.title: Average
reviews.text: This vacation resort was average at best. It has a pretty face but is lacking underneath. The royal service is the only way to go. The food is not good. Make sure you sign up for restaurants when you arrive. The open house rest and bad. Also sign up for the Bali beds ASAP on arrival too or you will not get one. They are the cabanas around the pool.  The whole tropical tiki hut feel is awesome though.

reviews.author: Robynquinn
reviews.title: Many pros, cons and tips to talk about.
reviews.text: Traveled with 15 people so the size of the resort was nice, wasn't too big and there was only one pool bar so we always could find each other. I'll list out my pro cons and tips to make it easier but overall and average place I would not return. One big thumbs up to the customer service and workers, all were great!Pros: gym and classes, great. some food was really good, but most was ave. but the theme of lunch everyday changed and was nice. Room service food was delish! staff was super helpful and kind, kids zone was awesome for my 6 and 9 year old, they did something new and special (like cooking) everyday. Hotel shows every night were great. Cons: everywhere in the hotel and restaurants were boiling hot - your "resort credits" are a joke, you had to carry around a coupon book, yes a coupon book to get anything. Wine upgrades were so over priced it was terrible. Bring cash because there were lots of extras and tipping was expected! If you want shade my the pool rent a cabana for $50 a day, ouch! TIPS: bring lots of cash and bring a float for the pool, the pool is just a touch too deep and everyone there has to by a float unless you are over 5'4, stick one in your suitcase and save $30! Book a photo shoot, its free and the pictures come out amazing (ps buy the disk so you own them). Talk your price down for everything, at the hotel, stores, rentling stuff, for anything you purchase it was harder to make a deal at the downtown markets than at the hotel.

reviews.author: worldtravelerNJ30
reviews.title: Poor service and housekeeping
reviews.text:
Dinner reservations can only be made two nights at a time and you have to do them by 7am otherwise you are eating at the buffet 3 times a day. Not enough variety at buffet.

Housekeeping does NOT speak any English. Had to communicate with Service Express, Housekeeping Managers, Housekeeping Supervisors EVERY SINGLE DAY to explain what i needed cleaned and how. Maid would claim no one spoke to her about anything. Dirty sheets used 4 days in a row.

Had to move from Pyramid 1 to 3 after first night because toilets didn't work and it was too too far to Pyramid 3 with kids. Check in young lady said it was the best tower and she clearly lied because she had no other rooms to offer us. We were promised an upgrade to oceanview when we arrived and they didn't give us that either. Highly disappointed

reviews.author: Cesar C
reviews.title: Travel with a one yr old
reviews.text:
The best thing about this resort is that it has cribs and booster seats, it also has a huge room in the basement cater to babies and kids. They have squishy floors and toys..and even babysitting services. 
Also the staff is super friendly and you get what you need right away. 
The food was ok, nothing amazing...but they did have lots of seafood, fish and ceviches and mussles. The drinks are pretty dam good..not watered down. Rooms are a bit outdated..but the minibars are great...always stocked with water, beer, pop and m&ms. 
I only had one issue which was at the Perla..is the retaurant outside...you cannot eat there if you are wet and you cannot take food out from there to the beach or pool area. I was turned away with my one year old son...I found it to be rude...and it would have been prevented if I knew this in advance. 
Overall, it was a nice resort..very family oriented...lots of people with kids..but a bit pricey for an august vacation.

reviews.author: Rosebud808
reviews.title: Overall, A Nice Vacation But would Not Go Back
reviews.text:
My family and I stayed at this resort from July 24 until July 31, 2014. This was our third visit to an all-inclusive resort in Mexico but our first at Paradisus. I decided to take my family  to this place after reading the good reviews that it received from previous guests. I realize, however, that these reviews were based on individual preferences and expectations. Having said that, I would try to be as fair as I can in expressing my opinions about this particular resort.

The first thing I noticed was the staff's fixation on knowing whether my husband was with me or not (I was accompanied by my 12-year-old son, niece, sister, and brother-in-law). Throughout our stay, there were three staff members who inquired on the whereabouts of my husband, which I found to be bothersome since I felt that it was none of their business (my husband passed away three years ago). I believe that they planned on offering us a membership to their resort but assumed that my husband was the head of the family who would make the final decision on the matter. In terms of customer service, it was either a hit or miss at this resort. Professional courtesy and hospitality were not consistent among the staff members. Although many of them were accommodating, some were rude including the restaurant managers and waiters. When we showed up at a restaurant on our last night, one of the head staff members bluntly told us that we could not be seated before we can even inform him that we actually made a reservation. At another restaurant, we requested a table for 7 since two of our friends were planning on joining us. However, they could not make it. In the middle of our dining, the manager approached us and said that we shouldn't have asked for a table for 7 since there were only 5 of us. All he had to do was politely ask if they could take the two chairs away for the other guests rather than reprimanding us. 

The selections of food at the restaurants were quite varied and the dishes were delicious, including the ones for room service. However, a dinner reservation must be made to most of the restaurants early in the morning for the following day. Most of the waiters were pleasant but the one at the Vento restaurant was the most unfriendly and cold. My friend had to ask this waiter if he had a problem serving us. It was only then that his demeanor changed to a better one. At the end of our dinner, we tipped him which made him a lot warmer and nicer (what money can do). Tipping, of course, was optional but it is customary for us to give a tip, especially since most of the staff at these places are truly hard-working. 

The view at the resort was beautiful. There were two huge pools and the one without the built in bar was not crowded at all. The beach had its white, gorgeous sand but beware when you see the Bali beds. My son and I took one of those not knowing that they were reserved for the VIP guests (a distinction can be made between the VIP guests and ordinary customers through the color of the bracelets that people are made to wear upon their arrival to the hotel). We were approached by a staff who told us that we had to pay $50.00 for using the Bali bed. I gave him our room number so that it could be charged to my account. He said that I couldn't do that. He was showing me a form although he could not articulate what it was all about. He said, "I don't speak English." My son and I packed up our stuff like two people evicted from their house. The resort should employ people in that line of work who can clearly converse with the guests since confusion and frustration can arise from poor communication. 

As I mentioned earlier, this review is based on my experience as a guest of this resort. The satisfaction and enjoyment that a guest derives from a resort is really contingent upon his/her preferences and priorities. When choosing a resort, out of the many, my family and I expect great food and excellent customer service that is consistent throughout. Although the food items and drinks were above average, the quality of customer service did not meet our expectations. Unfortunately, not even the good food and the breathtaking view could make up for the unpleasant aspects of our stay at this resort.

reviews.author: SooperJ2S
reviews.title: Ratings always subjective...
reviews.text:
This may be a long review so if you are seriously considering this particular resort, read on...if just browsing, may be too long to be of any interest...

We've just returned from a 7 day stay at Paradisus Cancun in the Family Concierge Room, main pyramid (3), ocean view...The view was AMAZZZING!!  The room however, is centered to the main pool so if there is music and/or people partying in the pool, you can hear it but it did not bother us.  Resort was built in the 70's so although quite beautiful architecturally, rooms are beautiful superficially if you do not look too closely.  With that being said, upon arrival, the resort was HOT.  It takes a day for your body to acclimate but even then, it is hot and humid.  The interior of the resort (to include most of the restaurants), it is NOT air conditioned. Upon arrival, yes, you do notice a strong smell of air freshener that blows out in random places.  As some other reviewers, the smell can be a bit much but you can get use to it...some even like the smell...again, this is subjective.  Our room had air conditioning problems from the first night and it took three staff members to try and correct it...We did not go to the sleep the first night until close to midnight.  Eventually, we were instructed to keep the air conditioning on "on" and not "auto" so that it ran ALL the time and was quite noisy...again, it is something we eventually got use to. Family Concierge included a "butler" for the family.  Our butler was Grace whom we adored.  She always smiled, made all our dinner reservations and got in touch almost every night with random treats -Mexican candy, fish food for the koi, toy for end of visit for the kids. We were given a phone to use during our visit to keep in touch with her.  We actually only needed that once to change a reservation.  Family Concierge also included cookies and milk each night and turn down service.  We received the turn down service twice...even though we reported the lack of this particular service...again, not something that was too bothersome.  One of the annoying things about our housekeeping however, was the lack of towels and inconsistency with the towels.  Almost every day, we had to ask for more washcloths...for four people, we would be left ONE washcloth.  Every day, we received 3 bath towels for four people, never 4, bath rug was left for us twice.  Again, you may receive an excellent housekeeper and never have this issue but even with our butler contacting them, it was a constant issue the entire time we were there.

Food:  Again, this is subjective and I will compare it to cruise food.  The resort is feeding guests that fill 800 rooms.  The buffet is pretty much the same each and every day with very little change.  There are omelet stations in the morning but the lines for eggs was enough for me not to place an order.  I enjoyed the fresh fruit, yogurts and nachos...yes, nachos for breakfast.  Lunch had several types of ceviches (scallop, fish, sometimes octopus, and shrimp), pastas, a meat of some sort or two, a soup, etc.  Dinner buffet was not as good as lunch, in my opinion. The other restaurants that we experienced for dinner were again, nothing overly fabulous but we enjoyed the BBQ outside by the pool overlooking the beach.  The service was also exceptional here with Mario.  Service was also great at the Market Grill for the rodisio-style "meat" dinner...Other then those two restaurants, you can keep the service we received from every one else.  Seriously.  They try hard with the atmosphere but service is mediocre at best.  

Drinks:  When served by servers poolside, you can't taste the alcohol, however, when you order at the pool bars, they are MUCH better.

Pool:  UGH...where do I begin?? This was a very annoying area for us the entire week.  Resort guests save their pool chairs at 6 and 7 AM...they come down, place towels down with maybe a plastic toy or a shirt and go back to bed.  Meanwhile, you can eat breakfast, get to the pool by 9 am, and there is not a seat in sight...no where.  Our first day at the pool was so frustrating.  We got to the pool at almost 10 and there were maybe a dozen people there but not a seat left.  We eventually decided to rent bali beds for the remaining days at $50 (minus $15 each day in coupons we received for staying 7 days) to save ourselves the frustrations of finding a seat.  This is a major sore spot for me because hotel guests are so ignorant but then there appears to be nothing the staff can do.  Apparently, there is "rule" that guests can not save chairs for more than 30 minutes but staff are not allowed to touch personal belongings.  So...no one does anything and everyone continues to be ignorant.  Fabulous.  Makes for frustrations as I watched two families arguing in Spanish over who moved who's things...You almost feel forced to purchase the Bali beds just for your families comfort and security of having a seat for the day.

Entertainment:  VERY small area for the nightly entertainment...We could hear the music, see a bit of something or another but unless you get there early, you will NOT be able to see what's happening.

TIPPING!!!  This is a HUGE topic!!!  When you purchase this all-inclusive package, you are told that the service providers all receive a portion of what you've paid to the resort already.  HOWEVER, you may be told that you do not need to tip and that it is included in your stay but EVERYONE expects to recieve tips...CONSTANTLY.  I wish more reviewers who rave on and on about how fabulous their service was would be honest about how they tipped and when.  In the U.S., we may tip after we've received our service so that we may tip accordingly but in Mexico, let me inform you that if you want a specific type of service, you need to tip BEFORE you receive the service and then continue to do so throughout your stay.  I contacted several reviewers regarding the tipping custom and was told how they tipped...it was hardly ever enough.  

We traveled at the end of July...This is when the Mexican kids are on their short summer break...NOT a good time.  We only met two other American families with kids and they also felt the same as us...second class citizens.  Because we could not speak Spanish, we did not feel as welcome as the Spanish speaking. Perhaps if we had traveled at a different time, our experience could have been better.

Overall, I will say that this is one of the most beautiful beaches I have ever seen.  My family and I had a fabulous time because we made it that way, even with the frustrations we encountered along the way.  Service is not impressive, food is for the masses and property needs some updating.  Our airport transporter told us that the Paradisus was once THE place to stay but has been steadily declining due to age and other amazing resorts going up around Cancun.  We will not be returning.  We will seek other places.  For kids older than 8, i think this resort lacks any type of program for them.  We've only stayed at an all-inclusive one other time and that was a Sandals resort in Jamaica for our honeymoon.  We are not all-inclusive veterans so perhaps our expectations were too high....a smile goes such a long way...we saw so little of this there that when we returned to the States, it made us really appreciate our fellow Americans!

reviews.author: Luv2share
reviews.title: Good value for the money
reviews.text:
Service:  Loved the staff.  Most were very helpful and always showed up with a smile.  

Food:  A couple of good restaurants (Fuego, Vento, Market Grill) but mostly average.  Portions are quite small and we're "little people".  La Perla was awful - poor food, very warm/muggy as it's outdoors, slow and inattentive wait staff.  We did enjoy the casual tacos only restaurant for late night snacks/second dinner (Blue Agave).  Breakfast was just OK.  Lots of options but most were average at best.  No sausage or bacon though - you'll need to ask for this.  Pool side bar/palapa wasn't bad for mid-day snack.  Wings were awesome.

Small rooms.  If you have a family of four, don't even try it unless your kiddos are under 5.  Fortunately we booked two rooms for a couple of teens and adults.  Lots of bugs in one of our rooms which gave us terrible rashes/bites.  Nothing could be done to get rid of them.  

Pools:  Main pool was nice though you'll need to get up by 6:15 to "reserve" a chair if you want something with shade.  Most mornings all were taken by 6:15 - 6:30.  Oh well - on the bright side I did get to see the sun rise every morning.  The rest of the "sun only" chairs are gone by 8:00.  Pool bar was excellent.  Make sure to ask specifically for your specific tequila/vodka/etc or you'll get a very short pour of the house brands.  Their not too bad though either for the fruity drinks.

Nightly entertainment:  be there by 8:00 or you'll end up standing to watch.  Surprisingly decent shows.  Had one cheesy night (Michael Jackson) but honestly the dance troups were quite good.  Though the venue is tiny, I'd actually have to say their entertainment was on par with some of the nicer hotels we've stayed at.

Overall a good value for the money but FAR from 5 star that most have rated. We travel a lot and typically stay in 4-star hotels if we're able.  Several brands are much better we thought and similarly priced.  Definitely not an Aqua/Westin/upper end Iberostar type resort though that usually commands 4-5 stars.  We'd rate this a 3.5 if half stars were available, mostly due to the efforts of the staff.  For the money we'd stay here again except we rarely stay anywhere twice.  Life's too short!

reviews.author: laura55505
reviews.title: Not a royal service
reviews.text: If you are expecting a royal service like the one in paradisus la perla, this is not the same service,we only see our concierge 2 times, when we called him sometimes he didn't answer, his name was Erick, we asked for Balinese bed on the pool area and he did it for the day that we returned, the bell boy showed up 1 hour before we asked to pick up our luggage and then he never came back.the food in the royal service's restaurant it is excellent, the same in Vento, Market grill, and Bana. I think we will never go back here, excellence playa mujeres or  la perla are much better.

reviews.author: Leah-Else
reviews.title: It's not a paradise
reviews.text:
Good quality food only in one restaurant Naos.

Bad aspects:
Noisy night club in the area
+ Noisy air condition in the room. 

Lack of respect for the guests: check-in at 3 pm, at 4pm the room still not ready.
We booked the room with king-size bed, we received two double beds (unnecessary bed was taking the space in the room and off course the size of double bed much smaller than king size). 
Balcony with flower place, not maintained, dry, old flowers. With one chair (of course we were two).

You have to wake up at 7 am and stand in the queue to book restaurant for the dinner ! Completely unacceptable system. 

The staff, especially in the restaurants, poorly speaking English. 

Prices for additional services much more expensive than outside of the hotel. 

Bali beds on the beach only for people drinking alcohol in big quantities, you have to order a huge bottle to have the right to sit there. 
This is how what the staff told us. 

Wi-fi very slowly.

reviews.author: marc s
reviews.title: disappointed
reviews.text:
stayed at the paradisus cancun july 20th -july26th and we were very disappointed. i have traveled the carribean and mexico many times and this was my 7th time in cancun . i will list pros and cons and as always feel free to contact me .

pros= location in cancun is great easy 20 min rides to airport and to club /shopping area, also aqua world is accross the street, rooms and resort are clean, beach is beautiful as are most of the beaches in cancuns hotel zone,  service  on beach for drinks , conceirge, andservice in the restaurants all very good. night club was great for a family resort  honorable mention to salvatore & antonio in the club, its air conditioned and  plays great  music 

cons= first  the food   they are trying too hard to be hip,  the food is definitely below par, i would consider this place  below  olive garden, were from philadelphia and we are foodies this place is not up to the ratings most people give, although i will say  the buffet is decent. many people have been saying that the resort is hot,  it is  very very hot  and most restaurants are in the main pyramid and there is  just about no airconditioning there, not that the room a/c worked much better, also shower curtains in the bathrooms that is something i cannot understand disgusting, housekeeping  although  the rooms were cleaned  we never got towells  i had to track down a maid  every day or call the desk for towels also  unacceptable. one last note  they have  fragrance diffusers all over the hotel  awful smell  chokes you  if you are close by.  this place needs updating. the pool is insanely hot   very pretty  and clean but  so hot it was uncomfortable,  

last year we stayed at the paradisus punta cana much nicer rooms and hotel was much nicer  also other the last time we stayed in cancun at the beach palace  was modern new  clean better food so  i will finally say i would not reccomend the paradisus to anyone there are far too many choices in cancun

reviews.author: Sanjaya S
reviews.title: Nice Location, Average Staff and Food
reviews.text: The location is great but what wouldn't be on Blvd Kulucan. The rooms are a nice size. However, the service, particularly the poolside was unfriendly. The food was average and even at the special restaurant where we paid $50 pp extra it was not worth it. The desserts had so much sugar they set my teeth on edge.

reviews.author: Brenda H
reviews.title: Awesome Staff
reviews.text:
Just returned...4 adults and an eight year old...the staff go above and beyond the call of duty...however "tipping" helps.   The food was fair...except for Blue Agave...excellent authentic Mexican food!  Didn't even attempt reservations at other restaurants because never knew what We wanted to eat the next day..that is a drawback ...you have to make reservations by 7am for the next evening...we did make one reservation at LaPerla...food was less than fair....ate most meals at the buffet which is decent and had variety....and Blue Agave.  Also loved the pool bar!  Ask for Rey!
Grounds are beautiful...beach is lovely..another drawback is no shade...so be sure to rent an umbrella or Bali bed...the heat is intense...which brings me to the heat in the lobby and some restaurants...no place to cool off except your room...which is an average room nicely decorated...
Took two excursions not through the hotel but through the various agencies at the hospitality desk...BD Travel had a great snorkeling excursion on a catamaran...wonderful trip.
We won't return mainly because of the lack of air conditioning and their strictness in making reservations for most restaurants...plus some are adults only...don't get me wrong..we enjoyed the trip...but now that we have experienced it...no need to return...food better on a cruise and it's cooler...

reviews.author: Michael G
reviews.title: Paradisis
reviews.text: I was disappointed in the accommodations, the bed was clean but rooms were small and I wanted suites and was feeling lucky when I was told I got two ocean view Jr suites. The were small. Great ambiance.

reviews.author: Viviana  R
reviews.title: Was not Happy
reviews.text: I recently stayed here and was very dissapointed.  I have stayed at the Paradisus in Playa de Carmen and wow what a difference.  Ive been to Cancun many times and this was the first time I experienced rudeness and many non helpful staff.  You pay for Royal Service and end up doing things yourself.  I didnt see my butler till the evening.  The 24 hour ahead reservations for restaraunts was a pain especially when noone was sitting in these restaurants.  The Pool is just way to deep really not enjoyable unless you are 6 feet tall.The kids section was basically for toddlers and babies.  The food was not great at all.  The only thing that helped was the grounds being clean and gorgeous.

reviews.author: Princess S
reviews.title: got sick
reviews.text: be sure to order bottle water. when i got home i have to go to d hosp for abdominal pain & dr found bacteria in my stomach fr contaminated food & water& now im on a treatment ,hopefully to irradicate the bacteria. I saw 1 server using bare hands putting pineapple in the cocktails. always wash ur hands & dont eat raw foods like sushi.i had shashimi at Bana rest. the rice is sushi was hard not fresh.

reviews.author: Dagmar W
reviews.title: Great location
reviews.text: My first vacation in 2 years and was very excited when we arrived. The hotel looked beautiful and has a perfect location. The beach was amazing. The upgrade to the royal service didn't give us anything special, our butler was never around. The only good part about it is that's adults only. I had 2 days out of my 5 because I got severe food poisoning and was sick and unable to get out of bed for the rest of my trip and 2 days after I got back home. We did not eat outside of the hotel.

reviews.author: Curlychick75
reviews.title: Could of been better
reviews.text:
Paradisus Cancun 6/28 – 7/3

We arrived in Cancun on Saturday 6/28 at 4:30pm we got our bags go through customs which probably took another 15-20min. It was not that bad as soon as you walk out there are people with signs all over people calling you to the counters where they tell you where your van service is but tell you that your van will be leaving in 15min. This is their cue to you to try and sell you excursions, after 5 mins the rep started mentioning another hotel and how if we go on a 90min presentation she will give us better prices on the excursions. We speak Spanish so I told her no thank you and that we were going to head out to our van. She said no problem and we walked away, I personally don’t like to purchase anything there at the airport. I rather get the excursions at my hotel which is what we did. 

1. We arrive at our hotel around quarter to 6 we are whisked away to a reception area off to the left of the hotel as soon as you walk in you smell something like either lavender or jasmine some sort of aromatic smell it was good the first day but after a couple of days I was a little nauseous from the smell. We get to the counter the young lady asks for our passports that they make a copy and keep on file during the stay. She gives us a little booklet that has coupons that you can use at the hotel market (store) where they sell souvenirs and such items. It also has discount coupons for the spa as well. When we booked we opted for the All-Inclusive we did not want to deal with money while there. Just a quick note also I know this hotel has live plants all over hanging from floor to floor and a glass roof in the middle of each building and there is a Koi pond in front of one of the restaurants but the hotel itself does not feel cold or cool I’m assuming it’s because of all the live plants and fish but if you’re a person that gets hot quickly take a small fan you will need it. 

2. Our room before we arrived I emailed the hotel mentioning that it was our 10th anniversary if they can do something special for us and they did. We open the door and our bed had rose petals in the shape of a heart and the number 10 in it. We also had a little platter with some fruits and a bottle of Champagne and very nice note welcoming us to the hotel. Even the TV had a little note welcoming us with our last name on it. The room was very ample and clean and it had two full size beds like we requested. It sort of smelled like fresh paint in the room like there was a wall that was freshly painted. The air in the room was not that strong it was cool but it was not comfortable. We mentioned this to hotel personnel and they said give the ac some time to cool off the room and to close our curtains since we were on the lagoon side the sun sets on that side and comes in at full force. While we went out to eat they put a small black machine that sort of cleans up the air I’m assuming we had this for like 3 days I guess at this point we were prone to the paint smell. Our rooms were done and freshened every night even one day we didn’t want them to clean they left us a note for us to pick a more convenient time. Which I thought was nice of them and they did come back in the evening to clean.  One night I was hungry and I decided to order room service which I did they mentioned it would take 45min to arrive and I was ok with that. When I ordered my burger I asked for well done.  I cut the burger in half to split it with my husband and as I am taking a bite he told me did you look at the meat I told him no. I look at the burger and it was red inside not med-well but rare I spit the burger out of my mouth. They called me 20min later to check how was my food in which I told them that it was raw. They wanted to send me another burger but I had already waited 1hr and didn’t want to wait and eat that late. They did apologize and say they would bring it up to the head of the kitchen staff.

3. Restaurants in the hotel were really nice some you have to make reservations for and some were adults only. We were travelling with my step-son who is 13 and we were not able to go to I believe it was 3 or 4 of the restaurants because it was adults only. The buffet restaurant in which I don’t remember the name I felt like was great for breakfast they had the omelet station where they made it whichever way you wanted. But for dinner felt like it was the same thing you had your choice of meats (Beef, Pork, and Chicken) the whole time we were there. I’ve stayed at other hotels where they would have the buffet set up with different themes every night which was great but here I felt it lacked variety. They also had a seafood station for shrimps, fish and mussels. Neither of which I eat nor my husband because of allergies. Another thing this restaurant was very warm inside, there were several spots on the floor in which had spills of water from the A/C. I saw a waiter spill everything on his tray due to the wet floor, so just keep in mind it is very warm in there. We did eat at the Blue Agave and had a waiter serve us and he was very kind and made sure our cups were never empty and recommended some great food. We also ate at Fuego we were iffy because the menu seem to cater more to seafood but on the entrée side we opted for the pork medallion which was like a steak and although it didn’t come with any sides like mash or rice it was very flavorful. The service was also great and the waiter was very kind. 

4. Beach and Pool like with all resorts you have to get up super early if you want a palapa anything later than 8:30am you are stuck out in the sun. I know your saying you go on vacation for the sun right but after 2-3 hours you want some shade as well. The good thing is if you talk to some of the hotel staff on the beach or pool they will find you available palapa. They told us that they walk around and sort of time the empty chairs under the palapas if they don’t see anyone coming back to them within 30min they usually take the towels off them so others can use them. They said people get towels and put them on the chairs and go off and do other things and sometimes never come back to use them. They don’t really have any sort of activities that the hotel staff organizes with the hotel guests. I think since the weather is so warm they should set up some water activities like pool volleyball and some sort of activity on the beach as well. They lack on activities that include the guests.

5. They have a spa, kid’s zone area which on the pamphlet said a game room my step son wanted to go and play because they had a pool table a foosball table. But we were not allowed in because we had to walk through the small kids area to get to the pool table they said we can watch him play but not participate. We left because there was no one there for him to play with.
 
6. They have a bar with these big beds set up which looks really nice but for them to do shows there I think it’s really small you have to get there 1-2hrs earlier than the show starts in order to get a good spot. If not you will have to stand and try and bob and weave to see in-between all the people standing. At a previous hotel I have stayed at they usually have a theater where they have all the shows at which I think is a great idea. 

7. We did have 2 people that we would see and kept checking up to see if we were doing ok if we needed anything first was Maury Sanchez she is the Quality Manager she was very nice from before we arrived I was on email with her. She’s the one that set up the welcome package in our room. We also had the pleasure of meeting Graciela or Gracielita this is how she likes to be called. When we checked in she gave us some coupons, walked us around and showed us where our room was the restaurants and such. She was amazing its people like her that make a great impression on us foreigners. We would see her throughout our stay and she would come over and chit chat with us to make sure we were ok if we needed anything. 

Over all we had an amazing vacation, I wouldn’t say I would come back to the hotel there are some minor things that need fixing. Yes they are not major things but you wait all year to go on a vacation sometimes more and you want to be pampered. If the minor things would be fixed we would give it a go but for next year we will look elsewhere to stay. 

I know everyone has different expectations and I’ve stayed at different hotels in diff country’s and no they were not all 5-6 star hotels but no matter which hotel you pick, you  should always leave knowing that the hotel you chose to spend your hard earned money exceeded your expectations and I feel ours lacked some. 

The Olea Family 2014

reviews.author: Littleton80127
reviews.title: They should change more than just the name
reviews.text:
This hotel was formerly the Gran Melia. They changed the name and put a new coat of paint on things but generally speaking, this hotel is a little dated. 

Check In
I walked in the hotel and noticed immediately a unique smell. It is a signature scent they are trying to achieve but it is strong and wasn't "fresh" persay, it was more like an orange ginger overkill. They indicated they would send my bag immediately to my room but after waiting for an hour I wanted to change and had to call and remind them that I hadn't received yet. 

Concierge
There was 1 person that performed the concierge function and I often stood in line for several minutes. Many people left because they waited so long and didnt want to wait anymore.  I asked for the concierge to check on something for me and I had to follow up multiple times since  there was no follow through. The last day I was there, Bruno was working the concierge desk (it was a woman all of the other times) and he actually was "fresh" and  pleasant and followed through. This is also where one books the dinner reservations. They probably fill the restaurants 50 percent. I am not sure if it is because of food cost and they would rather you eat at the buffet, but it was difficult to secure a reservation.  I asked one of the employees why the restaurants were so empty, and he said "So that we can provide great service". My recommendation here is simple- staff more and offer more availibility. 

Rooms and Overall Hotel Ambiance 
Rooms not impressive. There was an incident which I am not going to mention, lets just say the cleanliness of the room was in question and I asked to be relocated. They didnt seem eager to relocate me to make me feel more comfortable. They eventually did but did not follow up to see how things were and or apologize or anything. The bathtub in both rooms were just sorta old and icky so much so that it looked dirty. The maid service never left additional towels and I had to seek them out. The big thing was this resort inside is HOT. Usually you can go inside to get some relief but it was like a humid oven inside. Several individuals complained. Ironically the coolest place I found was where they take their club property tours. I knew I probably shouldnt have been in there but it was the only place I found relief. The air conditioners in the rooms say they are at 65 degrees (the lowest setting) but it feels more like 75 degrees. So not much relief there. I will say the decor inside of the hotel itself is really nice in the evenings with some of the lamps they have and the candles they light. 

Food and Drink 
I have had better but then again I never go to Mexico for the food.... The breakfast buffet is not as good as some I have experienced. My favorite dining options were La Perla (steakhouse) and outside during the day they had a brick oven where they made pizza - that was good. I could have had that each day if they were open.  I did get a little case of the stomach junk after eating at Mole, something I hadn't had in my last 4 trips to Cancun. (I come a lot) The bar outside (Cocos) was a neat little place to go and the best service on the property with Enrique & Samuel being both pleasant and attentive. They need more bartenders at the swim up bar. Service there was extremely slow. 

Outside Grounds and Activities
Volleyball was really fun here. The Activity team played and made it lighthearted yet competitive. They really have an amazing stretch of beach. The pool wasnt as refreshing as I had hoped cause it was so warm. What really was irritating is I could NEVER get a lounge chair to sit on. I literally sat on a barstool 3 of the 4 days I was there. The problem is they advocate for you to get these bali beds which are abundant but at an extra cost that takes up the real estate where they could place additional lounges for free. But honestly I couldnt manage to get one of those either (they were all booked up). Same thing going for the spots on the beach. There were none.  Finally on the last day before my workout (like 715 AM) I went out to put towels on some chairs. It was pretty amazing- I still almost didnt get one. 

Finally, dont make a decision based on the " cash back incentives" they give you. I didnt use one. An example: Spend $100 in the market store, get $10 back. Or get 30 off in the Spa (there isnt one treatment that is less than $150).  Also dont

reviews.author: horninco
reviews.title: 3.5 stars, Has it's flaws, but still a great value!
reviews.text:
Just traveled here with two adults and 4 kids.  We stayed for 6 days and were in a Family Concierge Ocean front room and ocean front 1 bedroom suite.  I am a long-winded reviewer, so buckle up.

Reception:  The Family Concierge (FC) is a great idea but we had an inauspicious start as they have one tiny check in desk and sometimes 6-7 families waiting to check in, or ask questions, or check out.  I went in here a dozen times during the week and I rarely had my issue resolved within 10 minutes.  It took us nearly 45 minutes to check in and get all our info in the system, passport copied, etc….  The girls were helpful though and did not rush us.  They promised us play toys for the beach, a bottle of rum and milk and cookies at night but we had to come back the next day and request it all again as they forgot it all the first time.  We met our Butler, Hevrick, who was very nice and helpful when we asked.  He offered to ride a bus with me to get my rental car since it was in an odd part of town, not the airport.  He ended up not being able to make it but it was a nice gesture. They gave us a phone to call the hotel, Hevrick or the pool butler and it was nice to have but we rarely used it.  In the end regular check in may have been quicker, but it was nice to have the snacks, the pool table, the xbox and the candy to distract the kids.

The Room:  We requested joining rooms with double beds high up in pyramid 2 or 4.  Pretty specific, I know.  We got adjacent rooms that did not connect with king beds and pull out couches.  The rooms looked nothing like the descriptions of the rooms on the Melia site.  They showed colorful rooms decorated to kids tastes, we got one very small cramped room no bigger than your average hotel room with old furniture that had broken glass on top of one nightstand, warped trim on the dressers from water damage and worn out bedding.  We were told we could not get joining rooms or rooms with two double beds if we wanted them side by side.  The second bedroom was larger with a separate sitting area and a second TV.  The furniture was in better shape but pull out couch was literally wet and stunk, and the bed spread in this room was a starchy duvet "filler" with a normal bed sheet spread over it and tucked to to give the illusion of a bed spread.  As is custom in Mexico, our King size bed did not have king size sheets but had queen sheets spread horizontally, so the ends of the mattress were not covered.  Both fridges were mismatched items that seemingly were plucked from the walmart shelves and shoved in place.  No professional fit and finish that you see in other hotels.  Our larger rooms had the oddest AC system.  Bathroom: nice.  middle seating area, ice cold, bedroom section, lukewarm and humid.

Bathrooms:  Some mold in the showers, cracked tub, the lighted makeup mirrors were corroded, the water pressure was decent but not great.  VERY slick floors, no bath mats to help with that.  We threw down towels.  Our toilet ran all week, we reported it but nothing happened.

Maid Service:  Ours usually didn't make it by until 5.  Once we corrected them we got milk and cookies every night but the milk arrived so warm the kids didn't want it.  Cookies were cripsy and bland.  Not a bad idea, but bad execution.  Our fridge was randomly filled, sometimes oreos and m and m's, sometimes chips, sometime no cokes, sometimes 4 cokes.  Very strange. I wondered if being in the last pyramid meant we got whatever was left?  THey did clean very well though.  It was always spotless and we should have tipped them extra for the condition the kids left their room in every day.

Lobby/Pyramid Common Areas:   Beautifully decorated and maintained, this was the best part of the hotel for me with one exception.  It was like walking through a mayan jungle but it smelled great.  Some have complained about the overpowering odor but I thought it was fine.  One thing here, AC in the common areas is nearly non existent.  We sweated through our meal at Bana bc it was SO HOT and humid.  No AC, no breeze.  It was better in the smaller pyramids.  We waited 20 minutes on our last day to get lunch and sat outside the buffet, still in the main pyramid and we were all SOAKED with sweat after 20 min.  It truly was like the jungle.  Other areas were no better, the lounge where the shows were held had to get up to around 85 degrees during the show, we stopped going just bc it was so hot.

Entertainment:  The nightly shows were great, especially for the kids, but you need to get there at 8 to have a decent seat.  Some people claim spots starting at 7pm.  Great shows though.

Staff:  95% were very helpful and happy, Eden at the pool bar is great, most of our waiters were happy and prompt.  We always got what we asked for and got it quickly.  Please tip these guys, they work hard!

The Pool: It was very warm, which was ok but if it were 90+ degrees it would have been no relief.  Very large, they kept it clean though.  THe FC pool area was not for us, mostly toddlers.  One pool bar which stayed busy, only one blender to make all those drinks though!!!

The chair game is in full effect, the beach front beds are hard to reserve (On wednesday all we could get was SUnday!!), the Palapas are not reserved but I was up at 6:30 to try and get one facing the ocean and only once in a week was I able to snag one.  SOme people went out at 10:30 or 11pm after the pool was cleaned and put stuff down overnight.  I have no problem with the game.  It is what it is.  Other chairs were easy to get if you came out before 10.

Great entertainment at the pool/beach.  Same stupid background music, just a constant thumping like you were at the club in 1998.  But it wasn't super loud so it could be ignored.

Beach:  Great beach here, as is the norm.  Resort is huge so it has a huge beach front, never crowded.  I did notice that the beach did not get picked up by the staff.  Now I mostly blame stupid guests who think all inclusive excuses them from picking up after themselves, but our last morning we walked the beach and there were hundreds of empty cups and bottle from paradisus, lot of towels and fragments of broken beach loungers.  A shame for such a pretty beach.  Should the staff sweep the beach too?  Yes, but I mostly blame the guests for being stupid.

Food:  Buffet was very good, it had good days and bad of course, some wonderful items would show up and then never return (Churros! Chicken Parm!  Watermelon Juice! Fritters!) while some items were staples.  I'll save the griping on what I wish was there from other resorts.  The food was good and there was good selection.  It was crowded though and at times you might wait 15 minutes to get seated.  Tip:  THe back of the buffet is actually an evening restaurant called Vento, and occasionally they would open that restaurants grill up to be a third omelet station and it was usually empty while 30 people waited at the other two.  The Fuego seating section is heavily air conditioned so if you are heat sensitive to the stuffy air in the buffet part, ask to sit in the there.

Pool Bar food:  they have a burger, nacho, hot dog, pizza and got wing bar set up for you.  Wings are actually great and the kids got plate after plate of chips and guac and Queso.  Pizza was ok, kids liked watching them cook it in the wood oven.  Burgers were blah.

MArket Grill:  Brazilian Meat served on huge skewers   Hit and miss.  Great atmosphere though.

Bana: Great sushi considering where you are.  Enjoyed it and the atmosphere minus the heat!!

Mole:  Very good experience but food was nothing special.  Nice change from the buffet though.

Blue Agave: Tacos and Quesedillas.  Good but not great.

Due to our schedule we didn't hit La Perla and La Palapa but we wish we had.

All in all it was a great trip and the kids loved it.  We got a great deal on the FC Ocean view rooms (cheaper than reg lagoon view at Fiesta Americana next door) so we were able to stomach the issues and just enjoy it.  If I had paid full price I would have been very disappointed.  I'd say 3.5 stars.

We talked with a couple that had done FC at Paradisus in Playa Del Carmen and they said it was much better,  THeir Butler came and found them three times a day to see how things were, they had inflatable slides in the kids pool, hair braiding and nails and pottery were free for the kids, if you wanted an inflatable raft for the pool they found you one…..and on and on…. I'd say try them if you have the coin.

reviews.author: UKMPH
reviews.title: Nice surroundings, shame about the service
reviews.text:
Stayed here last week for a family trip to Cancun with two small children. We read the reviews here before deciding on booking.

This was a trip of two different sides. 

The hotel itself is going to be an either a love it or hate it situation. It is designed as 5 separate buildings, each looking like a pyramid. There is a reasonable distance to walk between building 1 and building 5, but most of the restaurants are in building 3. There is a large amount of swimming pool space and the beach in front of the hotel is beautiful and amazing. The fountains inside the hotel are also lovely and the fact the hotel has spent money on spraying scents around the hotel is great.

The food at the a-la carte restaurants is superb. The south american fusion place is brilliant and the Market Grill in the evenings is excellent. Our hostess there - Jessica - was excellent.

Breakfast has a vast choice and the food is generally pretty good. Food from the buffet at lunch and dinner is also good. I would, however, avoid the food from the grill by the pool. It's fine - but it's not great.

The hotel is very clean and well kept in most places.

I would suggest avoiding any room in building 3,2 or 4 on floor 1. You're going to get lots of traffic going past all day - and in building 3, particularly on the path to building 2 - the fountains are very noisy (as fountains can be!)

The downsides of this place were the little gaps.

Service can be appallingly slow. Lunch from the menu at the Market Grill could end up being left on the hotplate for 15 minutes before being served. This wasn't due to lack of tips or anything such - it was simply a lack of waiters around to be able to do the service.

This seemed true all over the place. For example: when we first arrived, we were promised a crib and a roll away bed (given our request for twin beds was not possible). This took two hours and 3 phone calls from front desk (note: they called us to check if it had arrived - so that was a plus) to be delivered. Service around the pool and beach could also be slow with drinks.

Wifi is also very poor around the hotel - although free. We were on the 5th floor of building 1. The only wifi signal we could get was when our device was pressed against the door of the room - and even then it would drop if a fly went past. It worked, just about, in the main areas - but even then it was slow and unresponsive at points.

There were other annoyances - for example - the hotel has clear signs advising on a 'no reserve' policy for sun beds and Balinese beds with a clear 'we'll remove your stuff after 30 minutes' policy. This wasn't enforced at all. It was only on our second to last day (after we'd fallen into a firm 'if you can't beat them' mode) that beds were being cleared. I'd also add that the 'no reserve' policy only applies to Balanese beds which aren't otherwise booked up for fees for either the Club Melia or Family Concierge customers.

The reservations going on by customers is only necessary due to a lack of shade - particularly around the kid's pool area. They did erect three more sunshades while we were there - which was appreciated. I would, humbly, suggest to the hotel they consider removing the sunshades, moving the Balanese beds forward (to still make their money) and erect a single 'shelter' type structure from the wall at the back - they could then 'cram' in lots of sunbeds under that.

Equally on inconsistency - the area that is (apparently) officially reserved for the Family Concierge customers isn't policed. I didn't see if the same was true of the Royal Service area at the other end.

The hotel and the surroundings are in a generally very good condition. But there are some areas which are surprisingly poorly maintained. For example - the controls for the showers on the beach in front of La Perla have clearly been repaired - but the concrete hasn't been ... so it just looks unfinished.
