The Club Melia point is the last thing I want to really touch on. This is their (effectively) timeshare arrangement. Pay money upfront - get credits to book into 'special' properties with 'reserved' areas. Being pressured into attending a sales pitch by the concierge when you've just arrived with a very tired 3 year old and 1 year old in tow is NOT appreciated. We ducked the sales meeting. But the hotel should have known to not put pressure at this point. It put an extremely black mark on the entire trip within 15 minutes of arriving. 

I will add that when I say 'pressured' - I mean it. We weren't being given a choice or a get out. It was presented as mandatory and it wasn't a case of 'would you like' it was 'you will'. I politely declined 3 times without success before finally telling the lady that I was going to the room and would contact her later with a time. She STILL pushed for a time there and then. I just walked away at this point.

I will also add that I then witnessed the Monday morning 'pumping up' sales meeting - complete with high-bass music. I've worked with these kinds of sales teams and you should expect a high pressure sales environment. Anyone attending this hotel should be very wary of this pitch.

Incidentally - building 1, where we were, is officially 'exclusively' (their word!) for Club Melia people. Except it's not. We weren't Club Melia - and nor did we sign up.

We were able to put this behind us and enjoy the holiday - but this shouldn't be the first experience someone receives at an upmarket hotel with a good chain behind it.

These might all sound like minor points - but they add up to bring the overall impression down.

Would we go back? To Cancun? Yes. To this hotel? Not unless we knew the club melia element had been dropped and service improved.

reviews.author: Sym P
reviews.title: A bit of a hassle
reviews.text:
I stayed for 8 nights with the family (kids 6,8,9). I've been to Cancun about 10 times in my life. 

1. Beach and water was beautiful. The beach is in a great location in Cancun. There was a little kelp but that depends on the ocean currents on a particular day. This beach is shallow (waist deep) to about 300 feet with good waves higher than an average adult for wave jumping. It is most shallow by pyramid 4. 
2. The staff was friendly overall. The waiters at the buffets looked miserable and probably overworked. The waiters in the non-buffet restaurants were all great. You must try Tempo restaurant, it is worth the extra money.
3. The buffet food was pretty good by all-inclusive standards. I recommend the flank steak at Market Grill at Lunch (You must ask to sit outside to order). Omelet cooked to order and the juice/smoothie mix at breakfast was awesome. Dinner tends to be hit or miss even at the same restaurant. 
4. They clean the room twice for us maybe because we tip. Different staff fills the mini bar, water, and checks that the room is serviced. Each may or may not collect the tip. Since we left tip, we noticed a maid stopped just to take the tip and not clean the room? Apparently to take the tip before others come.
5. There is a kids area with some activities that you can drop off the kids at. This is a complimentary service. 
6. There is a sign in the bathroom to not drink the water. They provided bottled water. We had 3 rooms (2 for me + 1 for my brother's family) and the water was not provided in two of the rooms. The mini-bar was supposed to be stocked but I had to call to get it filled on check-in and continue to call to get it stocked. They also not consistent with providing bottled water for the bathroom so if you need it call.
7. Restaurants don't seem to want to provide bottled water even though it is free at the bar. Some waiters provide bottled and some don't. Seems like a policy to reduce cost. I had to push the waiter to provide bottled water the first few nights. Waiters claim the poured water is filtered which we tried (it tasted great) until my wife saw one of the waiters emptying "old" water glasses back into the pitchers they pour from. YUCK! We decided to carry water to the restaurants after that. 
8. Waiters want a tip but most folks apparently do not tip so you are left with some pretty frustrated wait staff. I am ok with tipping but I don't think they share the tips. Some waiters scope in at the last minute to take the tip and annoy others. Hand it to them directly and they tend to put it away. I saw waiter cursing after a table demands a lot of service and left nothing. This is for the buffet only; you have assigned waiters at the reserved restaurants. 
9. Reservations at the restaurants are a hassle. You have to book at 7AM for the next night. They fill up quickly. The iOS app is not reliable for booking. There is only one person and one computer doing all the booking. Apparently, you are supposed to paid for a butler to do this for you. The resorts makes more money that way. The butler service just books the restaurants, provide information, and other minimal services. They are a shared resources i.e. multiple rooms per butler. You will find plenty of empty tables at the restaurants. They are sometimes only 20% full. Apparently, the resort is pushing folks for the buffet because it is cheaper though the reservation system. There are occasional 5-10 minute lines to be seated at the buffet. 
10. Finding shade is difficult. The resort want you to rent a Bali bed. Most resorts have ample umbrellas or you can ask them to bring out more. This place has limited straw umbrellas (fixed) and Bali beds for rent. They will bring out chairs but not umbrella. 
11. There are bugs that bite (moquitos?) and the pillows in the common area and rooms may cause rash on sensitive skin; we had two cases. It maybe the clean solution or spray. Bug spray helps prevent the bites.
12. The atrium is awesome and beautiful (look at the pictures) with greenery around you as you sit in the Bana restaurant. The common area is not air conditioned.
13. The shows is at the Avenue bar. That means you can be up close sitting on a bed watching the show if you are there early. It also means, there is limited space. The show is only 1/2 hour. This is not an auditorium and it is not air conditioned. The night club is open late but depends on the clientele. It is quite most of the time.   
14. The pool is about 5.5 feet deep, huge, and beautiful. The kids pool area is by Pyramid 1. Some clientele don't use swim diapers and my daughter noticed a poopy diaper in the water. The water has minimal clorine smell. Someone puked near La Perla restaurant and no one clean the mess in the water for 2 days. 

The clientele is mostly American and a few rich Mexicans. The room is ok. It is a bit dated and has a bit of wear and tear. Overall, the food was better than usual if you are willing to fight for the reservation at 7am or wait at the buffet line. The service was inconsistent. For the higher price, you are paying for a great beach, slightly better food, and quite a few hassles to get more. I found the lack of bottled water at the restaurants and lack of shades annoying. I just felt disappointed but I love the beach, water, and the waves. I give it two star because I expected more from the 10th best resort in Cancun. At best, it is 4 stars if it was at a reasonable price. If price is no issue, pay for the butler (Royal Service) & Bali Beds but then you would probably want more exclusive place for the money.

reviews.author: Lalana1
reviews.title: Unsatisfied with the service
reviews.text:
I came on a family vacation 4 adults and 2 kids. The pro: the hotel is beautiful. They had 1 show every night and they were acing shows. Pool is large & the beach it clean. 
The cons: the show started at 8:30pm which was frustrating because it was the normal time we would enjoy having dinner. Also the show was held in a lounge not an auditorium so if you get there early you can see the show otherwise you end up standing in a crowd & try to catch a glimpse. The restaurants require reservations that you need to make a day before & you can't make it for all the restaurants at one time. When we called the only timings they had available was 6pm or 10pm & the odd thing was we would walk by the restaurant 7/8 o'clock & it would be empty! So the restaurants open at 7am, We called at 7:45am to make dinner reservations & we were told the same thing 6 or 10 are the only times available. It was very frustrating and it bothered us even more because the restaurants were empty. The pool is great but it's for those who know how to swim because it was deep, I'm 5'2 & We were stuck hanging around the stairs bc We can't swim. The pool service wasn't great they were clearly understaffed. Room service was terrible! The wait was an hour & a half & they will tell you that's how long the wait will be. The wifi does not work in the rooms, by the pool, beach & in certain restaurants. The buffet was good but it lacked variety. In our bathroom we had tiny bugs crawling on the vanity/ sink. Overall the only thing I liked about our stay was the nightly shows and food in 2 restaurants. I would not recommend this hotel.

reviews.author: Zeina A
reviews.title: Disappointed in Family Concierge, OK overall
reviews.text:
Overall our experience was good. We stayed in the family concierge one bed room. We had 2 connecting rooms because there is not an all-inclusive room that accommodates a family of 5. After reading all the accommodations that come with family concierge, I decided it was worth the upgrade. I was very disappointed with the family concierge service we received. We arrived early around noon on a Thursday. We asked for one king and the other room 2 queens. They were not able to accommodate our request.  We got 2 rooms with each having a king. The said they would give us a roll-away. We told them that was fine. We were assigned Nancy as our personal concierge. I had requested tooth paste and tooth brushes for the kids after checking in because I forgot to pack them. By 6pm that night I still did not have a roll-away and no tooth paste and bushes. I went to the concierge and let them know we still have not received the items we requested. They assured me they were on the way. By 8pm still no roll-away or tooth paste and brushes. I went down to the concierge again and was a bit frustrated. I let them know that we were not receiving the service promised with this upgrade. Finally by 8:30 we received the bed and the tooth paste. 

We were told that dinner reservations were to be made the day before. The day we got there I went and made all our dinner reservations for the week. One restaurant a night. the next day I went to check which restaurant we had that night and what time. Nancy told me I did not have a reservation for dinner that night. I explained to her that I made all my reservations the night before and demanded she find me reservations. When you pay for family concierge room, it says you get priority reservations. We never received any priority reservation, we received sorry you don't have a reservations, they are booked!

With the family concierge you get free WiFi. Our room was not able to get Wifi. I told Nancy that we do not have Wifi service in our room the day we got there. She said she would look in to it. Next day still not Wifi. I told her again and she said she will call. by Day 4 we still had no service. I ran in to another concierge (Hervik -He is amazing) He finally called and got someone to come and fix the Wifi in our room.

Under family concierge you have a pillow menu. I called family concierge to get our pillows changed because my husband is allergic to feathers. I asked her about our pillow options and she said there was a menu in the book. We did not have a menu so I asked her what our options were. she had no idea. She just said I'll send you pillow. So another amenity we could not take advantage of.

We were very disappointed with our concierge NANCY. We were there 6 days and we might have seen her 3 times. Hervik was not our concierge and he helped us more and we saw him more. We had friends that had Hervik and their kids were spoiled their whole say. He put notes on their beds every night. He put puppets on their beds. Made them a bubble bad on the verandah. My kids got nothing from Nancy. We had to beg for anything we needed. I feel like we payed for family concierge for nothing. We might as well have saved money and paid for a regular room.  

As far as the food they only have 1 buffet restaurant. The food is just okay. Not much flavor. The other restaurant you have to make reservations at were all good. Bana was my favorite. Our server Hever was the best server we had the whole stay. Service around the hotel was hit or miss. Sometimes they were nice and others were very dry. The drinks around the pool were not very good and tasted like syrup. 

The hotel itself was very pretty but the lobby of the main building where we stayed was very humid. There is no air conditioning. It took us a couple of days to get use to the humidity when we leave our room. Outside was not as humid. When you enter the hotel the smell is very overwhelming. If you have any sensitivity to smells, this is not the hotel for you. I wish they would take it easy on the smell the drench their hotel with. 

The pool are was very nice and the Bali bed were AWESOME. My favorite thing at the hotel. The hotel is location is amazing. The beach is amazing. We loved JUAN the Pool concierge. He was on top of any request you have! 

Like I mentioned the hotel itself is beautiful and located in the perfect location. Just disappointed that we did not received the upgraded service of family concierge we payed for. I wish we had a better concierge than Nancy. If you get a good concierge like Hervik the Family Concierge rooms are sooooo worth it. Especially the family concierge lounge that is only for family concierge guest. 
It has a nesspresso machine and a game room for the kids which they loved. 

Would I stay here again? Maybe because of the location and the Bali bed that we loved. For service, NO. For good food, NO. If we had Hervik as our concierge, YES.

reviews.author: Karen P
reviews.title: Average
reviews.text: Need more pool and nightly activities for families. No shopping on premises. You could bring in vendors in and around the 1st floor once or twice a week to bring culture and fashion on Mexico to your guests. Shopping was limited on premises.  Prices in market shop were outrageous.

reviews.author: Mark K
reviews.title: Ok for the money
reviews.text: Paradisus is a nice hotel but ready for an upgrade.  Overall clean and good service.  Nice Beach.  Food was good but felt like we were being pushed into the buffet over better restaurants.  OK for the $'s.

reviews.author: Vive S
reviews.title: Great Hospitality, Bad Rooms
reviews.text:
The hospitality offered at Paradisus is great on all counts except for the check in staff.
PRO:
- The all service personnel at the restaurants, hospitality, bars, pools and beach were great. Very courteous and helpful.
- Variety of food choices at the restaurants. Walkin were welcome as well
- Poolside are great, including the staff at the bars and activities moderators

CONS:
- The front desk will not accomodate any request of room change event after some of the things in the rooms dont work properly
- WIFI is HORRIBLE
- Reservations to the restaurants are difficult to get for parties of 6 or more
- Condition or rooms warrants refurbishing and renovation

reviews.author: Gary S
reviews.title: Royal Service - Paradisus Cancun
reviews.text: We recently returned from a small group trip in Cancun where we stayed the the Paradisus Cancun.  We chose the Royal Service, meaning the all adult side of the resort, for our trip.  Several items come to mind in regards to this resort that exhibits where the owners - Melia Resorts - have gotten it wrong in regards to Royal Services at the Paradisus Cancun.  Since the resort has a Family section with mulitudes of children, the Paradisus established the Swim Up Bar in the Family Section instead of the Royal All Adult Sertion of the resort.  This makes no sense since most Adults use the Swim Up Bar and not the children.  I am not against children on a family trip for vacation, just those that are unsupervised by their parents and hen we did make it into the swim up bar the parents of some of the babies present would place the infants/toddlers on the bar not wearing any form of diaper protection and some sitting on the bar bare bottomed.  This was very unsanitary and needs to be addressed by the Paradisus Management.  In the All Adult section, there were many times that there were not Pool Butlers or any of the Concierge personnel available to assist us.  Further, I cannot count the # of times we asked the children who had sneaked into the adult pool to leave.  Again, no security personnel to take care of this.  The breakfast food that was provided by the Adult section restaurant, La Palapa, in the mornings was brought out cold and not appetizing.  Again this needs to be addressed by the Paradisus management.  With all of this being said, there were some positve things that we exprerienced during our stay that I will share.  Gerardo and Salvadore in the Pool Bar made our experience more bearable and provided EXCELLANT service.  Melissa in the Royal Consierge Service center did all she could to assist our group and was very professional and pleasant.  I believe that the Melia Paradisus Cancun management should insist on turning this resort into an All Adult All Inclusive resort.  I feel more travelers would choose the Paradisus if it was not a primary family focused resort which just happens to have an All Adult side.  This maybe a 4 Star resort, but it has a LONG WAY TO GO before it could be ever considered a full 5 Star Resort.

reviews.author: Lavender53
reviews.title: Too Much Hype
reviews.text: The hotel was attractive and the pools were nice.  This is a very child friendly hotel.  One of the main restaurants that we wanted to visit was not open for the whole week.  Restaurants are difficult to visit if you don't pay the extra for concierge service and require booking 36 hours in advance. The food was advertised as international but truly was not.  We did not like most of the the food and it was not kept particularly hot.  In rainy weather, some of the rooms leak (ours did).  There were ample beach towels provided and plenty of chairs and umbrellas.  Entertainment was provided at night and was good.  We had a good time with our family but would not choose this resort again.  We did research this resort on tripadvisor before we booked it but I definitely would not rate this hotel as five star.

reviews.author: MonoAr
reviews.title: Facts you must know
reviews.text:
Stayed 6 days.
Tip is a must if you want a 4-5 stars service, be patient otherwise...
Bed or canopy cost at the pool or the beach is $30-50 us dollars per day (why not included?)
Reservations on restaurants must be done minimum 24 hrs in advance.
Be 20 mins early for night shows if you want to be seated.
Dont trust concierge w/ your lougage--they lost mine and i received other guest's lougage by mistake.
Dont stay in tower 3 if you want no noise.
Food is good, better than other hotels.
Beach is beautiful.
Pool is good size and shape.
Baby sitting is great.

reviews.author: JayW_Atl404
reviews.title: Very nice but.....
reviews.text: My family and I stayed at this location the second week in June. I will first start off by saying that the interior is simply beautiful. The staff keeps the property very clean and there are tons of places to have a seat, enjoy a drink and people watch. I had no issues with the exceptional courtesy displayed from the staff. I did however take issue with the  attempt to get us to participate in a 90 minute breakfast presentation about timeshares. We hadn't even seen our rooms yet. It's a turn off to be greeted with a sale pitch before you've even checked into your room. My parents wanted us to stay close together and as a result of that our rooms were on the bottom level. My parent's room was very nice. They had no complaints. I unfortunately cannot say the same for try my room. When I opened the door I was greeted by housekeeping. My room was not quite ready but she insisted that I come in. I did not have a working television and it took maintenance 3 tvs before he successfully located one that worked. My sofa and walls were stained along with my two sitting chairs. At this point I definitely was not interested in purchasing a timeshare. The aggressive incense smell that I read about in other reviews seems to saturate the entire property. It became incredibly obnoxious by the second day. It would be nice if management could tone it down a little. The food was ok. It wasn't horribly bad but it certainly wasn't anything to brag about. Overall I really enjoyed my stay and the service. However I would not pay as much as I did to stay here again.

reviews.author: VoodooKrewe
reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text:
Our vacation group has chosen Cancun for 11 years. This was the fourth hotel we've stayed at. We selected the Royal Service. We stayed from June 9th-16th. The property itself sits on the main boulevard and on a beautiful section of the beach. It's large and spread out just a bit so we all got a heavy dose of walking, not really a big deal. We were greeted at the front lobby and were given a walking tour to our exclusive Royal Service section in Pyramid 5, where check-in was easy. We were introduced to our personnel butler, and that was one of the few times we saw him the entire trip. The rooms are average in size. No ceiling fans and they are definitely needed if nothing else but for circulation. The view was spectacular as usual, somewhat restricted due to the building design. Would have liked a liquor cabinet as we were use to one at other resorts. They room fridge was not stocked daily not sure why. Wi-Fi was spotting outside the main lobby. As far as the restaurants, the breakfast buffet was limited and basically the same everyday. Other properties changed their choices daily. On most days only one poor lady was cooking omelets by herself which led to a long line and wait. The other grill was not being use during the busiest times. We ate dinner at the Market Grill where we were treated to a delicious multi-course meal. Without a doubt this wait staff seemed to enjoy serving and did so with a smile and conversation. 
The set-up outside is confusing. The main pool is big and deep. Many people seemed to stay to the edge. The bar was typical in regards to size. Here again our wait staff was not at all friendly. I tried several times to engage in conversation and was brushed off. The drinks were good and tasty. The chicken wings in the pool area are maybe the best around. Did notice a baby in a swim diaper sitting on the bar. Not cool. Also another young child swimming without any trunks. The Royal pool was off to the side and it was secluded. Very nice landscaping. The Bali Huts are nice, but several times our reserved card was removed by someone. Plenty of beds and huts, no problems there.Service in this area was spotty, the usually wait times for service was in excess of 10-15 minutes, and it was not busy at all. The shows were a nice break. As others have posted the area is small and that means warm. The best spot is the Red Lounge. Lots of energy, good music and A/C. As far as the staff, overall they were nice and polite but that was it. The Market Store on the lower level only accepts pesos. You find that out during check out. For some this property will be just fine. Avoid the Royal Upgrade it was non-existent for us. Several in our group visited a previous property and were warmly greeted by staffers as soon as they entered. All said the Paradisus is a typical Cancun property. I did express my concerns to senior staff members who were concerned about our experience. For most this property will be just fine. Our group is/was use to a different resort experience. To wrap things up our entire plane was hand searched by US customs which lasted around 2 hours.

reviews.author: zadik_11
reviews.title: In contact with the wildlife
reviews.text:
Once again, I experienced the dichotomy between the people that work close to the guests and the bean counters somewhere in an air conditioned room somewhere in the world.
From the modest house keeping lady, to the maintenance guys, the waiters and hostesses in the restaurants, all did a great job. They all let me feel welcomed.
So where is the problem?
1. Wildlife. The hotel might been built on a huge ant colony, since there is no way I can explain being on the 4th floor and having ants crawling on my desk, near the windows, inside the closet (yes, on my shirts, pants, socks, etc).
They guy had to come every second day to spray the room, but it didn't help much. 
2. A fish is not a crab!!!! Surimi is not crab. If you mention in the restaurant menu that you are serving a crab with the pasta, than serve a crab with the pasta. If you want to serve a crab imitation, that fine by me, just call it that way. "Surimi (Crab imitation) with fettuccini". 
Normally I wouldn't make a fuzz of this, but if you consider yourself a 5 star hotel, than at least treat your guests with basic decency and don't lye to them.   
3. Lack of Taxi service. The hotel doesn't provide transportation from and to the airport or any other destination. Ok, lets say that this is common in a 5 star resort. But when I asked them to call me a service and charge it to my room, they also said that they don't supply that service. I don't have pesos and I don't want to carry local currency, for a short 3 days trip.

reviews.author: Ieesha M
reviews.title: Very relaxing
reviews.text: Just got back from our 10 trip to Cancun.  We stayed at the Paradusis and it is a beautiful hotel.  This was my daughters graduation present.  We did not opted for the family or royal service because the hotel offers so much.  I'm sure its nice, but really didn't need it.  They employees are waiting on you continuously so by the end of the second day it felt like I've been there for weeks.  The complaints I had about the resort is that the main areas, elevators and hallways were not air conditioned, and our room air wasn't really working to its full potential.  Another problem was that the handle on our balcony was missing and when we closed the door it was very hard to open.  We were pushing the door with our hands to open and when it rained we had an inch of water in our room and we were on the 3rd floor.  We called the concierge but nothing happened.  We stayed in Pyramid 3  rooms 3306, 3305 which was nice, ocean-view and everything is right there.  We couldn't here the shows or the club downstairs. Most of the restaurants where pretty good our favorites were the Market Grill and Blue Agave.  The beaches and the pools were so nice.  At night they rake all the beaches and the water is so blue and just the right temp. LOVE IT!!! I was there every day.  Now about the beach chairs. I went in low season and i had no problem getting a chair in the morning.  The pool chairs do go quick, but i had no problems even though I did wake up at 6 every morning just to watch the sunrise and take a walk on the beach.  Just absolutely beautiful.  There is no need to go to the flea markets just go the the little shopping malls they definitely have better prices and more down to earth people not crooks like in the market. When we got off the plan you get greeted by time share people.  We actually got a fantastic deal just to sit through 2 hours.  We got for a family of 4 tickets to an all day all inclusive catamaran to Isla Mujeres  which was gorgeous and alot of fun.  An all day all inclusive to CHICHEN ITZA, great day but very long and this tour doesn't not go to the cenotes which i was sad, because that was something we all really wanted to do, and finally a 3 hour jungle tour with snorkeling.  It only costs us $220.00 Us dollars.  I was gonna book that online and i'm so glad i didn't save me over $1,000 dollars. It rained the last two days we were there so thats when we went shopping.  All in all the resort is very nice, and recommend it.

reviews.author: ilovesusielicious
reviews.title: Texas lady says its decent !
reviews.text:
I travel often to Caribbean & Mexico and stay at all inclusives.  I usually go cheaper and stay at Riu hotels..but we decided to spend a little more $$ and try something new.  This hotel has a GREAT BEACH and the hotel is clean and customer service is good. FREE WIFI with strong signal in the lobby and food areas.  Good for couples, families, singles.   

We stayed in Room 1401 and view was GREAT, but wi fi did not cooperate in bedroom...only the main areas of hotel.  There is NO SPORTS BAR ...but Marriott sports bar is literally next door within walking distance. (they had US sports on)

The buffet is  limited and I was a bit disappointed with the lack of options compared to other resorts I stayed at. The few options they had were good though- and they have several other restaurant options.

Location? Beach is perfect ...clubs & shops are NOT walking distance though. 

I HIGHLY RECOMMEND  the ISLA MUJERES catamaran tour. The vendor on beach charged us $50 each .. but it was worth it.  (includes snorkeling, booze, lunch, trip to the island Isla Mujeres)  ..bring extra CASH for $10 tax charge, shops, swim with sharks etc

Overall-- more good than bad.... I definitely recommend Paradisus Cancun.

reviews.author: Wade C
reviews.title: Great Resort, but food was NOT.
reviews.text:
My wife and I have stayed at this resort 3 times now - Most recently on May 7th, 2014. 

In our two previous stays the resort was named the Gran Melia..Not sure if it is now under different management, but the food used to be very good, and is now almost indedible.

Naos offered the best selection, but if not careful water would drip from the AC vents onto your plate... Which is known to be a cause of Legionnaires' disease. AVOID the Market Grill  -Meat is brought to the table on skewers, but this is NO Fogo De Chao. I could only try the beef...marinade was excellent and meat looked to be cooked to medium... but it was so tough I could not eat it..

There is a hidden buffet with Cheese Nachos, Hot Dogs, Chicken Wings and Brick Oven Pizza near the pool. I beleive it opened at 11:00. There are no signs.. If people were not walking by with plates full of wings we wouldn't have known it existed.

I will say that service was exceptional and we love the property. Rooms are nice and ocean view rooms are difinitley worth the added cost. 

In my opinion...If you have not been to Cancun...the Ocean and Beach at the Paradisus and most of the Hotel Zone is the possibly the nicest in the World. Sand is perfect and water is crystal clear.... My little girl thought the ocean was a giant swimming pool.

reviews.author: Margie C
reviews.title: Meh...
reviews.text: They really need to speed up their check in AND check out process, I have no idea what they were doing since there weren't many guests ahead of us plus they had more than enough staff. Pool servers were rude and inattentive. Restaurants were nice and clean but the food was awful.  Rooms are comfortable but they desperately need renovations (although I was under the impression that they had already renovated their rooms?)  On a positive note, the hotel is well maintained, clean, their best features are their pools and views. Beach area was clean. I love the courtyard/jungle-ey feel throughout the main pyramid.

reviews.author: Lizjet
reviews.title: Family Friendly
reviews.text: Overall average. Except reservation needed to eat at the restaurants it was quite annoying specially when you are traveling for vacations and all you need is Relax!!! They claim Restaurants are "always" fully booked and you have no option than eat the buffet!  The truth is their Restaurants are not busy at all!

reviews.author: TimShivers
reviews.title: Extremely good value
reviews.text:
I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at the Paradisus Cancun, mostly because I kept reminding myself of the value.  The hotel is beautiful, clean, feature rich and should meet everyone's need for those who book.  We had the junior suite on the ocean side and the view was gorgeous.
The Good, and even Great:
There are several restaurants in addition to the excellent food on the buffet. So you never get bored with your options for dining.  The tapas restaurant was really really good, with lots of interesting creations in just the right portions so you can have everything.  The Market Grill is a churrascaria style steakhouse with pretty decent meats, you will get stuffed. The pool areas are well laid out and we never had any problems finding chairs in either there or the beach, but we went in May.  Staff is very friendly, and despite what others have said, nobody is pushing anything on you inside the resort.  Drinks flow freely, and are strong. Oscar and the guys at the swim up bar were very good. The rooms is spacious and well appointed, with satellite TV, stocked fridge and a great bathroom with a big rainfall shower.  We got great service from the cleaning staff, our room was cleaned every day, sheets changed every other day (as stated in the room card) and got turndown service every night.
  
The thing that prevents me from giving Paradisus 4 stars is the unpleasant surprises.

The Not so great:
The hotel seems understaffed in general, it was difficult to make reservations (until I found a trick), but whenever we were at that restaurant at least half the tables were empty. Front desk and concierge agents were always busy and pretty unhelpful. We needed to change money, and it was difficult to get their attention. I wanted to request more beer in the fridge, not effective.  As well as things like this -  when we needed to print our boarding passes for the return flight, they charged us $2, that's silly at an all inclusive.  They couldn't make change for us so that we could keep tipping the staff. 
The specialty restaurants are underwhelming
Bana was not good sushi, very uninteresting if you regularly eat sushi. We had trouble getting seated where we wanted, even though it was nearly empty.  Fuego had bugs on the first table we sat at. Not really a big deal as the next one was very clean and this is a tropical location, but it does sort of indicate the reason I gave 3 Stars instead of 4. One additional oddness was that the food was always cold on the buffet, I don't know why you can't keep food warm but it wasn't. Still good, but just cool.

And last negative, but it is a big one, we specifically requested Pyramid 4 when we booked to avoid the noise in Pyramid 3.  I could even see it on the paper the front desk had, but they told us no Junior suite ocean view was available other than in Pyramid 3.  They assured us that by putting us on the 7th floor (out of 8) it would be very quiet. It was not. Not at all, it was a thumping bass heavy disco until 2AM each night.  We had the AC fan set to always on to drown some of it out, but would still be woken from a drunken food coma each night.  Way too loud, it really is hard to believe until you hear it.

It sounds harsh, but I really think this is a solid 3, and I wanted to detail why. Again, we really had a great time, and I would recommend it to anyone, but you have to set your expectations right. Oh, and the trick for the restaurants is to download their app on your smartphone, use the great Wifi reception to make your bookings for dinner and you can do it more than one day in advance, never had any problems getting in where we wanted.

reviews.author: SantaClaus60_12
reviews.title: Paradisus--Not Paradise--but close!!!
reviews.text: Five days for destination wedding--(people from all over the world--groom was Mexican) and we stayed in the upgraded Bldg 5 with butler service in Royal Service. Room is tired with really crappy showers and tubs--dirty windows, but otherwise large, clean and comfortable--super daytime and evening maid service, the butler works like a dog for you with respect to reservations for dining, but too typical for all inclusive with food that can be described as mediocre at best, regardless of where you were--noting that service at Royal service's exclusive poolside dining was just flat out slow--like molasses (you cant even tip your way to speed!!) and a limited menu once you've been there a few days..but no complaints..royal service is a good deal overall...The entire resort is well kept generally with beautiful atria that must be the hallmark...and the pools are quite good and the beach cannot be described--beyond beautiful with the only minus occasional rough surf...but one of the best beaches anywhere when calm. We loved the sushi restaurant, even though the size of its bar is stupidly small (who ever designed this part of the facility--on the ground floor of the main building, was an idiot), but service was quick and impeccable, and the Mexican theme restaurant (Mole)was nothing short of terrific...my wife and I were overwhelmed with the amazing service by our waiter Angel, who made sure all of our needs were met with a good assist from Sonia, the hostess. This is as good as it gets when in an all-inclusive. Don't overlook the Market Grill if you're a meat lover...also with a great staff. also, the sommelier is one of the best we've met in such a place. Now, a few negatives...some of the staff is often unengaged---going through motions with sometimes feigned attempts to be friendly--and tipping seems to pick it up, but almost to the point of expecting it or worrying you'll be ignored. I never have a solution nor seen a solution for this dynamic...so it just kind of comes with the territory--with my hope that the workers there are paid a fair wage. so, please, if you go, please leave $5 or so for the maid each day..it's the least you can do. We enjoyed our stay overall. One note of caution--we traveled to/from the airport with Olympus tours, who spent every waking moment harassing us to do a side trip. when we said no the first time, they kept calling our room, when we said no a second time, they became rude--even nasty--hanging up on us when we pleaded with them nicely to accept we weren't going--no way should these people be given a desk at the hotel. We said no when the first day at $78 all in then changed the next day to $15 for this and $3 for that and $5 for that per person as add ons. Be careful..this is how they trick you.

reviews.author: Dchowlv
reviews.title: Great service, and location but food quality and rooms were lacking.
reviews.text: Stayed here from May 6 through the 11th at the Royal service area. The staff is beyond great. Each were very helpful and truly kind. I believe some of the issues lies in the hotel itself and not with the employees. Like Many have said the rooms are a bit dated. My shower head was way to strong it felt like the water was drilling through my head. The shower curtains is hung in such a way where you can not shut it all the way resulting in a flooded bathroom. My biggest concern was how myself and my wife got very ill on our last night there while eating at Vento. A couple hours after dining we both could not stop throwing up. Which continues to the next day where we had constant diarrea. We shared the duck french onion soup and Seabass.

reviews.author: Brian S
reviews.title: VT Crew
reviews.text: This was a 3rd time to Cancun and we have always wanted to stay at this resort. In comparison to the other places we stayed it was just ok. Our experience at the other places were better. The resort itself is very beautiful. The food was ok, i did not like the layout of the buffet and the food was not the hottest. I did not realize till the last day that there was a menu at the buffet that you could order from and have a steak cooked to order, they don't tell you that. There was 24 hr room service that was included as well but they don't tell you that either, you have to figure it out for yourself. We tried most of the restaurants and the steakhouse and market grill were the best. The entertainment was not great, not much going on during they day to keep guests entertained. The nightly shows were basically a joke, the area where they put them on had no good place to sit and watch, you were always in someones way, it was the worst set up for shows that i have seen, very disappointed with that part of it, expected much more. Our group had the most fun entertaining ourselves with beach volley ball and then enjoying the pool bar in the afternoon. The pool bar was great (Bartenders Enrigue, Samuel, and Gerardo were the best A+++). The only problem at the pool bar was there were too many young kids splashing pool water in your drinks, no parental supervision. They should have a small pool bar for kids in the kid pool area. To sum it up it was great vacation with friends but i would probably not go back unless it was just my wife and i and we upgraded to royal service. We could not upgrade at the time as our group had 16 year old children and you have to be 18 to upgrade.

reviews.author: Heather H
reviews.title: Nice hotel, but not the room we wanted
reviews.text: The hotel was very nice and the food was good, but we had booked at ocean front room and when we arrived at the hotel, they said they were overbooked and only had a lagoon view. We paid extra for the ocean front room, but they said they had absolutely none left. They were not very apologetic about it either. We probably would not stay there again.

reviews.author: AMJ0715
reviews.title: Overall nice hotel, but.......
reviews.text:
5th day in to a 10 day vacation
Pros:
Beautiful beach and blue water, very walkable,too many big waves for swimming
Very romantic atriums
Hotel clean and maintained well
Loved Vento rest/tapas
Bars are nice, but very limited seating
Mole rest. Was just ok
Naos breakfast buffet good
Drinks were good
When we requested early housekeeping they complied
20 min. Taxi ride from airport
Brazilian rest. Ok
Royal service atrium nice

Cons:
Tiny dated bathroom for royal service room bldg. 5
Entire hotel heavenly scented, gave me headaches
Extremely warm, no air movement in common areas &restaurants
As soon as you arrive you will need to decide when &where you want to eat , you have to have reservations at most rest. You might get what you request
Pools are 5-6 ft deep, too deep for any pool activities or even walking unless you are over 6ft.
In 5days so far we saw pool activity staff 1x, rained all day , they only set up a Ping pong table in the Avenue Bar
There is no bar open in the hotel until 5pm
Fuego rest. Service extremely slow because staff has to walk far thru the extremely crowded buffet rest. To get food &drinks
Breakfast service at Royal service outside patio very poor
Unless you get up at 6 am and save chairs ,and hope the pool police don't remove your belongings,you will roast like a lobster; there is no available shade around the pool except for the very limited thatched table huts , which have all been saved, you have to go down to the beach and try to get shade there, maybe 
Balcony has a concrete front so unless you are standing , we had ocean view, you can't see the ocean &you get only 1lounger, you can't eat on the balcony, which we love to do
$1500resort credit is a joke , you have to spend a lot of $$,to get a small discount,then add tax &stipend, too.   Palace Resorts $1500 setup is much better, we always used a lot of it ie. wines, massages, tequila, manicures, pedicures .    I couldn't even get a $50 pedicure for free for staying 10days out of $1500 in coupons. Very disappointed.

To sum up
Royal service didn't help us at all really, not sure if we would have been just as happy without it
Staff works extremely hard , and we always tip generously
Most of these problems are the result of management policies, and some of it is just  an extremely
Inefficient way to do things ie. easy fix to stop people from fighting over shade is to put up portable umbrellas around the pools,they need to add a lot more waitstaff  everywhere too

For comparison we've traveled to Cancun 7x, 6 cruises, plus 3x Europe, and all over the states.
Couple in our early 60s, we usually stay at 4-5 star hotels

reviews.author: PecanSandy
reviews.title: Nice, standard all-inclusive
reviews.text:
My mom, aunt, cousin, and I had a girls' getaway at Paradisus Cancun. I have stayed at 3 other resorts in Riviera Maya, and, though the resort was very nice, it was not my favorite. 

The positives: We stayed in the main tower (tower three), and our room was great. It was clean and spacious, though there was no balcony furniture in either of our rooms. The Thierry Mugler toiletries are a nice touch. Staying in the main tower was key! We had wanted to upgrade to Royal Service, but it wasn't available, and I'm glad we didn't as the primary reason we wanted to do that was to get guaranteed seats at the private pool. But the main pool with the swim up bar was so much fun that I wouldn't have wanted to be in the private area! The resort had a diverse clientele which I appreciated, and they were all really fun and cordial. There weren't a lot of kids at the time I went. The nightclub/bar that opened late at night was super fun with a good DJ and a fun crowd. I also loved the make your own Bloody Mary bar (we put them in "to go" cups and took them to the pool!) and the juice bar at breakfast. 

The constructives: Most of the issues I had were around the pool b/c that's what I was there to do (swim and relax!). The biggest issue (which other reviewers have said) is that you literally need to get to the pool by 6:30am to get a good seat. Thankfully the moms are early risers and would get there at sunrise to reserve the seats. The main pool is extremely deep. There are no shallow areas (except near the kids area), and after a few drinks at the swim up bar, that's a struggle! The Zumba and  water aerobics were fun, though they were sometimes not offered with no notification. The pool water turned the white parts of our suits green, and we are still struggling to get it out using RIT and other whiteners. The food was average but as expected for an all-inclusive. We ate at the buffet most of the time b/c you can only make reservations for all the other restaurants one day in advance, and when the line opens at 7am, it is busy and reservations are often gone shortly after that. 

Bottom line is if you can get a good deal through Expedia or somewhere else, this is a solid hotel to stay in (just pack your alarm clock and a non-white bathing suit!).

reviews.author: CatGal_10
reviews.title: Not recommended for young families
reviews.text:
This 3rd time back to Cancun, first time at the Paradisus.. Stayed at this resort with my spouse, toddler and 6 month old baby. I want to like this resort; as there is a lot to love: the beach, the pools, the indoor gardens, architecture of the building, the cleanliness and most of the service personnel. 

However I cannot recommend this resort to families with young children.

There is a consistent lack of accessibility and accommodation for young children, particularly if you require the use of a stroller. The beach is not wheelchair/stroller accessible, you have to walk down 25 plus stairs to get to it, there is no ramp. The few times I went to the beach without my spouse, some members of the staff saw me going up/down and offered NO assistance for carrying the stroller up/down the stairs. We stopped using our stroller after a couple days...

If you are not on the beach by 7 AM, to secure a shaded spot, you may as well forget it! There are no beach (portable) umbrellas, just straw roofed permanently installed umbrellas. And you have to keep an eye on your spot. Even if you leave your personal belongings under the umbrellas, staff will remove them to vacate for others. There are bali beds for rent, but they are for adults only (on the beach). Around the pool are dozens of bali bed huts, for rent, which take up the space of the umbrellas… not good if you have small children and you’re trying to shade them from the sun.

Stay away from tower 3 (the central tallest pyramid), it’s the noisiest especially in the evenings, as all the bars/lounges are located on the 1st floor. It’s also very hot and humid, as per the building design, it is a greenhouse, with palm trees growing on the ground floor.

Food choices on the buffet were good some days, others not much. Overall repetitive but there is was something there for everyone. I found the breads to be stale every day. Deserts were consistently good. However one thing they never had was ice cream which would have been welcome. Restaurants we tried were La Perla (recommend the flank steak), Market Grill (brazilian rodrizio style meat on a sword shaved onto your place, but not too many choices of meat, therefore do not recommend), Vento (delicious tapas, make sure you get 3 cold, 3 warm), and Ibana (Japanese sushi was okay). Many other restaurants at the resort, however some are adult only.

The Kidszone which is a large colourful room on the ground floor of the 2nd tower, lacks toys, bouncy castle rarely inflated. The staff seemed to be doing activities with the kids, however I noticed there was always a bunch of tweens at the far end just playing video games. We did get to watch a magic show that was put on for the kids, which was a pleasant surprise. We asked at the beginning of the week if there was a kiddy pool, and were told that there wasn’t… however there is a kids pool, at the far rightside of the adult pool, behind La Perla. There are no signs giving directions to kids pool, only found the pool on our 2nd last day of our stay…Kids pool has no slides, or splash pad, just happens to be shallow enough. 

The rooms are standard, nothing spectacular about them. We arrived around 11 AM, and had to waiting for our rooms until 2 PM, not practical when travelling with young children. The crib provided in our room was ridiculous low, with a very high railing. I am 5’8” (173 cm) tall, and had a hard time reaching/placing my baby in the crib. Housekeeping was not on a consistent schedule, first two days our room was done before lunch, the remaining in the afternoon/evening, which was challenging when I have a baby and toddler napping after lunch.

And then let’s talk about the odours/smells: The elevators smell very musty. Then the ground floor and lobby are overpowered with spa-like scents on steroids that just gave me a headache.

I have to say, the one positive thing, was most  staff were attentive and hard working.  I have to give praise and a Shout-out to the following staff: Gregorio, Guillermo, Jorge, Sandra, David.

reviews.author: Mary G
reviews.title: Not all they seem to be
reviews.text:
Well, this is a normal basic 3 star hotel. I don't know where they get the nerve to call it 4 or some even 5 star hotel. I’m highly disappointed too at trypadvisor as they awarded an excellence award in 2013. Boy has trypadvisors standards gone down the drain. They give an award to anyone now days. I remember when this actually mean something but now, uff. 

Back to the hotel, Hotel is nice. Great location. A little outdated but so are most hotels in the hotel zone.  So the selling point if their outstanding service. Reading previous comments, I could not believe it that much till it happen to us. Wanting an A+ experience, we took the Royal Service package. For the high price plus additional cost for Royal Service - What a waste of money! Technically the only benefit you get is a butler, that if you’re lucky they answer their phone, then you’re in heaven. But not us. They will take care of all your reservations. BUT that doesn't mean you will get one or at a decent time. ESPECIALLY if the butler has an afternoon shift as all reservations for a good time slot are to be made before 8am. If your butler arrives for work in the afternoon, guess what? You are out of luck. And they say no one else can help you as he’s your butler. 

Furthermore, all the offerings on their website are not good / valid. Reserved Cabana beds while you’re there? You only get 2 per stay. If you want more, you need to get on a waiting list and then be on top of the people who assign them as if someone shows up with a large bank roll, you are out of luck. 

Service – waiters are almost nonexistent. If you want something, lots of times, you have go get it yourself.

Check in – almost 2 hours. Not because the room was not ready. But because our butler was not in to start his shift and no one else could help us according to them. Then only 2 people checking in patrons with a huge line. So much for Royal Service. 

Check out – at breeze. No issues here other than only 1 person doing check outs in the morning. So a little slow

Food – most of the food served is at room temperature or cold. Only hot meal we had was at the Market Grill. And good luck trying to get a reservation. Unless you want to have dinner at 6pm or past 10pm, you are out of luck. HOWEVER, all restaurants are half empty most of the time. Talking to several waiters and hotel staff, these actions are encouraged by the hotel management to push people to go out for food not using their restaurants, thus eating less thus increasing their bottom line. Which makes sense. It’s a business. BUT don't make it so obvious! Spoon feed us something to make us believe the restaurants are full because of the great food. They are just that dumb.  

Room service – good selection. Food is a C+ / B-. However the fastest we got our food was 1.5 hours! Least was 1.5 hours the most we waited was a hair under 3 hours. 

Mini- bar in room – if you drink / eat everything in there, good luck trying to get them to re-stock. They question you as if you were a criminal. 

So, in conclusion, this is a 3 star hotel with great location and not so good staff. For this money you can stay at any other location as this is one of the priciest places around. I highly recommend you opt out of Royal Service as you are practically giving them your money obtaining practically nothing (other than 2 Cabana reservations per stay) 

Maybe it was a fluke and my stay was horrible just for us. But I can tell you that while complaining, at least 5 other couples where there too doing the same. If you stay there, good luck. Maybe you’ll do better than us.

reviews.author: Randa S
reviews.title: Not worth the 4 1/2 stars it gets...
reviews.text:
The hotel itself is very clean and very close to the beach which I appreciated for sure.aside from that,the housekeeping sometimes didn't come in until 3 pm sometimes earlier too.at 8:00 am or 8:30 am don't remember the music and the waterfalls in the lobby comes on at the loudest setting waking people from their deepest slumber!! (Why don't they let people decide what time they want to wake up? We are on a vacation after all?) the food at the buffet sucks and the service is too slow,we had to wait in a long line for a piece of a tough tiny steak to be cook and so on,there is not a lot of variety.we made reservation at the other restaurants over there some were alright nothing extraordinary and again it takes too long.
There is only one 1 person at the concierge desk ,pretty much one person at every station,so god help you if you need to address an issue and there a person ahead of you,honesty I had to wait many half hours before someone addressed me.
The last straw came 2 days before we left,when as usual when my mom reserved our lounge chair by the pool by 7am ,and someone came by 10am and decide to sends our stuff to lost and found so she can take our reserved chairs because by then we are by the beach and pool and everywhere ( we're a family of 6) and we only reserve 3 chair to be reasonable. Of course I threw a fit because I've had enough of the bull.... Happening over there,I went to the supervisor in tears and vented about everything that happened (there is a lot more) but for the sake of writing I'm simplifying. What he offered me was a half an hour massage by an unlicensed massage therapist ,she didn't know what the heck she was doing.so my final point I will never pay again the 11000$ I paid to go there,because we took 2 rooms.

reviews.author: omm m
reviews.title: not a five star hotel
reviews.text: I  just arrive from this all inclusive resort, the hotel in itself is  nice some of the personnel are not very helpful or pleasant, all they want to do from the moment you check in is sit down with you and try to sell you time shares or excursions, I explain me and my husband were not interested since this was our second time and we had experience this before and just wanted to relax and enjoy the resort we were persona non grata in other words fend for yourself, the restaurants at the resort you needed to make reservation a day before you could not make them all at once ok no big deal but it was, b/c if you went the day before by 12noon the only reservations available were for 10pm you needed to be there by 7am in order to get a good reservation. Breakfast serve at 6:30am the food was already cold at this time. Even though Housekeeping very nice and servers at bar very pleasant I do not recommend this hotel at all.........do not go......

reviews.author: Erica A
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort, Don't upgrade to Fa,ily Concierge Service
reviews.text: Overall, the resort is clean and beautiful. The pool and beaches are gorgeous. The wait staff at the restaurants, pool and bars and wonderful. The food is okay. The restaurants are not very child friendly. It was hard to get a reservation for the restaurants and times that we requested, even with the family concierge upgrade.  This upgrade is not worth it. They promised us bed turn down service, dinner reservations, chairs at the pool and beach, chocolates our pillows, a pillow selection menu, and a kid friendly stocked mini bar as the upgrade. We were also assigned a butler who was supposed to assist us. None of the above were given to us or meet our expectations. Though, overall we had a fabulous week, despite us being dissatisfied with the upgraded service.

reviews.author: Vincent L
reviews.title: Could be better
reviews.text:
My family spent 4 nights recently at the Paradisus Cancun. Overall experience was OK. 
Let say the cons first:
The first room we got was not ready. It seems that someone still stay in that room. Then I had to walk all the way back to the lobby to tell them. The second room we got has a amazing ocean view on the second floor, but the equipment are lack of maintaining. The air conditioning and the door were making annoying sound once for a while. Faucet, shower were not functioning as they should be. The balcony was dirty. It says that there is free wifi, but you could barely get connection in the room, Lobby, restaurants and pools area have good wifi siginals. 
Pro:
The staffs are friendly and helpful. Foods good. The olny hold back is that you need reservations in all full services restaurants. Location is great.

reviews.author: TripnaTrip2009
reviews.title: Cancun was nice but..
reviews.text: The annoying part of this stay was the people who tries to sell you their membership club Malia.  Hotel was average.  Hotel rooms needs some serious renovation.  Saw cockroach in the lobby.  Buffet was great.

reviews.author: grooovydee
reviews.title: Beautiful beach
reviews.text:
Paridisus Cancun is a beautiful place with one of the most gorgeous beaches we have ever seen.  We visited for one week and just returned.  The hotel is beautiful and is meticulously maintained.  Our rooms were clean and comfortable.  We had read a lot of reviews about problems getting beach chairs, but on every visit to the beach we had no trouble getting chairs (there were 4 of us) and a thatched umbrella to sit under.  The staff is constantly asking to help.  The restaurants were great - lots of detail to good food and presentation.  One complaint was the breakfast buffet - waffles, pancakes and french toast were cold each and every day.  Since they are not made to order, the pans they are in do not keep them warm.    My son and daughter-in-law loved the fresh juice blends each morning.  We made it a point to sit in Alberth's section each breakfast - he was the best! 

A major negative to this resort - if you like to see shows each evening, this is not the place for you.  Although the shows offered were first-rate entertainment, it is impossible to see them in the area they are presented.  The shows take place in a small area that is surrounded by couches and lounger beds.  If you don't get there early (about 1 1/2 hours before showtime) to reserve a couch, you will not see the show.  There is very poor visibility in this lounge to see the performance area.  It is difficult to understand how a resort of this size would have no arena or area with proper seating for all guests present to see the performance.  It was a major disappointment and the main reason we would not return.  One night we arrived early to be sure to get a good spot and once the performance began people stood in front of us so that they could see the show blocking my husband's view.  We wound up leaving since we couldn't see.

Beach staff were constantly ready to serve drinks, etc.  Some drinks good, some weak.  Restaurant drinks were far better.

reviews.author: Kyle3w
reviews.title: Decent Stay - Not as great as you'd think - Read On For Details
reviews.text:
First Impression:
The hotel sits right on the water, has great restaurants (Vento and Blue Agave were our favorites).  Waitstaff is eager to please.  Get up early and claim your thatched roof beach/pool chairs with a towel and a personal item.  They fill up quick.

Smell:
The first thing you will notice when you take your first step into the hotel is an overwhelming smell of incense.  And it's always there, no matter where you are in the hotel, all day every day.  My wife and I found it very overpowering.  Not the worst thing in the world.  

Check-in:
After stepping foot in the hotel, we were ushered to the check-in area and went through the check-in process and our room wasn't ready.  Which was fine, we were told to sit down with a concierge to help us get acquainted with the hotel.  Her name was Corina.  Watch out for this.  Under the guise of helping my wife and I get to know the hotel, Corina kept pushing us to attend a 90 minute welcoming breakfast the following morning where we would get a voucher for discounts on the spa/outings.  It seemed very fishy.  She mentioned it 3-4 times in a 10 minute conversation.  We kept saying "No" but she kept pushing it on us.  Very weird.  It felt like she wasnt interested in walking us through the map of the grounds, but more interested in getting us to sign up for this 90 minute meeting.  Big turn-off for us.

Room:
We had a lagoon view suite with King Bed.  The lagoon view was totally fine, didn't need to have the ocean view.  We got beautiful sunsets on our balcony, which you cant get with the ocean view.  

When we finally got up to the room, our room keys didnt work.  Had to go back down to the front desk, and then wait for them to send up some maintence guy to open our doors.  After 1hr30min since we stepped foot in the hotel, we finally got into the room and they still hadn't brought up our luggage.  We had to call the front desk and they finally brought our luggage up.  One day our floor started flooding out of nowhere.  We had to call the front desk to have someone soak everything up.

Restaurants:
We thought Vento and Blue Agave were the best.  The buffet is good, but it gets old after a while because you eat there for breakfast and lunch everyday

Overall, it was a good stay, there were some setbacks (that Corina lady and flooding 5th floor room etc).  We'll try other hotels before thinking of trying Paradisus Cancun again.

reviews.author: amcaskey24
reviews.title: Beautiful but not a *****
reviews.text:
First of all- I have been to several AInclusives..... but I wouldn't consider myself to be "picky" but I do like great resorts.

Location is awesome. Walk right out to the street and get on a bus for $1 and go into town and check it out.
Royal Service. Not nearly as awesome as you'd like to think. Upgrade if you get it cheap, not worth it for full price. There is a private pool- but you don't need it as there is plenty of other pools, etc. 
Food. Average.
Alcohol. Average
Service. I was surprised at how often we had to ask people for drinks. I was actually really surprised by this. Don't get me wrong, there was good servers..... but I would rate service below a **** resort.
Beach. AMAZING
Ocean. Beautiful.
Bars. Make sure to stop at Avenue Bar around 5-7 and check out the view.... horrible horrible service though.
Omar and Michael at the Royal Service area were very helpful and willing to go over and above

reviews.author: TOCAN8
reviews.title: Rooms need updating
reviews.text:
Our family spent 7 days at this resort.  I am an avid reader of tripadvisor to determine where we should stay.  We travel annually to Mexico and have stayed in Playa del Carmen, Mayan Riviera and Cancun for the past 12 years.  Each destination has it's pros and cons.  I chose this resort based on the family concierge option.  We had stayed at the old Paradisus in Mayan Riviera and enjoyed the option of a private room and full service and not having to  worry about booking reservations.  The service is excellent, the staff in the family concierge is very attentive and friendly.   The nightly turn down service with milk and cookies were a nice touch. I'm a little surprised with the comments about the food selection and quality on this forum.  I have to say,  we had the best meal  at this resort.  There was a few we didn't enjoy but I thought the restaurant Vento was excellent.  We dined there twice because we enjoyed it so much.  The main restaurant Naos does get busy and depending on where you sit the service is hit or miss.  On the whole, we did experience excellent service.
The reason I only gave this restaurant a 3 rating is that the Spa was so disappointing.  The day I visited the spa, the steam room wasn't working, the indoor spa pool was dirty and cold.  There was someone working in the general lounge area.  Only the main shower head had hot water, the other jet heads had cold water.  I've been to many spas in Mexico resorts, I look forward to spending a relaxing couple of hours but this one was so disappointing I didn't even bother to book anything.  Also, the price is out of line for the premises and service. 
The other reason this resort rated poorly was the rooms that we had been shown and stayed in needed major reno.  It definitely showed it's wear.  The beds were not comfortable, the sheets looked worn, the couches had stains. The first room had two double beds and took up the entire room.  We upgraded to a corner one bedroom suite but the first one was horrendous.  They had a pull out couch for the kids that is reminiscent of going to the cottage and sleeping on a horrible mattress.  The curtains in the bathroom had stains and were held up with wires.  They were too small to close thereby, people walking in the adjacent pyramid could see you in the bathroom at night.  We finally moved to the last room which was in the fourth pyramid on the second floor.  It was a 1 bedroom suite with two full size beds. It was still a little too small for two adults and two kids to sleep comfortably in.
Lastly,  there were no organized activities for kids under 9.  The playstation games were all broken, there was a pool table in the family concierge but the kids got bored quickly.  There were no evening activities for the kids other than watching the shows in a small area of the disco club at 8:30pm with very little seating.   Most resorts have some sort of theatre  but not this one. The kids room in the basement was basically for very young kids, a little too dark and dingy.  I don't mind spending more for service and quality.  I like the All inclusive because it's a no brainer.  If this resort renovates the spa and rooms and updates their programs for kids I would come back.  But in it's current condition, we will be looking elsewhere for our next family vacation.

reviews.author: Anastasiya S
reviews.title: Not Impressed
reviews.text:
My friends and I stayed at Paradisus Cancun from March 1st to March 7th. We purchased the Royal Service Package and the service was not that royal at all. The hotel is huge and is divided into 5 pyramids. We stayed in Pyramid 5. 

The hotel itself is beautiful inside and out. However, the service -- not so much. Room service was slow and almost always unresponsive. The restaurants which we booked when we first moved in had good food but we waited for an hour and a half to get our food in Fuego and the sushi in Bana tasted like rubber. They weren't fresh and tasted horrible. For my friend's birthday we had dinner reservations at Tempo at 8pm, we waited for an hour to get our table and another hour for our food. The buffet food was the same everyday and was not always fresh. 

Having visited many resorts in Cancun, Los Cabos, and the Caribbean' we have witnessed exceptional service in almost all. However, we were disappointed at Paradisus. 

ONE Exception: At Naos buffet, we had one server that we stuck to the whole vacation because his service was EXCEPTIONAL!!! His name is Jesus Arzeta. What a great guy! He is very engaging and entertaining, always made jokes with us and made us laugh. Besides, he is very fast and helpful. Whatever we needed, he brought it within minutes. Really, the best service in the whole resort!!! Such a friendly and well-mannered individual!!! During our last day he even brought us souvenirs from Cancun to say thank you for staying there and wishing us a safe trip. It warms my heart to know there are people who actually love their jobs and wish to make others happy! THANK YOU JESUS! You rock!!!!!

-Anastasiya

reviews.author: dfarruggio
reviews.title: Not What We Expected
reviews.text:
After spending a week at the Paradisus, my wife and I both agreed that it did not live up to our expectations. 

PROS

Beautiful beach
Nice hotel/rooms

CONS

Subpar food
No activities included
No hot tub on premises
Weird zen music by the pool
No food variation in restaurants
Pool was freezing

reviews.author: leiny
reviews.title: This place is a giant biosphere with no breezes or windows that open!
reviews.text:
Stayed for 3 nights / 4 days -- and was very excited, based on excellent reviewed on TripAdvisor.  Unfortunately, our high expectations were not met.  We've stayed in many All-Inclusives in different Mexico cities, and Dominican, but were not impressed.  We go to Mexico for the beach and we felt like we went to a Biosphere.  None of the windows open in any of the restaurants except the Nano's one which is the main buffet style restaurants -- we like, open dining and the breezes of the sea.  Looks very pretty in the hotel at night, but again, felt muggy and musty inside with no fresh air.  Smelled in incense and candles and strong scents everywhere -- no thanks.  Believe me, we wanted to love it -- but would not return.  Would try a different place on the same beach--- should have stayed at Live Aqua like my friend recommended!  Uh -- so bummed.

PROS:
- Beautiful beach with crystal clear water!
- Nice pools that span the hotel
- Food was good - was easy to get reservations each night

CONS:
- Arrived at 10:30am, but room was not ready until 2:15pm.
- I signed up for Melia Rewards prior to our trip, requested early check-in online, but did not hear back and they did not give me any extra treatment for being a member
- We were immediately assigned a concierge at we stood in line to check in -- she asked us if we wanted a drink -- we ordered a Coke and a water -- she gave the water, and then held up a Diet Coke and said, we don't have a Coke and made no attempt to get one.  I said I'll take a water.
- After waiting in line for 15 mins -- we were told our room was not ready.
- Main dining area closed from 11am - 12:30 while they went to breakfast to lunch, disappointing since no other food to be found
- Reserved a Lagoon View Deluxe Suite and got Room 4014 in far right pyramid off in the middle of no where (near spa) which faced a back service driveway -- no lagoon.
- Bags were delivered within 10 mins after got into room, followed immediately by a welcome dessert.
- We were exhausted and took a nap, 2 hours in to our nap, there a constant noise at the door for 10 mins, went to see what it was, and it was the hotel staff trying to open the door, but the key pad did not work -- I opened the door, he apologized, I shut the door.
- After we came back from dinner that night, our key pad did not work, walked back to get new keys, still did not work, they sent someone to fix -- needed new battery, they fixed, and called to see it was OK
- Day 2 there was an envelope with note inside from hotel saying come to lobby for your Welcome Gift.  We sensed it was a push for a time-share hard sell, and decided to ignore.  
- Later that same day -- received a call in our room, asking if all was good, and if we are coming for our Welcome gift - I said no.  She asked if we already got it, I said, no thanks, don't want it.
- There was another message left on our phone, but we did not listen to it, could not figure out how to retrieve it.
- Felt the staff was very pesty.  We kept our Do Not Disturb sign from Day 2 on.
- Hardy any lounge chairs around pool, and had to put towel out by 7am to get a spot
- Downloaded their app, after seeing signs in the hotel, and it did not have all the most current info on it.  Tried to reserve Tennis courts -- and space was double booked. Asked front desk and they said the app doesn't work for Tennis.  
- Only one set of tennis rackets avail for rent -- and they are crappy rackets
- The fences around tennis court (yes, one court) is super low, easy to lose balls -- and hotel charges if you lose tennis balls

reviews.author: aajj53
reviews.title: Not what I paid for.
reviews.text: My husband and I purchased the royal service and stayed at the hotel from Feb 25 threw March 5th.  The ambience of the hotel is stunning but the service is extremely slow. We weren't able to use the royal service much due to the lack of response and follow through.  Several of the days the restaurants did not open on time. They would come in at weird times to clean our rooms if they came at all. On our last day there our coffee pot started to smoke and crackle we called down to the front desk and it took maintenance 15 minutes to get to the  room. They said it would take a couple hours for a replacement. We told them that we were packing to leave so that wouldn't work. They said the would send up an pot of coffee for us. That took 45 minutes. At 4 am I wouldn't assume room service is that busy. It is a nice hotel and for the most part everyone was friendly,  however I would not go to  this hotel with high expectations or you will be disappointed .

reviews.author: wanttobetheir
reviews.title: Nice but not that nice
reviews.text: My friends and I stayed here Feb.15th to the 22nd. We used his time share. To get there we went on a shuttle I had not used before but I will use it all the time now. Canada Transfers was awesome, 3 of us pd when we got to the hotel, had ice cold beers for a buck each and a cold towel. When we arrived we were taken to a lounge and had to wait for a half hour then went to check in. At check in we were told the extra room was more money when they had told us it was included. Not a good start. The rooms were ok. But if your there just for a room and not all incl. stay at the Marriott next door much better rooms. This hotel has a great pool and looks nice inside. But make sure u go down and save a chair really early or u don't get one. The swim up bar gets real busy so the wait is long. They do have good shows at nite but u need to get there 1hr early or no good seats left. If u are not all incl. they treat u pretty bad. We did the all incl. the last 2days so it was a little better. The food was ok. The service at the buffet so so. But the steak resturant was very good and service great. The maid we had was the best, keep the rooms very clean. The weight room and spe were very good. This hotel is ok but I would not want to go back.  Doug (Ut.)

reviews.author: Kimberly Z
reviews.title: Beautiful Beach, Average Resort
reviews.text:
My husband, toddler daughter, and I stayed at the Paradisus Cancun from March 12-16.  Our flight was delayed and we arrived around 6 pm.  We had no problems with check in and were taken straight to our room.  

The resort – My husband likened the layout of the central “pyramid” to an Embassy Suites.  The doors to the room face inward and there is ivy flowing over the sides of the interior balconies.  Unlike other resorts we’ve been to (both AI and non AI), there are no comfortable lounging areas where guests can hang out, chat, order drinks and snacks from waiters.  There is a tiny bar in the middle of the central atrium.  This area also contains the Japanese restaurant and you have to vacate the tables at 6 pm for diners.  There are timeshare people throughout the resort but they were not aggressive about getting us to sit through a presentation.  There aren’t any green spaces or outdoor lounging spaces, either.  The entire property is taken up by the huge edifice and pool areas.

The room - We reserved a deluxe junior suite with a lagoon view and were given an ocean view room.  However, the room was on the first floor so our view was obstructed by the roof of the restaurant below.  While it was clean, it was dated and didn’t fit with the ‘luxury’ atmosphere that the resort purports to have.  The mini bar was stocked with soft drinks, water, and beer.  At other AI resorts I’ve stayed at in the Cancun/Playa area, hard alcohol was provided in the room.  I understand that this is only provided to those who upgrade to Royal Service.  The beds and pillows were not comfortable.  The water in the shower would not run from the faucet, only the shower heads.  There was a bidet in the area with the toilet which made that area crowded.  Our room overlooked one of the restaurants in the atrium below so it would get pretty loud in the mornings when they staff was setting up for the day.  We were also right off the main lobby and down the hall from the night club so we could hear the music at night.  It never lasted into the wee hours, though.  Housekeeping was cursory in my opinion.  We were never provided with enough towels and I had to call regularly to have more provided.  They failed to come until late afternoon on our last day and I had to decline because my child was napping.  

Dining - Breakfast consists of the buffet.  It was very good and provided many options (although to my husband’s disappointment, there was no bacon).  We liked to sit outside during breakfast and lunch and the service was great.  Lunch consisted of the buffet and you can order from the Market Grill menu if you sit outside.  Dinner options included the buffet or reservations at one of the specialty restaurants.  We dined at Ibana and Fuego.  Ibana was ok and we weren’t able to finish our meal at Fuego through no fault of theirs.

Pool and Beach – The pool area is very large.  There are three sections and one is exclusive to Royal Service.  We spent most of our time at the beach and we never had an issue getting loungers.
