I didn't realise it was leaking and slipped on the water which was on the floor. The same thing happened in a colleagues room too. For a 5* resort I really did not expect this. I went to order room service and was advised it would take over 1hour!!

reviews.author: Sez0sborne
reviews.title: Fairly good
reviews.text:
The hotel itself is huge I didn't even get to see it all as I was only there 2 days.
Large rooms, but there was a group of us an we all had items in our rooms that didn't work, eg hair dryers, phones.

Staff were friendly and great location.
This is not a quiet hotel, there is music going and water fountains but fantastic if your in Cancun for a party.

reviews.author: dantle75
reviews.title: Good resort but disappointed services
reviews.text:
We are a group of multi-families (25 of us) and were staying at 5 days at Paradisus Cancun during past July 4th weekend. This hotel is beautifully decorated, the pools are great and beach is white sand and pristine clear. Food choices are excellent and the buffet is decent. There're no time share salemen as people stated here. The rooms are as nice as the pictures shown on website. The wi-fi internet is working great throughout the hotel and room. Here are a few things I want you to know before booking with Paradisus Cancun:
1)      You have to ASK for literally everything on what they claim they will provide. We booked Family Concierge rooms and according to the web site, we should get kid welcome packages. None of the room got it. We have to ask for them. We should receive $500 vouchers because of 5 nights stays but again, we have to ask for them and the vouchers won’t be available till next day. When we checked in, they’re rushing us out without even directing us to where to go to the rooms. (this resort is massive and you will be lost first time). They’re not even asking us for upgrade.
2)      The staff is nice overall but you HAVE to ask for everything.
3)      Services along the pool and beach are very slow. The resort is too BIG. It takes long time for them to go over each section of the pool.
4)      Forget about booking cabanas, they’re all reserved way in advance. But if you showed up late of the day, you can probably just hop onto the empty ones.
5)      The restaurants are HARD to book the time you’d like so be flexible and get ready. The buffet and a la carte ones do not provide much variety of sea foods. But lots of meats for meat lover.
6)      Nightly entertainment is just one hour and not much interaction like Riu, we’re quiet disappointed. We got in during the Mexico election time and there’re no alcohol served for 2 days at the bar.!!!
7)      It is so bloody hot in the lobby area and Avenue bar because there’s no AC. They have many fish ponds thus there are lot of MOSQUITOS. We got bitten quiet a bit. When I saw an OFF bottle in the room, I didn’t realize mosquitoes are in the rooms until my daughter got bitten so many times.
8)      TEMPO is very expensive. Even with the vouchers, we have to pay quiet a bit and they have all kind of service charges in the bill. So be aware of it. The food is good there but the cost does not justify it.
9)      Overall the foods are great. (Except not lots of sea food choices). We love Vento, Fuego and Bana. They’re hard to book so book in advance.
10)  Across the street is AquaWorld for water activities. You can kayak for free.
11)  The kid pool is very nice but it can be long walk. The adult pools are deep and they don’t have infinity pools.
 
We’ve been in Cancun before and have stayed at Riu and Oasis and this is our first time with Paradisus. We doubt that we will be back here, mostly because of services, lack of entertainments and mosquitoes in the lobby area.

reviews.author: Francine_jm
reviews.title: Tolerable
reviews.text: Karla from family concierge was one of the only reasons our entire trip was not entirely ruined!  When we first arrived a resort employee approached us and found our name on a list then directed us (family of 4 + 1 infant) to a wiring room with a line, after waiting in line and providing my printed out reservation confirmation paperwork the lady at the desk did allot of typing without acknowledging me to finally have someone tell me I had been directed to the wrong waiting room!  We then were taken to the family concierge waiting room where we waited another  30 minutes, while being taken care of I provided my $1000.00 resort credit paperwork to the female employee who said they had the info in the computer (never providing our vouchers) then we were introduced to Karla to take us to our room that was to be a lagoon view!  Karla was extremely friendly, informative and helpful!  When we arrived at our room #4017 I went straight to look at the view since we were told we couldn't upgrade to an ocean view with our $300.00 credit due to the resorts over booking issue, and our view was a wall not a lagoon not sand or grass or flowers but a wall to a ramp for the employees to travel by golf cart!  Karla was extremely apologetic stating she would try to help us with another room if possible, I explained I would try again the next day and for her not to worry!  The next day (06-27-13) after inquiring on how to use our resort credit we were finally provided with the vouchers we were suppose to receive upon arrival!  We were also told for 2 more days we could not be accomadated with a room upgrade, we had dinner prebooked requesting a different place everyday (through family concierge) we were booked market grill 3 days in a row but only went 1, Karla last minute was able to get us a reservation at vento after we were turned down at bana where we were supose to be reserved for (the hostess at bana was very unfriendly) which we were grateful! The childrens mini bar for 3 days was not being restocked to accommodate all 3 children but 2, Karla also took care of that for us!  Our room was'nt cleaned or restock the towels!  The first day cookies and milk for turn down time were not delivered that was also taken care of the delivery was between 8:30pm and 10:00pm which was very late so the baby was asleep for some deliveries but was able to eat his cookie as a pool snack the next day!  The kid zone we only utilized once on 07-02-13 the staff was very friendly,, one girl (can't remember her name her birthday was on 07-03-13 to make her 20yrs old) held the baby rocking him until he fell asleep just because she wanted to!  On 07-02-13 we looked all over the resort for any boxes to package an item we purchased to take on the plane, that was an all day project a store that sells tape & boxes would be helpful!  Over all some of the family concierge staff need to be more informative about services provided, thank god for a couple of the staff our stay was tolerable!

reviews.author: nicole s
reviews.title: For the price, its ok
reviews.text: I just returned 3 days ago from a girls getaway to the Paradisus.    We stayed in building 3 and while we thought the interior of the hotel was amazing we felt the food and entertainment were a bit lacking.    A word of advance, make reservations as soon as you check in.   We paid for all inclusive but then were told more than once that all of the places to eat were booked.   So we had to eat in the cafateria type setting.    Also, they do not have a coffee "station" which was frustrating.   You can order room service but it took 45 minutes.   Again, it doesn't feel all inclusive if you can't eat and drink where you would like.   We weren't asking for coffee at odd times, it was the morning.   You could get coffee in Naos, which is the cafeteria basically but you couldn't take it out of the area.   The beach and view are amazing so I suppose you have to consider the trade off.   It was clean and reasonably priced so I guess the other things are minor.  We also were disappointed that they had zero entertainment.   After 9:00 we would desperate for something to do.   They did have a few bars open but nothing was going on.  In fact they had small children running around in them.   Again, nothing tragic just little frustrations.

reviews.author: Evkvlev
reviews.title: Just Average
reviews.text:
The hotel is very nice and huge, common areas are relaxing, but our room was just average and not like the ones pictured(outdated furniture, ants in the kitchen, flat screen tv and free wifi). Pyramid two were the "members" stay was very neglected and seemed out of place with the rest of the hotel. The staff is friendly, but the elevator in our pyramid was constantly out of service, good thing we were on the second floor. The hotel did not seem to be overcrowded and our pyramid seemed almost vacant. There was only one ice machine in the pyramid, and to get the gym is a workout on its own. I think the hotel has night entertainment, but we really not informed; although one night we did hear drums. If you don't get the all inclusive plan expect to pay for everything, extra coffee, water, and even local calls. The pool is deep, and you have access to the beach. We were unable to use the concierge service, since we kept missing her. Concierge did leave messages for us, she wanted to meet us and would call around noon and was there only up to five. So I guess if you want to be locked up in your room and not sightsee or tan in the beach, then you can use the concierge.If you want to go out to the main road expect a long walk.

We stayed June 15-22. Upon checking our baggage was received by the bellhop, we were half way escorted to the check in area for "members" in pyramid 1. We were assigned to Pyramid2 which seemed to be quite neglected, the water fountain was turned off. The room was to sleep six in two beds and a couch which they refer to as a bed. My husband and I ended up sleeping in the very uncomfortable couch/bed. The last two or three days we were greeted by the stench of oil based paint, the water fountain was being painted and it was very strong.

Over all since we got a very good deal on the hotel we didn't complain about the room or paint.  On the plus side we were never approached by any sort of time share salesperson. I guess since for some reason we were considered "members" ( we don't own a time share) we were not approached by anyone.

reviews.author: cbc739
reviews.title: Hope it will get better
reviews.text: Ok I have read a lot of reviews on this place both good and bad, but I came here with an open mind.  I have stayed at other 5star resorts and other older and lesser resorts, so I feel that I am not a snobby person when it comes to expecting things out of your vacation resort..  I am writing this resort after my first day and I am hoping that it will get better... when we arrived we were greeted by a  woman who took us into a check in area and said that someone would be right with us. Well after 15 min waiting No one came so i went to the desk and asked if I could check in, he asked if someone came to speak to us and the answer was no, so he brought us the the royal service area,because we purchased the royal service and they check u in a totally different area.  You can feel the difference as u walk to that part of the resort...so much more quieter than main building .it was very  busy and over run with kids..  Well after speaking to the concierge desk they introduced us to our butler .. Well he seemed very nice and helpful at first ,and was going to do several things for us 1) get us another lounge chair for patio 2) make dinner reservations for us for tonight and tomorrow.  Because u need reservations to eat at he good restaurants. 3) call the airline to check on our lost luggage 4) get us some other beverages for our room that HE suggested.4) make sure that the one piece of luggage that did make the trip be sent to our room.  He said he would find us at the pool area with an update before he left his shift.  Well 3 hrs later I went looking for him and and NOTHING was done... I couldn't believe it ! I mean the bell man took my luggage and didn't bring it to my room I had to inquire 3 times to get my bag..!!!  did absolutely nothing that he was suppose to .

reviews.author: Sonia B
reviews.title: Fooled By The Appearance Of This Hotel
reviews.text: Hands down, this hotel looks amazing when you walk in. As we checked in, we asked about the complimentary extra bed the manager had offered us via e-mail. The check in staff could not find this offer anywhere on their computer. I was a bit disappointed but I figured oh well. As soon as we walked in, our luggage was taken. The check in clerk tried to offer us a room upgrade for an additional price of  $100 a night. We declined because we thought paying $4,300 for 2 adults and two children for six days was enough dough already. As we opened the door to our room, we noticed there were two small beds crammed into one small room. We then waited about 30 minutes for our luggage and had to call the reception desk. We were told that we had to have given the bell boy a ticket. What ticket????? Finally our luggage was delivered 20 minutes later. Second night we woke up totally hot in that room because the A/C wasn't cooling the room. We must have reported this problem about three times to three different people and still the problem persisted throughout our stay. We gave up and decided to take cold baths. The all inclusive deal seemed like the best choice. The food was ok, but the service was horrific!!!!!! Trying to get any drink from any waiter was like  pulling teeth!!! So If you were choking on some lettuce. too bad better bring your own drink. These waiters make it a point to avoid you like the plague. The two exceptions were Concepcion and Irving an awesome bartender who was very personable and very customer oriented. They seemed to care about customers. We complained a few times, but the managers were like ,"Oh sorry." The outdoor grill eating area had us waiting about 30 minutes to an hour for our food. The drinks were like forget it!!! To add insult to injury, we were offered a great discount price to visit any attraction. Come to find out the next day, it was for the lovely price of attending a time share sermon for their hotel. Your promised 90 minutes but it hit close to three hours. The biggest joke is that they want to sell you a time share that runs in the thousands for a hotel that delivers bad service. I would recommend for anyone that decides to book in this hotel to wait at least two days before you attend any time share, so that you can see how their service is for you.  The hotel has a lot of potential, although we feel that management really should focus more on customer service and then focus on trying to sell their time shares.  Were surprised they are still in business. Using trip advisor led us to choose this hotel because of the reviews, but seriously we would advise anyone else to pick another hotel. If you expect customer service, you will be disappointed.

reviews.author: Maha I
reviews.title: Not as expected
reviews.text:
I write this review while still there, I went to several resorts in Rivera Mayan, most of caribean but this is my first trip to Cancun. Negative points :1-  food at the buffet are same everyday, limit food choices. 2- no nightly entairtenment at all , we were 2 families & we got really boredom at night cause there is non to do except sitting at Avenue bar lounge which play very annoyed music like sever repeatative drum beats that gave you headache. Same music played every day!!!                           3- there is no beach service, you have to go to the bar yourself.        4- the pool is very deep start from 5,1 feet to 6 . This is ridiculus as I am short 5 feet & don't swim!!        5- the ground level of the hotels which is the most lovely area in the hotel is completely occupied with Japanese sushi restaurant ( I am not fan of sushi ) so I don't get a chance to sit there.                        6- the grill on the pool area late limited to burger & hotdog!             7- service are very slow unorganized. Barley to find any one to help you seating in buffet which really small& we have to find a big table for our family. If we got a table , it wouldn't be properly set for 6 persons. asked the servers to make it ready for us & ended up that we grap forks & knives from tables around us.       Positive points: 1- good size cleaned ocean view room.                    2- ver clean , nice interior d
decoration . I don't think I''l come back or recommend it to our friends.

reviews.author: akinang
reviews.title: Not bad but not 5 stars
reviews.text:
I just got back from this resort today.  Overall stay was pretty decent but a few problems.

Elevator was out of serive most of the time and if it was working... VERY SLOW.

Food... You don't have much options for breakfast of lunch.. and menu is very consistent. . We were there for 5 nights and by 4th day I couldnt even look at them.  They have other restaurants but they all require reservations except one but out of 5 nights we were there, ive seen this place open just once.   I cant say nuch of other restaurants because im very picky and all I can say is if u r picky this isnt the place for u. But they have an awesome juice bar for breakfast.

reviews.author: Saharism
reviews.title: Just OK
reviews.text:
My husband and I stayed there June 7-10, 2013. We did not do the Royal Service because it was sold-out. I had read most of the recent reviews of this resort prior to going. I would have to agree with those who believe the food is not good. It is actually surprising to read that people were pleased with the food. I am not a very picky eater, and we are not food snobs, but we enjoy eating out at great restaurants on regular basis so I know what "good" food should taste like.  There was not one dish that I thought was good.  So, food-wise we were disappointed.

As for the resort itself, we were pleased with the beach, our room and the total ambiance of the resort. There were some minor issues such as the jacuzzi in our balcony didn't work; the resort is huge and we were given the very last room on the 5th floor on the very last building to the right (1st tower), so we had a 10 minute walk in order to get to the center building that houses all of the restaurants, bars, and stores.  As you can imagine this is not everyone's cup of tea specially when you realize you've left the sunscreen back in the room. Also, the main elevator was broken the whole time, but the service elevator was available.

The resort staff were all very friendly. I specifically remember Leonardo was our waiter at The Market Grill restaurant and he was excellent, very kind, and friendly. 

As for drinks, they are not strong so just ask for what you really want and I'm sure they will accommodate you, as I said before the waitstaff are friendly. 

Also, we had no problem making reservations at the restaurants, but we were only 2 people. 
Also, there were plenty of chairs available by the beach and by the pool. 

One thing I would like to suggest to those traveling to this resort with children, I highly recommend  using the far right beach area (directly in front of building 1) as the currents are much calmer, because for some reason there is a sandy shore further into the water that breaks the waves before they hit the main beach area on that part. We found out about this on our last two days there.

Bottom line, even though we did not have the "Royal Service" we still had fun. But, would we go back? probably not because of how disappointed we were with the food.

reviews.author: Cassiopeea
reviews.title: Dissappointing!
reviews.text:
We stayed for 7 nights: end of May to beginning of Jun. This was my first trip to Cancun, and to Mexico.

Pros:
The hotel is beautiful.

Food was very good. Particularly, we loved the Japanese food at Bana restaurant (sashimi). The Market Grill steak was delicious, as well as the lobster.

There are some professional staff that are worth mentioning: Angelica at the Family Concierge, a true asset to the company, and a waiter at the Bana restaurant -the best we met there; unfortunately, I did not get his name.

The Family Concierge is a nice addition to a family with kids. They bring milk and cookies to your room at 7pm. They have a separate check-in/out, and separate activity rooms for kids.

Cons:
The room/suite is not very spacious and lacked the “wow’ factor. We stayed in a 1 bedroom ocean view - family concierge. The bedroom was smaller than the room/suites we stayed in at other 4 star hotels in the Carribeans, for considerably less money. The living room is extremely small, a bit larger than an opened sofa bed. The air conditioning in the living room was extremely noisy, you could not sleep, or worse, put a baby/toddler to sleep in there, as we originally thought of.

The bathroom is extremely small- the smallest I have seen in all my travels in the Carribeans. For a family with kids this may be difficult.

The ocean views are actually partial views- we had 2 balconies with partial ocean views.

The beach is quite steep. The waves were quite strong. There was a red flag all week. For somebody that pays a high price to come to Cancun just to bathe in a pool, that is really annoying.  

The hotel got flooded due to the storm and heavy rains. Our room got flooded, too (we had bad weather 4 days out of the 7 of our stay). They did come in and put towels on the floor, around the balcony door, when we called them. There was water dripping everywhere, including the restaurants, and all staff was desperately trying to clean it. One or two elevators were out of order for quite some time. But for a 4.5 star hotel, to see all these disturbances seemed quite embarrassing. 

Service was lacking quality in many areas. Water was not freely served at the table. You had to ask for it. In any (all-inclusive) restaurants water should be served at your table without having to ask for it, or at least be available for self service. Some waiters at morning or lunch buffet, seemed somewhat disorganized; you had to ask for coffee or water- sometimes having to remind them, instead of being asked if you needed anything. Some staff were not nice or probably waiting to tip them. Juan from the Family Concierge pool, would call you by your last name without using a Mr. or Ms.- plain rude. The 2nd and 3rd day of our stay we did not get the milk & cookies for our toddler, but after we complained to the concierge, we got them right on time.

Night Entertainment- completely inexistent. No shows, no dancing, no music in the hotel, no kids entertainment. Practically nothing to do at night, except for having a drink at the Avenue bar (which seems to be for adults only). As I said, we have travelled to the Carribeans for less money, and had stayed at hotels that had night entertainment every single day: excellent shows, followed by disco where everybody was invited to dance, very funny contests and lots of fun, live piano concerts in the lobby.

There is a scent throughout the hotel, probably coming from the spa, which was unpleasant for me; much like the scent in an Orthodox church during a Sunday service. 

The hotel credits- one can barely take advantage of them. First, if you bought a 7-day stay –all inclusive, on line or through a travel agent, you probably are eligible to receive $ 1,000 worth of resort coupons. My advice,  ask for them at check in time, or the receptionist will probably not tell you until the check out, as it happened to a friend of mine at Paradisus, Playa del Carmen. At check in, I was not told about the hotel credits, and I asked Fernanda at the end, who then told me that we qualified, and I should come the next day to pick them up. But here is the catch: The coupons are divided in such a way that one either spends more money on wine, spa treatments, or dinner at Tempo (adults only), or one loses them. The $1,000 is broken down as follows:

1*$300 to upgrade your room; chances are they will not be able to upgrade it, so you lose it- it happened to a family we met there.

3*$50 in spa treatments. Spa is extremely expensive. The only spa treatment I could find in exchange for one coupon was a wash and hair cut or a reflexology treatment, but I decided not to use it. You cannot buy a 30 min massage- and you have to sign that you agree with this. 

6* $50 worth of food or beverage. One can use one coupon only per meal (not per day). So if you order lobster for you, you cannot use another coupon to buy a second lobster for your spouse. Also, you cannot use another coupon to order wine at the same time. It happened to us, so we only ordered one lobster which we divided in two.

5*$20 worth of wine coupons. But the cheapest wine is around $50US-if I was told correctly by the waiter, so you end up paying more than the value of the coupon for a bottle of wine. There is no wine list hard copy, they give you a tablet to scroll through the countries and wines. Go to COSTCO and buy good wine there, for less than $15 a bottle.

1*$150 dinner at TEMPO.

We will never return to Paradisus, and probably Cancun either.

reviews.author: kenh79_13
reviews.title: 20th wedding anniversery
reviews.text: We were in the royal service for 1 week. We e-mailed the resort 3 times before arriving and got no reply to our emails. Called 1 once and no help. We arrived 5/30/13 and were told they were over booked and did not have a king bed room. A full size bed is very hard for a couple to sleep comfortable in(they called it a double). The coupon book they give you has a $300.00 room upgrade which does you no good because they don't have any rooms to upgrade you to. after 3 days I ask the front desk if there were any king rooms and I was told they would look into it and get  back to me but never did. The room we were given 5119 had no toilet paper in it when we first arrived and had to ask for the bed to be made up 3 times. No discount was ever offered or offer made to make it right for us. Samuel our butler was the greatest and I would ask for him again.The food was outstanding the need for reservation in the restaurants seems to be unneeded,because every time we made reservations the place had so many empty tables the whole time we were there. The bally beds and staff were outstanding. We would recommend royal service to anyone going without kids.

reviews.author: CacoFa
reviews.title: Excellent Service / so so maintenance
reviews.text:
Stayed at The Paradisus Cancun in April 2013.  We have been a fan of this hotel since it was the Gran Melia.  It is now an all inclusive resort.  We are not big fans of all inclusive, but I must say that this time it was worth it. Food options are good and well prepared.  Drinks are of good quality in general, need to pay extra if you want specific high brand liquor.  The inclusive wine selection is fair.

We took the Family Concierge option.  A private reception desk, personal concierge through our stay (they even give you a cellphone so that you can call your concierge!).  It is truly a remarkable service and they do go the extra mile.  Special thanks to Paty!  Paty would leave cookies and chocolate milk for the kids every night.  Kids received a welcome package...backpack, t-shirt, vanity kit and beach toys.  This is really designed for kids aged 2-6.

As usual, the hotel is beautiful.  Nice beach.  I presume that when close to full occupancy, it can be a challenge re pool area and restaurants.

Throughout our stay, the service was outstanding.

My bigger complain is maintenance. Our AC unit was not working properly and even when our room was a non-smoking one, there was an "old cigarette" smell coming from one of the AC's and they were never able to make it go away.  The sofa bed that my kids were sleeping in, was not in a good shape, but bearable. 

Second complain was the loud music around the pool bar...not so much the music, but the type of music.  I prefer a "nicer" environment.

All in all a great experience.

reviews.author: heal101124
reviews.title: Great stay minus the weather!!
reviews.text:
Just returned home from Cancun after 5 days.  Unfortunately, the weather ruined most of our plans while in cancun as well as our stay.  We were unable to enjoy the beach, pool, outdoor bars, etc. 
Rooms/Service: 
We had upgraded our reservations to the Royal Service.  This was definitely worth the upgrade for the most part.  Serlf-service bar with premium liquors, snacks all day/night, quick check in and out, liquor of choice in room, wonderful updated/modern room with a oceanview, etc. Although what seemed like so many extras really weren as we discovered the rest of the resort areas/bars.  The other bars had almost all of the same liquors minus a few and every other person who wasnt staying in the Royal Service could make reservations at the same restaurants that we could.. Ive stayed at many all inclusives and I will say that this one had amazing food.  Fuego and Venot being my favorite. 
 
The Royal Service side was very quiet which was nice, but almost too quiet at times.  Ive read many reviews about the Butler service but honestly we really didnt see or hear from ours other than the first night and the last night.  Victor at the concierge was great.  He upgraded our room the second day and was always seeing how we were doing.  He also made all of our restaurant reservations as we were never asked by our butler until the last day.  Consuelo who we ran into the first night was very accomodating and treated us like family during our stay.  She was aboslutely amazing!!!  

Overall:
Besides the overall disappoint of the weather which ruined all of our excursions, pool/beach, outside time, and did I mention the crazy flooding in the hotel because of the non-stop rain...the only other things that disappointed me was the lack of entertainment in the hotel and the lack of air condition. (The whole hotel was always very warn and muggy which made eating dinner uncomfortable ) There was never any music playing anywhere, games, shows, etc.  There was just not much to do in the hotel..and considering we were stuck inside it wasnt good.  Only place there was music was at Avenue bar at night which was basically the only bar to even go to at night.  Red lounge was closed almost every night we were there...probably from the flooding issue in the hotel.  I have stayed at other all inclusives that were less expensive and there was entertainment all day/night.  Nothing here at all!!  Basically if youre going just to relax on the beach, eat, sleep,  and then back to the room its the perfect place.

Overall the hotel was beautiful though.  Very clean and close to downtown and the airport.  We arranged transportation with USA Transfers which was great. Would I go back to the Paradisus???   Probably not, but not because of the service there or aesthetics of the hotel... just because of lack of entertainment and things to do.

reviews.author: Paolavpr
reviews.title: Not the place for me
reviews.text:
I just went on vacation with my fiancé, we usually go to ME Cancun but wanted to try something new for a change. We decided to try Paradisus Cancun, but it was not exactly what we expected but made the most out of it anyways. 

Our arrival to the hotel was OK, we were staying at the Royal Service which has some nice perks. Our butler came to get us and took us to the private check in area, which is on a different tower from the main hotel. It’s nice and more private and it’s only for adults, which is nice.  We felt like the overall hotel was very dark and gloomy, it could use a lot more light to make the ambiance better, does not feel too welcoming specially when you’re walking in between towers. 

One of the things we really liked was having our butler take us to the room to show us were everything was, as well as to take care of everything we needed. We had Hector as our designated butler and he was really nice and sweet. One of the perks we got was to get our clothes unpacked, which was nice not to have to worry about; he organized everything really nicely and neat. 

Another nice thing was having a private pool for the royal service, with cabanas and a bar, unfortunate the restaurant by the pool was not open during our stay due to rain as well as the La Perla restaurant which seemed really nice on the website but while we were there we found out that they are not always open so that’s a bit misleading. 

I think the food overall was really nice, especially at dinnertime, Fuego and Mole had amazing food. The Naos buffet was nice as well; it had plenty of options to choose from as well as Market Grill.  The service by the royal pool was excellent as well, the 2 bartenders there were very friendly.  Blue Agave was also excellent, specially at the bar, they had amazing cucumber margaritas. 

They definitely need to improve in a lot of areas and especially in their management, it’s a very large place and at times it felt understaffed, not everyone there was friendly which when you’re on vacation is so important to feel welcomed and special. Also our room was not what it looked like in the photo, since they changed to Paradisus from the Gran Melia I don’t think they upgraded the rooms, it was not modern and clean at all like it showed on the website. 

Was not the place for us but it might be the place for you if you don’t care so much about details.

reviews.author: Dave D
reviews.title: Great Pool Service but Average Hotel
reviews.text:
My wife and I traveled May 19th - 26th and opted for the Royal Service.  We were not there during the busy season, and my review is based on my experience.  There were both pros and cons to the resort, and I will try to outline the things that stood out for us:

1.  The pool staff of Vincente and Sergio at the Royal Service private pool were great and took the time get to know us and made us feel like true VIP guests.  They and other staff provided exceptional service with the Bali beds, drink , & food service. You truly don’t have to move from your chair if you don’t too with the exception of going to the restroom.  This was by far the best pool service my wife and I ever experienced.

2.  The hotel is located on the beach and the white sand and ocean are absolutely beautiful.  Cabanas and chairs were generally easy to get and did not see the chair reservation game you generally see other at all-inclusive resorts.  It is located about 15-20 min from the airport and a short bus ride $1(US) per person each way to the downtown area of Cancun.

3.  The rooms were adequate and had a comfortable king bed (We were only really there to sleep, shower and rest) Large enough and clean.  We opted for the ocean-front room and we had two chairs on our balcony, but we had about a 3.5 ft. wall that prevented a breeze or view while sitting on the balcony. Our air conditioning in our room was not a concern. 

4.  The food was good not great, but met our expectations for an all-inclusive.  Staffs at the restaurants were adequate, as you need to understand that things move at a slower pace.  

As for the cons of the resort:

1.  The biggest disappointment for me about the hotel is the lack of open-air seating and ocean views for dinner.  All of the restaurants with the exception of one was inside with a view of the interior gardens.  Please don’t get me wrong, they are beautiful, but I wanted to see the ocean and feel the breeze while eating dinner.   After being in the sun all day, the lack of any air movement or air conditioning in the restaurants made it uncomfortable.

2.  We lost power and water on a couple occasions as previous other reviews stated.  I understood about the losses as these things occur, but the lack of communication when we requested to information about the problem and resolution was horrible.  We were lied too and there was not a single apology from the Royal Service desk about the problem.  In addition, the lack of a contingency plan for these problems is concerning for such a large hotel as it put a slight damper on stay.  This was our first red flag about how the management treated their guests.

3.  We did receive letter-requesting volunteers to move to another hotel, but we declined.  We later found out that they were trying to make room for a large group of people to attend the hotel.  We heard about people not permitted to stay at the hotel even though they had reservations.

4.  Liquor was water down and beer was not as cold as I am accustomed to in the US.  The line I keep telling everyone when they ask me about the drinks at the hotel was  "Even the ice was not cold at the resort."

5.  Here is a breakdown of the liquor and beer at the resort:  Beer: Tec ate Light, Dos Equies and Heineken in the room only - Vodka was Absolute in all the bars and Grey Goose in the Royal Service lounge but it was watered down - Rum: Captain Morgan, Myers, and Malibu - Scotch was Jonny Walker Black - Tequilas were plentiful as expected.

6.  There is a younger famine gentleman that checked us in and was very rude and condescending.  We encountered this on many occasions by this gentleman throughout our stay as he was at the Royal Service desk.

7.  Our butler service was over hyped by the hotel as he tended to be over extended and would forget to follow up on requests and make our restaurant reservations.  After the second day, you will learn to make your reservations with the Royal Service desk and work directly with the Sergio and Vincente on making pool area or beach chair reservations.

8.  Hotel offered no shows or nightlife with the exception of the Red Lounge and Avenue Bar and these were just ok (again we were not here during the peak season).  I guess this is because downtown is so close, but I was not aware that there was no nightlife on the resort.

Overall your vacation is what you make of it and the rating I provided was on the hotel and amenities during my stay.   We had a great time and certain staff members were better than others.  I personally would not go back, but if you get a good deal I would not steer you away from this resort.  At the same time, if you are going to pay a premium for this hotel, you may want to read other reviews and be cognoscente that some of the reviews and high rating may have been inflated by marketing personnel of the hotel.

reviews.author: Nicole S
reviews.title: This place was OK
reviews.text:
I went here in January and forgot to review. The hotel itself was nice enough but I wouldnt call it 4 star. You have to walk half a mile to get to the lobby from your room if youre in any building other than the main building. At one point I slipped on the stairs and sprained my ankle because theres only 1 elevator per wing and countless floors. 
The buffet breakfast was good.Other than that the food was awful. I like to think of myself as a foodie, Im willing to try anything and there is no style food I will not eat.
The first night we went to the asian restaurant. We ordered tuna sushi and a curry dish. The tuna was warm, which if you eat sushi know that is kind of gross. The curry was by far the worst thing I ate there. It tasted like throw up. It was so bad we couldnt even eat it and had to order room service just for something somewhat decent.
The tapas restaurant they had wasnt the worst but anything that was fish related tasted fishy. The scallops were over cooked and reaked of fish to the point where I almost got sick at the table. 
The other two restaurants they have werent too bad, but they werent good. 
The pool was nice if a little cold. The beach was beautiful. We got yelled at for taking a late night stroll though, that wasnt very nice. 
Id say this was the worst part:
Check in time was at 3pm. I called before we left requesting early check in. By the time we got there we were told our room was almost ready and to just speak with a man and he will explain hte hotel to us and show us to our room. Well, this man was really telling us about a time share.There were excursions we wanted to take and he told us to go to the timeshare seminar and that it would take 2 hours and we would receive a discount. It took almost 4 hours, we lost an entire day of laying at the pool or doing anything and the guy that was speaking to us was annoyed that we werent really interested in the program that we just wanted the discounts. The worst part about this was that after spending the 4 hours to get a massage at half price, the massage was possibly the worst massage I ever had. I usually feel like passing out after a massage, after this one I felt like I was more tense. It was almost like they gave us a bad massage because we paid less.
I would definitely not recommend this hotel.

reviews.author: TheHotelInspector1
reviews.title: A very nice Hotel with so much potential but poor room and lack of staff training in some areas let it down!
reviews.text:
Just returned from 9 nights at the Paradisus Hotel which sadly I could only rate as average. First impressions of the Hotel were excellent as the communal areas were spotlessly clean, well organised and maintained.

On arrival, we were met by a friendly member of staff who showed us to reception whilst the bell boy took care of our luggage. The reception is located on the left hand side behind a glass partition. The check-in was slow and haphazard - it was clear that there is a lack of training. I enquired as to whether we could upgrade to an ocean view room and was told that as the Hotel was barely half full that this would be fine and not a problem. After a colleague had a word with him, he then told me (in a very timid way) it would be $35 a night when he originally appeared to indicate it would be free. It really puzzled me as I had a resort room upgrade credit of $300 so it wouldn't be costing me anything anyway so it was a pointless exercise! Having sorted out the room, we were then passed on to another person who sat us in the reception area and gave an overview of the Hotel. This process went on forever and as we had been travelling for 18 hours, it was too much. Eventually she said she would show us to our room. In fact, she showed us to the lift and said have a nice stay.

Our first impressions of the room were underwhelming. The whole room was very dated and tatty. Most of the fixtures in the bathroom were held together with white filler, the glass mirror was very tarnished and it was clear that a refurb was well overdue. The room itself was spacious, although the sofa and seat fabrics were stained. Again the furniture needed replacing and the room given a facelift. A fridge was provided which stocked water, sodas and beer which was nice. Flatscreen TV provided with a wide range of channels. The balcony was full of broken plaster and on examination, it was clear that the whole facade of the building was crumbling. The flower planter was full of plaster debris/ litter and it was disappointing that there was only one sun lounger and no table.

As 30 minutes had passed, we were getting frustrated that no luggage had yet arrived but remained patient. A further 15 minutes later, the phone rang from bell services to say our luggage was on its way. This arrived a further 15 minutes later so we waited an hour which is a little off.

We took a tour of the main building (which our room was located in) and were really impressed with the Hotel and its facilities. All the staff we encountered on this tour were very charming - always smiling and very pleasant indeed. The restaurants/ bars were all very well appointed, really clean and impressive - as were the pool areas.

On arrival back at the room, we decided to take a shower and have an early night. Water temperature was lukewarm at best and the water took an eternity to drain away in the bath and sink which was disappointing. Beds were comfortable but pillows were of poor quality and really thin. Air conditioning was very loud and ineffectual so room never particularly cool. Our room was located right above the bar/club so it was hard to sleep but I chose not to switch rooms so can't make an issue of this.

The following represents a summary of pros/cons of the Hotel following the rest of our stay:

PROS:
Fantastic staff at pool and in all the restaurants/ bars. 
Food was of excellent quality - no complaints here (although the food served at Fuego was always on the cool side due to distance from kitchen)
Fridge replenished fully every day 
Housekeeping to a very good standard in room
A special mention of the poolside waiter LUIS. He looked after us nearly every day and was fantastic in every respect - a fine ambassador for the Hotel. On my birthday, he got the kitchen to make a "cake" with "Happy Birthday David" iced on to the plate. He also got his colleagues to sing Happy Birthday to me whilst tapping a tray with a spoon - it was a lovely touch and very much appreciated. We were only sad that we left on Luis's day off and could not thank him once again before we left - what a star!
Lovely location and brilliant 
facilities
A special thank you to EMMA who looks after customers in and around reception, she looked after us in the reception whilst we were waiting for our airport transport - an absolute credit to the Hotel and highly professional (see below)
CONS
Rooms in desperate need of a full refurbishment and freshen up - especially the bathrooms
Questionable "top shelf" branded spirits - very watered down or not the real thing
Reservation service appalling - we were always told restaurants were fully booked or given times such as 630pm for dinner. If you just visited the restaurant they allowed you to book at more or less anytime or turn up without reservations 
On one occasion we returned to the room as key card was not working. After queuing for nearly an hour at reception (as no one else could help) our card was replaced after the agent had checked the name against the room. On returning to the room, the card still did not work. After waiting again, the same agent checked the card and said it was fine so the problem must be the actual room lock. He told me someone from maintenance would be right up. After waiting a further 30 minutes at the room without anyone coming, I returned to reception. On arrival, the same agent was walking away from the desk so I approached him to outline my anger. He literally turned his back and ignored me so as a result, I tapped him on his shoulder and he returned behind the desk and I told him that nobody had come to help. I got no apology, no nothing and when I repeated my room number, it was then clear that he had replaced my card but used the incorrect number which he was giggling about with his colleagues. At this point, I was so angry, I asked for a supervisor who dealt with the situation well - apologised profusely and accompanied me to the room. He assured me he would deal with the agent but it wasn't very reassuring when I passed reception later that evening that the so called supervisor was sharing a giggle with the same agent. Staff on reception are very poor indeed and inadequate to deal with guests professionally. I might add that an employee who tries to look after guests in reception called Emma looked highly embarrassed throughout and tried so hard to help me from the start. When I initially arrived at reception to explain the problem, she attempted to get the issue to sort the key out straight away (rather than me queue for an hour) but was shunned by the same agent!
We never received one evening turndown service throughout our 9 night stay which was very disappointing 
On one day we received no housekeeping whatsoever even though we left the room at 9 and returned at 6!

In summary, this is a beautiful Hotel with so much potential to be excellent. The staff on the whole really are superb - outstanding in fact. The restaurants are well appointed and the food is excellent. The communal areas are well maintained and clean. Sadly, the rooms needs a full refurb and some of the reception staff need to be trained to a much more acceptable standard. I would recommend the Hotel but give realistic expectations.

reviews.author: ZIA H
reviews.title: Bad rooms added with bad service
reviews.text:
We got 3 rooms.  2 guys per room. 
We were supposed to get 2 beds in each room but they gave us 1 bed and a rollaway cot in each room.  They didn't even bother to tell us, they just sent us to the room after they made us wait 2 hours at the beach. 
They told us that a huge oil company from Brazil (petrobras) and that they reserved 650 room and they have to give them our rooms with 2 beds. 

This is not fair.  We booked months ago and even called and verified that our rooms were available,  then when we got there it was not. 

Restaurant staff is very nice and the food is pretty good.  Who ever the head of restaurants is,  is doing a great job. 
He/ she should train the front desk and reception staff. 

We paid about $650 pre person and we're very disappointed. 

The hotel is from from all the shopping and clubs. 

The Bell staff wouldn't even call a taxi for us.  They made us walk 5 mind to the street to catch a taxi. ..
But when anyone said taxi for AIRPORT. . They Bell staff would jump over backwards to get a taxi. . Kick backs / commission. .. It's sad really. 

I have been all over the place abs this was my worst hotel experience. 

I would not recommend this resort.

reviews.author: NYCgrl23
reviews.title: Find a nicer hotel.
reviews.text: With so many hotels to choose from in Cancun, we chose this one based on a recommendation. What a mistake. It's simply not worth the money. Their idea of renovation is adding a few cool restaurants and some flat screen tvs in the rooms, but they really should've concentrated on the little details that people want more of.

reviews.author: 3broncs
reviews.title: 3rd paradisus resort experience and very disappointed
reviews.text: Let me start by saying this was our 3rd Paradisus Resort. We book the Royal Service always. In the past the luxury and amenities were always amazing. But for this resort;1st the price went down the day before trip, they wouldn't honor it because it was within the 48 hour change window. 2nd we arrived @ Royal Service check in and were supposed to get upgrade, we didn't. There was much confusion at Royal Service check in (huge language barrier). Our room needed to be fumigated. Our travelling companion's room - phone wouldn't ring for incoming calls, tv didn't have all channels, clock radio was on the wrong time and we couldn't correct it. We stopped at Royal Service to ask for the items to be fixed, clock was fixed right away, tv was fixed the night before we left, & the phone was never fixed. Our butler (which we paid extra for) was no where to be found after he dropped us and our bags off at check in - we called him on the cell phone provided several times and he never returned our phone calls. We had to make our own dinner reservations with desk. When we checked out price was in pesos not us dollars, so when we arrived home and checked our credit card the price was more than on our confirmation. We called and were told it was because of exchange rate at time of departure and they wouldn't adjust it. Strange how they wouldn't honor a price reduction the night before but had no problem charging us more once our stay was complete. We had to dispute the increase with our credit card company. We played tennis - court was in serious need of repair and rackets were old and they only had 2 balls. Positives - food was amazing, royal service pool was lovely and pool staff was great, private royal service beach and bali beds were also great.

reviews.author: CL5309
reviews.title: Mixed review
reviews.text: Common areas including beach, bars, restaurants and conference facilities were nice. Bartenders, restaurant and concierge staff were friendly and efficient. Checkin staff in Royal Service office seemed poorly trained (eg lots of confusion regarding my credit card at checkout).  My room was large, but had strong musty odor which took getting used to. Also ants were in room. I was glad I was here by myself for business because I would not have wanted to have my family put up with room. Bed was very saggy. Food was ok. 3 or maybe 3.5 star property at best. If you like the whole all-inclusive scene this may not be a bad choice, but if quality vs quantity is your priority and willing to spend more I would probably check out the JW next door.

reviews.author: FrostbiteMB
reviews.title: Average Stay
reviews.text:
I'll begin by saying I was originally booked in the Paradisus La Esmeralda (Playa del Carmen) until they decided to bump me therefore I arrived at the Paradisus Cancun not knowing what to expect.  I would also like to note that this was my first trip to Mexico and my first all-inclusive experience.

I had high expectations for the all-inclusive experience as I've heard many stories and read many reviews about attentive service.  Unfortunately, I can't say I was too impressed.  When we arrived at Paradisus La Esmeralda, we were greeted with a warm towel, cold beverage and the Porters took our luggage off our hands from the shuttle.  When we arrived to Paradisus Cancun, no one offered to take our luggage (or hold the door open for us), no warm towel or cool beverage.

We were originally given a standard room in the main building with a view of the lagoon.  Please note that the view of the lagoon is intercepted by the main road which is always busy (noisy).  the doors to the rooms are very thin and when the evening entertainment starts the music is easily heard in the room.  The standard room is just that.  Standard.  Bed, table, chairs, bathroom with shower/tub combo.  At the time they were repainting one of the atrium fountains and the smell/fumes easily made it's way into the rooms.  The building suffers from the typical problems of having high humidity indoors as shown by the crumbling plaster/concrete, peeling paint and indications of moisture build-up.

I would like to note though that the staff work very hard to keep the building and the grounds as clean as possible.  There are always workers cleaning windows, floors, groundskeepers etc. at all times of the day.  These Staff members were also always very friendly, always greeting you as you passed them in the halls.

Food and drinks at the restaurants and bars were very good although the burgers at the pool grill or room service aren't anything to brag about.  Service again was typically very friendly and good overall.

We spent a lot of time on the beach and we didn't get the all-inclusive service we were expecting.  Example, one day we spent 5 hours on the beach.  A waiter visited us only 2 times.  One time I didn't order anything, the second time he took our order and never came back.  Not exactly the luxurious service I was expecting.  In order to ensure I stayed hydrated on our next visit tot he beach I packed a bottle of water and soda from the room mini-fridge.  

The beach was beautiful with soft sand and turquoise water.  Keep in mind that the surf is rough and it is difficult to swim in.  I did find the pools challenging as well.  My wife and I are short (5'-5" and 5'-1") and don't swim very well.  The majority of the pool depths are approx. 5'-6' deep which makes things uncomfortable for us.

We received an upgrade the next day to a Studio Suite on the 6th floor in the Vacation Club building.  This room had a beautiful ocean view with a Jacuzzi on the balcony.  The balcony was actually smaller than the previous room with room for only one sun chair.

Again, we didn't get the sense of all-inclusiveness during our stay in the Studio Suite.  The mini-fridge was only replenished when we left a note to do so and we only got turn-down service once.  There were no mats on the floor and we found the marble to be cold and slippery at times so we had to wear our sandals in the room (I thought slippers & robes were supposed to be provided in all-inclusives).  

Did enjoy a morning in the spa which we received as incentive for attending the Vacation Club presentation.  The spa service was nice and the message was very good and relaxing.  The only thing is I wish they would tell you if you could continue to enjoy the amenities after your service as I felt as though I was rushed out when done.

Overall, this is a nice clean resort with good general service.  I'm not sure if I can say service went above and beyond as we did not experience evidence of such.  We're not sure if it was due to the fact that we had not originally booked with them or not.  Not as attentive or luxurious as we thought an all-inclusive would be.

reviews.author: STLCarib
reviews.title: Identity Crisis
reviews.text:
Paradisus is a nice place. But just a nice place. There is no way it is 4 to 5 star.

I agree with the reviewers that the grounds, beach and front line servers are absolutely wonderful. But the are certainly a lot of shortcomings.

On arrival, no cold drinks or towel, not even a bottled water...just a push to registration to a person with no smile, no thanks for coming...nothing. Then you are led off for a short orientation that isn't correct. Example, Naos...the morning buffet opens at 6 am per the person. Not true, you are lucky to get in by 6:40. You would think the management would discover that...but no.

The hotel is well laid out but shows considerable wear, cracked planter boxes, ragged plants, worn out mirrors, filthy room return vents. The rooms have spacious balconies but no furniture. No furniture? What is up with that? No lounge, no chair...just a plastic table from Walmart.

The breakfast buffet was a downer too, cold food and not very good in quality. One day bacon, the day next sausage, the next day neither....no breakfast meat. The whole restaurant system is run on the resort's convenience, not the customers. Reservations must be made even when the joint is empty. I saw lovely couples turned away when there were only 3 tables seated in Fuego. They were visibly upset but it was no matter to the staff....gotta follow the stupid reservation rule.

The bars have a great friendly staff but limited booze and mixer resources. Dos Equis is the only beer and lime is the only fresh fruit. You can sing "we have no bananas today" because there are none. I was surprised to see the resort re-using the plastic cups. A quick rinse of the cup and back in service it went, no matter where it was found...on the beach or any where. Not the most sanitary thing I have seen

As I have always found, the front line servers are very good and with a little monetary recognition they respond very well. Paradisus is tremendously overstaffed on the front line. There are more people standing around than working. 

The resort has the potential to be extraordinary but is managed to mediocrity.

reviews.author: hiram n
reviews.title: Hotel with glam, but lacking the whole package.
reviews.text: Just spent a week at the Paradisus Cancun.  At first glance when you arrive the hotel is spectacular and leads you to believe that you will have a great time full of great food and attractions.  That was not the case!  While the  staff was warm and friendly, and the rooms were very well kept and clean, the hotel did not deliver on the fun it promises.  The food was not to par with the glam appearance.  The restaurants were way too difficult to get into and often looked empty.  Restaurants would be closed on given days and not on others.  The food quality was poor and the restaurants never delivered it hot.  Bana looks the part of a award winning restaurant, but trust me, that sushi was something from a local super market.  The beach and grounds were amazing and the pool was nice but not enough life.  The red lounge needs a new DJ and the Ave Bar should be made into rooms with those beds, because it was so BORING.  The entertainment was rare but their Coco Bongo night was AWESOME !  Overall, I would say this hotel looks the part, and has all of the pieces to be a great hotel, but not made for a younger crowd or people looking for some fun in the sun.  More of an R&R type hotel.  I recommend doing the excursions offsite (Selvatica - Zip Lininig).

reviews.author: Sara1559
reviews.title: very nice staff, food ok
reviews.text: Our family of 4 (2 teenagers 14 & 18) spent 5 nights here in February. Every staff member we encountered was friendly and seemed to try hard but they couldn't always get the job done. We had constant problems with our room keys. The first time was our fault because the key was in a bag next to a phone which is not good for keys. It would have been a good idea to mention this when we were given our keys. They were very nice about getting us new keys. Another time, it was because the battery went on the door lock. Again, they were very nice about fixing this, but this possibility did not occur to them until after trying new keys twice more. The key thing went on with both of our rooms throughout the trip. The night before going on an early excursion the family concierge staff kindly offered to pack a back with towels, waters & snacks and have it sent to our room. Apparently they sent it to the wrong room. We called, they got one to us quickly and, again were very nice. We did not have high expectations for food and in some cases were pleasantly surprised - other experiences were just awful. Generally, we found the buffet to be pretty good. The grilled meat a the the open air grill restaurant was fantastic. We had very good food at Mole and the taco place. The Mediterranean tapas (this was not tapas) and the Asian restaurants were truly awful.  But, in every one of these places the staff could not have been more lovely. We did enjoy the Family Concierge service and the Bali beds by the pool were a nice perk. Our rooms were fine and they were clean - housekeeping was good - but a bit tired. I think there have been some renovations, but not our rooms. We booked two ocean view rooms (same price for each) but they were on the first floor and only one room actually had an ocean view (unless you stood on a chair).  We booked through a travel agency and, while not cheap, we felt as if it was very reasonable. The place is generally nice and the staff couldn't be nicer but next trip to Cancun, I'll look for another property.

reviews.author: Sue A
reviews.title: Melia turned Paradisus -- what's in a name!
reviews.text: This beautiful resort/hotel is trying to keep up with the current trend of being an all inclusive.  Don't believe it.  The Mexican restaurant is good and the breakfast buffet is outstanding but the rest of the restaurants are so-so.  I went of the ranch for all the rest of my meals. And they have now decided you have to wear a wrist band -- first year for that!  I felt like a dog being tagged.  Depending on your status it was a different color.  I have been coming to Cancun and the Melia for many years.  It is beginning to show its wear.  They need to put more into the physical place and less into the showy stuff like purple curtains in the bar.  As always the help are wonderful people.

reviews.author: michael d
reviews.title: POOR MANAGEMENT
reviews.text: just got back,average at best.by no means a 4 star resort.the working staff try very hard,but the management is top heavy.alot of staff that are some level of management but truely do not know their jobs.the food was o.k.but the best was victor in the market grill,he tryed so hard.this place has everything to be one of the best resorts but the big bosses are not wathing the store.

reviews.author: saminnewyork
reviews.title: Pros and Cons
reviews.text:
Trip: March 21st – March 29th
We decided to take this last minute family trip to Paradisus in Cancun since our college kids came home early, two adults plus three kids 21, 18 and 12.  This review is more factual points of pros and cons, rather than grievances.
Airport - first, when you get off the plane and head out past customs, DO NOT STOP !! go straight out through the sliding doors and proceed to go outside as quickly as you can. Do not stop to talk to any of the gray uniformed personnel flanking the exit to your right and left, they are TIME SHARE reps who will waste your time. They will try aggressive tactics such as : “Please follow me, it is my job to assist you”. Answer aggressively back “No thank you” and walk past them. Can’t believe I fell for it (they wasted ten minutes of our time before I realized what they were up to and gingerly left the area). Head out, look for your transportation representative (Apple – flowered shirts , Olympus tours – Orange shirts , GoGo – light blue shirts)  and they will take care of your party.

 The resort is very beautiful, with lush green plants and trees everywhere, kept immaculately clean by an ever present maintenance staff and because it was previously a non-all-inclusive hotel, the interior design is upscale but the logistics is definitely off and I’ll explain in a minute. The beach is exceptionally clean, sand is fine and the waters are gorgeous turquoise in hue. We’ve been going to all-inclusive resorts for the past twelve years so this is not our first time. Paradisus has recently been converted to an all-inclusive establishment and we learned that this is their first year in that capacity so for effort I would give them a solid 9/10, they do however need to improve a few issues.
Rooms:  the hotel is comprised of five pyramids, number three being the main building where the restaurants, club, lounges and bars are. I believe pyramids one and five are reserved for local folks who vacation and the inner pyramids are for tourists. 
Our reservation indicated a junior suite ocean view, but when we got there, we realized that their idea of a junior suite is two rooms adjacent to one another (not necessarily connecting) and even the connecting rooms available in the entire pyramid are very few and those are given on a first comes basis.  Our rooms were situated in pyramid three; rooms 3363 and 3364 with a beautiful ocean view. The housekeeping staff arrives nightly for a turn down service, offers complimentary plates of hors dourves and chocolates – really nice touch.
Housekeeping starts cleaning rooms at around 11:00 am and many times we would come back to the rooms at around 5:00 pm from the beach, and the staff would be so far away down the hall that any chance of getting our rooms fixed was slim. We ended up just asking them to come the next day and requesting fresh towels. Talking to other guests, we discovered that the housekeeping staff does it all the time to avoid cleaning all the rooms daily. 

Let me interject here and say from experience, that all places we visited outside the states had issues with punctuality, quality of service and attention to efficiency and a friend of mine said something rather true to me: when leaving the states, lower your expectations. 
Family concierge – we didn’t use but we heard other guests were very pleased with the service and you can rent cabanas for as low as $25 a day!
Food -   The place is definitely not ready as an all-inclusive resort. The dining hall has exactly 15 (we counted) indoor tables and on a hot muggy day, you will have to wait in line to sit in the air conditioned room. Outdoor ocean view seating is available but we just sat there sweating like pigs.
Sometimes, they decide to open the Fuego restaurant or the Vento restaurant (which are closely connected to the main dining room) for guests who have nowhere to sit but it’s at the discretion of the managers. Do not expect anything to open or start at the designated time. Immediately add another hour to any indicated time.  The breakfast buffet does not open at six, because by the time the staff sashays in at 6:30 and prepares everything, the place opens close to 7:00. If you have an excursion scheduled and is pressed for time, make sure you bring the issue to Francisco, the restaurant manager, and he will do his best to rectify the problem. ( I must say that the entire managerial staff is terrific and really tries to make sure all the guests are happy). In conclusion, the buffet room is tiny, food is okay, depends how picky you are.
Fuego restaurant – we loved it, it was exceptional Latin fusion cuisine and the service was impeccable.
Vento restaurant – It is Tapas bar and as you know the portions are small but they allow you to order 4 of each item per table.  Our reservation was for 6:00 pm, the food came out of the kitchen so slowly and so far in between, that the small portions were not enough for any of us so by 7:30 we just left and walked into the buffet to eat dinner.
Moles- Traditional Mexican cuisine – I thought the food was delicious, the onion buns and whipped cheeses were fresh and seasoned, I ordered the grouper and it was really well cooked, they accommodated my daughter who’s a vegetarian but my family didn’t think the food was anything special.
We didn’t try the Japanese, the Market Grill, Tempo or Blue Agave 
Pools-  Get your pool towels as soon as you get your rooms upon check in, by 5:00 pm the fresh ones are usually all gone.  Depending whether the hotel is at full capacity, you might have to go early in the morning (those who are seasoned all-inclusive travelers will know this already) and save yourselves chairs/palapas. Some people tip the outdoor maintenance staff and they put their towels and books on their desired chairs for them at 6:00 am. We are early risers so we did it ourselves. Pool bar does not open at 10:00 am, and the ice is brought in only at 11:00 am so take water with you from the mini-bar in your room.

Entertainment:  I must admit that the shows (if you can call them that) are more geared toward kids rather than adults (can’t believe I’m saying that but I missed the cheesy nightly shows we typically have in all inclusive resorts). The hotel does not have a huge theater to accommodate all the guests so the performers present their show at the “Avenue Bar” which is located across from the Japanese restaurant. The place is small and as I mentioned, there’s not enough room for people to sit/stand and watch the show so every evening there are arguments and fights – not cool. The bar has sprawling lounge beds, couches, little corners to sit and have a quiet drink and absolutely magnificent view of the ocean and pools. 
Word to the wise – alcohol in all hotels are typically watered down (we saw staff pouring water into liquor bottles!) but this time it was watered down so much that after five tequila shots I was able to walk back to my room when typically one glass or white zinfandel takes me out!
Daily activities – Very disappointing.  They do have a large wooden board right next to the main pool indicating daily activities at different times but no one is there on time and consequently the activities never happen. Since the don’t have an actual entertainment staff,  no games are organized like bingo, fun games for the kids in the afternoon like water balloon toss, dance competitions or morning exercise on the pool deck like other resorts have.

Kids clubs:   when the weather turns gray and rainy, parents opt to send their kids to the lower level of the main pyramid (the Lanzarote room) they have a huge room for kids (it looked to me ages 3-10 but I’m not sure) with inflatable rides, games and couches. A staff of 4-6 is constantly there to supervise and parents are welcome to come in and spend time there with the kids. Teen club in the nearby room is equipped with wii, Xbox and a pool table, plus a tv comfy chairs and a dvd player.  

Prices : Can’t tell you how outraged I was to realize that most places in Cancun try to rip you off and I’m not being sarcastic. I’m well aware that tourists are easy prey and the islands are notorious for overcharging, but $40 for sunscreen at the hotel boutique is criminal. Spa services are no better, basic massage starts at $200 and I bought three bananas with two Evian water bottles, they charged me $14 at the Airport – seething as I type this.

I was going to upload pictures but the traveller’s gallery here is truly sufficient and captures the entire hotel from every angle. 
Enjoy your trip, folks!

reviews.author: SR_BR_NY
reviews.title: Great location and beach, BUT!
reviews.text:
Beautiful lobby. Long wait to finally get your room. Be carefull! When you book a so called suite, it will be a regular room. For the price to stay here you have no walk in shower. Only tubs. Ridiculous! Every bathroom has lime deposits and hard water stains on all bathroom fixtures yet they keep the resort clean. Most people are very friendly but some are not.
Christian, of guest services and Max, head of food dept. made my stay much better. We had issues booking dinner reservations and some restaurants they plain suck! These two people made it a better experience and deserve credit. 
Fabulous weather every day. Easy to get everywhere and the buses comes often.
Don't buy pesos in the hotel. They will rip you off. Exchange downtown. Also, don't buy more than you need. If you exchange back to US dollars you get screwd!

reviews.author: CobraGT500
reviews.title: NOT what we were expecting
reviews.text:
For a resort on a beautiful beach and in an area where you can leave the resort to shop/explore, this is the place. However, if you are a vacation club member used to all of the pampering you get as part of the "perks" at other resorts, this is NOT the place for you! We were left to find the club member check in on our own after confusing directions and hand gestures to "help" us find our way through three buildings, then we were greeted with an attitude. The girl at check in was very condescending to the platinum Melia Club member we were traveling with. We have never encountered a rude person on ANY Melia Club properties until this trip. 
The food was unremarkable, usually cold and one note in flavor. Drinks were so slow that we began ordering doubles. Bana, the Asian fusion restaurant, had the best, most flavorful, fresh food. The sushi was excellent and the hot dishes came to the table hot. We were so impressed that we ate there two nights in a row. However, in the Brazilian restaurant, The Market,  I watched the waiter go to the buffet next door and "assemble" our appetizers and desserts-disappointing! I was told that another woman and I were laughing too loud in the Blue Agave bar, so everyone at the bar (17 of us) got up and left. The bartender was left without any customers thanks to the manager.
Our room was always clean, but I had to repeatedly ask to get the fridge restocked with water, then received a phone call telling me I only get one restock per day-that's all I wanted since it was never done to begin with!
Overall, this was an acceptable place to stay, but if you are a club member, the level of quality and service is not at the level that other Melia Club resorts offer. Playa Del Carmen was $6 more per night and 10x better in service, quality and dining.

reviews.author: Melissa M
reviews.title: Spectacular location and service, food was OK
reviews.text:
We just got back from a 5 night stay at Paradisus Cancun and had an amazing time.  

The pros: service was spectacular, location right on the beach, jacuzzi tub on our room's balcony facing the ocean, top shelf alcohol, poolside and beach side drink and food service.

The cons: food was very mediocre.  presentation was always great, but the food itself was either overcooked, tasteless, or cold.  the resort is so huge that it feels like a ghost town as you are walking through it, and it is always cold inside.  The building has a corporate feel when you walk rather than warm and laid back luxury.  We used our jacuzzi tub on the balcony every night, but it was basically broken (jets didn't work), and the faucets barely dripped water so it took about 45 minutes to fill.  Lastly, you are constantly being sold to and the beach towel check out for the hotel are actually just sales guys trying to hustle you into purchasing an excursion.

Overall, we enjoyed our experience, but might try staying at another resort the next time we go to cancun.

reviews.author: dianne40
reviews.title: Somethings great somethings not
reviews.text:
Our family just returned from 6 days at the Paradisus.  

Pros:
- Beach is beautiful.  Pools are pretty but too cold to swim.  
- Wait staff are all really friendly and do a great job
- Ocean front rooms are great for sleeping at night to the sound of the waves
- Lobby is really pretty
- Health club is nice and clean

Cons:

- Front desk staff is so so unfriendly.  When we were checking out - I stood at front desk for almost 5 minutes before the front desk clerk would even look at me.  She was busy on her computer.  After checking us out, she never said anything such as " Thank you come back again."  It was almost like we were bothering her.  
- No furniture on our balcony.  Not even one chair.  We had an ocean front room but, could not use the balcony because we never had any chairs.  I called front desk the first day and requested some chairs.  The front desk told me that they took our deck furniture to accomodate a room which had 4 persons.  I explained that we had 3 persons and not even a chair.  She said that she would try to get us furniture.  But, after 6 days, we never got any deck furniture.  We pulled the chairs out from inside the room.  
- hotel room - seemed like it needed some repairs.  - bathroom mirrow had chips and bit stains, some holes in the dry wall in bathrooms around the doors,  opening and closing the in room safe was difficult - it took 3 -4 times before it would work. 
- dinner reservations - when calling for reservations - frequently we were told that nothing was available.  Then we would go by the restaurant at the requested time and they were plenty of available tables.  It didn't make sense to any of the other quests as well.
- restaurant receptionists  - not friendly except at Fuego.  They act like the police.  We showed up for our reservation on time and they said they had no record of our reservation.    We after about 10 minutes they finally found it.  No sorry, nothing.  
- noise - we were in Tower 3.  The disco is very loud and the pounding of the bass was so loud that it was difficult at times to go to sleep.  Sometimes to 1am.
- my daughter got sick and I was bringing her a bowl of soup to the room.  The receptionist told me that I wasn't allowed to take soup to my room.  I told her my daughter was sick and couldn't get out of bed and she said that was the rule.  No soup for my daughter.  
- kids club - not real inviting for kids.  went to the kids club out by the pool and she sad that they weren't going to do activities today since they were not enough kids.  My daughter never went back.

reviews.author: callmej5
reviews.title: Picture perfect beach; average all-inclusive
reviews.text:
We stayed here prior to going to Paradisus La Perla in Playa, and this place definitely has its advantages and disadvantages.

Pros:
Short distance from the airport in the hotel zone
Courteous and attentive staff
Gorgeous beach with plenty of palapas and loungers
Wait staff serves food/drink on the beach
Both sides of the hotel look over water - either ocean or lagoon

Cons:
Mediocre food
Different sized rise and run on every stair you will climb!
Main tower music in the evening is quite loud if you stay in that tower and are trying to nap after a long day in the sun
Recurring sewage-like smell in the main tower in the evening near the bars/restaurants

I feel like I knew what to expect, and was okay with it.  Had a great time.  If you're a beach lover, great spot!  If you're into amazing food and luxurious accommodations, you may want to try La Perla.

reviews.author: k0sm056
